pg_0000.label: Register with UKMTO when entering and operating within the VRA.

pg_0002.label: Consult latest threat information when planning routes through the HRA.

pg_0003.label: Be ready to deviate from the planned route at short notice.

pg_0007.label: Follow Flag State and military guidance

pg_0008.label: Report to UKMTO and register with MSCHOA

pg_0011.label: Cooperate with other shipping and military forces

pg_0012.label: Cooperate with law enforcement to preserve evidence

pg_0014.label: Use BMP5 recommendations to plan the voyage through the high-risk region.

pg_0015.label: Apply measures to detect, avoid, deter, delay and report attacks.

pg_0016.label: Consult the UKMTO and MSCHOA websites for advice before and during transit.

pg_0017.label: Consult the latest IMO MSC Circulars and guidance on the Maritime Security Transit Corridor.

pg_0018.label: Use the MSTC (IRTC, BAM TSS, and connecting two-way route) when transiting the Gulf of Aden/Red Sea area.

pg_0019.label: Consider joining group transits or national convoys offered within the IRTC.

pg_0020.label: Notify insurers when the ship enters a JWC-listed area of perceived enhanced risk.

pg_0021.label: Check the JWC website for the current geographic limits of the listed area.

pg_0022.label: Obtain the latest military threat advice and threat assessments from UKMTO and MSCHOA before transit.

pg_0023.label: Seek supplementary information on threat characteristics, new tactics, and regional background from reporting centres/organisations listed in annex A.

pg_0024.label: Apply BMP measures to reduce opportunity for attack.

pg_0025.label: Incorporate risk assessment into voyage planning within the safety management system.

pg_0026.label: Identify prevention, mitigation and recovery measures combining statutory regulations with supplementary measures.

pg_0027.label: Apply these measures even for ships transiting the VRA without entering the HRA.

pg_0028.label: Consider flag state, company, charterer and insurer requirements in the assessment.

pg_0029.label: Evaluate the threat assessment and geographical areas of increased risk.

pg_0030.label: Assess background factors such as traffic patterns, local patterns of life, and fishing vessel activity.

pg_0031.label: Obtain an understanding of military presence from UKMTO and consider cooperation with military forces.

pg_0032.label: Decide on embarkation of Privately Contracted Armed Security Personnel (PCASP).

pg_0033.label: Evaluate ship characteristics, vulnerabilities and inherent capabilities, including citadel and/or safe muster points, freeboard, speed, and general arrangement.

pg_0034.label: Review ship's and company's procedures including drills, watch rosters, chain of command and decision-making processes.

pg_0035.label: Complete a detailed threat and risk assessment for each voyage and activity in the region.

pg_0036.label: Regularly review and update threat and risk assessments and plans as necessary.

pg_0037.label: Review the Ship Security Assessment (SSA), Ship Security Plan (SSP) and Vessel Hardening Plan (VHP).

pg_0038.label: Provide the Master with guidance on recommended routes, updated plans and requirements for group transits and national convoys.

pg_0040.label: Conduct due diligence on Private Maritime Security Companies (PMSCs) before possible use of PCASP.

pg_0041.label: Consider placement of hidden position transmitting devices.

pg_0042.label: Review company manning requirements and consider disembarking non-essential crew.

pg_0044.label: Minimize communications with external parties, especially regarding rendezvous points and waiting positions.

pg_0045.label: Control and limit email correspondence with agents, charterers and chandlers to the contractually required minimum.

pg_0046.label: Obtain the latest threat information and check current NAVAREA warnings and alerts.

pg_0047.label: Implement VRA/MSCHOA vessel registration and reporting requirements per section 6 and annexes D and E.

pg_0048.label: If PCASP are used, confirm the embarkation plan.

pg_0049.label: Confirm propulsion can operate at full speed.

pg_0050.label: Implement security measures in accordance with the Ship Security Plan (SSP).

pg_0051.label: Fully brief the crew on preparations and conduct drills with the Ship Protection Measures (SPM) in place.

pg_0052.label: Test SPM including security of all access points, lock-down conditions, bridge team security knowledge, and crew understanding of differing actions for pirate vs other attacks during drills.

pg_0053.label: Prepare an emergency communication plan including all essential emergency contact numbers and prepared messages.

pg_0054.label: Display the emergency communication plan at all external communications stations, the safe muster point, and/or the citadel.

pg_0055.label: Test communication devices and the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) before transit.

pg_0056.label: Define and apply the ship's AIS policy, keeping AIS switched on through the VRA/HRA but restricting broadcast data to identity, position, course, speed, navigational status, and safety-related information.

pg_0057.label: Reschedule planned maintenance on voyage-critical equipment to avoid it occurring during HRA transit.

pg_0058.label: Submit ship reports as specified in section 6 and annexes D and E.

pg_0060.label: Ensure all access points are limited and controlled.

pg_0061.label: Avoid drifting, waiting, anchoring and slow steaming, particularly in the MSTC.

pg_0062.label: Minimise use of VHF and use email or secure satellite telephone instead where possible.

pg_0063.label: Only answer known or legitimate callers on VHF.

pg_0064.label: Identify and plan applicable SPM during the voyage planning process.

pg_0065.label: Establish primary layer of defence: maintain good look out/vigilance, use motion sensors/CCTV, manage speed and freeboard.

pg_0066.label: Establish secondary layer of defence: harden doors, install gates/grates, maintain communication, use manoeuvring.

pg_0067.label: Establish last layer of defence: internal door hardening, razor wire, citadel/safe muster point, and PCASP if applicable.

pg_0068.label: Consider additional alterations, equipment, or personnel beyond BMP scope as determined by the Company.

pg_0070.label: Maintain an all-round lookout from an elevated position.

pg_0071.label: Consider shorter rotation of watch periods.

pg_0072.label: Maintain sufficient anti-glare binoculars for the enhanced bridge team.

pg_0073.label: Consider thermal imagery optics and night vision aids.

pg_0074.label: Maintain careful radar watch and monitor navigational warnings and communications, particularly VHF and GMDSS alerts.

pg_0075.label: Consider placing well-constructed dummies at strategic locations.

pg_0076.label: Consider using CCTV and fixed search lights for better monitoring.

pg_0077.label: Mount anti-piracy mirrors on the bridge wings.

pg_0078.label: Have the Master and officers practice manoeuvring the ship to build familiarity with its handling characteristics.

pg_0079.label: Practice avoidance manoeuvres while maintaining the best possible speed.

pg_0080.label: Use hydrostatic pressure created by manoeuvring rather than relying solely on speed.

pg_0081.label: Plan and install physical barriers around the vessel to increase the difficulty of climbing aboard for attackers.

pg_0082.label: Give special consideration to barrier placement on ships with sunken poop decks.

pg_0083.label: Ensure alarms are distinctive from one another.

pg_0084.label: Train crew members to recognize each alarm, especially the attack warning and the 'all clear' signal.

pg_0085.label: Back up all alarms with an announcement over the accommodation and deck PA system where fitted.

pg_0086.label: Conduct drills to confirm the alarm is heard throughout the ship and to measure time needed for all crew to reach safety.

pg_0087.label: Sound the ship's whistle continuously during an attack.

pg_0088.label: Use high tensile concertina razor wire with coil diameters of 730mm or 980mm.

pg_0089.label: Install a double roll of razor wire where possible.

pg_0090.label: If a double roll is not possible, place a single high-quality roll outboard of the ship's structure.

pg_0091.label: Secure razor wire to the ship properly, e.g. attach at least every third wire ring to ship's railings and rig a steel cable through its core.

pg_0092.label: Use personal protective equipment and wire hooks when moving and installing razor wire.

pg_0093.label: Obtain razor wire in short sections (e.g. 10m lengths).

pg_0094.label: Keep razor wire clear of mooring fairleads when at terminals.

pg_0095.label: Consider other barriers such as hanging swinging obstacles over the gunnels or purpose-built overhanging protection.

pg_0096.label: Apply blast resistant film to bridge windows in addition to existing lamination.

pg_0097.label: Prepare fabricated metal (steel/aluminium) plates for side/rear bridge windows and bridge wing door windows that can be quickly secured in an attack.

pg_0098.label: Install chain link fencing around bridge areas.

pg_0099.label: Place sandbags on bridge wings and inspect them regularly.

pg_0100.label: Deploy water spray and/or foam monitors to deter or delay boarding attempts.

pg_0101.label: Fix hoses and foam monitors in position covering likely access routes and operate them remotely.

pg_0102.label: Use fire hoses in jet mode with baffle plates fixed a short distance in front of the nozzle for improved water coverage.

pg_0103.label: Use water cannons to deliver water in a vertical sweeping arc.

pg_0104.label: Install water spray rails with spray nozzles to create a water curtain over larger areas.

pg_0105.label: Use foam only in addition to the ship's standard firefighting equipment stock.

pg_0106.label: Activate all available fire and general service pumps as needed.

pg_0107.label: Ensure supporting systems and additional power are ready for immediate use.

pg_0108.label: Conduct practice, observation, and drills regularly.

pg_0109.label: Control and deny access routes to accommodation and machinery spaces.

pg_0110.label: Ensure escape routes remain accessible to seafarers at all times.

pg_0111.label: Ensure doors/hatches on escape routes from manned compartments can be opened from the inside, even if locked.

pg_0112.label: Properly secure doors and hatches to the bridge, accommodation and machinery spaces to prevent opening from outside.

pg_0113.label: Designate a limited number of doors/hatches for security patrols and routine access, controlled by the Officer of the Watch.

pg_0114.label: Block external stairs or remove ladders on the accommodation block.

pg_0115.label: Fully dog down doors/hatches required for watertight integrity, in addition to locks, and use additional securing mechanisms like wire strops where possible.

pg_0116.label: Use removable barriers around pilot boarding points.

pg_0117.label: Fit steel bars to portholes and windows.

pg_0118.label: Brief crew on procedures for controlling access to accommodation, machinery spaces and store rooms.

pg_0119.label: Deny attackers access to ship propulsion.

pg_0120.label: Identify a safe muster point during the planning process that gives maximum physical protection to the crew.

pg_0121.label: If threat assessment shows risk of hull breach at or below the waterline, select a muster point above the waterline.

pg_0122.label: Consider the likely path of a blast when selecting the safe muster point.

pg_0123.label: Design and construct citadels to resist forced entry.

pg_0124.label: Supply citadel with food, water, sanitation, and reliable communications (ideally satellite phone and VHF).

pg_0125.label: Retain control of propulsion and steering during an attack if possible.

pg_0126.label: Use the citadel only as a complement to, not a replacement for, all other ship protection measures (SPM).

pg_0127.label: Drill the use of the citadel and define conditions and supporting logistics for its use in the Ship Security Plan (SSP).

pg_0128.label: Account for and confirm all crew members are inside the citadel.

pg_0129.label: Maintain two-way communication with the citadel.

pg_0130.label: Ensure the Master decides when to use the citadel.

pg_0131.label: Install and use CCTV cameras covering vulnerable areas, particularly the poop deck and bridge.

pg_0132.label: Locate CCTV monitors on the bridge and at the safe muster point/citadel.

pg_0133.label: Retain CCTV footage after an attack.

pg_0134.label: Where possible, arrange for CCTV to be monitored/recorded ashore by the company.

pg_0135.label: Maintain weather deck lighting around the accommodation block and rear-facing lighting on the poop deck.

pg_0136.label: Have search lights ready for immediate use if fitted.

pg_0137.label: Switch on over-side lighting once attackers are identified or an attack commences, if fitted.

pg_0138.label: Exhibit only navigation lights at night and never switch them off.

pg_0139.label: Leave deck lights on while at anchor.

pg_0140.label: Retain the ability to turn off all internal accommodation lights.

pg_0141.label: Secure all ship's tools and equipment in a locked, secure location.

pg_0142.label: Provide ballistic protection for gas cylinders or containers of flammable liquids where possible.

pg_0143.label: Store excess gas cylinders in a secure location or land them before the transit if possible.

pg_0144.label: Apply the same guidance used for selecting a Private Maritime Security Company (PMSC) when considering PCASP.

pg_0145.label: Confirm that use of PCASP is permitted by the ship's Flag State and any relevant littoral states before engaging them.

pg_0146.label: Assess the current threat and risk environment before deciding to engage a PMSC.

pg_0147.label: Review the company risk assessment, voyage plan requirements, ship speed, freeboard, and type of operations.

pg_0148.label: Check levels of protection provided by navies, coastguards and maritime police along the route.

pg_0149.label: Verify that the ship's Flag State and relevant littoral states permit PMSC deployment.

pg_0150.label: Only employ PMSCs accredited to ISO 28007-1:2015.

pg_0151.label: Ensure the PMSC contract is between the technical manager and the PMSC, does not prejudice the ship's insurance arrangements, confirms current compliant PMSC insurance, clearly defines the use-of-force procedure, and confirms the Master's overriding authority.

pg_0152.label: Confirm Flag State policy on deployment of PCASP before engaging any armed security provider.

pg_0153.label: If PCASP is not permitted, determine whether the Flag State provides or allows a military Vessel Protection Detachment (VPD) instead.

pg_0154.label: If a VPD is to be provided by another State, obtain Flag State approval for that arrangement.

pg_0155.label: Report and obtain acknowledgment from the Flag State for deployment of PCASP or VPD where required, and report deployment upon entering the VRA.

pg_0156.label: Establish and acknowledge the Master's overriding authority over PCASP.

pg_0157.label: Confirm the Rules for the Use of Force (RUF) are acceptable to both the Flag State and the company.

pg_0158.label: Master and PCASP must clearly understand and acknowledge the RUF as outlined in the contract.

pg_0159.label: Maintain documentation authorising carriage of weapons and ammunition.

pg_0160.label: Report any incident involving use of weapons or armed force at the earliest instance to the Flag State and Chief Security Officer (CSO).

pg_0161.label: PCASP must act strictly in accordance with the agreed RUF.

pg_0162.label: Register ship's movements with MSCHOA before entering the HRA, including position reporting forms and group transit participation if applicable.

pg_0163.label: On departing the VRA, check and comply with adjacent regional reporting requirements such as NATO Shipping Centre (Mediterranean) or ReCAAP/Singapore Information Fusion Center (SE Asia).

pg_0164.label: Incorporate Industry Releasable Threat Assessments (IRTAs) and Threat Bulletins (IRTBs) into the ship's threat and risk assessment process.

pg_0165.label: Report suspicious activity to responsible authorities with as much detail as possible.

pg_0166.label: Collect photographs, video, and radar plot data of suspicious activity if it can be done without compromising safety.

pg_0167.label: When in doubt whether activity is suspicious, report it anyway.

pg_0168.label: Send an Initial Report to UKMTO upon entering the VRA.

pg_0169.label: Send Daily Reports updating position, course and speed.

pg_0170.label: Send a Final Report upon departure from the VRA or arrival in port.

pg_0171.label: Report any suspicious or irregular activity to UKMTO when necessary.

pg_0172.label: Maintain reporting continuity per guidance in Annexes C, D and E throughout the passage.

pg_0173.label: Optionally contact UKMTO to arrange drills and exercises for passage planning.

pg_0174.label: Consult BMP5 Annex C to help identify suspicious or irregular activity.

pg_0175.label: Submit a suspicious/irregular activity report using BMP5 Annex D to UKMTO.

pg_0176.label: Report despite concerns about possible Port State investigation or delay.

pg_0177.label: Maintain effective visual and radar lookouts at all times.

pg_0178.label: Activate any additional protective measures and plans immediately, using whatever time is available.

pg_0179.label: Report the attack to UKMTO without delay.

pg_0180.label: Reconfirm all crew are in the safe muster point or citadel as instructed by the Master.

pg_0181.label: Ensure the SSAS has been activated; if not, report the attack immediately by telephone.

pg_0182.label: Commence small alterations of helm while maintaining speed as attackers close in.

pg_0184.label: Move calmly, slowly and deliberately with hands always visible

pg_0185.label: Comply fully and exactly with attackers' instructions

pg_0186.label: Leave CCTV and audio recording devices running

pg_0187.label: Stay mentally active, track time, remain physically active where possible, stay calm and positive

pg_0188.label: Do not take photographs, attempt to engage attackers, make aggressive movements, be confrontational, or resist

pg_0189.label: Take all way off the ship and stop the engines.

pg_0190.label: Direct all remaining crew to proceed to the citadel or safe muster point, locking all internal doors en route.

pg_0191.label: Have PCASP follow procedures pre-agreed with the company and Master.

pg_0192.label: Ensure all crew, including the Master, bridge team, and PCASP, are present in the citadel or safe muster point.

pg_0193.label: Establish communications from the citadel with UKMTO and the company, confirming all crew are accounted for.

pg_0194.label: Remain in the citadel until forced to leave by conditions or advised by the military.

pg_0196.label: Be humble and respectful to the pirates

pg_0197.label: Look out for colleagues' well-being and stay together as a team where possible

pg_0198.label: Accept the new pirate leadership while maintaining the hierarchy of rank among crew

pg_0199.label: Try to establish normal communication with the pirates

pg_0200.label: Maintain personal hygiene and save water and essentials

pg_0201.label: Stay positive, patient, and maintain routines including spiritual needs as permitted

pg_0202.label: Keep breathing regular, meditate, and stay mentally active

pg_0203.label: Respect religion of self, colleagues, and pirates

pg_0204.label: Do not offer resistance or argue with pirates or colleagues

pg_0205.label: Increase to maximum speed if not already doing so.

pg_0206.label: Steer a straight course to maintain maximum speed.

pg_0207.label: Initiate the ship's emergency procedures and activate the emergency communication plan.

pg_0208.label: Sound the emergency alarm and make an attack announcement per the communication plan.

pg_0209.label: Make a MAYDAY call on VHF Ch.16.

pg_0210.label: Send a distress message via DSC and Inmarsat-C as applicable.

pg_0211.label: Activate the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS).

pg_0212.label: Report the attack immediately to UKMTO by telephone (+44 2392 222060).

pg_0214.label: Activate water spray and consider activating other self-protection measures.

pg_0215.label: Secure all external doors and, where possible, internal public rooms and cabins.

pg_0216.label: Muster all crew not required on bridge/engine room at the safe muster point or citadel as instructed by the Master.

pg_0217.label: When sea conditions allow, consider altering course to increase an approaching skiff's exposure to wind/waves.

pg_0218.label: Check that the Voyage Data Recorder (VDR) is recording.

pg_0219.label: If PCASP are present, allow them to take agreed actions to warn off attackers.

pg_0220.label: Do not bargain with pirates for personal privileges

pg_0221.label: Brief and prepare the ship's crew to cooperate fully during any military action onboard

pg_0222.label: Instruct crew to keep low to the deck and cover head with both hands

pg_0223.label: Keep hands visible at all times

pg_0224.label: Be prepared to be challenged on identity

pg_0226.label: Avoid any movements that could be interpreted as aggressive

pg_0227.label: Brief crew before entering the threat area on what position to adopt if a blast threat is detected.

pg_0228.label: Instruct crew to lie flat on the deck if a blast is imminent.

pg_0229.label: Instruct crew to adopt a brace position (arms/legs bent, holding something solid, feet planted).

pg_0230.label: Instruct crew to move away from vulnerable areas such as port/starboard side, poop deck or engine room.

pg_0231.label: After a blast, ensure all crew and PCASP are accounted for.

pg_0232.label: Survey the area where the blast occurred.

pg_0235.label: Follow military advice if a missile attack warning is received.

pg_0236.label: If no warning is received and a missile is spotted, issue a PA warning to the crew.

pg_0237.label: Maintain awareness of the ship plot in the vicinity and keep clear of naval and associated ships if sea room allows.

pg_0238.label: Avoid all published or identified mine danger areas and maintain close liaison with military authorities.

pg_0239.label: If operating close to mine danger areas, manoeuvre clear of floating objects and keep the forward area of the ship clear of crew, maintaining effective lookouts.

pg_0240.label: Obtain specific self-protection advice from UKMTO when operating in mine danger areas.

pg_0241.label: In the early stages of an unclear attack, follow the piracy approach-stage initial actions.

pg_0242.label: Assess the speed boat's occupancy before classifying the threat.

pg_0243.label: Use the safe muster point before entering a citadel located below the waterline.

pg_0244.label: Arrange timely medical assessment and care (physical and mental) for seafarers after an attack or hostage situation.

pg_0245.label: Ensure the company has an emergency management plan covering attack response, long hostage negotiations, and family support.

pg_0246.label: Preserve evidence correctly following IMO Guidelines on Preservation and Collection of Evidence A28/Res.1091 and other industry guidance.

pg_0247.label: Complete a detailed, comprehensive report after any attack or suspicious activity, including witness statements.

pg_0248.label: Send a copy of the report to the company, the Flag State and appropriate authorities.

pg_0249.label: Preserve the crime scene and all evidence where possible.

pg_0250.label: Avoid contaminating or interfering with possible evidence; if in doubt, do not touch and leave items in place.

pg_0251.label: Do not clean up the area, including hosing it down, and do not discard anything no matter how unimportant.

pg_0252.label: Take initial statements from the crew.

pg_0253.label: Take photographs of the crime scene from multiple viewpoints.

pg_0254.label: Protect the VDR for future evidence.

pg_0255.label: Make a list of items taken (e.g. mobile phones with numbers).

pg_0256.label: Facilitate access to the crime scene and relevant documentation for law enforcement authorities.

pg_0257.label: Make crew available for interview by law enforcement authorities.

pg_0258.label: Contact INTERPOL within three days of a hijacking.

pg_0259.label: Consult INTERPOL on recommended practices for preserving evidence.

pg_0260.label: Monitor physical and mental health of seafarers and families exposed to the threat.

pg_0261.label: Provide independent support and other assistance as appropriate.

pg_0262.label: Direct affected seafarers/families to humanitarian programmes (e.g. seafarerswelfare.org, missiontoseafarers.org).

pg_0263.label: Transmit daily reports as requested by UKMTO while within the VRA.

pg_0264.label: Use the suspicious/irregular activity report form if such activity is observed.

pg_0265.label: Record time, position, and a brief description of the suspicious craft and activity witnessed.

pg_0266.label: Include any available imagery with the report.

pg_0267.label: Submit a detailed report of the event to UKMTO and MSCHOA after any attack or suspicious activity.

pg_0268.label: Provide a copy of the report to the IMB.

pg_0269.label: Assess vessel behavior and characteristics (e.g. no lights at night, multiple outboard motors, loitering without fishing activity, packages hung outboard, excessive antennas) against the suspicious indicator list.

pg_0270.label: Apply own seagoing experience and regional knowledge, since the list is not exhaustive.

pg_0271.label: If in doubt, report the observation and contact UKMTO.

pg_0272.label: Register the vessel's movements with MSCHOA before entering the Vessel Registration Area.

pg_0273.label: Obtain the 'Register a Vessel's Movements' form from the MSCHOA website or UKHO Chart Q6099.

pg_0274.label: Use one of the two principal methods to register the ship's movement with MSCHOA.

pg_0275.label: Register via the MSCHOA website using the register tab.

pg_0276.label: If online registration is not possible, use the downloadable form (updated March 2018) for offline completion.

pg_0277.label: If other options are unavailable, email the completed registration information to postmaster@mschoa.org with subject heading 'MSCHOA Vessel Registration'.

pg_0278.label: Include all mandatory (*) fields: ship contact number, ship contact email, owner name, operator name, operator address, DPA name, DPA telephone, DPA email.

pg_0279.label: Record the number and nationality of armed security personnel on board in the report.

pg_0280.label: Report entry point and entry date/time to the MSCHOA vessel registration area (78°E/10°S/23°N/Suez/Port).

pg_0281.label: Report exit point and exit date/time from the MSCHOA vessel registration area.

pg_0282.label: State intended IRTC transit, ETA to IRTC in UTC/Zulu time, and direction of transit (East/West).

pg_0283.label: Indicate intention to join a group transit or a National Convoy, and specify which convoy.

pg_0284.label: Provide crew numbers and nationalities, draught, freeboard of lowest accessible deck, and planned transit speed in metres.

pg_0285.label: Prioritise completing and transmitting the starred (*) fields on the reporting form first.

pg_0286.label: Provide remaining non-starred data if time and conditions permit.

pg_0287.label: Warn UKMTO and MSCHOA authorities of the attack or suspicious craft sighting.

pg_0288.label: Warn the rest of the fishing fleet.

pg_0289.label: Communicate contact details of the second (land-based) Master, who has vessel knowledge, to authorities.

pg_0290.label: For Purse Seiners, evacuate all crew from the deck and the crow's nest.

pg_0291.label: If pirates control the vessel and the purse seine net is deployed, encourage them to allow recovery of the nets.

pg_0292.label: If net recovery is permitted, follow proper stowage instructions and explain gear function to the pirates.

pg_0293.label: Make early contact with naval/military authorities before transiting the VRA.

pg_0294.label: Avoid transiting close to areas of conflict.

pg_0295.label: Maintain close contact with UKMTO throughout the voyage.

pg_0296.label: Check MSCHOA and International Sailing Federation websites for the most up-to-date information.

pg_0297.label: Avoid operating or transiting within 200nm of the Somali coast regardless of licensing status.

pg_0298.label: Do not commence fishing operations if radar shows unidentified boats present.

pg_0299.label: If polyester skiffs typical of pirates are sighted, move away at full speed sailing into wind and sea.

pg_0300.label: Avoid stopping at night; maintain bridge, deck and engine-room watch.

pg_0301.label: Maintain radar watch during fishing operations.

pg_0302.label: Use only mandatory navigation and safety lights at night.

pg_0303.label: If drifting while fishing at night, keep guard at bridge, deck and engine room with engine ready for immediate start-up.

pg_0305.label: Use VHF as little as possible.

pg_0306.label: Activate AIS when maritime patrol aircraft are operating in the area.

pg_0307.label: Register the fishing vessel with MSCHOA for the entire activity period off Somalia, including crew list and intentions.

pg_0308.label: Conduct training prior to passage or fishing operations in the area.

pg_0309.label: Provide MSCHOA access to Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) data if equipped.

pg_0310.label: Identify the vessel promptly when requested by aircraft or ships of any international/national anti-piracy operation.

pg_0311.label: Respond without delay to identification requests made by a fishing vessel being approached.

pg_0312.label: Monitor for a definite course alteration toward the ship combined with a rapid, unexplained speed increase by the suspected craft.

pg_0313.label: Watch for small craft maintaining the same course and speed as the ship for an unusually long period or distance.

pg_0314.label: Treat sudden course changes toward the ship accompanied by aggressive behaviour as a suspicious indicator.

pg_0315.label: Reference UNCLOS Article 101 as the formal legal definition of piracy.

pg_0316.label: Assess suspicious activity against BMP5 practical indicators (use or attempted use of violence, boarding attempts, use of ladders/grappling hooks/weapons).

pg_0317.label: Have the Master form a judgment on whether persons attempting to board are suspected pirates.

pg_0318.label: Report the piracy or armed robbery incident to the IMB PRC as a trusted point of contact, from anywhere in the world.

pg_0319.label: Expect the IMB PRC to immediately relay the incident to local law enforcement requesting assistance.

pg_0320.label: Expect the IMB PRC to broadcast the incident information to all vessels via Inmarsat Safety Net.

pg_0321.label: Report anomalies and incidents to the IFC via the Voluntary Community Reporting (VCR) scheme.

pg_0322.label: Contact INTERPOL's Maritime Security sub-Directorate (MTS) during business hours for guidance on preserving evidence after a pirate attack.

pg_0323.label: Outside business hours, contact INTERPOL's Command and Co-ordination Centre (CCC).

pg_0324.label: Send regular voluntary reports to UKMTO including position, speed, and ETA at next port of call.

pg_0325.label: Follow reporting format per Maritime Security Chart Q6099.

pg_0326.label: Receive and act on emerging information passed by UKMTO regarding threats or incidents.

pg_0327.label: Use NCAGS as a secondary emergency point of contact for mariners in distress if UKMTO cannot be reached.

pg_0328.label: Monitor NCAGS briefings, website, email, and duty phone for transit guidance.

pg_0329.label: Get threat information, review BMP guidance, and review Rules for the Use of Force.

pg_0330.label: Conduct a risk assessment and identify ship protection measures.

pg_0600.label: Pilots should use Standard Marine Communication Phrases (SMCP) approved by IMO when communicating.

pg_0601.label: An officer must check and verify that LSA equipment, including liferafts, is correctly fitted and stowed (painter secured) immediately after it comes aboard.

pg_0602.label: Raise identified safety deficiencies at safety meetings and ensure they are taken seriously by the Master.

pg_0603.label: Passenger formally reports the defect in writing using the Company's Customer Complaint Form.

pg_0604.label: Passenger follows up by telephone after no feedback within a month.

pg_0605.label: Cruise/Tour Operator directs passenger to the company responsible for vessel maintenance.

pg_0606.label: Discussion held on Corporate responsibility under Section 3 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974.

pg_0607.label: Operator agrees to refer the matter to the Ship Operator.

pg_0608.label: Passenger contacts Cruise/Tour Operator a second time after another month with no feedback.

pg_0609.label: Forward the safety report to the Managing Director of the ship operating company.

pg_0610.label: Verify whether the reported defect was already known and whether repair/approval by a the other vessel had occurred.

pg_0611.label: Modify the report handling process to ensure safety-related reports are reliably forwarded in future.

pg_0612.label: Maintain a proper lookout at all times (Rule 5).

pg_0613.label: Proceed at a safe speed appropriate to conditions (Rule 6).

pg_0614.label: Cut speed and look around to be aware of surroundings (RYA Sea Sense campaign guidance).

pg_0615.label: Report such incidents to the MAIB promptly.

pg_0616.label: Contact the Coastguard and/or Police without hesitation if a criminal act may have been committed.

pg_0617.label: Maintain a heightened lookout for lobster pot markers, especially in known high-density areas such as the eastern Solent and NE Isle of Wight.

pg_0618.label: Before restarting the engine after a suspected propeller fouling, verify the propeller and shaft are fully clear.

pg_0619.label: Employment agency/business must obtain information from the hirer about the position, including known health/safety risks and control measures (Regulation 18).

pg_0620.label: Request a copy of the hirer's risk assessment.

pg_0621.label: Verify the work seeker has necessary experience, training and qualifications for the position (Regulation 19).

pg_0623.label: Make the responsible Master or Officer aware of his responsibilities under the law and good seamanship.

pg_0624.label: Circulate a depersonalised version of the report to all company personnel involved in ship navigation.

pg_0625.label: Prioritise safety of life, the ship, and the environment above all other factors when making navigation or operational decisions.

pg_0626.label: Depart from the charted course and waypoints when good seamanship or the collision regulations require it.

pg_0627.label: Call the Master without hesitation if in any doubt.

pg_0628.label: Wait outside the channel (east of the islands) and confirm the pilot boat is on station before proceeding in

pg_0629.label: Establish a contingency plan for extracting the vessel from the channel if the pilot is not there by the time it narrows

pg_0630.label: Avoid attempting to stop or hold position with the current from astern

pg_0631.label: If the pilot is not present, proceed safely through the narrows without the pilot rather than stopping near the bottleneck

pg_0632.label: Do not let schedule pressure drive the decision to proceed into a hazardous narrow channel without proper pilotage assurance

pg_0633.label: Build contingencies into the passage plan, identifying possible anchorages and points where manoeuvres can be safely aborted.

pg_0634.label: Plan vessel arrivals and monitor execution of the plan, communicating changes in good time to port control.

pg_0635.label: Continuously plot approaching traffic using radar/ARPA and monitor CPA/TCPA.

pg_0636.label: Attempt contact with the approaching vessel via DSC and VHF, and if needed call the relevant traffic authority (e.g., Gris Nez Traffic).

pg_0637.label: Take avoiding action (hard to starboard) when the overtaking vessel fails to keep clear and collision becomes imminent.

pg_0638.label: Forward the report to the vessel operator discreetly.

pg_0639.label: Engage in correspondence with the operator and their lawyers when the operator did not respond as expected.

pg_0640.label: Advise the operator that information would be passed to their P&I Club.

pg_0641.label: Contact the P&I Club to confirm willingness to handle the issue before escalating.

pg_0642.label: Report the hazard/incident onboard to ship management.

pg_0643.label: Staff Captain and relevant officers review the incident at a safety meeting to determine recurrence risk.

pg_0644.label: Customer relations/technical department evaluate feasibility of structural modification to the railing/panel gap.

pg_0645.label: Assess whether filling the gap between the glass panel and deck is appropriate.

pg_0646.label: Coat the underside of trays with a non-slip material.

pg_0647.label: Encourage passengers to keep trays in the open deck cafeteria area rather than carrying them to the deck above the pool.

pg_0649.label: Maintain a risk register identifying and mitigating risks of routine activities.

pg_0650.label: Learn key helm orders and basic courtesy words in crew members' languages as master.

pg_0651.label: Use senior officers and bilingual crew as intermediaries to translate safety instructions into each man's own language.

pg_0652.label: Devise visual/physical demonstrations (e.g. pantomime) to convey safety messages at monthly safety meetings.

pg_0653.label: Identify and remove common hazards: buckets of water near ladder feet, unchanged lamp bulbs, unroped painted/dangerous areas, loose wood/shackles/spare parts on deck.

pg_0654.label: Check that a lifeboat is safe to lower before lowering it.

pg_0655.label: Carry out lifeboat and emergency drills frequently so every man knows his role.

pg_0656.label: Teach all crew in their own language what and how to do via bilingual speakers, under master's direction.

pg_0657.label: Establish a single common working language onboard adequate for routine operations.

pg_0658.label: Ensure the common working language is also used for training delivery.

pg_0659.label: Ensure the common working language supports effective emergency response.

pg_0660.label: Avoid informally accommodating multiple languages in an ad hoc manner despite good intentions.

pg_0661.label: Ensure all emergency escape/access hatches are operable in both directions at all times.

pg_0662.label: Stop the practice of locking emergency escape or access routes in the name of security.

pg_0663.label: Use digital locks with one-way, fail-open operation on bridge doors, engine rooms, and radio rooms.

pg_0664.label: Use fixed locks or bolts where appropriate instead of padlocks on escape routes.

pg_0665.label: Install remote locking of car deck doors with fail-to-safe or unlocked status, using hydraulics, compressed air, or electronic systems.

pg_0666.label: Deploy micro switches, intruder detection systems, CCTV, alarms, seals, or dedicated manual guarding as alternative security measures.

pg_0667.label: Select the appropriate combination of measures based on ship type and trading pattern.

pg_0668.label: Monitor the radar echo's track to assess closest point of approach

pg_0669.label: Dispatch the patrol boat ahead to investigate the echo and advise the other vessel of intentions

pg_0670.label: Confirm identity and equipment fit of the contact vessel

pg_0671.label: Issue an open letter to industry membership (via IMarEST/MER) to solicit opinions on whether the issue falls within program scope.

pg_0672.label: Weigh the two safety perspectives raised: immediate personnel risk vs operational viability risk.

pg_0673.label: Classify the issue as falling within the ISM Code based on balance of responses.

pg_0674.label: Gather further data on frequency of bearing/crankshaft failures, contributory factors, and effectiveness of mitigation measures.

pg_0675.label: Forward findings to relevant organisations for assessment once enquiries are complete.

pg_0676.label: Verify that any escape trunk locking/security system still permits two-way opening (escape and access) as per SOLAS Reg 13.3.1.5.2.

pg_0677.label: Log on to www.chirp.co.uk and click 'Submit Report'.

pg_0678.label: Enter contact details and complete the report in the window provided.

pg_0679.label: Submit the report, which is emailed directly from the website to CHIRP offices.

pg_0680.label: Request and check for confirmation that the report has been received.

pg_0681.label: Prepare appropriate measures for restricted visibility based on circumstances and own risk assessment.

pg_0682.label: Do not leave port into restricted visibility conditions without radar if avoidable.

pg_0683.label: When radar-equipped, account for the possibility that other vessels, especially leisure craft, may not have or be using radar.

pg_0684.label: Use sound signals in restricted visibility.

pg_0685.label: Maintain a proper look-out by sight, hearing, and all available means appropriate to conditions, per Rule 5.

pg_0686.label: Do not rely on the operation of equipment (e.g., radar) on another vessel to ensure your own safety.

pg_0687.label: Monitor the developing close-quarters situation and call the give-way vessel by name on VHF Ch.16 when action appears overdue.

pg_0688.label: Repeat VHF calls as range closes if no reply or action is observed.

pg_0689.label: As stand-on vessel, initiate own avoiding action (round turn to starboard) when it becomes apparent the give-way vessel will not act in time.

pg_0690.label: After the close-quarters situation is resolved, move to a working channel and advise the other vessel of the near-miss and question their understanding of the collision regulations.

pg_0691.label: Do not negotiate derogation from the COLREGS by radio.

pg_0692.label: Masters and Officers of the Watch must comply strictly with Rule 10 and apply all relevant requirements when using or crossing traffic separation schemes.

pg_0693.label: Stand-on vessel should maintain course and speed per the Rules rather than show unwarranted flexibility, even though it lacks an absolute right of way.

pg_0694.label: Company management must respond appropriately to the behaviour of the officers involved in the poor manoeuvre.

pg_0695.label: Maintain a safe speed per COLREG Rule 6 at all times in or near a TSS.

pg_0696.label: Reduce speed or wait for an appropriate gap if more time is needed to assess traffic or cross safely.

pg_0697.label: Cross traffic separation schemes or lanes on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the general traffic flow.

pg_0698.label: Only cross a TSS/lane if it is safe to do so; otherwise wait until a safe right-angle crossing can be made.

pg_0699.label: Make right-angle crossing the vessel's regular practice even when the TSS is empty, and draw the passage plan accordingly.

pg_0700.label: When behind schedule, do not alter the planned TSS crossing point/timing without first fully assessing traffic in the opposing lane.

pg_0701.label: If crossing traffic is present, request permission to cross via VHF but be prepared for refusal and have a safe fallback maneuver ready.

pg_0702.label: Do not rely on VHF agreement alone to resolve collision risk; use radar and AIS continuously to verify actual separation.

pg_0703.label: Maintain the obligation of safe navigation independently of vessel type or company fleet relationships.

pg_0704.label: Report and investigate near-misses company-wide, especially when the same maneuver is repeated by sister ships.

pg_0705.label: Maintain a high degree of alertness when transiting any traffic separation scheme.

pg_0706.label: Be prepared to act and react very quickly using rudder and engines.

pg_0707.label: Keep a sharp lookout at all times and think/plan ahead about developing traffic situations the vessel will shortly enter.

pg_0708.label: Take early and effective action that is clearly recognisable to all other vessels.

pg_0709.label: Reduce speed if more time is needed to assess the situation.

pg_0710.label: Apply normal COLREGS rules for open sea vessels to resolve any close-quarters situation within a TSS.

pg_0711.label: Avoid negotiating derogations from the Rules via VHF, even with AIS available.

pg_0712.label: Review security arrangements on doors to ensure they can be released/opened from both inside and outside without compromising security.

pg_0713.label: Fit removable hasps on weathertight doors allowing padlocking from outside, releasable from inside via a butterfly nut.

pg_0714.label: Fit mechanical keypads on other doors with quick release from inside, and ensure the access code is known to all ship's staff.

pg_0715.label: Monitor keypad performance in weather-exposed locations.

pg_0716.label: Ensure vessel manning levels are sufficient to allow full compliance with the Merchant Shipping (Hours of Work) (Regulations) 2002.

pg_0717.label: Post a rest/work Schedule under Regulation 7, using indicative hours where exact timing cannot be predicted (e.g., tug working in harbour).

pg_0718.label: If an individual believes the Regulations are being breached, direct them to raise the matter with the local MCA Marine Office.

pg_0719.label: Offer the reporting individual the option of confidentiality when raising the matter with the MCA.

pg_0720.label: Install a padlocked cover over the escape hatch external dog so it is not visibly altered from inside.

pg_0721.label: Issue padlock keys to the officer of the watch and all deck ratings.

pg_0722.label: Release the padlocked cover and use a spanner on the dog's spindle to release the dog when access is needed.

pg_0723.label: Maintain active lookout for pot marker buoys and make course corrections to avoid them during pilotage in constricted waters.

pg_0724.label: Upon sudden loss of drive/speed near hazards, immediately hoist sail to regain steerage and control.

pg_0725.label: Divert to safe passage/sail clear of the entrance once control is regained, then proceed to a safe haven for repair.

pg_0726.label: Report the hazard of unmarked/unfamiliar floating pick-up lines on pot markers in constricted harbour entrances.

pg_0727.label: Report encounters with unmarked fishing gear or flotsam/jetsam to CHIRP, the Coastguard, MAIB, RYA, or local Harbour Authority as appropriate.

pg_0728.label: Consider whether a report to local Harbour Authority, Coastguard, or MAIB would be more appropriate than CHIRP.

pg_0729.label: Use the CHIRP reporting facility specifically when wishing to protect identity, share a 'Lesson Learned', when other procedures are unavailable/inappropriate, or when other reporting has not adequately addressed the issue.

pg_0730.label: Report hazardous incidents to the local Coastguard Station, or call the MCA's 24hr info line (0870 6006505) for other matters.

pg_0731.label: Complete the report form, adding extra pages if required.

pg_0732.label: Place the completed form in a sealed envelope (no stamp required) and send to the CHIRP Freepost address.

pg_0733.label: Alternatively contact CHIRP via the confidential 24hr telephone, freefone, or fax numbers provided.

pg_0734.label: For e-mail reports, first request a security certificate from confidential@chirp.co.uk using only 'Certificate' in the subject line, submitting no other information at that stage.

pg_0735.label: Provide name, address, postcode, telephone number, and preferred contact date/method.

pg_0736.label: Complete the relevant information about the event/situation in the report.

pg_0737.label: As stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, hold course and speed per Rule 17.

pg_0738.label: Do not alter course to port for a vessel on the port side.

pg_0739.label: If concerned about the other vessel's intentions, attempt communication with that vessel, VTS, or the Master.

pg_0740.label: Do not alter course to port when taking action under Rule 14 (head-on) or Rule 17(c) (give-way vessel action).

pg_0741.label: Take a large alteration of course to starboard (a round turn) or reduce speed as the acceptable action under Rule 17(c).

pg_0742.label: Keep the Master advised of any navigational hazards or developing close-quarters situations, and call the Master whenever in doubt.

pg_0743.label: Make the sound and light signals prescribed by Rule 33(d) when taking avoiding action.

pg_0744.label: Do not rely on VHF for collision avoidance.

pg_0745.label: Consider establishing Company/Master's Standing Orders on acceptable passing distances.

pg_0746.label: Discuss this case with deck officers to ensure awareness of the dangers of altering to port and the obligation to call the Master.

pg_0747.label: If incorrect port alterations are found to be commonplace, investigate the root cause and implement remedial measures such as a fleet circular, additional assessment and training.

pg_0748.label: Continuously monitor radar plot and CPA/TCPA of contacts in restricted visibility, not relying solely on clear-visibility passing margins.

pg_0749.label: Increase sea room and passing distance margins in restricted visibility, and consider speed reduction in confined waters.

pg_0750.label: Avoid using VHF to negotiate deviations from the Collision Regulations.

pg_0751.label: If VHF communication is deemed necessary, use it only to confirm compliance with the Rules, not to agree alternative passing arrangements.

pg_0752.label: Confirm the identity of any vessel communicated with beyond doubt before acting on any agreed arrangement.

pg_0753.label: Maintain alertness and be ready to take immediate emergency action (e.g., hard-a-port) if the other vessel's actions contradict the expected passing situation.

pg_0754.label: Keep a continuous anchor watch monitoring other vessels entering the anchorage, especially in strong wind/current conditions.

pg_0755.label: Sound the whistle and immediately call the Master to the Bridge when risk of close quarters develops.

pg_0756.label: Keep main engine on short notice (10 minutes) while at anchor in strong wind/current conditions.

pg_0757.label: Use AIS to identify any vessel involved in a near-miss for reporting and follow-up.

pg_0758.label: Give manoeuvring orders verbally on the bridge rather than relaying them over open VHF when possible.

pg_0759.label: If internal radio communication is necessary, use a low-power UHF set instead of VHF.

pg_0760.label: Confirm and if necessary change VHF channel before relying on it for intership coordination.

pg_0761.label: Where radio is unreliable or risky, use direct shouted commands on the bridge/deck.

pg_0762.label: Send a reminder letter to ship's staff emphasizing the importance of near-miss reporting.

pg_0763.label: Publish an extensive article on near-miss reporting in the company safety newsletter.

pg_0764.label: Reduce the interval between bridge team training courses.

pg_0765.label: Review the familiarisation procedure used when a new ship is taken under management.

pg_0766.label: Complete the incident investigation even after the Master involved has left the company.

pg_0767.label: Incorporate lessons on selecting and proceeding to a safe anchorage, considering leeway, set, drift and windage.

pg_0768.label: Ensure Competent Harbour Authority includes operational communications in its risk assessment.

pg_0769.label: Ensure radio communications are properly prefixed (e.g., with vessel/station identification).

pg_0770.label: Consider alternative communication methods such as 'Talkback' systems.

pg_0771.label: Take early and substantial action to avoid a head-on situation rather than waiting.

pg_0772.label: Use VHF only as a last resort to clarify intentions, not as a substitute for COLREGS compliance.

pg_0773.label: When altering course to avoid collision, make the alteration large enough to be readily apparent, not a marginal 5-degree change.

pg_0774.label: Take any collision-avoidance action in accordance with the Rules, making it positive, timely, and in keeping with good seamanship.

pg_0775.label: Avoid relying on minimal course alterations (e.g. 5°) made at short range (<2.5nm) and short time (<7 minutes) before closest approach.

pg_0776.label: Consider adopting a 'leave waypoints to port' offset when planning routes.

pg_0777.label: Remain alert to overtaking risk even when using waypoint offsets or following recommended routes.

pg_0778.label: Alter course to starboard when a head-on risk of collision situation is identified.

pg_0779.label: Use AIS and radar together to identify and track approaching vessels at range (e.g. 10nm).

pg_0780.label: Continue monitoring CPA/TCPA even after initial avoidance action, especially with multiple vessels in proximity.

pg_0781.label: Ports/pilotage authorities should proactively manage pilot working-hour risks rather than relying solely on the pilot's own judgment.

pg_0782.label: Only attempt repairs or modifications you are competent to undertake.

pg_0783.label: Always check the function of controls and equipment after maintenance or repair.

pg_0784.label: Do not undertake mechanical work while under the influence of alcohol; work only under close supervision.

pg_0785.label: When anchoring, provide additional lighting (e.g., deck lighting) as suggested by Rule 30(c) of COLREGS, especially in areas with background shore lighting.

pg_0786.label: Ensure the anchored vessel presents a conspicuous radar target (e.g., radar reflector).

pg_0787.label: Notify the Harbour Authority (not only the Coastguard) when anchoring within or near a main shipping channel.

pg_0788.label: Do not anchor in the main navigation channel.

pg_0789.label: If anchoring in the channel is unavoidable (e.g. emergency), contact the Harbour Authority immediately and advise position and type of vessel.

pg_0790.label: Study the relevant, corrected and up-to-date chart of the area.

pg_0791.label: Ensure the vessel is adequately lit, accounting for background lighting and prevailing conditions.

pg_0792.label: Ensure the vessel presents an adequate radar target by hoisting or permanently fixing a suitable radar reflector.

pg_0793.label: Keep a good lookout and maintain a listening watch on the appropriate VHF channel throughout.

pg_0794.label: Share near-collision and safety-related information obtained through company SMS with CHIRP or other bodies.

pg_0795.label: Report near-collision encounters to the other ship's owner/operator and/or Flag Administration's investigation body.

pg_0796.label: Consider establishing Colreg competence through pre-employment screening rather than relying solely on certification.

pg_0797.label: Consider reducing speed as an option when resolving close-quarters/near-collision situations.

pg_0798.label: Encourage and mandate crew to report all near misses and incidents as frequently as possible through the company Quality system.

pg_0799.label: Consolidate reports at head office, analyze them, and distribute findings back to vessels across the fleet.

pg_0800.label: Review onboard follow-up actions via Internal Auditing procedures.

pg_0801.label: As the overtaking vessel, keep clear of the vessel being overtaken per Rule 13.

pg_0802.label: Take collision-avoidance action that results in passing at a safe distance and continuously monitor its effectiveness until the other vessel is finally past and clear, per Rule 8(d).

pg_0803.label: Use the sound signal prescribed in Rule 34(d), or a recognized version of it, when overtaking.

pg_0804.label: Continuously plot and monitor the overtaking vessel's course, speed, and CPA from first detection.

pg_0805.label: Contact the overtaking vessel on VHF Ch.16 and request a wider berth.

pg_0806.label: Assess the risk of altering course to port against the sea state before taking avoiding action.

pg_0807.label: Report the incident as a 'Near-miss' through the company Safety Management System after the event.

pg_0808.label: Recalculate alternative actions (e.g., altering course away from danger) for future reference.

pg_0809.label: If any doubt exists as to whether a vessel is overtaking another, assume that it is and act accordingly (Rule 13(c)).

pg_0810.label: Use Standard Marine Communication Phrases (SMCP) when communicating with an OOW whose first language is not English.

pg_0811.label: Take early, decisive action under the Rules rather than debating their application over VHF as vessels close.

pg_0812.label: When overtaking another vessel while a third vessel's intentions are unclear, proactively communicate intentions to the vessel being overtaken.

pg_0813.label: When in doubt whether the other vessel is taking sufficient action to avoid collision, immediately sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.

pg_0814.label: Supplement the whistle signal with a light signal of at least five short and rapid flashes if available.

pg_0815.label: Avoid relying solely on VHF conversation to resolve uncertainty about relative bearing or overtaking status.

pg_0816.label: Alter course to starboard to avoid the fishing vessel while monitoring the overtaking vessel's position.

pg_0817.label: Make a visual check on the overtaking vessel before executing a large course alteration.

pg_0818.label: Contact the overtaking vessel by VHF (channel 16 then 77) to clarify roles and request course alteration.

pg_0819.label: Restate the give-way obligation and the calculated CPA/time to the overtaking vessel, demanding immediate action rather than a delayed alteration.

pg_0820.label: When the overtaking vessel maintained course and speed despite verbal assurances, alter own course substantially to starboard to avoid collision.

pg_0821.label: Reduce speed for a short period when intentions of the vessel being overtaken are uncertain.

pg_0822.label: Delay and plan the overtaking manoeuvre until after the other vessel completes its leg (e.g., the westbound leg) if intentions remain unclear.

pg_0823.label: Maintain continuous visual/radar monitoring of traffic rather than focusing on reaching the next waypoint.

pg_0824.label: Do not assume a vessel's future track based solely on absent AIS destination/ETA/draught data.

pg_0825.label: Accurately determine the actual speed differential between own vessel and the vessel being overtaken before planning the overtaking manoeuvre.

pg_0826.label: Account for the extended duration of an overtaking manoeuvre when speed differential is small before committing to a course alteration near the vessel being overtaken.

pg_0827.label: Conduct a full review (Master and Fleet Safety Specialist) of recorded navigation data after a close-quarters situation.

pg_0828.label: Do not conduct or continue cargo operations when no safe means of access/egress exists for emergency evacuation.

pg_0829.label: Rig a proper gangway or equivalent safe access before crew attempt to board/disembark, rather than using unsecured ladders or stepping over workboats.

pg_0830.label: Prohibit crew from climbing the jetty face or clambering without a ladder to retrieve equipment.

pg_0831.label: Terminal should review and tighten procedures governing vessel access during low water periods for small LOA vessels.

pg_0832.label: Ensure both ship and terminal jointly provide adequate and safe ship/shore access at all times.

pg_0833.label: Provide a secondary means of escape from the ship in case the normal/primary access becomes unusable in an emergency.

pg_0834.label: Comply with HSE 'Bulk Transfer of Dangerous Liquids and Gases Between Ship and Shore' requirements for jetty access practices.

pg_0835.label: Do not request or grant use of the Dover Strait Deep Water Route unless vessel draft exceeds the charted minimum (16m).

pg_0836.label: Traffic control (e.g., Gris Nez) should verify draft against charted requirements before granting DW route permission.

pg_0837.label: Stop the engine immediately when unexplained smoke appears.

pg_0838.label: Investigate for source of smoke, noting whether engine noise changed.

pg_0839.label: Identify alternative smoke dispersal path (e.g. heater air intake) when whole-vessel smoke spreads too fast for a single localized fire.

pg_0840.label: Open the suspect heater locker cautiously with a fire extinguisher ready.

pg_0841.label: Determine root cause (shorted diesel cut-off solenoid) once immediate danger is ruled out.

pg_0842.label: Recognize that the overtaking vessel has a clear and unequivocal obligation to keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken under Rule 13.

pg_0843.label: Exercise caution and anticipate and react to situations prudently while on watch in overtaking scenarios.

pg_0844.label: Keep Rule 2 in mind when deciding what action to take.

pg_0845.label: Monitor vessels on a parallel or converging course even after initial sighting, not just at first notice.

pg_0846.label: Shout/signal to the approaching vessel to bear away as soon as risk of collision is apparent.

pg_0847.label: After collision, furl sails, start engine, and pursue to establish the other vessel's identity.

pg_0848.label: Exchange vessel/skipper details by VHF once alongside.

pg_0849.label: Evaluate smoke detection system design (sensor placement, type) and plan for worst-case activation impact on communications.

pg_0850.label: Discuss with engineers exactly what engine availability exists for manoeuvring before or during overtaking situations.

pg_0851.label: Consider remaining on manoeuvring 'full ahead' a little longer when planning or executing an overtake.

pg_0852.label: Submit depersonalised incident reports to CHIRP and review them internally.

pg_0853.label: Continue submitting reports of unmarked fishing gear incidents to CHIRP within its terms of reference.

pg_0854.label: Report hazardous incidents to the local Coastguard Station.

pg_0855.label: Use the MCA's 24hr Info Number (0870 6006505) for relevant inquiries.

pg_0856.label: Plot an approaching vessel on radar/ARPA before committing to a VHF-agreed course of action.

pg_0857.label: Verify the other vessel's actual track relative to fixed navigational marks (buoys) before deciding on own alteration of course.

pg_0858.label: Give fixed marks (buoys) a greater distance when passing to leave sufficient sea room for other traffic.

pg_0859.label: Prepare a checklist for any job or major job that lists all valves, pumps, etc. that must be isolated/verified before equipment is opened or removed.

pg_0860.label: Have the Chief Engineer check and verify the isolation checklist before work begins.

pg_0861.label: Ensure the designated onboard medical officer (2/O) is properly trained and know what to do in an emergency to apply first aid.

pg_0862.label: Arrange immediate transport of the injured crew member ashore to a doctor/hospital via the agent.

pg_0863.label: Continuously monitor the movement of other vessels regardless of other bridge activities underway.

pg_0864.label: Assess planned manoeuvres and their impact on nearby vessels, especially near charted buoys.

pg_0865.label: Where special circumstances exist, the stand-on vessel may need to depart from strict Rule application (e.g., alter to starboard) to give the other vessel more room.

pg_0866.label: Do not rely on VHF communication alone as confirmation that a developing situation is being safely managed.

pg_0867.label: Conduct a careful risk assessment before beginning the work activity, examining what in the nature of the operation could cause harm.

pg_0868.label: Identify hazards present at the place of work and the significant risks arising from the work activity, including existing precautions such as permits to work, restricted access, warning signs, or PPE.

pg_0869.label: Implement a permit-to-work system with appropriate double-checking before maintenance begins.

pg_0870.label: Before removing valves or filter covers or performing similar operations on pressurised systems, isolate that part of the system by closing the appropriate valves and open drain cocks to confirm pressure is off.

pg_0871.label: When breaking joints of pipes or fittings, do not fully remove fastenings until the joint has been broken and it is confirmed that no pressure remains within.

pg_0872.label: Before overtaking, assess the situational factors: presence of other vessels, own vessel's speed and manoeuvrability, and the nature of the sea area (e.g., where close passing is normal).

pg_0873.label: Prepare, explain, and execute a clear passing plan, including intended track to avoid the separation lane and return to the transit route.

pg_0874.label: Communicate overtaking intentions via VHF and respond to the other vessel's suggestions, even if a different course is chosen.

pg_0875.label: Document and justify any variation from accepted overtaking practice (e.g., passing to port instead of starboard).

pg_0876.label: Report radar PI setup difficulties through the vessel's Safety Management System (SMS).

pg_0877.label: Treat Parallel Indexing as a fundamental navigational skill all navigating officers must be able to use.

pg_0878.label: Escalate systemic equipment design concerns to industry bodies (Nautical Institute, IEC, MarESIG) when internal reporting reveals a pattern.

pg_0879.label: Confirm the unit of measurement explicitly when depth, draught, or clearance figures are exchanged by radio.

pg_0880.label: Remain alert to unit confusion especially when transiting between regions or countries with differing measurement conventions.

pg_0881.label: Treat ambiguous or unclarified depth/draught figures as a safety-critical issue requiring clarification before acting.

pg_0882.label: Immediately cool a scald/burn with cold water as soon as it occurs.

pg_0883.label: Cover the cooled area with a dry, non-fluffy dressing.

pg_0884.label: Follow longer-term treatment recommendations in SCMG p82-83 if definitive medical care is not immediately available.

pg_0885.label: Ensure all responsible officers (except on the smallest coastal vessels) have received medical first aid training.

pg_0886.label: Obtain hands-on familiarisation with a radar's controls and menus before relying on it operationally.

pg_0887.label: Establish VHF contact with the approaching vessel on Channel 16, then shift to a working channel

pg_0888.label: Ask the other vessel its intentions and remind it of its duty to keep clear

pg_0889.label: Monitor CPA continuously while the other vessel maintained course and speed

pg_0890.label: Alter course to starboard to cross ahead/clear of Vessel B

pg_0891.label: OOW must notify Master at least 15 minutes before a CPA of 1 nm is predicted to occur, per company QMS and Master's standing orders.

pg_0892.label: Investigate near-miss reports forwarded by external bodies (e.g. CHIRP) and respond with root cause analysis.

pg_0893.label: Raise a non-conformity and discuss the incident at the next Safety Committee Meeting.

pg_0894.label: Provide additional training to the OOW involved, if still serving with the company.

pg_0895.label: Distribute an information circular fleet-wide and discuss it at each vessel's Safety Committee Meeting.

pg_0896.label: Develop a clear appreciation of the overall traffic situation well before a crossing develops.

pg_0897.label: Select a better opportunity to cross a routeing scheme earlier, rather than attempting to cross close to another vessel using the route.

pg_0898.label: Practice 'defensive navigation' by anticipating and avoiding situations that force reliance on the COLREGs for resolution.

pg_0899.label: Deny the request to pass green/green.

pg_0900.label: Advise the other vessel to maintain its course and speed.

pg_0901.label: Take own action to keep out of the other vessel's way.

pg_0902.label: Persist in communicating/persuading the other vessel to hold track despite resistance.

pg_0903.label: Report the concern to the local Coastguard after the encounter.

pg_0904.label: Conduct vessels in restricted visibility strictly according to the Colregs, not via VHF negotiation.

pg_0905.label: Interpret 'so far as possible' in Rule 19(d) to prohibit altering course to port while it remains possible to alter to starboard or stop the ship in time.

pg_0906.label: Issue a fleet letter addressing the incident and reinforcing existing instructions on restricted visibility conduct.

pg_0907.label: Instruct Masters to place the subject on the agenda of their next Navigational Safety Meeting.

pg_0908.label: Require navigation officers to complete the onboard CBT refresher on Colregs.

pg_0909.label: Acquire ARPA plot and maintain visual bearings on the approaching vessel

pg_0910.label: Cross-check other vessel's position and course using AIS

pg_0911.label: Contact the other vessel via VHF at 1NM range to ask intentions and request more sea room

pg_0912.label: Take own avoiding action (alter course 10 degrees to port) despite being stand-on vessel

pg_0914.label: Operator forwards the report to the vessel's Master and requests his comments and that he discuss it with all Navigational Officers onboard.

pg_0915.label: Operator reviews the incident against Anti-collision regulations and Fleet Regulations (navigational section).

pg_0916.label: Operator reviews whether Fleet Regulations themselves need improvement.

pg_0917.label: Operator identifies the need for improvement in the 'human element' of navigational watchkeeping, not the regulations.

pg_0918.label: Operator distributes the incident fleet-wide via Fleet Circular as a Learning Event.

pg_0919.label: Present the hazardous incident report to the operator of the give-way vessel for assessment.

pg_0920.label: Self-report the incident to the MAIB when it occurs within UK waters.

pg_0921.label: Submit voluntary hazardous incident reports to MAIB where relevant.

pg_0922.label: Initiate radar plot on detected target as soon as observed.

pg_0923.label: Continue monitoring and assess if close quarters situation is developing.

pg_0924.label: Sound warning signal when target fails to give way.

pg_0925.label: Repeat warning signal multiple times if no response.

pg_0926.label: Contact local coastguard and attempt VHF Channel 16 and DSC calls to the target vessel.

pg_0927.label: Alter own vessel's course to avoid collision when no response is received.

pg_0928.label: Maintain a good lookout astern as well as ahead at all times.

pg_0929.label: Forward wake-wash incident reports to the responsible vessel operator for investigation and follow-up.

pg_0930.label: Operator issues a notice to all Masters reminding them of their responsibilities and professionalism when approaching smaller vessels.

pg_0931.label: All vessel types, not just tugs, should remain aware of the impact of their wake-wash on others afloat or ashore.

pg_0932.label: Maintain a steady, predictable course under autohelm while closely observing the approaching vessel.

pg_0933.label: Keep a hand on the helm/controls ready to alter course if necessary.

pg_0934.label: Monitor the approaching vessel's bridge for visual confirmation of their awareness.

pg_0935.label: Maintain continuous visual lookout for fishing gear markers, especially in areas known for pot fishing or tidal races.

pg_0936.label: When possible, proceed under sail with propeller folded/disengaged in known fishing gear areas.

pg_0937.label: Submit incident reports to CHIRP for collation and forwarding to MCA, the other vessel, and RYA.

pg_0938.label: Maintain careful lookout for lobster pot buoys and floating debris, especially on well-used coastal routes known for heavy pot density.

pg_0939.label: Include anticipated fouling hazards and a response plan for fouling in passage planning.

pg_0940.label: If fouled and disabled with no means of propulsion, call for lifeboat/rescue assistance promptly.

pg_0941.label: Report sightings of unmarked or inadequately marked fishing gear to CHIRP or relevant authority.

pg_0942.label: Raise the overtaking vessel by VHF early to state destination and intended course alteration.

pg_0944.label: Repeat/remind the overtaking vessel of the intended manoeuvre if no action is observed.

pg_0945.label: Continuously assess the situation before executing the planned course alteration.

pg_0946.label: Overtaking vessel must keep clear of the vessel being overtaken until finally past and clear, and should overtake from the starboard side per general seamanship practice.

pg_0947.label: Give way or take early, substantial action when risk of collision exists, as required by the rules of the road.

pg_0948.label: Respond promptly to VHF calls or signals from other vessels regarding collision risk.

pg_0949.label: Use radar/ECDIS plotted tracks as a planning aid, not as a rigid instruction to be followed blindly regardless of actual traffic.

pg_0950.label: Maintain proper lookout and situational awareness independent of plotted navigation lines.

pg_0951.label: Assess the situation under COLREG Rule 8 and determine the only viable avoidance action.

pg_0952.label: Put the rudder hard to port immediately to open distance from the other vessel.

pg_0953.label: Inform the Master immediately and have him present on the bridge during the manoeuvre.

pg_0954.label: Record and report the incident, including closest point of approach and circumstances, for investigation.

pg_0955.label: Immediately suspend the hot work upon discovery of the conflict.

pg_0956.label: Report the near miss to the yard safety officer and master without delay.

pg_0957.label: Convene a meeting shortly after the incident with all involved parties.

pg_0958.label: Hold a mass toolbox briefing the next day with all contractors on the vessel.

pg_0959.label: Amend the Safety Management Plan or HSE contractual terms so hydraulic actuation/flammable fluid transfer is included in the yard's permit to work system.

pg_0960.label: Review the venue and format of daily work planning meetings (location, noise, seating, attendee list, disturbance policy).

pg_0961.label: Ensure key messages from daily planning meetings are passed to yard workers and sub-contractors via daily toolbox talks.

pg_0962.label: Ensure all parties involved in vessel repair work are made fully aware of the work of others and which systems remain in operation.

pg_0963.label: Thoroughly vet the efficiency of the shipyard's permit to work system.

pg_0964.label: Incorporate permit to work system vetting into existing HSE inspections used to maintain shipyards on the approved list.

pg_0965.label: Put measures in place to ensure recommendations arising from inspections are actually implemented.

pg_0966.label: After a collision, stand by the scene ready to render assistance.

pg_0967.label: Share incident report information as widely as possible within the company and industry.

pg_0968.label: Remove the OOW from watchkeeping duties and repatriate at the next opportunity following the incident.

pg_0969.label: Board the vessel at the earliest opportunity, take statements, and secure evidence including SVDR data.

pg_0970.label: Interview the OOW at the operator's office and review the investigation report alongside VDR data.

pg_0971.label: Positively identify observed targets and lights and compare them against radar targets before acting.

pg_0972.label: Use all available means (sight, hearing, visual bearings, AIS, radar including auto-acquisition/guard rings) to detect and identify navigational hazards.

pg_0973.label: Advise the lookout whenever course alterations are made, especially small autopilot increments.

pg_0974.label: Regularly adjust radar range scale and tuning (gain, sea clutter, rain clutter) throughout the watch.

pg_0975.label: Establish strong OOW-lookout communication, including discussion of traffic/navigational situation and positive confirmation of reports.

pg_0976.label: Encourage the lookout to use navigational aids such as radar.

pg_0977.label: Issue the OOW a written formal warning.

pg_0978.label: Target the OOW for additional Bridge Team Management (CRM) training before next appointment.

pg_0979.label: Require the OOW to undertake a management course to improve leadership and integrated team working.

pg_0980.label: Promulgate incident details fleet-wide, highlighting mistakes and best practices.

pg_0981.label: Raise identified best-practice failures with institutions conducting company CRM courses.

pg_0982.label: Forward incident details to CHIRP and the Nautical Institute's MARS scheme.

pg_0983.label: Reduce to manoeuvring revolutions and turn the vessel around after the collision

pg_0984.label: Inform the Master immediately after the collision is detected

pg_0985.label: Prepare the rescue boat and lifesaving appliances

pg_0986.label: Inform the nearest coast radio station and coastguard

pg_0987.label: Attempt radio contact with the fishing vessel

pg_0988.label: Call the Operator's 24hr duty phone and advise of the situation

pg_0990.label: Stand by until a coastguard vessel rendezvoused with the fishing vessel

pg_0991.label: Continue voyage only upon instruction from local authorities

pg_0992.label: React immediately to the horn blast by going to the cockpit and visually assessing the situation around the genoa.

pg_0994.label: Disengage the self-steering by turning the Hydrovane through 90 degrees rather than unclamping the tiller first.

pg_0995.label: Allow the Hydrovane's auxiliary rudder to initiate a turn to starboard.

pg_0996.label: Return to the tiller, free it, and use the main rudder to complete the turn.

pg_0997.label: After the close pass, resolve to look around the genoa more frequently (at least three times) as an ongoing watchkeeping practice.

pg_0998.label: Limit sleep breaks to about 20 minutes, often waking earlier.

pg_0999.label: Fit two additional forward-facing windows in the coach roof.

pg_1000.label: Install an active radar target enhancer on a separate stern-mounted spar, 3m above water.

pg_1001.label: Cover the top section of the mast with fluorescent orange vinyl.

pg_1002.label: Keep genoa and main part-reefed even after wind dropped.

pg_1003.label: Exhibit the masthead tricolour light while under sail at night.

pg_1004.label: Plan single-handed transits of busy traffic areas with particular caution, considering transit length and timing.

pg_1005.label: Select a course that avoids known areas of dense traffic or crosses them as quickly as possible, ideally near-perpendicular to the traffic flow.

pg_1006.label: Shine a light on the sail at night.

pg_1007.label: Maintain continuous lookout and do not rely solely on radar enhancers.

pg_1008.label: Do not rely on radar enhancers (reflectors/transponders) as a substitute for proper lookout.

pg_1009.label: Maintain a continuous, vigilant visual and radar lookout, especially at night or in conditions with reduced light visibility.

pg_1010.label: Be prepared to take independent action (including sound signals) to avoid collision rather than assuming the larger vessel will detect and avoid you.

pg_1011.label: Form an early appreciation of and reaction to the overall traffic situation.

pg_1012.label: Comply with the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) and ordinary seamanship practice at all times, including while racing.

pg_1013.label: As stand-on vessel, take action by maneuver alone as soon as it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action.

pg_1014.label: If so close that collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel's action alone, take whatever action best aids collision avoidance.
