pg_1015.label: Take avoiding action when a racing vessel's conduct creates a risk of collision.

pg_1016.label: Report flagrant or dangerous rule violations by professional skippers to CHIRP or relevant authority.

pg_1017.label: Submit a near-miss report to CHIRP when identity protection is a concern.

pg_1018.label: Companies should share near-miss reports received through their Safety Management Systems with CHIRP.

pg_1019.label: Assess relative speed and point of sail to decide whether to hold course as stand-on vessel.

pg_1020.label: Continue to hold course and speed while monitoring the approaching give-way vessels.

pg_1021.label: Take independent avoiding action once it became clear the give-way vessel would not act and collision was imminent.

pg_1022.label: Turn sharply to port rather than starboard given the specific circumstances (short-handed, disabled crew, no time to transfer helm).

pg_1023.label: Make vessel intentions clear to less-frequent transiting vessels even if passing distances are routine for regular traffic.

pg_1024.label: Prioritize assessing and reacting to the close-quarters situation over attempting VHF contact.

pg_1025.label: Make a prompt alteration of course or reduction of speed when approaching close quarters.

pg_1026.label: Ensure the person holding Master/OIM authority on a DP unit has competence in navigation, anti-collision rules, and the effects of wind, wave and current.

pg_1027.label: Ensure the Master retains unimpaired authority to exercise personal judgement and discretion in emergencies, including rights under SOLAS Chap. XI-2 Reg 8.

pg_1028.label: Maintain clear, unambiguous lines of responsibility for who holds the con/overall authority on the bridge.

pg_1029.label: Resolve conflicts between marine and non-marine managers in favour of the Master's safety authority, especially regarding weather-related suspension of operations.

pg_1030.label: Refer to the Offshore Installations and Pipeline Works (Management and Administration) Regulations 1995 (MAR), regulation 6, to clarify UK legal responsibility.

pg_1031.label: Monitor both crossing vessels' CPA/TCPA closely as the situation develops.

pg_1032.label: Attempt to contact vessel A via VHF Channel 16, repeating calls and identifying own vessel.

pg_1033.label: Assess the effect of reducing own speed given vessel's loaded condition and proximity of other vessels.

pg_1034.label: Engage hand steering as the close-quarters situation developed.

pg_1035.label: Alter course to starboard by 25 degrees once vessel A was observed ahead.

pg_1036.label: Duty holder ensures the most appropriate competent person is in charge of the installation at any given time.

pg_1037.label: Duty holder demonstrates in the installation's Safety Case that its safety management system ensures compliance with the law, including MAR requirements.

pg_1038.label: Once HSE accepts the Safety Case, follow its arrangements exactly.

pg_1039.label: Where overall charge is transferable, duty holders should address potential conflicts in the Safety Case and/or operational procedures.

pg_1040.label: Consult operational staff to identify and resolve conflicts over who holds charge.

pg_1041.label: Service and pressure test fire extinguishers in accordance with Flag State and/or manufacturer's requirements

pg_1042.label: Pay particular attention to extinguishers stored in exposed or damp locations

pg_1043.label: Conduct a risk assessment considering potential risks posed by pressure vessels before undertaking work

pg_1044.label: Be prepared to stop the job if an unexpected risk is encountered

pg_1045.label: Treat any old or unidentified fire extinguisher found during clearance/dismantling work as a potential hazard before handling.

pg_1046.label: Inspect extinguishers for corrosion or damage before attempting to move them, and avoid unnecessary manipulation of suspect units.

pg_1047.label: Raise awareness among crew and industry personnel of the risk posed by old extinguishers encountered during dismantling or clearance operations.

pg_1048.label: Consult the Ship Captain's Medical Guide if residual symptoms remain after an electric shock.

pg_1049.label: Obtain shore medical advice and refer to a doctor at the next port if necessary.

pg_1050.label: Report to Flag State, Classification Society, Company, and notify Port State if the emergency generator cannot be operated due to a defect such as a holed sea-water pipe.

pg_1051.label: Conduct a risk assessment before commencing work and issue necessary permits and notices, including power isolation.

pg_1052.label: Properly maintain and check wiring runs and temporary cables/extension leads.

pg_1053.label: Officer in Charge communicates mooring station status changes (singling up) to bridge via VHF as instructed.

pg_1054.label: Officer in Charge reports the riding turn and inability to provide slack on the spring to the Master.

pg_1055.label: Master should confirm status of all lines before ordering thruster/engine movement.

pg_1056.label: Investigate whether a similar incident could occur on your own vessel and identify preventive steps.

pg_1057.label: Ensure mooring lines are run through split drum winches/reels as designed.

pg_1058.label: Visually confirm all ropes are clear before using the bow thruster.

pg_1059.label: Maintain active bridge-to-forecastle communication, with backup via VHF radios held by both Master and Chief Officer.

pg_1060.label: If normal reporting/communication channels fail, contact the DPA directly.

pg_1061.label: Identify that AIS Static & Voyage Data (ship name, call sign) is missing while dynamic data is correct.

pg_1062.label: Attempt to report the poor AIS data to the nearest MRCC as required by the relevant M Notice.

pg_1063.label: Use fax or other available means to contact the local MRCC.

pg_1064.label: Check AIS display for own ship's transmitted data (name, call sign, dynamic data).

pg_1065.label: Contact a nearby vessel (e.g., by VHF) to confirm what data they are actually receiving from your AIS.

pg_1066.label: Reset the AIS unit if a discrepancy is found between transmitted and displayed data.

pg_1067.label: Institute a routine of resetting the AIS unit at the beginning of every watch.

pg_1068.label: Report AIS data irregularities to CHIRP and to the equipment manufacturer.

pg_1069.label: Continuously monitor an approaching light's bearing and range rather than assuming safe passage from colour alone.

pg_1070.label: Use radar to confirm the target's course, speed, and closing rate when in doubt.

pg_1071.label: Take immediate avoiding action (take the helm, disengage autopilot, turn hard to starboard) when a close-quarters situation is recognised.

pg_1072.label: When altering course near another vessel, give a visual signal (e.g. 2 flashes on Aldis lamp) or sound signal (siren blasts) to indicate awareness of the other vessel.

pg_1073.label: A give-way vessel (here the tanker) should alter course to starboard when appropriate rather than toward the other vessel.

pg_1074.label: Evaluate close-quarters situations from the other vessel's perspective, asking 'How close would I like someone to be if I were on the other ship/boat?'

pg_1075.label: Do not rely solely on a Radar Target Enhancer (RTE) to assume you have been seen by another vessel.

pg_1076.label: Do not rely on a single data point (e.g., light colour) to assess collision risk; monitor bearing trend instead.

pg_1077.label: Have the vessel independently checked (e.g., via RNLI free sea check in the UK).

pg_1078.label: Report recurring equipment hazards (e.g., overheating lighting) through the Designated Person/ISM reporting system.

pg_1079.label: Ensure decorative/hidden lighting installations are fit for the intended purpose and installed per manufacturer's instructions.

pg_1080.label: Call the other vessel on VHF Channel 16, identifying it by position and relative bearing, to establish its intentions.

pg_1081.label: Monitor the bearing of the other vessel continuously.

pg_1082.label: If the other vessel does not respond or give way, alter own course substantially (e.g., onto a different tack) to pass clear.

pg_1083.label: After the close-quarters situation is resolved, re-establish contact with the other vessel to express concern over the encounter.

pg_1084.label: Intervene when an unsafe situation is observed developing on board.

pg_1085.label: When correcting a more junior colleague, explain the risks involved clearly.

pg_1086.label: Consider and adapt approach when intervening with a more senior colleague.

pg_1087.label: When receiving an intervention from a colleague, thank them and acknowledge they were correct, especially if they are more junior.

pg_1088.label: Be prepared to discuss the situation, the risks involved, and corrective actions after an intervention.

pg_1089.label: Call the other vessel on VHF to clarify intentions and request action.

pg_1090.label: When the other vessel refused to alter course and range closed to 0.9 NM, take immediate manual control: ring slow ahead and place a man on the wheel.

pg_1091.label: Execute a bold turn to port, threading between the fishing vessels to port.

pg_1092.label: After clearing, contact the other vessel's Chief Officer again to formally note the dangerous and careless navigation.

pg_1093.label: As give-way vessel, alter course to starboard or slow down promptly once a close-quarters risk is identified, even if the other vessel's manoeuvre appears unexpected or non-compliant.

pg_1094.label: Issue clear standing orders specifying when the Officer of the Watch must call the Captain to the bridge.

pg_1095.label: Ensure officers understand the Captain's requirements for being alerted to potential close-quarters situations, particularly where sea-room is restricted (e.g., by fishing vessels).

pg_1096.label: Cultivate an onboard environment where guidance from senior officers is received as constructive rather than as criticism or 'bludgeoning.'

pg_1097.label: Inform the other vessel that the incident will be reported.

pg_1098.label: Request and obtain the other vessel's position.

pg_1099.label: Terminate the VHF exchange once necessary information is obtained.

pg_1100.label: Record the incident in the vessel's log.

pg_1101.label: Report serious near misses to the Coastguard at the time they occur.

pg_1102.label: Double-check all data (dates, times, distances) when reporting to MAIB and/or CHIRP.

pg_1103.label: Consider how your vessel's actions and perceived distances appear to smaller craft.

pg_1104.label: Maintain a good visual and radar lookout on all approaching, departing, and crossing traffic in the area.

pg_1105.label: Use radar range and bearing markers to assess whether the other vessel would pass clear, rather than formally plotting CPA.

pg_1106.label: When the give-way vessel's late course alteration created an immediate risk of collision, alter course to port to place her on the starboard beam, per Rule 17a(ii).

pg_1107.label: Choose the direction of turn considering sea-handling conditions (avoid turning to starboard which would mean lying beam-on to steep quartering seas and closing under the other vessel's bow).

pg_1108.label: After the close encounter, hail the other vessel on VHF Channel 16 to raise the COLREGs breach.

pg_1109.label: When the ship is moving or anchoring, the Master holds full command authority.

pg_1110.label: When anchored or on DP, allow the Mine Manager to direct mining operations.

pg_1111.label: Master retains an effective veto over the Mine Manager whenever ship or personnel safety is involved.

pg_1112.label: Reduce speed through the channel, especially at low water, to minimize wake wash.

pg_1113.label: Harbour master to issue standard practice guidance requiring slow, sensible speed for large vessels in the channel.

pg_1114.label: Small craft occupants should wear life jackets when in the channel.

pg_1115.label: Harbour Authority to continue emphasising to Masters and Pilots the need to proceed at slow speed.

pg_1116.label: Harbour Authority to monitor vessel speeds and make visual checks on wash effect.

pg_1117.label: Owners/operators of small craft to remain observant to the approach of large vessels and alert to possible wash.

pg_1118.label: Harbour Authority to consider re-issuing/updating the Notice to Mariners highlighting wash dangers at low water.

pg_1119.label: People in small craft to consider wearing lifejackets at all times.

pg_1120.label: Harbour users to report any wash-related problems to the Harbour Authority at the time or soon after.

pg_1121.label: If a serious problem persists, conduct a more fundamental review of issues and mitigating measures.

pg_1122.label: Ensure certified calibration kits for pressure and temperature gauges are carried onboard.

pg_1123.label: Calibrate the boiler pressure gauge and obtain a calibration certificate during dry-dock/boiler survey.

pg_1124.label: Enable monitoring of critical boiler parameters (pressure and water level) from the Engine Control Room.

pg_1125.label: Contact the owner of the other vessel to invite their comment on the incident.

pg_1126.label: As stand-on vessel in a close-quarters situation, reflect on whether additional action (e.g. slowing down) could have increased the passing distance.

pg_1127.label: Start and maintain a radar plot on both 3cm and 9cm radars as soon as a target is detected (8 miles out, 4 points on port bow).

pg_1128.label: Cross-check radar plot with AIS data to identify the vessel concerned.

pg_1129.label: Continuously monitor CPA/TCPA as the situation develops.

pg_1130.label: When the give-way vessel shows no sign of taking action under Rule 15, take independent avoiding action as the stand-on vessel.

pg_1131.label: Reduce speed (halved speed at 8 cables range) to increase separation and allow the give-way vessel to pass ahead.

pg_1132.label: Remind the other vessel of the COLREGS requirement for early and substantial action to avoid a close-quarters situation.

pg_1133.label: Place engines on instant notice despite being under sail.

pg_1134.label: Repeat the request for course alteration when the other vessel failed to act.

pg_1135.label: As the give-way vessel, take early and substantial action to keep well clear of the other vessel as required by Rule 16.

pg_1136.label: Avoid invoking claims of 'commercial superiority' over another vessel when deciding right of way.

pg_1137.label: Keep VHF communications calm and professional at all times.

pg_1138.label: Record vessel identification details (name, MMSI, call sign, destination) from AIS when a TSS contravention is suspected.

pg_1139.label: Capture ECDIS video/screenshot playback with timestamps (GMT) and vector lengths showing vessel track over time.

pg_1140.label: Note the observed navigation lights (masthead, sidelights, stern light, and any additional all-round lights).

pg_1141.label: Review submitted video evidence of the vessel's track and light display.

pg_1142.label: Contact the Flag State of the other vessel.

pg_1143.label: Attempt to contact the crossing vessel on VHF channels 11, 13 and 16

pg_1144.label: Request assistance from the VTS authority (Gris Nez Traffic) to contact the non-responding vessel

pg_1146.label: Lodge a formal complaint with Gris Nez Traffic after the encounter

pg_1147.label: Raise safety equipment deficiencies immediately when observed, regardless of crew seniority.

pg_1148.label: Attach lifebuoy lights to lifebuoys before departure/during passage preparation.

pg_1149.label: Verify lifebuoy lights and other safety equipment are fitted and positioned as intended, not improperly stowed.

pg_1150.label: Foster a safety culture where all crew/persons onboard are aware of hazards and actively think through precautions.

pg_1151.label: Intervene when observing a hazard or unsafe situation rather than staying silent.

pg_1152.label: Re-read the ColRegs periodically to refresh knowledge.

pg_1153.label: Use computer-based training aids to test ColRegs knowledge if available.

pg_1154.label: Consider how the other vessel's watchkeeper will perceive your maneuvering action, especially when passing small craft.

pg_1155.label: Reflect on past experiences as the stand-on vessel to assess whether your own actions would have fully complied with the regulations had a collision occurred.

pg_1156.label: Verify the Master had been called to the bridge during the close encounter.

pg_1157.label: Confirm the bridge team worked cohesively together.

pg_1158.label: Apply Rule 17 (Action by stand-on vessel) correctly.

pg_1159.label: Sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle, supplemented by a light signal, per Rule 34.

pg_1160.label: Avoid using VHF/radio to exchange invective with the other vessel.

pg_1162.label: Shipowners/managers should review recruitment and verification processes to confirm deck officers have proper ColRegs knowledge and apply it correctly.

pg_1163.label: Verify the approaching vessel's course and closing situation using radar.

pg_1164.label: Sound five short blasts on the horn.

pg_1165.label: Attempt to contact the approaching vessel by VHF, initially by describing position (not by name, as name unknown).

pg_1166.label: Alter course to starboard as the other vessel closed, to make the approaching ship the overtaking vessel.

pg_1167.label: Re-attempt VHF contact using the vessel's name once legible at close range.

pg_1168.label: Obtain the original reporter's agreement before sharing a disidentified copy of the report with the other vessel's manager.

pg_1169.label: Send the disidentified report to the coaster's manager for review.

pg_1170.label: Manager discusses the report with the Master and Chief Officer.

pg_1171.label: Treat lack of crew acknowledgment as inconclusive but value the manager's personal follow-up as a safety-culture action.

pg_1172.label: Attempt VHF contact with the approaching vessel on Channel 16 as early as possible.

pg_1173.label: Monitor the target continuously by radar/plotter to assess CPA and track behavior.

pg_1174.label: Report the incident, including the vessel's name and registered port, to CHIRP for follow-up with the coaster's owners/operators.

pg_1175.label: Monitor the approaching vessel's aspect and bearing to assess risk of collision while holding course as the stand-on vessel.

pg_1176.label: Attempt to establish VHF communication with the other vessel when it becomes apparent they have not seen or heard the yacht or are ignoring it.

pg_1177.label: Take independent avoiding action (bear away, increase speed, pass well ahead) once it is clear the give-way vessel will not act.

pg_1178.label: Recalculate avoidance manoeuvre accounting for actual tidal set and rate, not just estimated/atlas data.

pg_1179.label: Use the chart plotter's tide/current display function (rate and direction) in addition to COG & SOG when planning and executing avoidance manoeuvres.

pg_1180.label: Conduct a thorough check of engine and transmission outputs after the loud bang and rpm drop.

pg_1181.label: Conclude the propeller is fouled once checks rule out other causes and the engine cannot exceed 1700rpm.

pg_1182.label: Match the port engine rpm to the reduced starboard engine rpm (1700rpm) to maintain balanced propulsion.

pg_1183.label: Proceed to the intended destination (B.O.C.) at reduced matched speed.

pg_1184.label: Lift the boat out of the water the next day to inspect and remove the fouling.

pg_1185.label: OOW should call the Captain when a situation becomes highly unpredictable or beyond standing orders.

pg_1186.label: Captain should explicitly advise the OOW that he is taking over the con.

pg_1187.label: Take avoiding action in accordance with Rule 17 when acting as the stand-on vessel.

pg_1188.label: Make sound signals in accordance with Rule 34 during maneuvering.

pg_1189.label: Assess the developing crossing situation and determine stand-on/give-way status under COLREGs.

pg_1190.label: Make VHF call to identify own vessel and relative position to vessel 'B'.

pg_1191.label: Request vessel 'B' take early and substantial action per COLREG Rule 15 as give-way vessel.

pg_1192.label: Re-contact vessel 'B' via VHF when no action was observed and distance had closed to 3nm.

pg_1193.label: Monitor vessel 'B's' actual trajectory and compliance against verbal assurances.

pg_1194.label: Call the skipper to assist in classifying an approaching vessel's lights when uncertain.

pg_1195.label: Take a series of bearings on the approaching vessel.

pg_1196.label: As give-way vessel, prepare and execute avoiding action to pass clear ahead in good time.

pg_1197.label: Continue monitoring the target's bearing and aspect closely even after forming an initial assessment.

pg_1198.label: Sound the doubt/danger signal (5 short flashes) when the other vessel's action creates uncertainty or risk of collision.

pg_1199.label: Order rudder to starboard in the critical moment.

pg_1200.label: Do not alter to port despite the close-quarters situation.

pg_1201.label: Avoid further starboard alteration beyond what was ordered.

pg_1202.label: Do not rely on speed reduction as a collision-avoidance measure in this scenario.

pg_1203.label: Investigate and repair any inoperative navigation light immediately, using bridge panel fault warnings.

pg_1204.label: Do not display special/local-requirement lights (e.g. dangerous cargo indicator) once at sea if not applicable.

pg_1205.label: Switch off or shield deck lights that impede proper lookout or could confuse other vessels.

pg_1206.label: As the give-way vessel, make a bold, early alteration to starboard once risk of collision is identified.

pg_1207.label: Ensure all persons on board are absolutely clear as to who is in charge of the vessel at all times.

pg_1208.label: If responsibility for the vessel must be transferred during a voyage, do so formally.

pg_1209.label: Advise all crew of any transfer of responsibility.

pg_1210.label: Record any transfer of command in the logbook.

pg_1211.label: Conduct thorough passage planning from berth to berth, including fuel calculations.

pg_1212.label: Assess whether remaining fuel is sufficient to safely complete the passage and enter the intended port.

pg_1213.label: Identify whether a contingency plan exists for the low-fuel scenario before continuing on the current plan.

pg_1214.label: If risk is judged unacceptable, intervene and insist on an alternative plan.

pg_1215.label: Arrange sludge/slop removal only via the agent using an approved contractor.

pg_1216.label: Obtain prior approval of the relevant authority before contracting a sludge removal service.

pg_1217.label: Inspect hose and coupling condition before commencing discharge, and halt operations if damage or improvised repairs (e.g., taped joints) are found.

pg_1218.label: Heed warning signs noted prior to an operation rather than proceeding regardless.

pg_1219.label: CHIRP Director (Maritime) writes to the vessel manager about the alleged COLREGS violation.

pg_1220.label: Withhold the identity of the original reporter in correspondence with the manager.

pg_1221.label: Encourage use of computer-based training tools for initial training, refresher training, and testing of watch-keepers on COLREGS.

pg_1222.label: Give-way vessel should allow a reasonable margin of safety in passing distance rather than cutting it fine.

pg_1223.label: Stand-on vessel watch-keeper must judge when to invoke Rule 17b if the give-way vessel fails to act appropriately.

pg_1224.label: Use CO2 bottle locking pins only during maintenance and/or refit, per manufacturer and Planned Maintenance procedures.

pg_1225.label: Immediately inform the bridge if a CO2 bottle is accidentally released.

pg_1226.label: Evacuate personnel from machinery spaces as a precaution following accidental CO2 release.

pg_1227.label: Safely discharge and ventilate released CO2 to atmosphere via the CO2 room connection.

pg_1228.label: Revert to the original, correct procedure as instructed by the ship's superintendent.

pg_1229.label: Fit the safety cap on CO2 cylinders before transportation for recharging.

pg_1230.label: Consult the ship's superintendent for clarification before changing onboard procedures for complex systems.

pg_1231.label: Alter course to starboard to present a broader red light and signal intent for crossing vessels to pass astern.

pg_1232.label: Reduce speed when it became apparent the crossing vessels were not giving way and were increasing speed.

pg_1233.label: Stop engine and reduce speed further to 6 knots.

pg_1234.label: As stand-on vessel, continuously assess whether the give-way vessel is taking appropriate action under the Rules.

pg_1235.label: Take early and substantial action to keep clear when required as give-way vessel.

pg_1236.label: Stand-on vessel should keep her course and speed per Rule 17(a)(i) rather than altering course unilaterally.

pg_1237.label: Report perceived close-quarters incidents to CHIRP for independent review.

pg_1238.label: Ship managers should follow up disidentified CHIRP reports with full statements from Officers of the Watch.

pg_1239.label: Maintain course and speed as the overtaken (stand-on) vessel while being passed

pg_1240.label: Monitor the overtaking vessel's position and intentions as she closes and crosses ahead

pg_1241.label: Review the CHIRP report when received to understand the issues raised.

pg_1243.label: Follow up directly with the individual officer involved.

pg_1244.label: Strengthen procedures across the whole fleet.

pg_1245.label: Submit a report of the close-quarters overtaking incident to CHIRP.

pg_1246.label: CHIRP forwards the report to the manager of the other (overtaking) vessel.

pg_1247.label: Emphasise the company's No Blame Policy for reporting incidents and near misses during pre-joining induction of officers.

pg_1248.label: Circulate a Safety Alert Bulletin fleet-wide and to offices highlighting the lapses, especially misuse of VHF for collision avoidance.

pg_1249.label: Incorporate a training module on the negative aspects of VHF as a collision-avoidance device during onboard training.

pg_1250.label: Brief Masters to appraise new personnel's professional abilities and reinforce belief in the internal reporting system.

pg_1251.label: Assess masters proposed for appointment to small ships on their small ship handling experience.

pg_1252.label: Place a notice on the main engine tachometer on the bridge warning that the M/E is not in standby until it reaches 600 rpm constant speed.

pg_1253.label: Advise the duty engineer that failure to follow documented and familiar safety procedures is unacceptable.

pg_1254.label: Revise procedure so that the bow-thruster is always powered by 3 generators rather than the shaft generator, on the vessel and her sister vessel.

pg_1255.label: Review and update Safety Management System guidance relating to the use of tugs.

pg_1256.label: Fully discuss the passage plan to and from the berth with the pilot using a 'one team' approach, including expected towing speed.

pg_1257.label: Bridge Team to closely monitor execution of the passage against the agreed plan; Master to voice concern to the pilot and intervene if deviations occur.

pg_1258.label: Communicate key points of the plan to all involved parties, including engine room and tugs.

pg_1259.label: Power thrusters from independent generators rather than the shaft generator during manoeuvring; raise the issue on board, with the DPA, or with CHIRP if this is not current practice.

pg_1260.label: Conduct thorough investigation after any such incident to identify root causes and implement preventative action on the specific ship, sister vessels, and fleet-wide.

pg_1261.label: Call the non-transmitting vessel on VHF and advise them of the issue.

pg_1262.label: If there is no response or the vessel cannot be identified, advise the Coastguard immediately by VHF.

pg_1263.label: Submit a report of the incident to CHIRP, including vessel identity if known.

pg_1264.label: Assess whether the other vessel has seen you or intends to give way.

pg_1265.label: Alter course, increase speed, and aim to pass well ahead of the oncoming vessel.

pg_1266.label: Note and, if possible, identify the vessel exhibiting the incorrect or misleading light (name, flag, AIS data).

pg_1267.label: When you notice a hazard, say or do something to correct it rather than staying silent.

pg_1268.label: Report hazardous incidents and lessons learned to a near-miss reporting programme such as CHIRP.

pg_1269.label: Encourage crew and shore managers to actively report near-misses and hazardous incidents each month.

pg_1270.label: Use CHIRP as a confidential conduit when individuals fear personal disadvantage from reporting directly to their company.

pg_1271.label: Avoid treating all infractions or non-conformities as criminal acts except in cases of extreme negligence.

pg_1272.label: Self-assess annually how many hazardous incidents/situations were observed and how the individual intervened to correct them.

pg_1273.label: Challenge the approaching vessel on VHF Channel 16 when a close-quarters situation develops.

pg_1274.label: Monitor and act on Navtex notices regarding rig-shift operations before transiting the area.

pg_1275.label: Report to a port doctor when suffering an injury or illness while serving.

pg_1276.label: Advise the company/relevant parties of the medical unfitness and request relief.

pg_1277.label: Continue making repeated requests for relief if initial requests are not actioned.

pg_1278.label: Declare intention to sail no further if the situation becomes untenable.

pg_1279.label: When planning to pass between two vessels in open water, assess CPA to both and continuously reassess as their motion/heading becomes apparent.

pg_1280.label: If a vessel calls to express concern about CPA, treat it as a signal that the passing distance is being perceived as unsafe, not just an informational call.

pg_1281.label: Make a clearly adequate course alteration (not a marginal one) when a close-quarters concern is raised, and consider confirming with the concerned vessel that the new CPA is satisfactory.

pg_1282.label: Include Nav-tex information in the passage plan and annotate it on the chart.

pg_1283.label: Treat your own indisposition the same way you would treat a key officer's (e.g. Chief Officer) indisposition.

pg_1284.label: Relieve the indisposed person of normal duties, reallocate essential tasks to others, and defer non-essential items.

pg_1285.label: Assess the risk of fatigue in the indisposed/remaining crew.

pg_1286.label: If fatigue risk is present, arrange rest before continuing critical operations, e.g. delay sailing by some hours or postpone transit through a difficult channel.

pg_1287.label: Inform the ship manager/DPA of the situation and the actions being taken, with reasons.

pg_1288.label: Do not look directly towards the light source.

pg_1290.label: If vision is temporarily affected, call others to the bridge to provide support.

pg_1291.label: Advise the authorities as soon as possible.

pg_1292.label: Immediately remove the re-frozen food products from stock.

pg_1294.label: Remind all personnel in the fleet of the danger of re-freezing thawed food.

pg_1295.label: Bridge team looks away from the laser source to protect eyesight.

pg_1296.label: Contact the other vessel (ferry) to report the laser and request it be dealt with.

pg_1297.label: Continue vessel on track into the approach channel despite the laser interference.

pg_1298.label: When laser is pointed again, bridge team again looks away and continues operations.

pg_1299.label: Assess the probability that the patrol craft will need to assist competitors in an area hampered by buoys and floating lines.

pg_1300.label: Evaluate the consequences if the patrol boat itself is unable to assist or becomes disabled by a fouled propeller, factoring in weather and tidal conditions.

pg_1301.label: Consider alternatives such as relocating the starting area (e.g., using a committee boat) or declaring the affected area prohibited for the race.

pg_1302.label: Pursue constructive dialogue with local fishermen in the medium term to find mutually agreeable solutions.

pg_1303.label: Remove the failed ladder from service and mark it as broken.

pg_1304.label: Purchase a new, more suitable ladder at first opportunity.

pg_1305.label: Inspect all portable ladders onboard for suitability and structural integrity, condemning and disposing of any found in poor condition.

pg_1306.label: Have the Chief Officer brief crew and officers on the importance of thorough pre-use equipment checks.

pg_1307.label: Include all portable ladders in the Register of Lifting Appliances (ROLA) subject to regular recorded inspections.

pg_1308.label: Add ladder inspection to the Shipboard Safety Officer's inspection regime.

pg_1309.label: Avoid procurement or retention of ladders with plastic hinges.

pg_1310.label: Carry a digital camera aboard to photograph hazardous incidents as they occur.

pg_1311.label: Submit photographs along with written incident/near-miss reports to CHIRP.

pg_1312.label: Consider adding a prompt for photo submission on the CHIRP Report Form.

pg_1313.label: Investigate equipment-related incidents thoroughly to identify root causes beyond simple technical failure.

pg_1314.label: Take remedial action following investigation findings.

pg_1315.label: Share lessons learned through the company's reporting scheme and with CHIRP.

pg_1316.label: Include photographs, diagrams, and/or electronic plots when submitting Maritime Report Forms.

pg_1317.label: Ensure equipment purchased for shipboard use is fit for the marine environment.

pg_1318.label: Maintain a Ladder Register and check ladders quarterly alongside PPE inspections.

pg_1319.label: When towing a vessel stern-first with a single tug, use the tug to provide sternway so as to negate transverse thrust.

pg_1320.label: Use helm and ahead engine movements to control the stern of the vessel.

pg_1321.label: Use bow thrusters to control the bow.

pg_1322.label: If the ship is a 'dead ship' (no engine power available), arrange for two tugs rather than one.

pg_1323.label: Mentally or verbally ask 'What if...' before undertaking an operation and think through contingencies in advance.

pg_1324.label: Talk through the situation and assessment with someone else where possible.

pg_1325.label: For small craft, assess fouled propeller risk, lee shore proximity, sea-room, anchor/chain/warp holding capacity, and communication means before going to sea.

pg_1326.label: STOP before entering an enclosed space and consider oxygen depletion, presence of gas, breathing apparatus failure, and availability of back-up.

pg_1327.label: Follow the vessel's Safety Management System procedure for enclosed space entry.

pg_1328.label: VTS Operator calls the vessel on VHF channel 16 to warn it is standing into danger.

pg_1329.label: Repeat the call until a response is received.

pg_1330.label: Vessel alters course hard to port upon receiving the warning.

pg_1331.label: Harbour Authority forwards incident details to the local Coastguard office.

pg_1332.label: Treat close-quarters track deviations shown on VTS as navigational near-misses with significant risk, even if the Master believed actions were safe and intentional.

pg_1333.label: Conduct navigation audits using a senior Master or navigator riding on vessels to monitor practices and advise improvements.

pg_1334.label: If a dedicated navigation auditor is not feasible, have a superintendent review the vessel's previous passage plan with the Master during a port visit.

pg_1335.label: Discuss with the Master and navigation officers how they apply parallel-indexing techniques.

pg_1336.label: Check that navigation equipment is functioning and charts are corrected up to date.

pg_1337.label: Report near-miss incidents promptly through official channels (e.g., CHIRP).

pg_1338.label: Company management should review reported near-misses and disseminate them as training material across the fleet.

pg_1339.label: Rig the mainsail boom preventer whenever sailing downwind.

pg_1340.label: Use a distinctly bright-coloured (orange) line for the preventer so it is clearly identifiable from other lines aboard.

pg_1341.label: Verify the preventer is listed in the yacht's inventory and check it is present and correct before each charter.

pg_1342.label: Brief clients on the dangers of gybing, including the risk of the boom and mainsheet sweeping the cockpit, before each charter.

pg_1343.label: Ensure skippers and mates meet MCA code of practice experience requirements prior to charter.

pg_1344.label: Place a vessel calling for pilot services repeatedly under closer radar/visual surveillance once noted as potential crossing traffic.

pg_1345.label: Monitor the give-way vessel's progress while maintaining own course and speed.

pg_1346.label: Contact the other vessel by VHF (ch16 then ch6) when CPA/TCPA became dangerously close to clarify her intentions.

pg_1347.label: Alert the captain to the bridge once the other vessel continued to turn the wrong way (port) and remained on a collision course.

pg_1348.label: Execute own last-resort emergency maneuver (hard turn to starboard, full 360-degree turn, speed reduced to 4 knots) when range closed to about 1 mile and collision course persisted.

pg_1349.label: Communicate the reason for the maneuver to the other vessel over VHF ch16.

pg_1350.label: When acting as give-way vessel approaching a crossing situation, take early and substantial action to keep well clear rather than relying on a marginal passing distance.

pg_1351.label: Communicate intentions (e.g., via VHF) in advance to the other vessel when planning to pass at a close margin, especially in recommended/high-traffic routes.

pg_1352.label: Keep the Master on the bridge and monitoring the OOW's conduct during crossing situations in congested waters.

pg_1353.label: Treat differing margin-of-safety perceptions between bridge teams as a recurring hazard and use such incidents as training material.

pg_1354.label: Treat the ferry as a 'vessel constrained by her draught' (Rule 3h) until clear of the shoal area south of the channel.

pg_1355.label: Treat the passage between the buoyed channel and the 10m depth line to the East as a Narrow Channel under Rule 9(b).

pg_1356.label: Small craft/yachts approaching or departing the port should keep well clear of frequent large vessel movements per local instruction.

pg_1357.label: Maintain watch on VHF Ch 16 in addition to the local working channel (Ch 14).

pg_1358.label: Attempt to contact the approaching vessel by name on VHF Ch 16 when concern arises.

pg_1359.label: When range closes to under 1 mile with no response and no course change, take independent avoiding action.

pg_1360.label: Choose an avoidance maneuver appropriate to the vessel's configuration (gybe and turn to port rather than attempt a starboard turn).

pg_1361.label: Avoid direct fastening of dissimilar metals without isolation (e.g. insulating washers/coatings)

pg_1362.label: Inspect structures like radar towers and masts for galvanic corrosion at fastening points

pg_1363.label: If constrained by draught, exhibit the Rule 28 signals (three red lights in a vertical line, or a black cylinder) and/or announce status by VHF.

pg_1364.label: Slow down if constrained by draught and in a close-quarters situation.

pg_1365.label: Assess whether the area in question genuinely constitutes a 'narrow channel or fairway' before relying on associated ColRegs rules.

pg_1366.label: Before running downwind with a poled-out genoa single-handed, plan in advance how to quickly alter course or douse the pole.

pg_1367.label: Notify the Coastguard when the vessel is in a situation of danger due to propeller fouling.

pg_1368.label: If not in imminent danger but requiring urgent assistance, send a Pan-Pan signal instead of a distress call.

pg_1369.label: Small boat owners should pre-plan their response to potential propeller fouling by rope or fishing gear.

pg_1370.label: Skipper immediately suspects rope fouling and visually inspects over the stern to confirm.

pg_1371.label: Attempt to unfurl jib to maintain steerage/course under sail.

pg_1372.label: When crew cannot free the rope and vessel is drifting toward a rocky coast in poor visibility, contact CROSS Corsen via DSC before the situation becomes more dangerous.

pg_1373.label: Coastguard authority decides to launch a lifeboat with a diver based on combined environmental factors.

pg_1374.label: Lifeboat diver enters water despite swell to clear the rope from the propeller once conditions/visibility assessed.

pg_1375.label: Since the rope was too substantial to haul aboard, lifeboat takes the rope in tow for disposal.

pg_1376.label: After freeing propeller, check engine, couplings, and bearings for damage before resuming passage under power.

pg_1377.label: Disconnect and check fwd and aft batteries when electrolyte needs topping up.

pg_1378.label: Monitor charging current and investigate unusual smells (e.g., battery gas) rather than attributing them solely to high charge rates.

pg_1379.label: Ensure adequate time delay between battery charging and engine start.

pg_1380.label: Regularly inspect and properly tighten battery terminal connections, especially butterfly nuts in vibration-prone areas.

pg_1381.label: Ensure battery compartments have adequate access and ventilation (consider positive ventilation) especially in confined/compact stowage or spaces like galley/saloon.

pg_1382.label: Exercise care when fitting a high capacity generating set aboard a vessel.

pg_1383.label: Ensure proper venting of the battery compartment is maintained or upgraded.

pg_1384.label: Turn off the battery isolators immediately after an explosion or suspected battery gas incident.

pg_1385.label: Retrieve a fire extinguisher and check for visible flames.

pg_1386.label: Open hatches to ventilate the compartment.

pg_1387.label: Evacuate the vessel after securing isolators and ventilating.

pg_1388.label: Ensure all battery cells (including inaccessible forward/aft batteries) can be physically inspected and electrolyte levels checked during maintenance.

pg_1389.label: Apply a robust change management procedure to any proposed change to equipment, systems, or procedures.

pg_1390.label: Conduct technical consideration/assessment of every proposed change.

pg_1391.label: Obtain proper authorisation before implementing the change.

pg_1392.label: Do not make or receive mobile telephone calls while conning a vessel in confined waters.

pg_1393.label: Properly review and discuss the proposed passage plan before executing it.

pg_1394.label: Reject the excuse 'there is no time for that' when safety checks are at stake.

pg_1395.label: Master to raise concerns directly with the pilot about distracting behaviour (e.g. mobile phone use) and insist it stop.

pg_1396.label: Insist on discussing and agreeing the departure/passage plan with the pilot before getting underway.

pg_1397.label: Direct tugs to make fast as planned despite pilot's reluctance.

pg_1398.label: Maintain safe passing distance from moored vessels regardless of pilot's urgency.

pg_1399.label: Do not allow pilot to disembark until vessel is clear of the port entrance.

pg_1400.label: Report the incident to the appropriate local authorities after the event.

pg_1401.label: If the master is declared medically unfit and cannot hand over command to the Chief Officer, keep the vessel alongside.

pg_1402.label: Only proceed to sea if the vessel can remain within safe manning levels appropriate to the work involved, with a fit person in command.

pg_1403.label: Wait alongside until a relief is found or the master is declared fit for work again.

pg_1404.label: Manager discusses the situation directly with the master.

pg_1405.label: Manager obtains guidance from the flag state before any decision is made.

pg_1406.label: Presume the vessel should not proceed to sea unless proper risk consideration and management is completed and approval is given.

pg_1407.label: Report hazardous incidents, even minor ones, to CHIRP.

pg_1408.label: Reflect personally on whether safety consciousness is maintained both on and off the vessel.

pg_1409.label: Even if considered stand-on vessel, take action to avoid collision once it is clear the give-way vessel's action alone will not suffice.

pg_1410.label: Make a large alteration of course early rather than slowing down rapidly.

pg_1411.label: The small craft should urgently weigh anchor or let the anchor line go (carefully, avoiding fouling the propeller) and move away from danger.

pg_1412.label: Don life-jackets as soon as a hazardous situation is arising, per RNLI recommendation.

pg_1413.label: Transmit a Mayday if the situation escalates to imminent danger to life or property requiring immediate assistance.

pg_1414.label: Envisage the encounter from the other vessel's watch-keeping perspective (small craft vs. large vessel and vice versa).

pg_1415.label: Exhibit correct day shapes: fishing vessel (other than trawling) to show two cones apex-to-apex or a basket if under 20m; tug to show a diamond shape if tow exceeds 200m.

pg_1416.label: Maintain a proper lookout, using binoculars, to assess risk of collision and identify that the tug was towing another vessel while still two to three miles apart.

pg_1417.label: Prepare to weigh anchor and move out of the tug's track once vessels are within about two miles of each other.

pg_1418.label: Monitor approaching large vessels' course and speed while anchored, even in open clear water.

pg_1419.label: Release remaining anchor warp to gain mobility when collision risk becomes apparent.

pg_1420.label: Prepare crew to cut the anchor line if necessary to avoid collision.

pg_1421.label: Listen on VHF Channel 16 for warnings from approaching commercial/tow vessels.

pg_1422.label: Monitor and close the unidentified radar contact cautiously while assessing possible piracy threat.

pg_1423.label: Use all available means (visual, radar, AIS) to positively identify the contact before taking action.

pg_1425.label: Hail the vessel on VHF to verify her status and check if she had been compromised by pirates.

pg_1426.label: Advise the other vessel's Captain of her COLREGS obligation to display navigation lights and warn of approaching head-on traffic.

pg_1427.label: Continue monitoring the blacked-out vessel after the VHF exchange as she proceeded toward expected end-on traffic.

pg_1428.label: Do not switch off navigation lights unless sanctioned by the authorities.

pg_1429.label: If reducing illumination is deemed prudent, switch off deck lighting only, keeping navigation lights on.

pg_1430.label: Avoid engaging in protracted or heated VHF exchanges with vessels that appear to be contravening ColRegs.

pg_1431.label: Develop and follow a Ship Security Plan that explicitly directs the Master on how to transit high-risk areas without contravening ColRegs.

pg_1432.label: Display navigation lights during hours of darkness (sunset to sunrise), in restricted/reduced visibility, and at any other time deemed necessary.

pg_1433.label: Maintain contact with other vessels to make them aware of your vessel's condition/status.

pg_1434.label: Do not rely solely on AIS receiver data for collision avoidance or traffic awareness.

pg_1435.label: Cross-check AIS picture continuously against radar and visual/lookout observations.

pg_1436.label: Treat AIS-derived speed/course data (e.g., 'steaming' status) with caution, especially for anchored or moored vessels.

pg_1437.label: Investigate installation quality (antenna type, height, placement) if a receive-only AIS unit shows inconsistent reception.

pg_1438.label: Do not rely on an AIS receiver alone to detect other vessels in restricted visibility.

pg_1439.label: Use AIS only as supplementary information to aid interpretation of the traffic situation, alongside other means of detection (e.g. radar, lookout).

pg_1440.label: Treat vessels showing 'underway' AIS status while visibly at anchor or in port as a sign of poor bridge data input discipline, and verify data accordingly.

pg_1441.label: Monitor the other vessel's bearing and lights to assess collision risk.

pg_1442.label: Stand on initially as the stand-on vessel under the Colregs.

pg_1443.label: Alter course 30-40 degrees to port to pass green to green when it became clear the other vessel would not give way.

pg_1444.label: Identify the offending vessel via AIS after the incident.

pg_1445.label: Forward the incident report to the vessel's manager without disclosing the identity of the other vessel (the dredger).

pg_1446.label: Have the manager follow up with the master regarding the close encounter.

pg_1447.label: As stand-on vessel, keep course and speed initially.

pg_1448.label: Only take independent action once it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not acting appropriately under the Rules.

pg_1449.label: Avoid altering course to port for a vessel on your own port side in a crossing situation (power-driven vessels).

pg_1450.label: Prefer slowing, stopping, or making a large alteration to starboard (up to 180° or 360°) as evasive action.

pg_1451.label: Continuously monitor approaching radar target with OOW and identify vessel by name.

pg_1452.label: Attempt to contact the approaching vessel on VHF Channel 16 at 3 miles range to request 0.5nm clearance and inform of dredging operation.

pg_1453.label: When no response received and CPA remained 0.1nm, abort the dredging operation and lift the pipe clear of the seabed.

pg_1454.label: Increase speed and alter course approximately 20° to port.

pg_1455.label: Re-attempt VHF contact with the vessel after it had passed clear.

pg_1456.label: Forward near-miss report to the vessel manager for follow-up with the Master.

pg_1457.label: Acknowledge fault openly (ferry should have kept clear of the yacht).

pg_1458.label: Review bridge procedures and implement bridge team management training programme.

pg_1459.label: Apologise to the affected yachtsman for anxiety caused.

pg_1460.label: Stand on initially, expecting the other vessel to keep clear.

pg_1461.label: Take emergency evasive action (crash gybe) when collision became imminent at ~100m range.

pg_1462.label: Select neutral to stop the propeller immediately upon sighting the hazard close ahead.

pg_1463.label: Drop anchor, switch on anchor light, and stop the engine once fouled.

pg_1464.label: Check that the prop shaft rotates freely by hand.

pg_1465.label: Inform VTS of position and intentions, and keep them updated.

pg_1466.label: Use a dinghy grapnel anchor to haul the line to the surface.

pg_1467.label: Attach the retrieved end to the aft pulpit and cut the seaward end of the line with a knife.

pg_1468.label: Have another vessel's dinghy pull the fender clear of the rudder.

pg_1469.label: Check steering for full and free movement and engine in ahead/astern before resuming passage.

pg_1470.label: Weigh anchor, extinguish anchor light, inform VTS, and continue passage.

pg_1471.label: Harbour Authority craft to remove fishing gear found to be improperly marked or laid.

pg_1472.label: Other Port/the other vessel should consider adopting a similar removal policy.

pg_1473.label: Contact the company owning the vessel involved in the close-quarters incident to seek explanation and corrective action.

pg_1474.label: Reinforce guidance to skippers to avoid close-quarters situations at speed.

pg_1475.label: Encourage and compliment reporting of such incidents by other mariners.

pg_1476.label: Maintain windlass and anchor-handling machinery in efficient working condition.

pg_1478.label: Move the vessel to a safe position before weather worsens.

pg_1479.label: If personnel must go forward, turn the vessel to provide shelter and ensure proper PPE including harnesses is worn.

pg_1480.label: Carry out a risk assessment before working on deck in bad weather.

pg_1481.label: Make a VHF call to the approaching vessel to advise it that it is heading towards anchored yachts and a dinghy.

pg_1482.label: Remain at anchor until the fast-approaching vessel has passed rather than weighing anchor into its path.

pg_1483.label: Take early action before the onset of heavy weather.

pg_1484.label: If deck access becomes necessary despite bad weather, review the specific hazards to personnel.

pg_1485.label: Determine and implement preventive action to mitigate identified risks.

pg_1486.label: Conduct both formal and dynamic risk assessments.

pg_1487.label: Use AGM (absorbed glass mat) sealed batteries instead of standard 'wet' lead-acid batteries for marine applications.

pg_1488.label: Install a gas detector in battery compartments, ideally a dual-head unit with one head positioned at the top of the compartment.

pg_1489.label: Fit forced ventilation (e.g., a 12v computer fan) that activates when batteries are charging from alternator or shore power.

pg_1490.label: Monitor charging systems/regulators for failure and avoid overcharging batteries.

pg_1491.label: Permanently secure one length of rope to the outboard end of the boom, with its other end clipped temporarily near the inboard end (e.g. to the kicker fitting).

pg_1492.label: Run a second rope forward through a block on the gunwale, then back to the cockpit.

pg_1493.label: When needed, unclip the first part from the boom-side fitting and re-clip it to the gunwale-rigged line, then tighten.

pg_1494.label: Captain should delay safety-critical operations if key personnel are fatigued.

pg_1495.label: Superintendent/senior manager should fully support the Captain's decision to delay the ship.

pg_1496.label: Senior managers should verify that safety management procedures consistently reinforce prioritizing safety over commercial pressure.

pg_1497.label: Seafarers under pressure to compromise safety should discuss the issue with a senior officer or the company's Designated Person.

pg_1498.label: If internal channels fail, contact CHIRP confidentially.

pg_1499.label: When crew have worked excessive continuous hours to fix a breakdown, stop work and allow a rest period before resuming operations or getting underway.

pg_1500.label: Chief Engineer/Master should raise fatigue concerns and recommend rest breaks to superintendent before critical operations (e.g., heaving anchor, proceeding to sea).

pg_1501.label: Sound fog signals continuously in restricted visibility as required.

pg_1502.label: Fit a radar reflector that meets ISO standard and mount it as high as possible, per manufacturer instructions.

pg_1503.label: Consult MCA MGN349 and the MAIB/QinetiQ reflector performance report for guidance on reflector selection and installation.

pg_1504.label: Do not assume radar carriage or reflector fitting excuses non-compliance with sound signalling rules.

pg_1505.label: Report the observed contravention to the Channel Navigation Information Service (CNIS) at Dover.

pg_1506.label: CNIS verifies the reported track against VTS data.

pg_1507.label: Notify the counterpart VTS authority (Gris Nez) of the confirmed contravention.

pg_1508.label: OOW closes the laptop lid when screen light impairs night vision.

pg_1509.label: Master reports the pilot's behaviour to the pilotage authority after being briefed by the watch-keeping officer.

pg_1510.label: Pilotage authority acknowledges the report and admonishes the pilot.

pg_1511.label: Monitor VHF traffic for vessels announcing intentions to cross a traffic lane.

pg_1512.label: Visually/AIS-track the crossing vessel's course and heading over time.

pg_1513.label: Query the Traffic Separation Scheme authority (Gris Nez Traffic) when a possible contravention is observed.

pg_1514.label: Refrain from debating the authority's interpretation over VHF.

pg_1515.label: Submit a report (e.g. via CHIRP) documenting the disagreement with the authority's interpretation.

pg_1516.label: Master should report unsafe pilot behaviour to the pilotage authority after the event.

pg_1517.label: OOW should alert the Master immediately upon having a concern about the pilot's actions.

pg_1518.label: Junior officers must be mentored to intervene whenever they are concerned about a safety issue, including challenging a pilot or senior officer.

pg_1519.label: Senior officers/pilots must respond constructively when challenged by junior staff.

pg_1520.label: Conduct Bridge Resource Management (BRM) training for ships' staff and pilots.

pg_1521.label: Use a rigid replica of Code flag 'A' as provided for under Rule 27.

pg_1522.label: Take measures to ensure the flag 'A' replica is visible all round the vessel.

pg_1523.label: Only display the flag 'A' signal while the vessel is actually engaged in diving operations.

pg_1524.label: Observe an unidentified small craft carefully for signs of activity or movement before deciding how to pass it.

pg_1525.label: Alter course early to give a wide berth to any vessel of uncertain status.

pg_1526.label: Attempt radio contact with the other vessel when their actions or signals are unclear or cause concern.

pg_1527.label: Do not assume a flag signal streamed downwind will be visible to an approaching vessel; actively look for the required rigid day-shape for diving operations.

pg_1528.label: Determine whether a vessel is 'engaged in fishing' per ColReg Rule 3(d) based on gear used (nets, lines, trawls restricting manoeuvrability), not merely because occupants are angling.

pg_1529.label: If at anchor, exhibit a single black ball shape where it can best be seen.

pg_1530.label: Watch-keepers on other vessels (e.g., tug) should look for anchor/shape signals to correctly assess the status of nearby small craft before assuming it is underway and acting as give-way vessel.

pg_1531.label: A vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre (e.g., tug towing) must exhibit the appropriate shapes to indicate this status.

pg_1532.label: Treat observation of a towing vessel or diamond shape as a cautionary cue even if not definitive proof of restricted manoeuvrability status.

pg_1533.label: Do not claim 'vessel engaged in fishing' status if using trolling lines or apparatus that does not restrict manoeuvrability.

pg_1534.label: Carry an anchor ball when anchored.

pg_1535.label: Maintain a proper lookout by sight, hearing, and all available means even while at anchor, especially offshore where large vessel traffic is expected.

pg_1536.label: Swing out the rescue boat with full crew aboard per drill protocol.

pg_1537.label: Commence lowering using the single arm davit and three-part wire bridle.

pg_1538.label: After the eye-plate detached, immediately ascertain whether the remaining crew member (officer in charge) was securely held.

pg_1539.label: Lower the boat to the water once the officer's safety was confirmed.

pg_1540.label: Recover the three crew members who had fallen into the sea.

pg_1541.label: Rig a webbing strap to replace the failed third bridle part while the boat was in the water.

pg_1542.label: Conduct subsequent examination of the failed bolts and eye-plate.

pg_1543.label: Arrange an urgent survey of similar rescue boats of the same age/model on other vessels.

pg_1544.label: Send failed bolts to the manufacturer for analysis.

pg_1545.label: Do not fit multiple-LED replacement bulbs into directional navigation lamp housings (tricolour masthead, bicolour, or single sidelight fittings).

pg_1546.label: Restrict use of these LED bulbs to all-round lights only (e.g., anchor lights and other all-round lights).

pg_1547.label: Be alert when interpreting another vessel's navigation lights that appear ambiguous or show overlapping colour segments.

pg_1548.label: Submit only safety-related issues; do not use this form for industrial relations complaints.

pg_1549.label: Acknowledge receipt of the report and provide a comprehensive closing response unless the reporter opts out.

pg_1550.label: If the report concerns non-compliance by another vessel (e.g., COLREGs), follow up with that vessel's owner or manager unless the reporter withholds permission.

pg_1551.label: Consider the report for summarized publication in Maritime Feedback unless the reporter declines.

pg_1552.label: Indicate preferences by ticking the relevant boxes (no response needed, no third-party contact, no publication).

pg_1553.label: Maintain full concentration and airmanship discipline on every trip regardless of distance or familiarity.

pg_1554.label: Keep a continuous, disciplined lookout scan at all times, even when engaging with passengers.

pg_1555.label: Avoid routing through areas where other traffic is likely concentrated (e.g., routes used to avoid an ATZ) when distracted by secondary tasks like showing a passenger a location.

pg_1556.label: Maintain a continuous, proper lookout scan at all times, even on familiar, routine, low-workload trips.

pg_1557.label: Do not assume that spotting one other aircraft/vessel means no further traffic is present.

pg_1558.label: Limit non-essential distractions (e.g., instructing a passenger, pointing out scenery) during critical phases of flight/navigation such as descent or approach.

pg_1559.label: Upon detecting a steady-bearing, closing contact, take immediate evasive action (climb, apply power, turn) to increase separation and improve visibility of the other traffic.

pg_1560.label: Keep a good all-round look-out at all times, visually and by radar.

pg_1561.label: Maintain situational awareness of how quickly a traffic situation can change.

pg_1562.label: Do not assume the other vessel has seen you; use light/sound signals or searchlight per ColReg 36 if necessary to attract attention.

pg_1563.label: Think 'What if...' and plan in advance what action to take if the other vessel takes unexpected action or fails to comply with the ColRegs.

pg_1564.label: Allow a prudent margin of safety and respect the other vessel's safety margin.

pg_1565.label: Maintain a proper visual and radar lookout at all times, especially when the vessel is on autopilot.

pg_1566.label: Take early and substantial avoiding action when a risk of collision is detected.

pg_1567.label: Ensure navigation lights and radar reflectors are displayed and effective, and account for background shore lighting that may obscure them.

pg_1568.label: Inform the Coastguard before departing port

pg_1569.label: Detail crew members to keep lookout for fish farm marker lights on approach

pg_1570.label: Rely on prior knowledge of the fish farm's location when no lights were visible

pg_1571.label: Re-check for marker lights when departing the marina later

pg_1572.label: Refer reported navigational hazard to the Commissioners of Irish Lights (General Lighthouse Authority).

pg_1573.label: Mark aquaculture farm cages per IALA guidelines: two lighted buoys seaward side, two unlighted buoys/beacons shore side.

pg_1574.label: Conduct inspection of the fish farm site by the Commissioners' Inspector.

pg_1575.label: Reinstate lighted buoys following inspection findings.

pg_1576.label: Maintain a proper lookout visually and by radar at all times, even when briefly engaged in essential duties like plotting position.

pg_1577.label: Post a dedicated lookout on the bridge during darkness in addition to the OOW.

pg_1578.label: Keep wheelhouse lights off at night.

pg_1579.label: When risk of collision becomes apparent (e.g., at ~2 miles/12 minutes before closing), call the skipper immediately.

pg_1580.label: Direct at least five short and rapid flashes of a flashlight toward the approaching ship.

pg_1581.label: Illuminate the yacht's sails with a flashlight.

pg_1582.label: Attempt to contact the ship by VHF.

pg_1583.label: Ensure crew wear lifejackets if not already doing so.

pg_1584.label: As stand-on vessel, consider action under Rule 17(b) if the give-way vessel fails to act.

pg_1585.label: Consider starting the engine to assist avoiding action.

pg_1586.label: CHIRP refers the report to the tanker's manager while protecting reporter/vessel anonymity.

pg_1587.label: Manager investigates and obtains a corroborating report from the Master.

pg_1588.label: Manager identifies specific failures (lack of BRM, failure to warn Master, poor judgment/coordination, inadequate incident knowledge, failure to follow rules).

pg_1589.label: Master conducts training for all deck officers on company safe navigation procedures in congested waters, separation zones, coastal and open sea areas.

pg_1590.label: Case circulated fleet-wide for awareness and corrective action.

pg_1591.label: Manager arranges further training for officers and Master when next in the office.

pg_1592.label: Ensure passage plans account for known fixed hazards such as rig positions.

pg_1593.label: Masters must ensure their presence on the bridge while doing other tasks does not reduce watch-keeper alertness.

pg_1594.label: Commence and maintain a radar plot on any approaching vessel whose track threatens the rig or own vessel.

pg_1595.label: Continue monitoring even after the other vessel appears to be taking avoiding action for a different target (e.g. the rig).

pg_1596.label: Assess whether the other vessel's actions are producing an appreciable reduction in risk of collision, not just a change in CPA relative to a third object.

pg_1597.label: When satisfied the give-way vessel is taking no appreciable action and CPA has closed to a dangerous range (0.03nm at 8 cables), take positive remedial action by altering course to starboard.

pg_1598.label: Continue turning under increased power once the other vessel makes its own avoiding alteration, until it has passed clear astern.

pg_1599.label: Complete a round turn under reduced power until risk of collision has gone.

pg_1600.label: Immediately call the Master to the bridge upon receiving an unclear Mayday.

pg_1601.label: Check AIS to identify other vessels in the area who may have also heard the Mayday.

pg_1602.label: Make contact with the vessel and verify whether it genuinely sent the Mayday.

pg_1603.label: Conduct a follow-up conversation to double-check the vessel's safety status once contact is established.

pg_1604.label: Close communications only after confirming the Mayday was not genuine.

pg_1605.label: Clearly instruct whoever handles communications during a drill that external transmissions must be simulated, not actually sent.

pg_1606.label: Explicitly define and communicate the 'communication boundaries' of any exercise, i.e. which external parties may genuinely be contacted and which must be role-played.

pg_1607.label: Do not place sole blame on the individual who made the error; review whether proper instructions were given beforehand.

pg_1608.label: Continue to credit and encourage realistic drill execution while fixing the procedural gap.

pg_1609.label: Sound the horn early to attract the attention of the approaching vessel as soon as collision risk is suspected.

pg_1610.label: Get everyone in the cockpit or on deck.

pg_1611.label: Don lifejackets if not already worn.

pg_1613.label: Be prepared to slip the anchor.

pg_1615.label: Call the Master to the bridge when officer of the watch is concerned about another vessel's actions.

pg_1616.label: Assess available sea-room and other vessels' positions before maneuvering.

pg_1617.label: Query the overtaking vessel by radio as to why she did not overtake on the correct (starboard) side when free to do so.

pg_1618.label: Advise the overtaking vessel to reduce her own speed and keep well clear.

pg_1619.label: When the overtaking vessel made no response and continued course/speed, reduce own speed to let her pass ahead, then alter hard to port around her stern once clear, returning to intended course.

pg_1620.label: If fitting a fan to force-ventilate a battery compartment, select one certified as having a spark-proof fan motor.

pg_1621.label: Choose fan/ventilation units complying with ISO 8846 (Small craft - Electrical devices - Protection against ignition of surrounding flammable gases) or the equivalent US standard.

pg_1622.label: Avoid at all costs any electrical components capable of producing a spark in an area classified as IEC Zone 1 (likely to have an explosive gas mixture).

pg_1623.label: Configure the ventilation system so exhausted gas is directed overboard where it can safely disperse.

pg_1624.label: Request explicit permission from the escorting warship before leaving the convoy formation.

pg_1625.label: Remain in convoy and maintain lane discipline until formally dismissed by the warship.

pg_1626.label: Communicate course and speed changes clearly to all convoy vessels and the warship during any deviation.

pg_1627.label: Weigh the actual security/time benefit of leaving convoy early against the risk created for other ships.

pg_1628.label: Inspect stainless steel through-bolts, fittings, and wire rigging for signs of anaerobic corrosion, especially where bolts are tightly fitted (e.g., GRP installations) but may allow slight seawater seepage.

pg_1629.label: Check wire rigging inner strands, not just outer strands, when inspecting stainless steel wire for corrosion.

pg_1630.label: Treat any loosening of equipment secured by stainless steel bolts (e.g., radar support tripods) as a potential indicator of underlying bolt corrosion.

pg_1631.label: Avoid combining high tensile stainless steel (HTSS) fittings with galvanized (zinc) components in marine environments.

pg_1632.label: When investigating suspect HTSS fittings (bolts, nuts, washers, chain), check whether they have been in contact with galvanized backing plates, washers, nuts, or shackles.

pg_1633.label: Do not rely solely on routine visual or standard non-destructive inspection to clear HTSS fittings as satisfactory.

pg_1634.label: Treat design use of 'high tensile' stainless steel as materially different from ordinary 18/8 stainless steel when selecting fasteners for marine fittings.

pg_1635.label: Connect the piston lifting device to the piston crown at TDC using the specified bolts before attaching the crane hook.

pg_1636.label: Maintain continuous visual monitoring of chain tension/slack throughout the lowering operation, not just verbal communication with the other operator.

pg_1637.label: Ensure the crane operator focuses on the lifting process under their control rather than solely on maintaining eye contact with the turning gear operator.

pg_1638.label: Verify the chain hoist is correctly paying out chain in coordination with the piston's descent speed.

pg_1639.label: Ensure materials selected for rescue boat fittings (e.g. bolts, backing plates) are suitable for the environmental conditions they will be exposed to.

pg_1640.label: Avoid using different metallic materials together in fittings such as backing plates and bolts.

pg_1641.label: Inspect GRP rescue boat lifting eyes and surrounding structure for integrity, not just the metal fitting itself.

pg_1642.label: Assess whether it is viable to attach the crane chain at Bottom Dead Centre (BDC) instead of TDC as currently specified in the work card.

pg_1643.label: Position the turning gear operator on top of the engine adjacent to the crane operator.

pg_1644.label: Pay out a suitable initial length of chain before turning the engine.

pg_1645.label: Post an observer at the crankcase door to signal when the piston reaches BDC.

pg_1646.label: Stop the turning gear immediately if a situation arises.

pg_1647.label: Position the piston at Bottom Dead Centre (BDC) and remove the securing bolts, allowing gravity to hold it in place.

pg_1648.label: Turn the engine so the piston is at Top Dead Centre (TDC).

pg_1649.label: Attach the piston lifting device and lift the piston using the crane from the TDC position.

pg_1650.label: Follow the engine manufacturer's guidance for the specific procedure and account for all associated risks, including crane-related risks.

pg_1651.label: Report near-misses and safety concerns to CHIRP under guarantee of confidentiality.

pg_1652.label: When CHIRP investigates a navigational near-miss, contact the owners of the 'other ship' involved to determine what went wrong.

pg_1653.label: Read CHIRP Feedback newsletters published several times a year.

pg_1654.label: Maintain the charterer's standing orders to run 2 or 3 diesel generators during DP operations depending on power load.

pg_1655.label: Bridge watch officers should request additional generator(s) be brought online upon observing an approaching squall.

pg_1656.label: Engine room watch should react immediately upon observing problems with the power management system.

pg_1657.label: Turn the vessel head to wind and slow down significantly

pg_1658.label: Reject an alteration to port as the sole action

pg_1660.label: Attempt light signals, sound signals, and radio contact with the cargo ship

pg_1661.label: Maintain a sharp, continuous lookout using a 'seaman's eye'

pg_1662.label: Have the Officer of the Watch call the Master in good time when a potential close-quarters situation is developing.

pg_1663.label: Maintain good situational awareness of other vessels in the vicinity.

pg_1664.label: Properly assess the risk of collision and weigh up possible actions.

pg_1665.label: Start and use engines when needed to maneuver.

pg_1666.label: Carefully monitor the situation until the other vessel has passed clear.

pg_1667.label: Take vessel manoeuvring characteristics (especially of large sailing vessels) into account when determining a safe CPA.

pg_1668.label: Monitor the other vessel's movement on ARPA/AIS once risk of collision is first detected.

pg_1669.label: Call the OOW to the bridge when CPA reaches zero at a significant range (5NM).

pg_1670.label: Verify the other vessel's identity and type via AIS.

pg_1671.label: Contact the other vessel by name on VHF and clarify its intentions once it has taken no action at 3.5NM with steady zero CPA.

pg_1672.label: Remind the other vessel it is the give-way vessel and ask what action it will take to comply with COLREGs.

pg_1673.label: Sound two series of five short blasts and flash light signals when the other vessel takes no further action.

pg_1674.label: Start the engine and alter course hard to starboard when the give-way vessel fails to respond or act.

pg_1675.label: Call the other vessel on VHF Ch16, then switch to a working channel to clarify intentions.

pg_1676.label: Remind the overtaking vessel that she is the give-way vessel under Rule 13 and must alter to starboard.

pg_1677.label: Take own avoiding action (alter course to starboard to pass astern) when the other vessel fails to act and distance closes to 0.5nm.

pg_1678.label: Forward a disidentified copy of the report to the vessel's management for internal follow-up.

pg_1679.label: Master to brief the officer of the watch on avoiding misunderstandings between vessels during overtaking.

pg_1680.label: Use ARPA radar data, not AIS, for CPA/TCPA assessments in collision avoidance decisions.

pg_1681.label: Overtaking vessel (ferry) must keep clear of the vessel being overtaken until past and clear.

pg_1682.label: Sound appropriate signals and/or communicate intentions before overtaking in close proximity.

pg_1683.label: Report close-quarters incidents to the Coastguard for follow-up with the other vessel's Master.

pg_1684.label: Alert the ferry operator's manager to the reported close-passing incident.

pg_1685.label: Promote discussion among officers regarding safety margins and allowance for contingencies such as engine or steering failure.

pg_1686.label: Regularly inspect safety-critical components such as shackles, even when access is difficult.

pg_1687.label: Share lessons learned from incidents via reporting schemes.

pg_1688.label: Inspect lower rigging at the start of each season.

pg_1689.label: Take the mast down periodically to inspect upper rigging and hound fittings.

pg_1690.label: Replace flat cross-section stainless shackles with round-section shackles fitted with captive pins.

pg_1691.label: Confirm with marina/harbour authority why buoys are missing (e.g. removed for dredging).

pg_1692.label: Check whether a Notice to Mariners has been issued and whether the Coastguard has been notified.

pg_1693.label: Monitor Coastguard Marine Safety Information broadcasts (issued every four hours).

pg_1694.label: Do not rely exclusively on a navigation buoy as the primary aid; use the leading light's white sector to confirm the safe channel.

pg_1695.label: If a Local Lighthouse Authority needs to remove a buoy (even temporarily), confirm it obtained approval from the General Lighthouse Authority (e.g. Trinity House).

pg_1696.label: Hold course and speed to give the overtaking vessel space and time to take avoiding action.

pg_1697.label: If the overtaking vessel shows no sign of taking avoiding action, take independent action (e.g. tack and pass behind) to avoid collision.

pg_1698.label: Maintain continuous watch even when under auto-helm.

pg_1699.label: Debrief as a crew after close-quarters incidents and identify lessons learned.

pg_1700.label: Obtain formal training (e.g. RYA course) to ensure watchkeepers know and can apply IRPCS.

pg_1701.label: Take in two rolls (reef) on the genoa when sailing single-handed

pg_1702.label: Take in three rolls in heavy wind conditions

pg_1703.label: Maintain active lookout to leeward despite single-handed operation

pg_1704.label: Verify correct orientation of multi-leg lifting bridles before each lift, ensuring longer fore/aft legs are mounted as the outer pair on the master link and shorter stabilizing legs are inner.

pg_1705.label: Inspect GRP rescue boat lifting eyes/lugs for structural adequacy and consider replacement if design is known to be weak.

pg_1706.label: Report any rescue boat lifting incidents to CHIRP.

pg_1707.label: Immediately close the door if irritation or unusual atmosphere is detected upon entry

pg_1708.label: Report the 'smell' or anomaly to an officer without delay

pg_1709.label: Do not linger in the suspect space during investigation; exit promptly if symptoms (e.g. light-headedness) occur

pg_1710.label: Investigate to identify the source of the hazardous atmosphere

pg_1711.label: Dispose of remaining dry ice and thoroughly ventilate the affected space

pg_1712.label: Establish VHF contact with the converging vessel to clarify intentions.

pg_1713.label: Request the other vessel to slow down and pass astern.

pg_1714.label: Monitor the other vessel's bearing and range continuously after the request is refused.

pg_1715.label: Stop engines and go slow astern when the other vessel closed to a dangerous range.

pg_1716.label: Complete the Ship/Shore Safety Check-List in full before commencing LNG loading.

pg_1717.label: Conduct proper dialogue between ship and shore personnel on each individual checklist item.

pg_1718.label: Conduct Cold ESD test and pre-loading safety discussion between Loadmaster and Chief Officer before loading commences.

pg_1719.label: the other vessel must confirm and communicate actual cooldown status of ship's lines before authorizing loading start.

pg_1720.label: Refuse/stop loading if vessel is not correctly lined up or lines are not sufficiently cooled.

pg_1721.label: Issue a Letter of Protest to the terminal when loading is commenced in violation of agreed procedure.
