pg_1722.label: Tug master alerted the outbound ship to the developing problem with the motor boat.

pg_1723.label: Tug master confirmed it was safe to reduce power before doing so.

pg_1724.label: Tug reduced power to lessen the propeller wash.

pg_1725.label: Motor boat operator continued to distance himself from the area once he recognised the danger, until the outbound ship had passed.

pg_1726.label: Near miss reported to the tug company and the Port Authority.

pg_1727.label: Inspect the lifejacket bladder cover material after any inflation event, not just at annual checks.

pg_1728.label: Examine the sewing/sealing around the whistle attachment point specifically.

pg_1729.label: Report the suspected widespread manufacturing fault to relevant authorities/manufacturer.

pg_1730.label: Reduce tug power when aware of nearby vessels at risk from propeller wash, provided it does not compromise the safety of the berthing operation.

pg_1731.label: Report such incidents as a near miss to the Port Authority.

pg_1732.label: Consult and heed local marine guides for known hazards such as tug propeller wash in harbour areas.

pg_1733.label: Maintain a proper lookout at all times by sight, hearing, and all available means.

pg_1734.label: Scan the horizon more frequently than perceived, verifying actual intervals rather than assumed ones.

pg_1735.label: Account for closing speed when assessing risk of collision.

pg_1736.label: Regularly inspect lifejacket outer casing and straps for damage.

pg_1737.label: Check that the gas bottle is screwed tight without disturbing the bladder stowage.

pg_1738.label: Re-stow an inflated lifejacket's bladder strictly per manufacturer's instructions, seeking advice if uncertain.

pg_1739.label: Have lifejackets inspected by a competent inspector per manufacturer's recommended schedule, including gas bottle examination and weighing.

pg_1740.label: During inspection, inflate the lifejacket to prescribed pressure and verify it holds within allowance, accounting for temperature.

pg_1741.label: As stand-on vessel, continuously monitor the approaching vessel's heading and crew presence, and take avoiding action when collision is assessed as inevitable.

pg_1742.label: Monitor AIS and radar continuously to identify vessels that may pose a collision danger.

pg_1743.label: Call merchant ships on VHF at long range (e.g., ~11 miles) to confirm mutual awareness of position and intended course.

pg_1744.label: Re-contact the vessel at closer range (e.g., 8 miles) if initial contact denied seeing the yacht on radar.

pg_1745.label: Treat the situation as urgent and decide on avoidance action once range closes to about 6 miles with no confirmed resolution.

pg_1746.label: Avoid any unpredictable maneuver while remaining the stand-on vessel among other traffic.

pg_1747.label: Attempt repeated radio contact with the approaching vessel to clarify intentions.

pg_1748.label: When the give-way vessel confirms it will not alter course or speed, take independent action by turning onto a reciprocal course until the ship has crossed the intended track.

pg_1749.label: Apply Rule 19 (Conduct of vessels in restricted visibility), not Section II give-way/stand-on terminology, when vessels are not in sight of one another.

pg_1750.label: Take avoiding action in ample time once risk of collision is detected by radar.

pg_1751.label: Proceed at a safe speed appropriate to restricted visibility.

pg_1753.label: Contact the Coastguard if there is a risk of mishap.

pg_1754.label: Attempt to restart and diagnose the engine when it stops unexpectedly, testing operation in neutral before engaging gear.

pg_1755.label: If gear stalls the engine when engaged but it runs fine in neutral, suspect propeller fouling and avoid forcing the drivetrain.

pg_1756.label: Return to berth under sail/alternative means rather than relying on the compromised propulsion.

pg_1757.label: Arrange for divers to inspect and clear the propeller and have the vessel lifted for inspection/repair.

pg_1758.label: Mark fishing buoys conspicuously (e.g. bright colour, adequate size) so they are visible in rough/white-crested water.

pg_1759.label: Follow MCA 2008 revised guidance on marking of fishing gear.

pg_1760.label: Expect Southampton Harbour Master's patrol craft to remove improperly marked gear in the Solent.

pg_1761.label: Attach the fishing signal (two cones apex to apex, one above the other) to the masthead via a halyard rather than a fixed lashing.

pg_1762.label: Inspect shackle pins on all similar rescue boat lifting attachments to confirm they are the correct type, not substituted with fully threaded stainless steel bolts.

pg_1763.label: Check the size of the doubling plate under the lifting eye, ensuring it has an area of at least 4 times that of the top plate.

pg_1764.label: Verify that the fibreglass hull/structure in the lifting eye region is locally thickened.

pg_1765.label: Treat seemingly minor non-compliances (e.g., improper disposal of oily rags) as potential serious hazards.

pg_1766.label: Conduct a comprehensive investigation when such incidents occur.

pg_1767.label: Apply lessons learned across the entire fleet.

pg_1768.label: Pay out a length of hoisting chain equivalent to the engine stroke before removing the connecting rod top bolts from the top joint.

pg_1769.label: If the engine turning gear is disconnected after the piston is removed, take precautions to prevent crankshaft assembly rotation.

pg_1770.label: Ensure the job card is written correctly before work begins.

pg_1771.label: Ensure only fully experienced operatives operate the crane and perform the lift.

pg_1772.label: Assess and account for the torque generated by the engine turning gear before commencing work.

pg_1773.label: Extinguish the fire rapidly using portable fire extinguishers and fire hoses.

pg_1774.label: Conduct an in-depth investigation despite no injuries, pollution, or permanent damage.

pg_1775.label: Audit fleet-wide construction of garbage receptacles used for oily rags.

pg_1776.label: Update initial outfit standards for new vessels to include compliant receptacles for oily rag storage internally and externally.

pg_1777.label: Develop guidance on spontaneous combustion hazards of linseed/vegetable oils and biofuels.

pg_1778.label: Ensure a full inventory of all chemicals carried on board is maintained.

pg_1779.label: Highlight the case to chandlers and reinforce packaging and MSDS requirements in contract terms.

pg_1780.label: Modify procurement procedures for comprehensive checking of stores received and positive reporting to the chief engineer of non-compliant goods.

pg_1781.label: Run an awareness campaign on chemical management and promote proactive use of MSDS.

pg_1782.label: Review Job Hazard Analyses related to chemical work after the awareness campaign.

pg_1783.label: Review the Garbage Management Plan with special regard to oily rag management.

pg_1784.label: Intervene politely but firmly to correct an unsafe distraction.

pg_1785.label: Before raising a discussion, ask 'Is this a suitable and safe time for us to discuss…?'

pg_1786.label: If the Master or Officer determines it is not a safe time, state this clearly and defer the discussion.

pg_1787.label: Shore staff should reinforce, not undermine, the Master's authority over vessel safety.

pg_1788.label: Complete Pilot/Master exchange before proceeding with pilotage.

pg_1789.label: Monitor bridge team effectiveness continuously, especially when distractions occur.

pg_1790.label: Repeat and confirm berthing arrangements before execution, even if previously discussed.

pg_1791.label: Directly and firmly intervene to stop disruptive noise/conversation on the bridge when it threatens to distract the team, especially approaching a critical maneuvering phase.

pg_1792.label: Take collision-avoidance action that is positive, made in ample time, and with due regard to good seamanship, per ColRegs Rule 8.

pg_1793.label: Keep inter-ship VHF communications professional and concise.

pg_1794.label: Refer to MGN 324 guidance on use of VHF radio and AIS at sea.

pg_1795.label: Appreciate the anxiety felt on the stand-on vessel's bridge when CPA is small, and communicate/act accordingly rather than dismiss their concerns.

pg_1796.label: Implement a robust Safety Management System procedure governing any changes to vessel equipment and systems.

pg_1797.label: Conduct a risk assessment before carrying out modification work.

pg_1799.label: Supervise the work as it is carried out.

pg_1800.label: Check all radar wiring for any kind of damage.

pg_1801.label: Pick up slack in cables and secure them with cable ties.

pg_1802.label: Check other bridge equipment for slack cables and signs of wearing.

pg_1803.label: Have service engineers accompanied by an appropriate member of ship personnel during installations.

pg_1804.label: Maintain own course and speed once CPA is being assessed, while continuing to track the overtaking vessel.

pg_1805.label: Contact the overtaking vessel directly on VHF when her CPA remains dangerously low (here, at 1.7 miles).

pg_1806.label: Explicitly state a minimum acceptable safe passing distance (e.g., 5 cables/half a mile) when the other vessel's officer is evasive or dismissive.

pg_1807.label: Allow or rely on VTS intervention when direct ship-to-ship communication fails to produce a safe course alteration.

pg_1808.label: Report the observed non-conformance (incorrect HRU fitting) to the company, including photographic evidence.

pg_1809.label: Company acknowledges the report and thanks the reporter.

pg_1810.label: Company rectifies the non-conformance on the HRU/valise.

pg_1811.label: Company provides feedback to the reporter on remedial action taken.

pg_1812.label: Assemble safety/guard rails on tenders fully and correctly after launching, before carrying passengers.

pg_1813.label: Use proper rated fittings (shackle or pelican hook) to secure guard-wire attachments rather than tied/cut rope.

pg_1814.label: Report any observed safety deficiency immediately to ship staff (hotel staff, purser desk) for forwarding to the deck department.

pg_1815.label: Follow up on reported safety defects to confirm corrective action was taken and inform the reporting party.

pg_1816.label: Carry out walk-around checks of the vessel's safety equipment, including liferaft HRU rigging, as part of the ship's safety team routine.

pg_1817.label: Verify HRU installation against correct diagrams/manufacturer guidance for the specific HRU type.

pg_1818.label: Confirm and document that any identified HRU rigging issue has been corrected promptly.

pg_1819.label: Do not carry out fly-shooting (or similar radical-manoeuvre fishing operations) within a Traffic Separation Scheme.

pg_1820.label: Report any observed contravention of the Traffic Separation Scheme immediately to the UK or French Authorities.

pg_1821.label: Maintain continuous radar/ARPA plot on small targets detected on the bow.

pg_1822.label: Cross-check visual lookout identification against AIS equipment.

pg_1823.label: Contact the closer overtaking vessel (container ship) by VHF before altering course to starboard.

pg_1824.label: Continuously reassess the target's light display as range closes.

pg_1825.label: Report the incident to the traffic/coastal authority (Cap Gris Nez) on VHF Ch13 after the fishing vessel had cleared.

pg_1826.label: Review and challenge flag-state minimum manning certificates for coastal vessels where watchkeeping hours and workload indicate fatigue risk.

pg_1827.label: the other vessel should inspect and consider detaining a vessel if the manning composition is assessed as unsafe or fatigue-inducing.

pg_1828.label: Detain the vessel if rest-hour records are found to be falsified.

pg_1829.label: Ensure compliance with hours-of-rest regulations for Master and Mate sharing watches.

pg_1830.label: Maintain a dedicated look-out at night.

pg_1831.label: Keep and allow audit of company records of hours of rest.

pg_1832.label: Report fatigue concerns confidentially to CHIRP.

pg_1833.label: Observe and report near-miss incidents encountered during work operations.

pg_1834.label: Improve personal and crew safety awareness and understanding of risks posed by the specific workplace/operation.

pg_1835.label: Take personal responsibility to report hazardous incidents rather than assuming someone else will.

pg_1836.label: Intervene when a hazard is observed by pointing it out to ship's staff.

pg_1837.label: Share the lesson learned with the wider community (e.g., via CHIRP reporting).

pg_1838.label: Inspect pilot ladders and lifeboat painters for plastic tape wrapped around manila rope

pg_1839.label: Remove any tape found and examine the rope underneath for rot

pg_1840.label: Replace any ropes found to be compromised promptly

pg_1841.label: Investigate and ascertain the source of fumes entering accommodation

pg_1842.label: Replace/secure the open inspection hatch in the AC trunking

pg_1843.label: Check all air conditioning trunking hatches prior to any work involving fuel tanks

pg_1844.label: Carefully and frequently check passenger accommodation during such work

pg_1845.label: Add this control measure to the Workplace Risk Assessment reviewed with Permits to Work

pg_1846.label: Treat any report of fumes or smells in accommodation with urgent attention to determine the cause

pg_1847.label: On joining any vessel, check all cold room doors to confirm push rods are long enough to operate the exterior catch from inside.

pg_1848.label: Test that the entrapment alarm bell for each cold room is functioning.

pg_1849.label: Weld extensions onto any undersized push rods and repair faulty alarms across all cold rooms.

pg_1850.label: Establish a regular testing regime for cold room push rods and alarms.

pg_1851.label: Identify specific risks relevant to the vessel's systems (e.g., cooling water loss)

pg_1852.label: Devise contingency measures for identified risks

pg_1853.label: Practice the contingency measures through drills

pg_1854.label: Investigate unusual loud noises from machinery spaces immediately.

pg_1855.label: Start the stand-by generator to maintain electrical power.

pg_1856.label: Sound the engineers' alarm call to mobilize the engine room team.

pg_1857.label: Follow the technical emergency reaction checklist to isolate the cooling water system using remote isolation valves.

pg_1858.label: Rapidly refill the system header tank using the remotely operated high-capacity cooling water pump.

pg_1859.label: Restart main engines as soon as cooling water is restored.

pg_1860.label: Man the Engine Room immediately and implement emergency flooding procedures.

pg_1861.label: Activate emergency bilge injections using two separate pumps.

pg_1862.label: Review and amend operating procedures regarding care needed when filling ballast pipelines, per Fleet Group change management procedures.

pg_1863.label: Revise handover requirements for personnel new to the vessel class.

pg_1864.label: Update the cargo-handling manual with clear guidance on refilling evacuated ballast lines.

pg_1865.label: Visually monitor the bearing of the approaching vessel for signs of change.

pg_1866.label: Cross-check the visual bearing assessment using AIS receiver data (course, speed, MMSI, name).

pg_1867.label: Attempt to attract the other vessel's attention using a large torch directed at the ship, repeated as range closed.

pg_1868.label: Continue observing the other ship's course for any change after signaling attempts.

pg_1869.label: When no course change was detected, alter course to port and tack, showing the green sector of the navigation light, to pass behind the vessel.

pg_1870.label: Continue to monitor the other ship after the avoiding action to confirm no further course change.

pg_1871.label: Use a large torch/searchlight beam directed toward the danger to attract the other vessel's attention when necessary.

pg_1872.label: Alter course to starboard and gybe away from the approaching ship rather than altering to port and tacking towards it.

pg_1873.label: Carefully observe the other vessel throughout the avoiding action.

pg_1874.label: Use AIS receiver data to identify the approaching ship.

pg_1875.label: Fit DSC radio on small craft even though not mandatory.

pg_1876.label: Make a general VHF call to attempt contact with an unidentified vessel appearing in restricted visibility.

pg_1877.label: Once the vessel's name is visible, re-establish contact by name on a working channel.

pg_1879.label: Review available documentation and interview the senior watch officer when electronic data is no longer available due to delayed reporting.

pg_1880.label: Apply company bridge procedures defining minimum actions, including sounding signals, when visibility is considered less than moderate.

pg_1881.label: Acquire and track approaching small vessels both electronically (radar) and visually, especially when passing rain showers may obscure radar targets.

pg_1882.label: Make radio contact and agree passing arrangements with other vessels when a close-quarters situation is identified.

pg_1883.label: Use AIS as a supplementary aid for vessel identification and detection, not as a replacement for radar and visual watchkeeping.

pg_1884.label: Welcome and encourage small craft (e.g., yachtsmen) to proactively alert larger vessels of their presence.

pg_1885.label: Make sound signals in or near areas of restricted visibility, even on small craft.

pg_1886.label: Maintain a listening watch on VHF channel 16.

pg_1887.label: Fit and use AIS on vessels, including small craft where practical.

pg_1888.label: Fit and use DSC (Digital Selective Calling) equipment.

pg_1889.label: Report near-miss incidents promptly rather than months later.

pg_1890.label: Treat a weakened forestay as a hazard requiring immediate attention.

pg_1892.label: When a roller-furling jib jams, avoid repeatedly and forcefully alternating tension on jib sheet and roller reefing line to free it.

pg_1893.label: If freeing attempts fail, lower the jib to the deck rather than continuing to force it.

pg_1894.label: Inspect rigging wires immediately after any unusual strain is imposed on them.

pg_1895.label: If there is any doubt about rigging condition after an incident, review/inspect it before further use.

pg_1896.label: Do not rely solely on radar for early warning in poor visibility; maintain other means of detection (sound, lookout).

pg_1897.label: Promptly decide and execute a collision-avoidance action (hold course/speed or alter to present a smaller end-on target) when warned of a crossing threat.

pg_1898.label: Immediately call the other vessel on VHF to obtain its name and home port after a close-quarters encounter.

pg_1899.label: Maintain course if the other vessel's course cannot be determined.

pg_1900.label: Do not rely on a VHF call to an unidentified vessel in a fast-developing close-quarters situation.

pg_1901.label: If collision with a fast boat in fog cannot be ruled out: get everyone into the cockpit/on deck, don lifejackets per RNLI guidance, and plot the vessel's position.

pg_1902.label: Test radar performance against visual sightings of other vessels in clear conditions and call a service engineer if targets seen visually are not detected by radar.

pg_1903.label: Fully test all navigation lights and newly fitted equipment before sailing.

pg_1904.label: Stop using the tricolour light if it is compromised by reflection and revert to using separate side lights.

pg_1905.label: Cover the reflective radar enhancer unit in black self-amalgamating tape to absorb rather than reflect light.

pg_1906.label: Report the issue to the equipment manufacturer/rigging company and the MCA.

pg_1907.label: Monitor a closing vessel continuously for signs it is taking appropriate avoiding action, not just assume it will.

pg_1908.label: Hail an apparently inattentive vessel early when risk of collision is suspected.

pg_1909.label: Maintain a dedicated lookout and keep a helmsman actively at the helm when underway, especially in busy areas.

pg_1910.label: Avoid relying on a vessel with very low boat speed (under spinnaker in light wind) to be able to take late avoiding action.

pg_1911.label: Do not exhibit fishing vessel lights or shapes when not engaged in fishing.

pg_1912.label: Avoid permanently displaying the rigid replica of flag 'A' diving signal even though Rule 27(e)(ii) does not explicitly forbid it when not diving.

pg_1913.label: Maintain a proper lookout at all times as a prime responsibility.

pg_1914.label: Use an air-horn in addition to hailing to attract the attention of another vessel.

pg_1915.label: Encourage seafarer to raise concerns with senior officers or the DPA first.

pg_1916.label: If seafarer is reluctant to approach DPA, allow them to report concerns confidentially to CHIRP.

pg_1917.label: CHIRP discusses the issue with the seafarer and agrees a course of action.

pg_1918.label: If seafarer agrees, CHIRP may contact the DPA on their behalf.

pg_1919.label: If the issue involves a serious regulatory breach, CHIRP may alert the appropriate authority.

pg_1920.label: Never disclose the identity of the reporting seafarer regardless of action taken.

pg_1921.label: Identify the traffic situation early upon leaving harbour.

pg_1922.label: Recognise that a crossing situation may exist even with a vessel broad on or abaft the starboard beam.

pg_1923.label: Give a comprehensive description of the traffic situation during watch handover.

pg_1924.label: Do not prioritize adherence to the planned track over compliance with the ColRegs.

pg_1925.label: Maintain a careful radar watch on areas with thick low clouds or rain near the vessel's track.

pg_1926.label: Adjust radar range and rain clutter settings when tracking targets near precipitation.

pg_1927.label: Harbour Master and staff provide educational presentations to the recreational sector on risks of close-quarters approaches.

pg_1928.label: Allocate patrol launch escorts to large vessels where possible.

pg_1929.label: Establish port user forums involving both commercial and leisure users at major ports.

pg_1930.label: Use experienced volunteers to engage and persuade transgressing leisure boaters to improve boat handling and seamanship.

pg_1931.label: Contact the ship's manager/operator when erroneous AIS data is suspected from another vessel.

pg_1932.label: Cross-check AIS data against other sources of information.

pg_1933.label: Periodically check the accuracy of the AIS data being transmitted by your own vessel.

pg_1934.label: Display appropriate signals indicating vessel constrained by draught.

pg_1935.label: Sound five short blasts when small craft approach or cross close ahead.

pg_1936.label: Sound appropriate sound signals prior to commencing turns.

pg_1937.label: Request Harbour Master launch to reprimand offending vessels.

pg_1938.label: Record names/sail numbers of offending vessels for reporting to the Harbour Master.

pg_1939.label: Continuously monitor an overtaking vessel's aspect and CPA/TCPA even while attending to other traffic (e.g. a fishing vessel in a radar blind spot).

pg_1940.label: Take prompt avoiding action (alter course) when the collision alarm indicates a closing CPA.

pg_1941.label: Explicitly request that the other vessel wait until clear before altering course again, and slow down if possible to assist separation.

pg_1942.label: Account for other constraints (e.g. a fishing vessel astern) when deciding how much to slow down or maneuver.

pg_1943.label: Remove and dispose of the incorrect/incorrect starting handle from the lifeboat.

pg_1944.label: Brief all crew at a drill/meeting on the accident and refresh starting engine safety precautions and procedures.

pg_1945.label: Place a copy of the starting procedures inside the engine compartment.

pg_1946.label: Conduct a shipboard toolbox talk to formulate a risk assessment for the starting procedure with all crew involved.

pg_1947.label: Position the yacht between the casualties and the oncoming ferry rather than moving away

pg_1948.label: broadcast an 'ALL SHIPS' call on Channel 16 stating identity, approximate position, and nature of the situation

pg_1949.label: Request assistance from rescue services in the area

pg_1950.label: Delegate recovery tasks to guests aft while remaining at the helm

pg_1951.label: Refrain from using engines once a casualty slipped under the bathing platform

pg_1952.label: Assign a guest to keep visual contact on the drifting third casualty

pg_1953.label: Go aft personally to assist once unable to use engines

pg_1954.label: Stop/avoid using engines when persons are in the water near the stern.

pg_1955.label: Post a dedicated look-out to maintain visual contact with a casualty still in the water.

pg_1956.label: Issue a MAYDAY RELAY call, or activate the DSC red distress button, when persons are in grave and imminent danger.

pg_1957.label: Skipper should don a lifejacket and set the example for others before/at the earliest opportunity.

pg_1958.label: Clear low deck area (e.g., lower the dinghy) to create a rescue platform before casualties arrive.

pg_1959.label: Physically haul casualties aboard even through very tight spaces between platform and dinghy.

pg_1960.label: Return to helm and radio promptly to update Coastguard on number of casualties recovered and status of other vessels assisting.

pg_1961.label: Accept RIB-landed crew/lifeboat-men aboard to assist and follow Coastguard instruction to transport recovered casualties to the nearest port.

pg_1962.label: After the incident, review whether a MAYDAY RELAY or DSC distress button activation would have been more effective than the All Ships call.

pg_1963.label: Reconsider policy on guests wearing lifejackets at all times, and conduct a thorough safety briefing before departure.

pg_1964.label: Require guests boarding the vessel to wear lifejackets, citing RNLI advice firmly but courteously.

pg_1965.label: Before starting a rescue, take about two minutes to discuss the proposed rescue plan and precautions with the crew ('Take Two').

pg_1966.label: Don lifejackets and, if appropriate, safety harnesses before working on the stern platform during a rescue.

pg_1967.label: Conduct a safety briefing for all persons when they board the vessel.

pg_1968.label: Regularly run safety drills, including man-overboard exercises, even on leisure craft.

pg_1969.label: Keep a careful, continuous watch on an approaching vessel rather than assuming you have been seen.

pg_1970.label: Fit an effective radar reflector to the yacht.

pg_1971.label: Resume original course once the close-quarters situation has safely passed and no further contact attempts are needed.

pg_1972.label: Treat all commercial vessels in shipping lanes with increased caution going forward.

pg_1973.label: Bear away or gybe early to ensure approaching vessels on barely-changing bearings pass safely ahead, even when technically the stand-on vessel.

pg_1974.label: Keep navigation and steaming lights on and be ready to use a spotlight to increase visibility when under power at night near commercial traffic.

pg_1975.label: Maintain a continuous lookout with two crew on watch while approaching the shipping lane.

pg_1976.label: Take and record a bearing on the sighted vessel using a hand-bearing compass.

pg_1977.label: Cross-check the contact on radar against the EBL.

pg_1978.label: Attempt to contact the approaching vessel by VHF on Ch16 then Ch13, using an approximate position since the name could not be identified.

pg_1979.label: When no response was received and the vessel closed to under 0.4NM on an unchanged bearing, order the helm to bear away sharply to starboard.

pg_1980.label: Assume you may not have been seen by the other vessel.

pg_1981.label: Sail defensively at all times in a channel encounter.

pg_1982.label: Fit a DSC radio and obtain an AIS receiver to identify and call a specific vessel's MMSI if seeking assurance of being sighted.

pg_1983.label: Activate bilge pumps and use buckets to reduce water level immediately on discovering ingress.

pg_1984.label: Systematically check all seacocks, rudder, and prop shaft for ingress sources.

pg_1985.label: Start engine, stow sails, and proceed to a sheltered bay to investigate.

pg_1986.label: Inspect the fore-cabin compartment under the bunks containing the new battery installation.

pg_1987.label: Inspect the watertight bulkhead penetrations for the windlass cables.

pg_1988.label: Secure the cabling and reseal the bulkhead holes.

pg_1989.label: Empty, wash down with fresh water, dry, and spray electrical components with WD40.

pg_1990.label: Inspect bilges more frequently going forward.

pg_1991.label: Fully inspect any completed refit/repair work, especially cable runs through watertight bulkheads.

pg_1992.label: Seal any holes drilled through a bulkhead for cables with an appropriate bulkhead gland.

pg_1993.label: Route cables through the top of the bulkhead rather than the bottom where possible.

pg_1994.label: Make a precautionary call to the Coastguard upon initially discovering water ingress.

pg_1995.label: Track approaching vessel initially on radar, then confirm identity and closing data via AIS once in range.

pg_1996.label: Assess CPA/TCPA data on the chart-plotter to decide whether to cross ahead or duck astern of the tanker.

pg_1997.label: Alter course 90 degrees to starboard to pass astern of the tanker.

pg_1998.label: Monitor AIS alarm and course indications during the turn.

pg_1999.label: Check that flares are in apparent good condition and in-date.

pg_2000.label: Ensure anyone who may use a flare is fully familiar with the instructions.

pg_2001.label: Make an earlier decision to alter course and duck behind a vessel once it appears on radar.

pg_2002.label: Keep a 'tanker scarer' torch and a white flare readily accessible on deck, not stored below.

pg_2003.label: Continue radar watch and terminate non-essential VHF conversation once clear of shipping is not yet achieved.

pg_2004.label: Question whether the larger vessel is keeping a proper watch 'at all times and by all means' and whether its radar is correctly set.

pg_2005.label: Alter course to starboard well before the situation becomes critical.

pg_2006.label: Maintain a dedicated lookout in addition to the officer of the watch during hours of darkness.

pg_2007.label: Use attention-attracting signals to be seen, not to intimidate other vessels.

pg_2008.label: Assess sea conditions before allowing a diver overboard.

pg_2010.label: Evaluate the possibility of the diver cutting himself/herself.

pg_2011.label: Confirm availability of protective equipment such as face mask and wet suit.

pg_2012.label: Plan the means of re-boarding the yacht.

pg_2013.label: Arrange potential support to the diver from others on board.

pg_2014.label: If outside assistance is available, take it instead of diving.

pg_2015.label: Make an advisory call to the Coast Guard as well as Port Control when immobilised.

pg_2016.label: Prepare the anchor for letting go, with extra warps attached if needed, if being swept toward a hazardous area.

pg_2017.label: Carefully assess the swimming and diving ability of the person intending to dive before attempting to clear a fouled propeller.

pg_2018.label: Carry a face mask aboard to enable clearing a fouled propeller by diving when safe to do so.

pg_2019.label: Task a local dealer to drain water from the fuel system and pressure-test the tanks for leaks.

pg_2020.label: Fill tanks to the brim and fit extension tubes to the fillers to observe for overflow/leak behaviour.

pg_2021.label: Lift the deck to physically inspect the bilge and tank area.

pg_2022.label: Remove the RIB from service and bring it ashore pending resolution of safety issues.

pg_2023.label: Replace fuel tanks found to have integrity concerns.

pg_2024.label: Commission professional marine engineers to conduct a thorough risk assessment of fuel tank and control line arrangements.

pg_2025.label: Ensure any petrol leak gas cannot pass from the bilge into the console containing electrics.

pg_2026.label: Route control lines through gas-tight ducts.

pg_2027.label: Secure the replacement fuel tanks properly.

pg_2028.label: Fit gas alarms in the bilges where practicable.

pg_2029.label: Intervene when witnessing an unsafe situation, regardless of rank or position.

pg_2030.label: Report hazardous incidents to CHIRP or equivalent confidential reporting programme.

pg_2031.label: If all electrics cut out near a wind farm, attempt to restore power by pressing the ON switch.

pg_2032.label: Report the incident and compare experiences with other vessels in the area.

pg_2033.label: Plan a passing route maintaining at least the recommended safe distance from the salvage operation (1 nm) when converging/overtaking traffic is present.

pg_2034.label: Acknowledge guard vessel's initial advisory on location and recommended safe passing distance.

pg_2035.label: When given a specific course-alteration instruction, move the conversation to a working channel and question the guard vessel's reasoning.

pg_2036.label: Independently verify CPA/TCPA with the other converging vessel before accepting or rejecting the guard vessel's instruction.

pg_2037.label: Decline the instruction if own assessment shows sufficient sea room, and restate intended track.

pg_2038.label: Continue to monitor and maintain the planned safe passing distances for both the salvage zone and the other vessel through to completion of the transit.

pg_2039.label: Salvage company reviews and reissues detailed rules of engagement to sub-contracted VTS officers.

pg_2040.label: Mariners should critically assess and not automatically comply with instructions from a guard ship/VTS officer that go beyond expected navigational authority.

pg_2041.label: If concerned for safety near an exercise area, contact the Coast Guard initially on Channel 16.

pg_2042.label: Use AIS receiver data only as additional supporting information when assessing a traffic situation.

pg_2043.label: Do not assume all vessels will be detected by AIS or that transmitted data is absolutely reliable.

pg_2044.label: Do not rely on a single source of information when making navigational decisions.

pg_2045.label: Avoid steering parallel to the passenger ship to pass port to port.

pg_2046.label: Do not gybe in the prevailing conditions.

pg_2047.label: Do not assume a vessel is absent or safe to disregard simply because it is not showing on AIS.

pg_2048.label: Check receiver/aerial condition and weather effects before concluding another vessel has an AIS fault.

pg_2049.label: Monitor Coast Guard broadcasts for notice of naval exercises in the area.

pg_2050.label: Report any suspected unusual AIS interference (e.g., near wind farms) to CHIRP or the MCA.

pg_2051.label: Investigate and respond to a disidentified CHIRP report through the ship's manager and Master.

pg_2052.label: On realizing a close-quarters situation exists, assess it accurately and communicate with the other vessel to maintain course and speed while altering own course.

pg_2053.label: Acknowledge over VHF radio that the reaction was late.

pg_2054.label: Officer of the watch reports the incident and his own late reaction to the Master.

pg_2055.label: Master issues an apology to the affected yacht's crew and relays findings via the ship's manager.

pg_2056.label: Post a dedicated lookout on the approaching vessel as soon as risk of collision is suspected.

pg_2057.label: Call the vessel on VHF Ch.16, stating own position and aspect, and request its intentions.

pg_2058.label: Repeat the VHF call multiple times in quick succession if no response is received.

pg_2059.label: Escalate messaging to an urgent demand for 'immediate avoiding action' when the close-quarters situation becomes critical.

pg_2060.label: Maintain own course and speed as the stand-on vessel throughout, per IRPCS, despite the near-miss.

pg_2061.label: Use good seamanship/engineering practice to recognise when a situation is hazardous.

pg_2062.label: Intervene as appropriate to correct the hazardous situation.

pg_2063.label: Report the near-miss or safety issue so lessons can be learned.

pg_2064.label: If reluctant to report to the company, submit the report to CHIRP in complete confidence.

pg_2065.label: Ensure risk assessments are completed, safe systems of work established, and work permits used appropriately.

pg_2066.label: Maintain effective communication between crew and shore management.

pg_2067.label: Conduct a full investigation into the watchkeeping failure.

pg_2068.label: Review and strengthen assurance processes for watchkeeping compliance.

pg_2069.label: Detect and radar-plot the approaching vessel as early as possible (12 miles) and separately tag its AIS identity on radar.

pg_2070.label: Visually sight and confirm the other vessel's navigation lights once in range.

pg_2071.label: Place own vessel into hand steering when CPA indicates a close-quarters situation.

pg_2072.label: Use an Aldis light to signal the other vessel when it does not appear to be taking avoiding action.

pg_2073.label: Commence and continue a starboard turn to increase passing distance, adjusting as the other vessel maneuvers.

pg_2074.label: Question the other vessel's bridge team about their visual and radar watch practices after the incident.

pg_2075.label: Keep a good all-round look-out and maintain proper situational awareness while anchored.

pg_2076.label: Be prepared to weigh anchor if a close-quarters or hazardous situation develops.

pg_2077.label: Alert the Coast Guard if a hazardous situation is arising.

pg_2078.label: Continuously monitor approaching vessel traffic while at anchor and assess closing range/course for risk of collision.

pg_2079.label: Check AIS data on the approaching vessel to confirm speed and course.

pg_2080.label: When direct calls go unanswered, contact Coast Guard immediately and explain the situation.

pg_2081.label: Start engine and prepare to cut the anchor line while awaiting resolution.

pg_2082.label: As give-way vessel, give way early by slowing or waiting before entering the narrow channel.

pg_2083.label: Sound appropriate sound signals and take avoiding action if collision becomes imminent despite stand-on status.

pg_2084.label: Treat an angling vessel at anchor as relying on her anchor ball for identification, not as a vessel 'engaged in fishing' under ColRegs.

pg_2085.label: Bridge watchkeepers should identify an anchored small craft as early as possible, ideally beyond about 2 miles.

pg_2086.label: Do not assume a small craft's movements are predictable or that holding course/speed while 'watching to see what the boat does' is acceptable without full ColRegs compliance.

pg_2087.label: Consider passing distance from the small boat's perspective, not just from a professional mariner's confined-waters standard.

pg_2088.label: Small craft should not rely solely on a VHF Channel 16 call to alert an approaching commercial vessel; use DSC/GMDSS alerting where possible.

pg_2089.label: Do not assume the other vessel will keep clear; actively assess the situation before committing to the channel.

pg_2090.label: If uncertain, hold back and delay entry into the narrow channel until the crossing situation is resolved.

pg_2091.label: As a power-driven vessel, anticipate that an approaching yacht may suddenly and unexpectedly alter course due to wind gusts.

pg_2092.label: As a sailing vessel in strong wind, shorten sail early to retain maneuverability needed to comply with the ColRegs as either stand-on or give-way vessel.

pg_2093.label: Keep as far to the starboard side of the channel centre as possible and avoid increasing speed while transiting.

pg_2094.label: Ensure robust procedures exist for inspecting pilot ladders and that they are actually applied on commercial vessels.

pg_2095.label: If a pilot observes a defect in boarding arrangements, report it to the port state authority.

pg_2096.label: If reluctant to report directly to port state authority, contact CHIRP instead.

pg_2097.label: Where a pilot ladder uses aluminium grippers or ferrules, carefully inspect the condition of the rope.

pg_2098.label: Replace snap shackles in rescue boat lifting bridles with conventional shackles.

pg_2099.label: Cross-check all charted hazards (e.g. fish farms) against current UKHO charts before approach

pg_2100.label: Investigate any anomalous or unexplained lights near the intended track rather than assuming they are unrelated to navigation

pg_2101.label: Report uncharted/unnotified hazardous lights to the Coastguard after the incident

pg_2102.label: Retrace the inbound track in daylight to locate and confirm the position of the hazard

pg_2103.label: Check the obvious bits of rigging when chartering a boat before departure.

pg_2105.label: Charter companies should identify and correct deficiencies before the client boards.

pg_2106.label: If conditions allow (not too windy), slacken the foresail halyard, unroll the sail, and pull it down to reunite the shackle with the furling drum.

pg_2107.label: Read the referenced MAIB report on the fatal incident.

pg_2108.label: Review own club/organisation's safety procedures against the findings.

pg_2109.label: Report any near-miss incident, especially in the engine room, to the ship's manager through the normal reporting route.

pg_2110.label: If unwilling to report to the ship's manager for any reason, contact CHIRP directly instead.

pg_2111.label: Subscribe to the CHIRP website/newsletter and encourage colleagues to do the same.

pg_2112.label: Report incorrectly lit or confusing navigation marks to the relevant Local Aids to Navigation Inspector/General Lighthouse Authority.

pg_2113.label: Change private/fish farm marker lights to flashing yellow per IALA recommendation.

pg_2114.label: Conduct a thorough check around the boat, including rigging and sail fittings, before departure.

pg_2115.label: If a critical fitting (e.g., shackle pin) cannot be properly reinserted underway, improvise a secure temporary fix such as a multi-turn lashing.

pg_2116.label: Report the defect to the charter company at the end of the charter.

pg_2117.label: Maintain a good, continuous lookout on all vessels in the vicinity, especially small fishing boats.

pg_2118.label: Exercise extra caution and allow a wider safety margin when the other vessel is a small fishing boat.

pg_2119.label: Do not assume an overtaking vessel acquires fishing-vessel give-way rights simply by being close ahead and engaged in fishing activity.

pg_2120.label: Request an independent lifeboat service company to investigate the incident once the vessel arrives in port.

pg_2121.label: Remove and closely scrutinise the remaining air cylinders.

pg_2122.label: Check date stamps on cylinders to verify hydro-test currency.

pg_2123.label: Assess material wastage/corrosion of cylinder walls.

pg_2124.label: Determine economic viability of repair versus scrapping the TEMPSC.

pg_2126.label: Raise the matter with the organisation that conducted the LSA survey.

pg_2127.label: Conduct regular inspection and survey of all parts of pressurised gas/air bottles, including hidden or concealed areas.

pg_2128.label: Review and strengthen the survey and inspection regime for lifeboat-related pressure equipment.

pg_2129.label: Ensure no personnel are nearby or working in/on the lifeboat during periods of elevated risk from pressurised components.

pg_2130.label: Verify lifejacket Wheelmark certification and request test documentation from the European authority and manufacturer when doubts arise about suitability.

pg_2131.label: Select lifejacket type based on intended use: lighter designs for routine work, bulkier 2010-standard designs for abandonment situations only.

pg_2132.label: When a vessel engaged in fishing is nearby, even if it was previously the overtaking vessel, treat it as having right of way and manoeuvre to keep clear.

pg_2133.label: Use main engines to execute a safe passing manoeuvre when a vessel engaged in fishing stops close ahead.

pg_2134.label: Maintain course and speed as the stand-on/right-of-way vessel while assessing if the other vessel will take appropriate action.

pg_2135.label: Take avoiding action (turn to starboard) once it becomes clear the other vessel will not take corrective action.

pg_2136.label: When individual early and substantial action toward each vessel is not possible due to traffic density, reduce speed to allow the regatta/fleet to cross ahead safely.

pg_2137.label: Apply Rule 2(b) (special circumstances) of the collision regulations when standard rule-by-rule action is impractical due to special circumstances.

pg_2138.label: Bridge teams should try to visualise the situation as perceived from the cockpit of a yacht, and yachtsmen should try to visualise it from the ship's bridge.

pg_2139.label: Use checklists properly as a genuine verification tool during routine operations.

pg_2140.label: Avoid treating checklist completion as a mere 'tick the box' exercise.

pg_2141.label: Notify the company manager of the deviation from the recommended IRTC track.

pg_2142.label: Manager instructs the Master to strictly comply with recommendations.

pg_2143.label: Manager issues a Fleet alert to all vessels.

pg_2144.label: Agree (or not) to have the report forwarded to the other vessel's manager.

pg_2145.label: Ask 'Why?' repeatedly (five times) starting from the immediate symptom to uncover deeper causes.

pg_2146.label: Identify that the shaft was not correctly secured as the immediate cause.

pg_2147.label: Recognise inattention and lack of experience as a contributing human factor.

pg_2148.label: Check for absence of proper preparation, risk assessment, and work permit.

pg_2149.label: Evaluate whether the company and crew recognised the job as dangerous beforehand.

pg_2150.label: Establish and use a well-established internal near-miss reporting system.

pg_2151.label: Contact CHIRP confidentially if safety culture concerns are not addressed by master or ship's manager.

pg_2152.label: Delay departure and remain alongside when a main engine fault is reported, especially during strong spring tides.

pg_2153.label: Notify the pilot promptly of delays and give required advance notice once ready.

pg_2154.label: Maintain full bridge team roles during pilotage (helmsman, officer logging/charting, Master monitoring courses).

pg_2155.label: Voice concerns immediately to the pilot when vessel position appears unsafe (e.g., too close to shore).

pg_2156.label: Request pilot refrain from further course alteration until vessel is clear of hazard.

pg_2157.label: After the transit, remind pilots of their advisory role and the need to communicate intentions to the bridge team.

pg_2158.label: Query the pilot's intentions immediately when an unexplained course change threatens to take the vessel out of the buoyed channel.

pg_2159.label: Prioritize safety of navigation over managing pilot behavior, especially given fishing gear hazards.

pg_2160.label: Placate the agitated pilots to de-escalate the situation.

pg_2161.label: Resume safe course alteration (back to starboard) once pilots departed.

pg_2162.label: Retain full command authority and responsibility throughout the pilotage.

pg_2163.label: Assess risk of departing at the scheduled time against the status of unresolved technical issues.

pg_2164.label: Maintain continuous, careful monitoring of the vessel's passage by the bridge team.

pg_2165.label: Establish open dialogue with the pilot at the time of boarding during the passage plan discussion.

pg_2166.label: Ensure senior team members remain receptive to questioning and challenge from other team members, including the pilot.

pg_2167.label: Report hazardous ColRegs encounters to CHIRP or the relevant authority even as a small-craft operator.

pg_2168.label: Ship manager should acknowledge the incident and investigate it when notified.

pg_2169.label: Apply lessons learned fleet-wide, not just to the vessel involved.

pg_2170.label: Detect and plot approaching vessel early using radar and ARPA.

pg_2171.label: Identify vessel via AIS and establish VHF contact at 4.0nm to ascertain intentions.

pg_2172.label: Request XXX to alter course to starboard, citing her open water and own vessel's restricted ability to do so.

pg_2173.label: When no response was received despite repeated calls and risk persisted (vessel under 3nm), contact Engine Control Room and reduce speed.

pg_2174.label: Engage hand steering and alter course to starboard while reducing speed.

pg_2175.label: Call the master to the bridge.

pg_2176.label: Once CPA with XXX reached 0.5nm and she was clear, increase speed and resume original course.

pg_2177.label: Conduct a pre-crossing discussion and radar scan 20 minutes before entering the TSS to identify all vessels in the area.

pg_2178.label: At 4.5 miles, signal the other vessel with an Aldis lamp and follow up with a VHF call on CH16, then move to a working channel.

pg_2179.label: Request the other vessel comply with COLREGs by altering course to starboard and passing astern.

pg_2180.label: Monitor the other vessel's actual course changes via AIS after agreement is reached.

pg_2181.label: When relative speeds and surrounding traffic made the original plan unsafe, execute a controlled full round turn to starboard before resuming passage.

pg_2182.label: Establish VHF contact with the approaching vessel when CPA is assessed as too close.

pg_2183.label: Assert stand-on vessel status and request the give-way vessel take appropriate action.

pg_2184.label: If the give-way vessel maintains course/speed and CPA remains unsafe (<0.5 NM), take independent avoiding action by reducing sail and altering course away from the other vessel's track.

pg_2185.label: After the close-quarters situation resolves, radio the other vessel to register concern over non-compliance and advise the incident will be reported.

pg_2186.label: Report the incident to CHIRP/the vessel's management, with reporter and vessel identity kept confidential.

pg_2187.label: Plan the TSS crossing in advance.

pg_2188.label: Communicate the crossing plan clearly with the bridge team.

pg_2189.label: Treat crossing traffic within the TSS as having right of way, not the vessel proceeding along the TSS.

pg_2190.label: Practice good housekeeping and fuel management for biodiesel-blended fuel.

pg_2191.label: Conduct regular checks to ensure fuel tanks remain free of water.

pg_2192.label: If a bacterial growth outbreak occurs, empty and clean tanks or treat with biocide additives and filtering.

pg_2193.label: Replace fuel filters once, outside the normal service interval, after 2 to 3 tank throughputs of new biodiesel fuel.

pg_2194.label: Inspect and potentially replace fuel seals in sight gauges on older fuel storage tanks.

pg_2195.label: Investigate and identify the cause of blocked fuel filters following any intermittent engine power loss.

pg_2196.label: Review fuel husbandry practices and fuel quality, especially where bio-diesel content is used.

pg_2197.label: Examine fuel system seals for signs of leakage.

pg_2198.label: Turn over fuel in any tank at least every 6 months and no more than every 12 months.

pg_2199.label: Keep tanks as full as possible when in use, balanced against expected usage/duration.

pg_2200.label: Drain water off regularly from tanks.

pg_2201.label: Consider modifying drain facilities to improve effectiveness.

pg_2202.label: Inspect and replace seals and fuel system components as necessary.

pg_2203.label: Check and clean strainers and filters more regularly.

pg_2204.label: Where possible, purchase diesel without biodiesel content.

pg_2205.label: Use test kits to check for contamination if concerned about fuel quality.

pg_2207.label: Help others by looking out for their safety.

pg_2208.label: Make a personal commitment to safety.

pg_2209.label: Do not react with frustration or anger when another vessel fails to give way.

pg_2210.label: Identify the close-quarters situation as soon as the other vessel's aspect/light change indicates a course alteration into a crossing situation.

pg_2211.label: Request the other vessel take preventive/give-way action in accordance with Rule 15 of the ColRegs.

pg_2212.label: Monitor the range continuously and make a follow-up VHF call when distance decreases further (e.g., at 3 miles).

pg_2213.label: Obtain Captain's presence/awareness on the bridge during the developing close-quarters situation.

pg_2214.label: Monitor the other vessel's aspect and light changes (green to red) to detect unexpected course alterations.

pg_2215.label: Order rudder to starboard to avoid collision when the give-way vessel crosses close ahead again.

pg_2216.label: Maintain full speed and pass port to port once committed to the avoiding action.

pg_2217.label: OOW calls the Captain when facing an unpredictable or developing close-quarters situation.

pg_2218.label: Captain takes over the con from the OOW.

pg_2219.label: OOW must interpret night orders in light of the actual traffic situation, not literally.

pg_2220.label: Manager investigates reported incidents personally and reviews competency assurance in recruitment.

pg_2221.label: Introduce ColReg training and testing software fleet-wide.

pg_2222.label: Immediately stop the stevedore from using the open flame near dangerous cargo.

pg_2223.label: Inform the stevedore that use of any open fire is strictly forbidden aboard.

pg_2224.label: Report the concern to the charterers and the stevedoring company.

pg_2225.label: Instigate improved security, requiring the watchman to search all bags brought aboard.

pg_2226.label: Place one hand to firmly grasp the lifejacket just below the chin and pull down.

pg_2227.label: Place the other hand over the nose.

pg_2228.label: Only display Not-Under-Command lights/shapes when the vessel is genuinely unable to manoeuvre due to an exceptional (rare/extraordinary) circumstance, per ColReg Rule 3.

pg_2229.label: If engine is stopped routinely and vessel is not anchored, continue to adhere to collision avoidance responsibilities as a power-driven vessel underway under ColReg Rule 18.

pg_2230.label: Do not use deck working lights to signal that the vessel is drifting.

pg_2231.label: Avoid drifting close to the coast (within two or three miles) while engine is stopped.

pg_2232.label: Ensure a valid gas free certificate is obtained before any entry into ballast tanks or enclosed spaces.

pg_2233.label: Report unresolved safety concerns or near-misses to CHIRP if internal channels are inadequate.

pg_2234.label: Submit a near-miss report on any hazardous incident encountered, taking only a few minutes to do so.

pg_2235.label: Report areas of particular interest: errors and error-enforcing conditions, operating/maintenance/support procedures, regulatory aspects, unsafe practices or design.

pg_2236.label: Agree with CHIRP on publication terms; CHIRP edits reports only to remove identifying text.

pg_2237.label: Maintain and use the company's own near-miss reporting programme as part of a well-established safety culture.

pg_2238.label: If the occurrence falls outside the scope of the seafarer's own SMS, or involves another company's SMS affecting their activities, submit a report to CHIRP.

pg_2239.label: Reduce speed to a safe speed for the restricted visibility conditions (11.2 kts).

pg_2240.label: Continuously plot the approaching vessel's movements using multiple radars.

pg_2241.label: Call the approaching vessel on VHF and request they pass astern per the Collision Regulations.

pg_2242.label: When the other vessel refused and claimed it would pass ahead despite insufficient speed to do so, independently assess the geometry using radar data.

pg_2243.label: Stop engine to reduce own speed further as the final collision avoidance action.

pg_2244.label: OOW must comply with the Collision Regulations and take early and decisive action when identified as the crossing vessel.

pg_2245.label: OOW should call the Master when a close-quarters situation appears imminent.

pg_2246.label: Company should undertake OOW training to improve understanding of the Collision Regulations.

pg_2247.label: Company should audit Bridge operations for adequacy.

pg_2248.label: Take early and decisive action rather than subtle speed reductions.

pg_2249.label: Reassess safe speed in restricted visibility rather than maintaining habitual speed.

pg_2250.label: CHIRP contacted the shipowner of vessel A to obtain the OOW's account of the encounter.

pg_2251.label: OOW on vessel A altered course to port to increase CPA from 1.0 to 1.5 miles after VHF communication with the reporter.

pg_2252.label: OOW declined the reporter's request to pass astern.

pg_2253.label: Plan vehicle loading to account for passenger health and safety, not just space/trailer logistics.

pg_2254.label: Passengers requiring assistance should declare this at check-in or via the company website prior to boarding.

pg_2255.label: Deck crew must assist any passenger who appears to need help or asks for it.

pg_2256.label: When queries arise about hazardous loading decisions, the loading officer or responsible party should be willing to explain the reasoning to a concerned passenger or observer.

pg_2257.label: Attempt to contact the approaching vessel by VHF from all survey vessels (seismic vessel, chase and guard vessels).

pg_2258.label: Dispatch the chase vessel to intercept the yacht.

pg_2259.label: Escalate signalling methods: searchlight, ship's whistle, then bullhorn.

pg_2260.label: Make contact by shouting vessel-to-vessel once in proximity.

pg_2261.label: Direct the yacht to motor out of the danger area once contact was established.

pg_2262.label: Optimise radar settings for prevailing weather conditions.

pg_2263.label: Position chase vessels to maximise early detection and intervention opportunities.

pg_2264.label: Maintain enhanced visual lookout, especially when sun angle and wave height obscure small craft.

pg_2265.label: Ensure project operations are properly promulgated via Navtex/Notice to Mariners.

pg_2266.label: Educate leisure/yacht users on hazards of operating near offshore seismic operations.

pg_2267.label: Conduct a full root cause/incident investigation in cooperation with the client after a hazardous occurrence is reported.

pg_2268.label: Issue recommendations to all vessels in the fleet covering guard vessel positioning and additional means of attracting attention of uncooperative vessels (e.g., white parachute signal flares).

pg_2269.label: Conduct a full review of operator procedures together with chartered chase vessel operators.

pg_2270.label: Publish the investigation findings and recommendations.

pg_2271.label: Volunteer as an Ambassador by emailing mars@nauticalinst.org or john.rose@chirp.co.uk if wishing to improve local seafarer safety culture

pg_2272.label: Receive briefing material and coaching provided to Ambassadors

pg_2273.label: Drain off a litre or so of diesel from each tank sump at regular intervals and after every rough passage.

pg_2274.label: Change tank and engine fine filters at least twice a year.

pg_2275.label: Avoid relying solely on a 'Fuel Polishing' system if its filtration is coarser than the tank filters used.

pg_2276.label: Dose tanks liberally with a water dispersant additive and occasionally a biocide.

pg_2277.label: Leisure craft operators should drain off water/contaminants and change fuel filters frequently per RYA advice.

pg_2279.label: Mariners must independently assess whether a given stretch of water constitutes a 'narrow channel or fairway' before relying on Rule 9.

pg_2280.label: Exercise caution near entrances to designated narrow channels, especially regarding right-of-way assumptions under Rule 9.

pg_2281.label: Report hazardous occurrences and near misses to CHIRP (or equivalent reporting body) even when no harm resulted.

pg_2282.label: Build extra time into work planning stages to run a proper Management of Change process before altering equipment, spares, or pipework.

pg_2283.label: Update ship's documents and plans whenever equipment, spares, or pipework are changed.

pg_2284.label: Conduct an electrical (amperage) audit of equipment when fitting out recreational/small craft.

pg_2285.label: Report hazardous occurrences at the ship/shore interface (pilot ladders, tug operations, line handling).

pg_2286.label: Require manufacturers to produce operating and maintenance manuals to a common document standard with uniform layout, terms, abbreviations and symbols.

pg_2287.label: Encourage use of simplified technical vocabularies and icons, with adequate-quality photographs/drawings and translations into an agreed number of languages.

pg_2288.label: Have a relevant authority verify documentation compliance at design/approval/acceptance stage and audit continued compliance thereafter.

pg_2289.label: Control produced documents and notify manufacturers of through-life operational changes (e.g. change of ownership, crew nationality).

pg_2290.label: Provide a single manual covering the entire integrated system where such systems are fitted, with attention to Failure Mode Effect Analysis.

pg_2291.label: Amend training regimes to ensure seafarer familiarity with standardized manuals.

pg_2292.label: Ensure up-to-date, accurate, user-friendly technical operating and maintenance manuals are available on board for all equipment, especially safety-critical marine equipment.

pg_2293.label: Use IACS Recommendation No.71 (Guide for the development of shipboard technical manuals) as a model when developing manuals.

pg_2294.label: Provide manuals in the ship's working language, or in English, French, or Spanish if the working language is not one of these.

pg_2295.label: Encourage ship designers/shipbuilders to supply diagrams and drawings explaining integrated ship system operation, including emergency operation.

pg_2296.label: Enforce manual availability and quality via ISM Code implementation and enforcement mechanisms.

pg_2297.label: Demand in purchase orders that supporting documentation be provided in plain English before delivery is taken.

pg_2298.label: Require manufacturers to provide written procedures in plain English.

pg_2299.label: Ensure operation and maintenance manuals comply with IMO MSC.1/Circ.1253 and are included in the delivery specification.

pg_2300.label: Apply a Management of Change (MOC) process during any fleet addition or equipment change, including transfer of documentation.

pg_2301.label: Ensure all manuals reflect current needs for operation and maintenance of the ship and equipment.

pg_2302.label: Consult the Classification Society if deviation from equipment manufacturers' instructions is needed.

pg_2303.label: Consult seagoing staff for feedback prior to implementing significant changes.

pg_2304.label: Coxswain notifies supervisor immediately upon observing unsafe overside work without buoyancy aids

pg_2305.label: Port supervisor attends the quay and assesses the full situation, including crew out of view of the pilot cutter

pg_2306.label: Supervisor challenges the ship's officer and highlights the lack of buoyancy aids

pg_2307.label: Supply buoyancy aids (lifejackets) before allowing work to continue

pg_2308.label: Harbour staff encouraged to note safety concerns and intervene when necessary

pg_2309.label: Stop work overside immediately when there is a risk of personnel being washed off or injured by passing vessel wake.

pg_2310.label: Issue advice to harbour staff to maintain vigilance when patrolling and observing vessels in the harbour.

pg_2311.label: Conduct a risk assessment and implement a permit to work system before any overside work.

pg_2312.label: Ensure Charterer's QHSE policies are matched by an equivalent SMS on Owner/Master controlled ships in commercial pools.

pg_2313.label: Submit a report of the hazardous occurrence to CHIRP/Nautical Institute via the joint CHIRP-MARS programme.

pg_2314.label: CHIRP follows up directly with the ferry operator to investigate the report.

pg_2315.label: Ferry operator issues a fleet-wide memorandum reconfirming the requirement for officers to comply with standard safety announcement procedures.

pg_2316.label: Furl the headsail and resume motoring when fog suddenly descended.

pg_2317.label: Switch radar back on immediately upon entering fog.

pg_2318.label: Designate the yacht with the more reliable radar (CL) to lead, with the other vessel (D) keeping station astern and in VHF contact.

pg_2319.label: Maintain dual VHF watch on channel 6 (working) and channel 16 (distress/calling).

pg_2320.label: Assign a dedicated crew member to keep radar watch with the screen visible to helmsman and other crew.

pg_2321.label: Plot the concerning contact (3-4 miles, starboard bow) for approximately five minutes before acting.

pg_2322.label: Make a bold 90-degree alteration of course to starboard (from north to east) when risk of collision was judged to exist.

pg_2323.label: Determine by radar whether a close-quarters situation and/or risk of collision is developing.

pg_2324.label: Avoid altering course to port for a vessel forward of the beam (other than one being overtaken).

pg_2325.label: Avoid altering course towards a vessel abeam or abaft the beam.

pg_2326.label: Keep an active, continuous radar plot of all contacts (on paper or chinagraph) rather than relying on a quick glance.

pg_2327.label: Use north-up stabilised radar in preference to course-up/head-up mode.

pg_2328.label: Make proper, active use of available radar/AIS equipment regardless of its sophistication.

pg_2329.label: Maintain close visual, auditory, and radar watch at all times in restricted visibility.

pg_2330.label: Do not rely solely on AIS for situational awareness in restricted visibility.

pg_2331.label: Avoid altering course to port except for a vessel on the starboard quarter, and only after careful consideration of all other options.

pg_2332.label: Consider reducing speed or stopping as an alternative to altering course.

pg_2333.label: Make a large, decisive course alteration (e.g., 90 degrees) rather than a modest change.

pg_2334.label: Use own sound signals in fog despite doubts about their effectiveness, rather than conserving them indefinitely.

pg_2335.label: Use radar, not AIS, as the primary tool for collision avoidance and vessel plotting.

pg_2336.label: Remain aware that AIS signals may not be detected due to human error or equipment setup, especially Class B (recreational) transmissions by Class A (SOLAS) receivers.

pg_2337.label: Maintain situational awareness of bow wave risk from large vessels even after they ease off propulsion.

pg_2338.label: Review and maintain redundancy in the vessel's safety equipment inventory, e.g. carry a hand- or mouth-operated horn as backup.

pg_2339.label: Ensure safety boat crews receive appropriate training and certification (ideally RYA Powerboat Level 2 and RYA Safety Boat qualification) before taking up duties.

pg_2340.label: Provide crews with regular experience using safety boats, not just one-off certification.

pg_2642.label: Verify all torches onboard are intrinsically safe and approved by a competent authority; collect and custody any private torches with the chief officer until sign-off.

pg_2650.label: Put in place necessary protection against unauthorized use of machinery, tools and equipment.

pg_2660.label: Do not conduct unnecessary close-quarters high-speed passes for non-operational purposes (e.g. filming).

pg_2662.label: Reinforce company Safe Navigation policy with crews after such an event.

pg_2669.label: Use the ship's Safety Management System (SMS) to report the hazardous occurrence (e.g. a doubtful OOW) to the ship managers.

pg_2672.label: Avoid ill-advised use of painted 'snap back zones' during mooring operations.

pg_2679.label: Take independent avoiding action: turn 20 degrees to port and harden up the sails to pass astern of the ship.

pg_2680.label: Ensure full DP certificates are held for DP Class 2 & 3 vessels; limited certificates only used on DP Class 1 ships.

pg_2681.label: Clearly define DPO and OOW roles and responsibilities in the SMS as a bridge resource management issue.

pg_2682.label: Maintain master/OOW as the default responsible party for a safe navigational watch at all times.

pg_2683.label: Ensure charterer's representatives only advise and monitor, not directly instruct operational conduct.

pg_2684.label: Establish and apply a bridging document for significant projects and term charters.

pg_2685.label: Report hazardous incidents through the appropriate channel.

pg_2686.label: Empower the master to ensure the bridging document is complied with.

pg_2687.label: If company SMS cannot achieve this, use CHIRP for truly confidential reporting.

pg_2688.label: Refer to IMCA Information Note TCPC 12/04 and OGP431 for guidance on client representative and worksite roles.

pg_2689.label: Master retains overall responsibility for the vessel and safety of all persons on board at all times.

pg_2690.label: Agree day-to-day and watch-basis operations for the project beforehand, documented in a bridging document.

pg_2691.label: Treat any unsanctioned vessel/cargo operation instructed by non-crew personnel as a reportable hazardous occurrence.

pg_2692.label: Reject any charterer's representative request falling outside standard operating procedures or the supporting risk assessment, pending ship manager review.

pg_2694.label: Master exercises veto authority to stop any operation he judges compromises vessel safety, without question.

pg_2695.label: Charterer's representative must immediately support the master's veto without appearing critical.

pg_2696.label: Only allow client representatives to intervene directly when they witness an unsafe operation or act.

pg_2697.label: If experiencing intimidating behaviour onboard, reference available support material.

pg_2698.label: Consult the 'Guidelines to shipping companies' provided by the European Community Shipowners Associations and European Transport Workers Federation.

pg_2699.label: Access further material via the CHIRP website or accompanying video.

pg_2700.label: Verify interlock and safety device functionality after any modification to incinerator systems before returning it to service.

pg_2706.label: Ensure supervisor and personnel involved review the job hazard analysis together prior to starting the task.

pg_2707.label: Require crewmembers to wear life vest and safety harness as specified in the company risk assessment when working outside the rails.

pg_2708.label: Review past fatal accident lessons-learned reports (e.g., the 2010 gangway-handling fatality) with ship personnel.

pg_2714.label: Encourage crew to report defects, malfunctions, unsafe work practices, or substandard equipment conditions as 'learning events' rather than treating it as paperwork.

pg_2719.label: Only use portable lifting appliances that have been inspected, tested, and confirmed suitable for use.

pg_2723.label: Do not use any lifting appliance/equipment that has not been tested or inspected per the required schedule.

pg_2725.label: Ensure all portable lifting appliances have a stamped or attached permanent identification mark indicating suitability for the intended job.

pg_2726.label: Ensure all crewmembers involved are fully aware of these procedures.

pg_2728.label: Consult COSWP Chapter 21 (Provision and Care of Lifting Plant and Carrying out of Lifting Operations) for detailed guidance.

pg_2729.label: Remove all flooring from the freefall lifeboat.

pg_2733.label: Discuss the matter with the safety officer and deputy safety officer.

pg_2734.label: Obtain confirmation from ship managers that corrective actions were appropriate.

pg_2735.label: Institute a master-directed policy of checking for water accumulation during each weekly lifeboat inspection and removing it immediately if found.

pg_2736.label: Conduct weekly visual inspection of survival craft, rescue boats and launching appliances.

pg_2737.label: Do not chip corroded air bottles.

pg_2738.label: Land heavily corroded air bottles for overhaul/testing.

pg_2739.label: For light surface scale, use a wire brush and repaint.

pg_2740.label: Follow planned maintenance system (PMS) guidelines for the lifeboat release mechanism.

pg_2741.label: Ensure the simulation test procedure document is available on board.

pg_2742.label: Test/try out the release mechanism at least once a month.

pg_2743.label: Grease all touching/moving parts of the release system regularly.

pg_2744.label: After liferafts return from annual service, verify painters are attached to a strong point on the ship's construction suitable for automatic activation.

pg_2745.label: Discuss the issue with all crewmembers during a boat drill briefing.

pg_2746.label: Add liferaft painter/securing checks to weekly routine inspections.

pg_2747.label: Master to conduct a full briefing of the bridge team when the pilot arrives.

pg_2748.label: Conduct briefing prior to arrival and departure from a port.

pg_2749.label: Hold a debrief on completion of the pilotage/port operation.

pg_2750.label: Implement a Permit to Work system for cleaning of moving machinery tasks.

pg_2751.label: Implement a Lock Out/Tag Out (LOTO) system in conjunction with the Permit to Work.

pg_2752.label: Check the effectiveness of the Safety Management System (SMS) and related training.

pg_2753.label: Conduct a safety 'toolbox' meeting prior to the work to identify moving machinery hazards.

pg_2754.label: Carry out a job-specific Risk Assessment/Job Hazard Analysis for the task.

pg_2755.label: Stop the pump/machinery before performing cleaning work (hazard elimination).

pg_2756.label: Apply power isolation/lock-out as a second safety barrier prior to commencing cleaning work.

pg_2757.label: Have officers giving distances-off state only the distance, without additional commentary.

pg_2758.label: Do not require radio acknowledgment of every distance report.

pg_2759.label: Have officers and helmsman repeat orders positively and quietly, without triple repetition.

pg_2760.label: Verify electrician/ETO certification before authorizing electrical panel work.

pg_2761.label: Confirm checks on electrical work are driven by SMS procedures rather than ad hoc individual initiative.

pg_2762.label: Replace temporary paper notices with a physical engineering control, such as a multi-lock or 'Lock Out for Life' system on the panel casing.

pg_2763.label: Identify and list all enclosed spaces on board the vessel.

pg_2764.label: Produce and implement a written enclosed-space entry procedure.

pg_2765.label: Issue an entry permit via a permit-to-work system for every enclosed space entry.

pg_2766.label: Maintain an enclosed-space entry log for each entry event.

pg_2767.label: Conduct and document a Job Risk Assessment before entry.

pg_2768.label: Deliver onboard training to all crew on enclosed space hazards and procedures.

pg_2769.label: Instruct the Electrician (or responsible crew) to isolate power to the equipment before maintenance begins.

pg_2770.label: Post a 'DO NOT OPERATE' / warning notice tag at the control position/electrical panel.

pg_2771.label: Issue the relevant work permit before work commences.

pg_2772.label: Verify (inspect) that isolation and tagging instructions have actually been carried out before personnel begin work.

pg_2773.label: Use standardized company-issued laminated 'DO NOT OPERATE' tags (A5 size, 8 per vessel) for uniform implementation across the fleet.

pg_2774.label: Hold a toolbox safety meeting at the work site immediately before every work activity.

pg_2775.label: Include all personnel who will be involved in the work in the toolbox meeting.

pg_2776.label: Issue an entry permit and complete required safety checks before anyone enters the pump room.

pg_2777.label: Post a warning notice at the pump room entrance stating safe entry procedures.

pg_2778.label: Enforce the Company's work permit system for all pump room entries.

pg_2779.label: Test all waste oil incinerator alarms and trip devices per the monthly checklist.

pg_2780.label: Investigate root cause of the disconnected interlock.

pg_2781.label: Repair the interlock immediately and apply LOCTITE glue to the securing bolts.

pg_2782.label: Instruct the officer in charge and incinerator operator to check all safety devices on the incinerator before every operation.

pg_2787.label: Engine staff should keep both air bottles open, or be ready to quickly open the balancing valve.
