pg_2789.label: Avoid painting the fulcrum points and sliding/rolling surfaces of levers and handles.

pg_2790.label: Lubricate fulcrum and moving surfaces instead of painting them.

pg_2791.label: Improve crew knowledge and work standards/guidelines regarding maintenance of safety valve mechanisms.

pg_2792.label: Test the engine astern before entry into port.

pg_2793.label: Ensure the Engine Room completes pre-arrival/pre-departure checks and the Bridge confirms this.

pg_2794.label: Determine and record the volume of the air tanks and the capacity of the compressors.

pg_2795.label: Engineers must know the number of engine starts remaining.

pg_2796.label: Factor adequacy of starter air supply into the ship's design phase.

pg_2797.label: Instruct the Chief Officer to keep the hand pump stowed near the manifold during cargo operations.

pg_2798.label: Check the oil level of the hand pump regularly.

pg_2799.label: Train crew in operation of the hand pump.

pg_2800.label: Ensure deck officers are familiar with the operation of the hand pump for cargo control valves.

pg_2801.label: Include maintenance of the hand pump in the Planned Maintenance System (PMS).

pg_2802.label: Add regular practice in the use of the hand pump to the ship's drills programme.

pg_2803.label: After painting safety valve or similar items, check levers for smooth operation.

pg_2804.label: Remove any unidentified chemical/oil containers found in inappropriate locations.

pg_2805.label: Store all chemicals/oils in their designated locations with reference to the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS).

pg_2806.label: Ensure safety and protective equipment is available for immediate use wherever chemicals are stored.

pg_2807.label: Discuss the incident in a safety meeting with all crew.

pg_2808.label: Check that any MSDS sheet associated with stored chemicals is dated.

pg_2809.label: Immediately return the relay box switch to the 'On' position upon discovery.

pg_2810.label: Re-instruct the chief cook and electrical engineer on proper handling of the switch.

pg_2811.label: Electrical officer to check the switch status during daily rounds of the vessel.

pg_2812.label: If found off, enquire as to why and by whom before switching it back on.

pg_2813.label: Bring the matter to the attention of the master and chief engineer.

pg_2814.label: Ensure the SOLAS-compliant wet chemical fire suppression system over high-risk equipment (e.g. deep fat fryers) remains switched on at all times.

pg_2815.label: Master to address and correct any instance of the fire suppression system being switched off.

pg_2816.label: Train galley personnel on correct use of the waste grinder and garbage disposal procedures before accessing restricted waste disposal areas.

pg_2817.label: Improve supervision and ensure guidelines for machinery use and waste handling are followed.

pg_2818.label: Conduct an additional inspection with the bosun and chief officer.

pg_2819.label: Identify all anti-slip areas requiring marking.

pg_2820.label: Explain to the bosun and chief officer how anti-slip areas should be marked and painted.

pg_2821.label: Conduct crew familiarization training on the arrangement of MARPOL drain lines and correct valve settings.

pg_2823.label: Include Wilden pump line-up and remaining drain tank capacity in cargo planning.

pg_2824.label: Follow planned inspection and maintenance schedules for the suction well and remove meshes/clean wells before entering port.

pg_2825.label: Discuss drill failures at the after-drill meeting to identify corrective measures.

pg_2826.label: Structure operating and maintenance manuals to support ease of access and inference.

pg_2827.label: Apply rule-based design principles supported by research and theory when producing manuals.

pg_2828.label: Fit non-slip material covering on all steps.

pg_2829.label: Highlight top and bottom steps in yellow/white.

pg_2830.label: Discuss the resuscitation skills gap with crew immediately after the drill.

pg_2831.label: Conduct resuscitation training for crew members.

pg_2833.label: Ensure officers receive STCW-mandated resuscitation training and refresher training.

pg_2834.label: Submit safety-related report to CHIRP, noting industrial relations issues are not accepted.

pg_2835.label: Indicate whether CHIRP may contact the owner/manager of another vessel regarding non-compliance, or withhold permission.

pg_2836.label: Indicate whether the report may be published in Maritime Feedback, or withhold permission.

pg_2837.label: Alter course to port to open distance from the give-way vessel.

pg_2838.label: Place engine astern to reduce speed and allow the other vessel to pass ahead.

pg_2839.label: Embed a commitment to safety as a value shaping decision-making at every level ashore and at sea.

pg_2840.label: Proactively encourage near-miss and hazardous occurrence reporting rather than only reacting after injury or asset damage.

pg_2841.label: Account for fatigue minimisation when determining manning levels, recognising the Safe Manning Document minimum may be insufficient during high workload periods.

pg_2842.label: Report fatigue or safety concerns confidentially to CHIRP if no response is received from company managers.

pg_2843.label: Proceed at safe speed in a crossing/close-quarters situation.

pg_2844.label: As the give-way vessel, take action and avoid crossing ahead of the other vessel in a crossing situation, even if a VHF agreement has been reached.

pg_2845.label: If the other vessel does not consent or act, reduce speed and alter course to pass astern instead of ahead.

pg_2846.label: Organize training with the OOW to study and fully comply with COLREG.

pg_2847.label: Use true vector radar output to monitor anchored vessels for nil vectors (confirming they are stopped).

pg_2848.label: Set radar trails to detect the first signs of a vessel beginning to move within the anchorage.

pg_2849.label: Approach the anchorage via a longer route, parallel to anchored vessels, to stem current/wind/tide.

pg_2850.label: Exit the anchorage parallel to and ahead of anchored vessels until well clear.

pg_2851.label: Keep courses parallel, not converging, with other vessels moving within the anchorage.

pg_2852.label: Follow the golden rule of never passing ahead of an anchored vessel.

pg_2853.label: Attempt to signal the overtaking vessel via Aldis lamp and VHF when it closes to within about 1nm.

pg_2854.label: If no response or course alteration is received and CPA remains dangerously low, take independent avoiding action (e.g. alter course to starboard) despite being the stand-on vessel.

pg_2855.label: Record/document the incident, including screenshots of radar/AIS data.

pg_2856.label: Third-party ship managers worked with current officers after the overtaking incident.

pg_2857.label: Report the RIB accident to the Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) as required.

pg_2858.label: Replace RIBs, improve aft seat securing measures, and issue automatic inflatable lifejackets instead of manual ones.

pg_2859.label: Ensure management clearly communicates all safety precautions to employees before taking to the water.

pg_2860.label: Monitor the other vessel visually and via AIS to track CPA/TCPA as it closes.

pg_2861.label: Make an early alteration of course to starboard.

pg_2862.label: Reassess options when initial alteration fails, avoiding a port alteration (risk if ferry turns starboard) or further starboard turn (would put yacht in ferry's path).

pg_2863.label: Apply full throttle and cross ahead of the ferry's bow, then alter to port once clear.

pg_2864.label: As soon as it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action, take your own action under Rule 17(a)(ii).

pg_2865.label: If collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel alone, take the best action possible under Rule 17(b), executed in time.

pg_2866.label: Do not alter course to port in a crossing situation under Rule 17(c); instead use a round turn to starboard.

pg_2867.label: Assess the 'big picture', including third and fourth vessels in proximity, by mentally placing yourself in the position of other ships.

pg_2868.label: Sound the horn and flash lights at the other vessel per Rule 34(d).

pg_2869.label: Recognize that yachts often do not appear on radar beyond about 5 miles due to GRP hull radar wave behaviour, shallow beam angle, wave interception, and inverse-square signal loss.

pg_2870.label: Do not rely solely on radar reflectors for detection enhancement.

pg_2871.label: Understand that even at closer range a yacht may be hard to detect on radar due to wave clutter.

pg_2872.label: Install an AIS transponder (or a transponder incorporating a receiver) on the yacht, even at additional cost.

pg_2873.label: If battery power for AIS is a concern, run the engine to keep batteries charged.

pg_2874.label: Report failures of proper lookout and VHF Channel 16 listening watch to the Flag State authority when a vessel/company fails to respond to a hazardous incident report.

pg_2875.label: Think twice before calling the other vessel on VHF when risk of collision exists

pg_2876.label: Master of Vessel 'A' reduced speed slightly under Rule 8(e) to gain more time to assess the situation.

pg_2877.label: Master of Vessel 'A' contacted OOW of Vessel 'B' via VHF to clarify intentions.

pg_2878.label: Master of Vessel 'A' asserted that Vessel 'B' should comply with COLREGs Rule 15.

pg_2879.label: Master of Vessel 'A' attempted to re-contact Vessel 'B' on VHF after no acknowledgement.

pg_2880.label: Company instructed Master to refresh COLREGs training (especially Rule 15) with all deck officers.

pg_2882.label: Hold extraordinary Safety Committee meeting with all deck officers to discuss the case.

pg_2883.label: Arrange for Company Port Captain to attend the vessel at next port and debrief officers at sign-off.

pg_2884.label: Use the Bridge Navigational Watch Alarm System (BNWAS) while at anchor, if available.

pg_2885.label: Follow clear standing instructions for calling the Master in good time, tailored to the specific anchorage.

pg_2886.label: VLCC master refused to deviate from course when first contacted by the overtaking container ship via VHF, citing deep draught status.

pg_2887.label: VLCC master advised the container ship via VHF that its 13m draught meant it should not be using the Deep Water Route and should transit south and east of Sandettie instead.

pg_2888.label: VLCC master warned the container ship against overtaking within the DWR, noting another deep-draught vessel was also using the route.

pg_2889.label: VLCC began an early alteration into the DW route to create additional sea room as the container ship passed close on her port side.

pg_2890.label: Take collision-avoidance action that is positive and made in ample time, in accordance with Rule 8, whenever circumstances permit.

pg_2891.label: When overtaking a large vessel such as a VLCC, pass on her starboard side to allow a planned course alteration to starboard, or alternatively slow down until ample room is available.

pg_2892.label: Continuously assess whether an alteration made by the other ship is sufficient to produce a safe CPA, and be prepared to act further if in doubt.

pg_2893.label: Apply good seamanship alongside strict Rule compliance when deciding on avoiding action.

pg_2894.label: Before closing with another vessel, assess whether your own intentions are completely obvious to the other ship.

pg_2895.label: Take actions that are positive and made in ample time when in a closing situation.

pg_2896.label: As the overtaking vessel, keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken until finally past and clear, and do not overtake if there is insufficient sea room.

pg_2897.label: Account for interaction effects (hydrodynamic) when passing close to another large vessel, especially in constrained depth of water.

pg_2898.label: Ensure the passage plan conforms to local routeing and manoeuvring guidance (e.g. Deep Water Route rules) with alternatives available.

pg_2899.label: Plan the TSS arrival in advance: timing, bridge manning, and Master's presence on the bridge.

pg_2900.label: Treat the passage plan as a basis for change, not a rule to follow regardless of real-time circumstances.

pg_2901.label: Begin planning how to slot into traffic flow from at least 10 nautical miles out when approaching or navigating a TSS.

pg_2902.label: Slow down if in doubt, bearing in mind the vessel astern.

pg_2903.label: Do not overtake unless there is ample time to CPA and sufficient space within the safe straight part of the TSS.

pg_2904.label: Overtake only on the starboard side of the vessel being overtaken where possible.

pg_2905.label: Masters should issue clear order book or verbal instructions on expectations for speed/course alterations, overtaking, and traffic density handling.

pg_2906.label: Maintain visual lookout (look up and out) and use electronic aids as a supplement, not a sole dependency.

pg_2907.label: Consider the situation from the other ship's point of view.

pg_2908.label: Engage hand steering and activate the second steering motor in preparation for evasive action

pg_2909.label: Plan crossing manoeuvres of a TSS at locations where a higher than average number of other crossing vessels is not expected (e.g. avoid known ferry crossing points)

pg_2910.label: Continuously plot the position, course and speed of all vessels in the TSS, including those in the opposite lane.

pg_2911.label: Detect course or speed changes of other vessels immediately.

pg_2912.label: Take early collision-avoidance action rather than attempting VHF communication with the other vessel.

pg_2913.label: Maintain constant vigilance even in familiar or busy TSS areas.

pg_2914.label: Account for the limited manoeuvrability of large vessels such as VLCCs when assessing risk and timing of action.

pg_2915.label: Identify and mark a 'crossing window' on the chart in advance.

pg_2916.label: Plan in advance when and under what circumstances the Master needs to be on the bridge.

pg_2917.label: Assess traffic in the lanes well ahead and choose a moment to cross where a gap is likely or where only one crossing situation arises at a time.

pg_2918.label: Use the Mark 1 eyeball combined with compass bearing assessments (using azimuth rings if fitted).

pg_2919.label: Use ARPA trial manoeuvre to decide the moment of turn.

pg_2920.label: Use relative tails on radar to quickly confirm new CPAs after the turn.

pg_2921.label: Use AIS to monitor other ships' course changes and track data for destination/intention assessment.

pg_2922.label: Brief and motivate lookouts; bring an additional officer to the bridge if in doubt.

pg_2923.label: Do not approach dead astern when overtaking another vessel.

pg_2924.label: Make intentions clear in plenty of time and avoid introducing doubt.

pg_2926.label: Keep a good lookout all round, including astern, and be aware of blind arcs.

pg_2927.label: Monitor all vessels, especially those with unclear intentions.

pg_2928.label: Act early in unexpected circumstances or worsening conditions.

pg_2929.label: If urgent/emergency action is needed, stay calm, follow drills, and apply safety procedures deliberately.

pg_2930.label: Promote and maintain a positive safety culture from leadership down.

pg_2931.label: When assessing CPA, visualise the consequence of a machinery or steering breakdown on either vessel.

pg_2932.label: Stay alert for converging traffic near common waypoints or shipping concentration points.

pg_2933.label: Do not rely solely on bridge electronics for CPA assessment; cross-check with visual assessment.

pg_2934.label: Act on the first instinct that an anchorage or situation is becoming untenable, rather than delaying.

pg_2935.label: Shift berth or take precautionary action early in worsening weather rather than waiting until forced to act urgently.

pg_2936.label: Establish a formal procedure for crew boarding tenders/small craft, including mandatory lifejacket use.

pg_2937.label: Don a lifejacket before boarding a tender or small craft in a seamanship evolution.

pg_2938.label: Crew members must challenge and correct missing PPE immediately, even after tasking has begun.

pg_2939.label: An overtaking (burdened) vessel must make her intentions to keep out of the way clearly known.

pg_2940.label: Maintain a genuinely safe passing distance when overtaking, beyond the minimum required by Rule 13.

pg_2941.label: Cut and inspect pipes/nozzles during unrelated maintenance work to check system integrity

pg_2943.label: Re-route nozzles and pipe-work (like for like) for easier future inspection access

pg_2945.label: Replace original globe valves with stainless steel ball valves on the fire main branch

pg_2946.label: Fit stub pipes with an additional ball valve immediately after the isolating ball valves on each line

pg_2947.label: Pause and assess risk before undertaking urgent repair work, even under time pressure.

pg_2948.label: Apply the ship's permission-to-work and Working at Height procedures before sending a crewman over the side.

pg_2949.label: Ensure the bridge is informed and tracks exactly when the man is over the side and when he is back inboard.

pg_2950.label: Maintain safety standards routinely, not just under pressure.

pg_2951.label: Report near-misses and unsafe practices observed, as the tug crew did.

pg_2952.label: Check for water leaking past the isolating valves.

pg_2953.label: Connect an air hose and blow air up through the supply lines and nozzles to prove them clear.

pg_2954.label: Enter this check into the Planned Maintenance System as a routine (probably monthly) job.

pg_2955.label: Fit plugs in the ball valve outlets whenever not in use.

pg_2956.label: Fit clear signage on the valves indicating their purpose.

pg_2957.label: Stop entry immediately once a procedural miss regarding enclosed space entry is noticed.

pg_2958.label: Submit a near-miss report promptly when the issue is brought to the Master's attention.

pg_2959.label: Conduct further training for all deck and engine officers and crew on enclosed space entry.

pg_2960.label: Develop an eLearning course to enhance enclosed space entry training package.

pg_2961.label: Adjust shipboard procedures to align with updated COSWP requirements.

pg_2962.label: Initiate corrective action when design shortfalls are identified, including redesign, material selection changes, avoidance of water traps (u-bends), and improved testing techniques.

pg_2963.label: Check similar installations on other ships for the same design shortfall.

pg_2964.label: Ensure regular and reliable inspections are followed, including for equipment that is 'out of sight, out of mind'.

pg_2965.label: Invest in maintenance of emergency gear of all kinds, including firefighting equipment.

pg_2966.label: Conduct enclosed space entry and rescue drills bi-monthly.

pg_2967.label: Fit remote testing equipment onboard ships.

pg_2968.label: Know the equipment and observe available guidelines for transfer operations.

pg_2969.label: Pay attention and keep alert during all transfer activities, both those transferring and those supervising.

pg_2970.label: Do not transfer, or allow transfer, unless it looks and feels right; intervene if needed.

pg_2971.label: Treat any ambiguous space as enclosed if in doubt.

pg_2972.label: Maintain Safe Systems of Work, Permits to Work, risk assessments, and regular emergency drills for confined space entry and rescue.

pg_2973.label: Conduct departmental briefings/debriefings and lead by example to build a robust safety culture.

pg_2974.label: Immediately inform the pilot of any engine failure or non-response to an order.

pg_2975.label: Use thrusters and sufficient tugboat assistance as standard procedure when proceeding at low speed in narrow waters.

pg_2976.label: If deceleration fails, take emergency action such as laying the vessel against fenders to use friction as a brake.

pg_2977.label: Ensure clear bridge communication and conning position layout for manoeuvring in confined waters.

pg_2978.label: Vessel management to review the incident and implement a reactive health and safety process.

pg_2979.label: Develop a comprehensive drill for dealing with fouled anchors.

pg_2980.label: Conduct a thorough master-pilot information exchange covering procedure, sequence of events, engine control and limitations, the overall plan, recent defects, and contingency actions.

pg_2981.label: Perform timely pre-arrival checks, including control position changeovers and machinery control checks.

pg_2982.label: Define the aim and assess how necessary its achievement is.

pg_2983.label: Identify hazards and assess likelihood and severity of potential harm.

pg_2985.label: Determine how the task may be done to minimise risk.

pg_2986.label: Determine how unavoidable residual risk may be mitigated.

pg_2987.label: Ensure preparedness in the event of harm.

pg_2988.label: Pause and reconsider necessity again before acting.

pg_2989.label: Conduct a risk assessment and briefing before taking action in unusual circumstances, using a checklist even if brief.

pg_2990.label: Conduct an operational risk assessment, even if abbreviated, against a checklist before attempting to clear a fouled anchor.

pg_2991.label: Deploy a rescue boat with all crew wearing life jackets.

pg_2992.label: Station two crew members at the bow to operate the anchor winch and observe the boat.

pg_2993.label: Maintain VHF communications between boat, bow, and bridge.

pg_2994.label: Have one tender crewman work to release the fouled line while confirming it is not electrical, while the other crewman manoeuvres the boat.

pg_2995.label: If release is unsuccessful, recover boat and crew, let the anchor go again, and seek commercial diver assistance.

pg_2996.label: Refuse unlawful orders to dump oily waste, machinery, or oil drums overboard even if financial recompense is offered.

pg_2997.label: Report concerns to authorities at the next port of call if crew are directed to dump waste illegally.

pg_2998.label: Exercise heightened vigilance and proper collision-avoidance practice when overtaking or crossing within a TSS.

pg_2999.label: Incorporate avoidance of overtaking in constrained TSS sections or near corners into passage planning.

pg_3000.label: Maintain active lookout and anticipate traffic ahead ('look and think ahead').

pg_3001.label: Ensure vessels keep clear of the separation line and follow the general direction of traffic flow when navigating a TSS.

pg_3002.label: Assess berth suitability and snapback hazard zones before positioning crew to tend mooring lines during close-quarters departures.

pg_3003.label: Attempt to contact the errant vessel on the designated VTS/sector working channel (VHF60).

pg_3004.label: If no response, escalate to VTS/port approach on VHF16 to intervene and instruct the vessel to monitor the correct sector channel.

pg_3005.label: Maintain situational awareness of all three vessels (own ship, opposite-lane ship, overtaking ship) and monitor CPA continuously.

pg_3006.label: Hold course within the lane as far as sea room allows despite being constrained to starboard by a navigational buoy.

pg_3007.label: Make an independent avoiding action (360-degree turn to starboard) when the give-way vessel fails to alter course despite request.

pg_3008.label: Pass clear under the stern of the other vessel after taking avoiding action.

pg_3009.label: Avoid positioning crew within the after mooring station's snap-back zone during periods of surge loading.

pg_3010.label: Employ available mooring bollards rather than relying solely on roller leads.

pg_3011.label: Monitor ARPA true vectors to assess CPA and crossing-ahead distance in a developing crossing situation.

pg_3012.label: Establish VHF communication promptly to clarify the other vessel's intentions when CPA appears too small.

pg_3013.label: As Master, exercise professional judgement on whether to stand on or alter course based on observed CPA, vessel conditions, and COLREG obligations.

pg_3014.label: As Master, refuse a berth considered unsafe for the vessel's size based on observation and professional judgement.

pg_3015.label: Free twisted anchor chain links using a chain hook.

pg_3016.label: Update the vessel's list of spaces to be inspected to include the cofferdam adjacent to fuel tanks.

pg_3017.label: Order replacement D shackles with security pins for enclosed space evacuation stretchers.

pg_3018.label: Order a replacement magnetron for the X-band radar.

pg_3019.label: Rectify all noted bridge defects (wing repeater illumination, water ingress in navigation consoles, speed log interruptions) through remedial maintenance.

pg_3020.label: Give-way vessel must act to give way even if it believes the proposed CPA is safe.

pg_3021.label: Think from the point of view of the other ship, especially if she is larger or more burdened.

pg_3022.label: Consider how the position would look in the event of a machinery or steering gear breakdown, and factor in stopping distances.

pg_3023.label: Stand-on vessel may raise concern and take action when it perceives a risk of collision.

pg_3024.label: Identify and mark alternative 'tension spots' on the mooring deck as relatively safe standing/operating points.

pg_3025.label: Forbid roaming and unauthorised movement on working decks during mooring operations.

pg_3026.label: Fully comply with the ISGOTT ship/shore safety checklist, including any required repeat checks.

pg_3027.label: Conduct thorough cargo planning and ensure all personnel understand the planned operation.

pg_3028.label: Check procedures for any valve manipulation prior to operation.

pg_3029.label: Have a responsible officer double check cargo valve settings before starting or restarting cargo operations.

pg_3030.label: Treat any doubt about risk of collision as risk existing (COLREG Rule 7).

pg_3031.label: As stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, consider slowing down rather than altering course to port.

pg_3032.label: Only alter course to port once the other vessel has crossed the bow and the crossing situation no longer exists.

pg_3033.label: Use a 360° turn to starboard only as a last-resort action.

pg_3034.label: Exercise caution and maintain an alert all-round lookout before and during a 360° turn.

pg_3035.label: Establish a dedicated fire watch before and during all hot work operations, whether conducted by ship's staff or repair yard personnel.

pg_3036.label: Clear combustible debris and rubbish from the vicinity of hot work before starting.

pg_3037.label: Ensure adequate curing/drying time between successive paint applications and avoid excessive buildup of paint layers.

pg_3038.label: Verify appropriate firefighting equipment is available and suitable for the type of fire expected during hot work.

pg_3039.label: Verify correct cargo line-up before and during tank changeover and discharge operations

pg_3040.label: Maintain reliable ship/shore communication throughout cargo operations, especially during topping-off

pg_3041.label: Ensure adequate supervision during changeover of cargo tanks and restart of operations after a stoppage

pg_3042.label: Manifold watch to immediately report any change of flow or pressure increase to the Cargo Control Room

pg_3043.label: OOW to suspend discharge immediately upon noting abnormal pressure increase

pg_3044.label: Treat partially open spaces as potentially dangerous and include them on the enclosed space list

pg_3045.label: Mouse stretcher shackles as an alternative to using a split pin

pg_3046.label: Check radar magnetron performance at regular intervals and schedule replacement in the planned maintenance system

pg_3047.label: As give-way vessel, alter course if the stand-on vessel expresses concern about risk of collision

pg_3048.label: Continuously practice 'what-ifing' scenarios (e.g., steering gear failure)

pg_3049.label: Conduct thorough, unpredictable inspections and encourage crew alertness at all levels

pg_3050.label: Ensure emergency/life-saving equipment (e.g., lifeboats) is maintained and tested so it is operable when needed.

pg_3051.label: Remain continuously alert to unexpected signs (noise, movement, smell, heat, water) during normal operations.

pg_3053.label: Keep suitable fire extinguishers to hand during hot work.

pg_3054.label: Visit all adjacent compartments on completion of hot work.

pg_3055.label: Conduct frequent checks for at least 2 hours after completion of hot work.

pg_3056.label: Issue and complete a hot work permit to work before any hot work begins.

pg_3057.label: Verify training for personnel conducting hot work is completed and in date.

pg_3058.label: Clear the hot work area of combustible materials, including old paint, rubbish, and solvents.

pg_3059.label: Post a dedicated fire watch with fire extinguishers readily available during and after hot work.

pg_3060.label: Consult product data sheets and makers' advice on paint/solvent flammability before working near painted surfaces.

pg_3061.label: Include galleys and similar high-risk areas in routine day and night rounds.

pg_3062.label: Take early and substantial avoiding action (slow down, alter course to starboard/head to wind, illuminate sail with a torch).

pg_3063.label: Never conduct hot work without leadership/management knowledge and a comprehensive check-off list (e.g., UKCOSWP 2015).

pg_3064.label: Switch off galley power at end of use, when unattended, and at end of each working day; fit external galley power breakers.

pg_3065.label: Rely on COLREGS rules for collision avoidance rather than ad-hoc VHF 'arrangements' between vessels.

pg_3066.label: Take early, positive and ample avoiding action as soon as it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not complying with COLREGS.

pg_3067.label: Small craft such as yachts should keep engines available for maneuvering, especially in light winds at known dangerous crossing points.

pg_3068.label: Bridge watchkeepers on larger vessels should account for the poor detectability of yachts (weak radar returns, dim/intermittent lights) when assessing risk at range.

pg_3069.label: Base collision avoidance decisions primarily on visual observation and/or radar information.

pg_3070.label: Apply the COLREGS instinctively as the primary basis for bridge watchkeeping decisions.

pg_3071.label: Avoid spending time attempting VHF communication during a developing close-quarters situation.

pg_3072.label: If VHF is used for deconfliction, do not assume the other vessel has taken the 'arranged' action until it is independently verified as happening.

pg_3073.label: Maintain an alert visual lookout at all times, not relying on AIS or instrument displays alone.

pg_3074.label: Base collision avoidance decisions primarily on visual and/or radar information, not AIS.

pg_3075.label: If using VHF radio as a collision avoidance aid, keep the provisions of the COLREGs uppermost.

pg_3076.label: Yacht skippers should fit high-power (e.g. LED) navigation lighting conforming to COLREG stipulations, and consider burning normal navigation lights instead of a masthead tricolour.

pg_3077.label: Yachts should consider fitting an active (transmit and receive) AIS system, especially in busy shipping areas.

pg_3078.label: If illuminating a sail, continue doing so for an extended period where possible.

pg_3079.label: Yachts should consider fitting active radar reflectors rather than relying on passive ones.

pg_3080.label: Take positive and ample action in good time to avoid collision in accordance with the COLREGs once risk becomes obvious.

pg_3081.label: When the other ship alters to port at just under a mile giving only a 3-cable CPA, slow down and alter course to starboard.

pg_3082.label: Pass under the stern of the vessel being slowly overtaken on the starboard side.

pg_3083.label: Plan well ahead and maintain a complete all-round lookout when approaching a TSS.

pg_3084.label: If overtaking, complete the manoeuvre as quickly as possible.

pg_3085.label: If sea room is at a premium, slow down and do not overtake; consider slotting in astern instead.

pg_3086.label: Apply the COLREGS instinctively and take early and substantial action when circumstances require, rather than relying on give-way vessels to act correctly.

pg_3087.label: Use VHF in collision avoidance only in exceptional situations and with utmost caution.

pg_3088.label: Verify chart identity, source and date against the ship's provider when discrepancies are found during passage planning.

pg_3089.label: Use only IMO-approved ECDIS, not unlicensed Electronic Chart Systems (ECS).

pg_3090.label: Ensure navigators and Masters receive high-quality ECDIS training meeting IMO model course requirements.

pg_3091.label: Conduct structured familiarisation with each specific ECDIS system's capabilities and limitations before relying on it.

pg_3092.label: Correctly apply safety depths, safety contours, and alarms, and accurately input vessel data including draught.

pg_3093.label: Use automatic route check facilities during passage planning.

pg_3094.label: Verify charts are up to date via proper automatic or manual correction procedures.

pg_3095.label: Carry out passage planning on charts at scales allowing identification of necessary detail.

pg_3096.label: When encountering a close-quarters situation, consider giving more sea room and/or decelerating.

pg_3097.label: Conduct final visual checks along the whole track before the voyage, looking for obstructions, shallows, and traffic management systems.

pg_3098.label: Conduct broader checks along the track for high shipping density or strong tidal streams.

pg_3099.label: Brief the whole passage plan to the bridge team.

pg_3100.label: Apply the APEM/APREM model (Appraisal, Planning, Execution, Monitoring, Review) per IMO Res A.893(21) and NP232 ECDIS guidance.

pg_3101.label: Ensure both the Planning Station and ECDIS are updated to the latest chart catalogue and ENC updates during the appraisal phase.

pg_3102.label: Read UKHO Notices to Mariners, SCA navigation circulars, and NtM Section VIII for withdrawn/cancelled ENCs.

pg_3103.label: Order and carry Egyptian-issued paper charts for the Suez Canal regardless of digital navigation capability.

pg_3104.label: Avoid using too small a chart scale during active navigation and pilotage.

pg_3105.label: Practise plotting visual and radar fixes on ECDIS in benign conditions.

pg_3106.label: Use each piece of navigation equipment only for the role it is designed for (e.g., do not use an ECDIS/AIS overlay for collision avoidance).

pg_3107.label: Cross-check depth, chart data, ECDIS position, radar information and the ship's estimated position against each other.

pg_3108.label: If information sources disagree, slow down, stop, or re-check as appropriate to clarify the discrepancy.

pg_3109.label: Train, familiarise, and practice with all bridge equipment, including understanding that ECDIS can be used like paper charts without GPS input if necessary.

pg_3110.label: Maintain a healthy instinct to crosscheck automated displays rather than trusting them unquestioningly.

pg_3111.label: Physically check valves reported or assumed 'shut', including testing handle/gearbox integrity, not just visual lashing indication.

pg_3112.label: Replace the necessary components once the concealed defect and blanks were discovered.

pg_3113.label: Fit bulldog grips correctly and inspect lashings for wear and tear.

pg_3114.label: Properly stow and secure gas cylinders (oxygen/acetylene).

pg_3115.label: Remove securing turnbuckles only as per procedure before heaving crane boom from rest stand.

pg_3116.label: Conduct a risk assessment, issue an electrical permit to work, isolate equipment by tagging/locking out, hold a toolbox talk, and ensure proper supervision before electrical work.

pg_3117.label: Periodically inspect electrical cables beyond routine planned maintenance of generators.

pg_3118.label: Identify and colour-code all ventilation fans and flaps, and keep emergency exit doors unobstructed.

pg_3119.label: Maintain frequent, open ship/shore communication between office superintendents and the vessel.

pg_3120.label: Hold a daily job/toolbox meeting before maintenance work on electrical panels.

pg_3121.label: Wear insulated rubber gloves when working near live electrical equipment.

pg_3122.label: Use non-conductive tools (not metallic brushes) near live electrical components.

pg_3123.label: After finding damaged cable insulation on one generator, inspect all other generators for similar cable damage.

pg_3124.label: Conduct routine inspections of valves and lashings.

pg_3125.label: Evacuate the engine room immediately upon CO2 high pressure alarm activation and visible gas release.

pg_3126.label: Investigate the CO2 room to identify the cause of the release.

pg_3127.label: Depressurise the system before manually closing the pilot operated section valve.

pg_3128.label: Carry out routine checks before, during, and on completion of any job.

pg_3129.label: Plan, supervise, and properly signal all lifting operations using the ship's crane.

pg_3130.label: Secure all equipment, especially before heavy weather.

pg_3131.label: Provide and ensure use of face shields, aprons, and gloves at chemical lockers.

pg_3132.label: Plan and discuss all jobs, routine or otherwise, in advance via toolbox talks.

pg_3133.label: View worksites in advance to identify hazards.

pg_3135.label: Inspect control valves of pilot cylinders during annual service and pressure test ball valves; blow through pilot lines.

pg_3136.label: Rectify and record any material defect (e.g. missing valve) immediately, including ordering replacement parts and documenting the reason for temporary fixes such as blanks.

pg_3137.label: Discuss outstanding defects and temporary repairs with the company office and at ship staff handover.

pg_3138.label: Treat escape from an elevator as a measure of last resort, only in a genuine emergency.

pg_3139.label: Lock out all deck access points when an elevator is out of service, and maintain taut use/maintenance procedures.

pg_3140.label: Wear facemask and rubber gloves when cleaning equipment (e.g. fresh water generator) with chemicals.

pg_3142.label: Develop and make available pre-planned responses and actions for every alarm activation.

pg_3143.label: Conduct routine tests of alarms, including checks of settings and thresholds.

pg_3144.label: Apply the permit to work system and isolation procedures rigorously, including 'do not operate' notices.

pg_3145.label: Ensure effective information exchange within spaces, especially engineering spaces, at handover or after maintenance.

pg_3146.label: Ensure gauges and components fitted meet correct specification.

pg_3147.label: Record oil residue tank level measurements during routine checks, not just observe them.

pg_3148.label: Post warning signs on stopped pumps/closed valves awaiting repair.

pg_3149.label: Replace damaged pressure gauges only with units of the correct specification matching maximum line pressure.

pg_3150.label: Design and follow robust, comprehensive planned maintenance systems that account for heat, humidity and time-related degradation.

pg_3151.label: Verify manufacturer's locking pins are removed from CO2 systems before they are relied upon.

pg_3152.label: Use only manufacturer-approved components on compressors and air bottle connections.

pg_3153.label: Refer to and apply COSWP sections 18.25.1 and 18.25.2 for handling high-pressure equipment.

pg_3154.label: Segregate oxygen and acetylene cylinders in separate cages.

pg_3155.label: Lock cylinder cages for security, keeping keys accessible locally in a break-glass box.

pg_3156.label: Segregate gas stores by gas type and cylinder size, and ensure screwed cap colour codes match the cylinder colour code.

pg_3157.label: Place cylinders on wood, not directly on steel deck, and individually secure them with a quick-release mechanism.

pg_3158.label: Maintain a bulkhead or three-metre separation between oxygen and acetylene cylinder cages, with 'Danger – No Smoking' signage.

pg_3159.label: Consult COSWP Chapter 24.8 if uncertain about cylinder handling or storage.

pg_3160.label: Do not use improvised or fabricated lifting tools (e.g., a U-clamp welded to a cylinder cap) to lift gas cylinders on board.

pg_3161.label: Attempt to clear blockage using air first.

pg_3162.label: Fill the pipe with water to check if it is clear.

pg_3163.label: Apply heat to the pipe to clear the blockage.

pg_3164.label: Stand clear of the pipe outlet when heating a blocked, water-filled pipe.

pg_3165.label: Confirm that all unions/adapters between BA compressors and air bottles are the correct design as specified in the onboard instruction manual.

pg_3166.label: If the instruction manual is unclear on correct fittings, consult the ship's manager.

pg_3167.label: Apply additional control measures, such as securing a length of cordage tie-wrapped around the hose, where deemed necessary.

pg_3168.label: Review and strengthen planned maintenance instructions so inspections involve thorough checks rather than a simple 'tick the box' task.

pg_3169.label: Ensure shore-based management and manufacturers commit to detailed, effective Planned Maintenance System requirements.

pg_3170.label: Hold a toolbox talk to identify hazards associated with the job.

pg_3171.label: Refer identified hazards to a competent person for formal risk assessment if needed.

pg_3172.label: Maintain 'Green' status if no changes occur to the planned work.

pg_3173.label: Move to 'Yellow' status and stop to think if one item changes.

pg_3174.label: Move to 'Red' status and stop work entirely if a second item changes.

pg_3175.label: Mitigate walkway hazards by fitting a grated walkway over pipework post-build.

pg_3176.label: Ensure all shipboard locations meet the stipulated minimum head clearance of 2.1 metres.

pg_3177.label: Use the approved dedicated trolley for moving single oxy-acetylene cylinders; stop use of homemade lifting tools.

pg_3178.label: Brief all personnel on the hazards of pipe-clearing tasks and keep clear of both openings of a choked pipe.

pg_3179.label: Conduct a toolbox meeting using brainstorming for hazard identification before undertaking any task.

pg_3180.label: If the first corrective plan fails, hold a second toolbox talk incorporating a new risk assessment.

pg_3181.label: Design toolbox talk forms to prompt discussion on hazard sources (heat, pressure, moving/falling objects, electricity) without being prescriptive or filed as a tick-box exercise.

pg_3182.label: Reduce speed promptly to increase CPA/bow crossing range when unable to alter course.

pg_3183.label: Cross a TSS as close to right angles as possible, and shape up for crossing as soon as possible after leaving port.

pg_3184.label: Maintain a bow crossing distance (BCD) of no less than 1.5 miles when crossing ahead of another vessel, unless heavy traffic prevents it.

pg_3185.label: Consider the situation as perceived from the other vessel's bridge before deciding to pass ahead.

pg_3186.label: Call the other vessel by radio to identify own position and ask its intentions when CPA became unsafe.

pg_3187.label: Take independent avoiding action by starting the engine and turning hard to starboard, completing a 360-degree turn around the car carrier's stern.

pg_3188.label: Record the AIS track of the other vessel and file an incident report.

pg_3189.label: Maintain continuous lookout and monitor own and target vessel tracks (via AIS/radar).

pg_3190.label: Compare and record tracks (screenshots) of own and target vessel to assess closing situation.

pg_3191.label: Monitor anchor position and set anchor watch during cargo operations.

pg_3192.label: Maintain a minimum CPA of 1.5 miles when crossing ahead of another vessel, especially a fast one.

pg_3193.label: Brief all crew on hazards of moving/automatically-starting parts before work begins.

pg_3194.label: Use a screwdriver or socket drive end instead of fingers to check belt tension or freedom of movement.

pg_3195.label: Isolate and tag out all equipment before personnel begin repair work.

pg_3196.label: Carry out a risk assessment and hold a toolbox talk discussing results and safety precautions with all involved.

pg_3197.label: Supervisor should step back and maintain oversight rather than directly performing the work.

pg_3198.label: Ensure good regular communication, suitable gloves, proper supervision, and a 'stop work authority' during machinery space activities.

pg_3199.label: Use a Permit to Work system to add controls preventing machinery operation without checks in place.

pg_3200.label: Maintain initial course rather than making late, unnecessary manoeuvres when another vessel's actions are uncertain.

pg_3201.label: Review the VDR of the incident in detail.

pg_3202.label: Consult the senior master to discuss the findings.

pg_3203.label: As stand-on vessel, maintain course and speed rather than altering to starboard into give-way action.

pg_3204.label: If a close-quarters situation must be resolved, consider passing astern of the other vessel instead of cutting across the TSS at an angle.

pg_3205.label: Apologise to the reporter and raise wider learnings with the bridge team.

pg_3206.label: Make contact with a vessel showing unclear intentions as early as possible, well before close quarters develop.

pg_3207.label: Use AIS transponders (e.g. on smaller craft like yachts) to improve detectability and situational awareness.

pg_3208.label: Employ 'Trial Manoeuvre' exercises when planning a TSS crossing.

pg_3209.label: Manage speed to avoid arriving too early for the pilot and entering a holding pattern.

pg_3210.label: Apply enhanced Bridge Resource Management during holding/waiting situations.

pg_3211.label: Use VDR data proactively to investigate incidents, follow up, and train crew.

pg_3212.label: Maintain a dedicated, effective anchor watch at all times, especially when other crew are distracted by unrelated issues.

pg_3213.label: Act immediately on radar anchor-watch alarms rather than merely acknowledging them.

pg_3214.label: Monitor VHF calls and sound signals from nearby vessels for warnings of dragging or close-quarters situations.

pg_3215.label: Request the vessel astern to move away when own ship cannot manoeuvre effectively due to engine problems.

pg_3216.label: Use the anchor(s) and main engine together to attempt to arrest unwanted movement.

pg_3217.label: Weigh anchors and manoeuvre with engine power once anchors fail to arrest the drag.

pg_3218.label: Maintain a proper anchor watch at all times while at anchorage.

pg_3219.label: Keep the main engine on immediate readiness in crowded anchorages or where dragging is possible due to bottom, current, or topography.

pg_3220.label: Conduct a thorough risk assessment before agreeing to immobilise engines, considering prevailing circumstances and vessels in the vicinity.

pg_3221.label: Respond promptly to bridge alarms and avoid distraction from cargo operations while at anchor.

pg_3222.label: Use the embarkation platform only in close collaboration between vessel and pilot boat depending on the individual situation.

pg_3223.label: Use a clearance table showing pilot door/platform height above waterline relative to vessel draught and communicate this precisely to the pilot boat.

pg_3224.label: Fit a removable handhold stanchion when the embarkation platform is folded away and not used.
