pg_3522.label: Verify VHF radio/handset functionality before critical communications during pilotage.

pg_3523.label: Ensure vessel speed is fully under control when approaching a berth.

pg_3524.label: Consider each instruction to a tug carefully before transmitting it.

pg_3525.label: Account for the tugmasters' view and their means of communication when giving orders.

pg_3526.label: Follow guidance in 'Standard Pilot Orders for Tugs' on intervals between pilot orders, especially with more than two tugs.

pg_3527.label: Clear away both anchors ready for use upon loss of propulsion.

pg_3528.label: Restart generators and restore electrical power and systems.

pg_3529.label: Test main engine and bow thruster after power restoration before proceeding.

pg_3530.label: Consult with the master and jointly agree to resume the approach.

pg_3531.label: Advise the pilot of the cause of the blackout.

pg_3532.label: Ensure adequate electrical power is available before standby, engaging additional generating plant as necessary prior to reaching the pilot boarding ground.

pg_3533.label: Clear anchors beforehand when the vessel is close to shore (e.g. two miles off the beach).

pg_3534.label: Verify pre-arrival checks are appropriate and correctly implemented, with confirmation by the company.

pg_3536.label: Ensure navigation lights comply with COLREGS Annex 1 visibility requirements irrespective of other onboard lighting.

pg_3537.label: Shade deck lighting adequately so it permits safe on-board movement without obscuring regulatory navigation lights.

pg_3538.label: Continuously reassess the identified navigation light colour and the relative track of a crossing vessel as range closes, rather than relying on an initial impression.

pg_3539.label: Cross-check observed light colour against the vessel's relative track/bearing movement for consistency.

pg_3540.label: Do not assume own vessel's stand-on/give-way status based solely on an uncertain navigation light sighting; treat ambiguous light identification as a risk of collision.

pg_3541.label: Ensure own vessel's navigation lights are bright enough to stand out against other onboard lighting, and avoid coloured deck lights that could be confused with navigation lights.

pg_3542.label: Verify bulwark height meets the minimum standard of 1,000mm during flag state surveys.

pg_3543.label: Conduct a risk assessment at the design stage for any deviation from standard bulwark height or similar structural features.

pg_3544.label: Apply a Management of Change process to any design alteration.

pg_3545.label: Obtain ship managers' approval for design changes.

pg_3546.label: Raise crew awareness of tripping hazards from low bulwarks, especially at night.

pg_3547.label: Report the hazardous bridge wing platform condition to Port State Control.

pg_3548.label: Conduct a risk assessment of the area with inadequate bulwark height/gap.

pg_3549.label: Implement appropriate interim measures (e.g. physical barriers, warnings) based on the risk assessment.

pg_3550.label: Direct the vessel/company to bring the platform/bulwark into compliance with the 1000mm minimum height requirement as soon as practicable.

pg_3551.label: Have the company's port captain follow up on corrective action.

pg_3552.label: Secure stairwell/access gates with their fitted securing devices at all times, especially when the vessel is proceeding to sea.

pg_3553.label: When working at height, ensure the Code of Safe Working Practices control measures are properly applied, including correct use (not just wearing) of safety harnesses or approved alternative controls such as a ladder supported by another crew member.

pg_3554.label: Use power tools only in designated safe locations (e.g., a workshop with a vice), not improvised methods in public or passenger areas.

pg_3555.label: Report unsafe practices to CHIRP if company/onboard management response is inadequate.

pg_3556.label: Require safety briefings to be broadcast on all passages.

pg_3557.label: Review the emergency exit plan for all vessels and ensure doors intended for use as exits are marked with 'EXIT' signs.

pg_3558.label: Devise an effective, quick-to-deploy barrier to bridge the gap between the lowered gangway and fixed stern railings.

pg_3559.label: Review mooring policy to eliminate trip hazards from mooring fittings/hooks at the quay.

pg_3560.label: Do not rely solely on the generic 'two metre rule' to determine if work-at-height controls are needed.

pg_3561.label: Use a permit to work system that accounts for the specific location of the work and its potential hazards.

pg_3562.label: Consult CSWP Chapters 8, 11, and 17 when planning or assessing work aloft/at height.

pg_3563.label: Maintain close attention and ongoing review of working-aloft safety culture and leadership.

pg_3564.label: Verify that manropes are secured to strong points on deck, not to handrails.

pg_3565.label: Inspect handrails for deformation or bending before relying on them in any transfer arrangement.

pg_3566.label: Do not handle any munitions under any circumstances.

pg_3567.label: Immediately contact local authorities wherever in the world the discovery occurs.

pg_3568.label: Identify and inspect any non-standard devices attached to the pilot ladder rigging before use.

pg_3569.label: Require the ship and its Classification Society to implement a definitive SOLAS-compliant solution to hold the ladder firmly to the hull.

pg_3570.label: Conduct a full risk assessment before applying any Management of Change process to boarding arrangements.

pg_3571.label: Secure both the pilot ladder and the accommodation ladder to the ship's side regardless of whether a winch reel is used.

pg_3572.label: Ensure all pilot boarding arrangements comply with SOLAS Regulation V/23 and IMO Resolution A.1045(27) as amended by A.1108(29).

pg_3573.label: Fit fall preventer devices (FPDs) before any training boat launch.

pg_3574.label: Swing out, lower, and recover the boat empty before use.

pg_3575.label: Verify that lifting strops are attached to the correct, designated lifting points on the boat (transom), not to unrelated hull strongpoints.

pg_3576.label: Recover the malfunctioning boat safely using a heaving line secured to the mooring deck to bring it to horizontal.

pg_3577.label: Compare lifting strops between port and starboard boats and test-lift the starboard boat before use.

pg_3578.label: Investigate root cause of the strop slack/tilt.

pg_3579.label: Reposition strops to correct strongpoints on the transom and re-test launch both boats.

pg_3580.label: Permanently mark the correct strongpoints on the hull.

pg_3581.label: Ensure appropriate supervision and cross-checking/testing whenever equipment is replaced, even with identical certified parts.

pg_3582.label: Take full notes/photographs when equipment is removed or replaced and keep them on board.

pg_3583.label: Encourage crew to seek clarification when uncertain about correct fitting procedures.

pg_3584.label: Include clear, unambiguous photographs and notes in vessel operating procedures for launching, recovery, and strop changeout.

pg_3585.label: Conduct a briefing and risk assessment before undertaking lifeboat strop changeover or similar tasks.

pg_3586.label: Ensure LSA/SOLAS training manuals are kept fully up-to-date with a process for regular review.

pg_3587.label: Use colour coding of strops as a preventative measure where applicable.

pg_3588.label: Ensure changeover procedures for bridge equipment/controls are clearly understood and implemented by all bridge team members.

pg_3589.label: Include testing of the changeover procedure as part of pre-arrival checks.

pg_3590.label: Design changeover-of-controls systems to be simple, unambiguous, with appropriate operational instructions.

pg_3591.label: Test bow thrusters prior to arrival even if tugs are expected to be used.

pg_3592.label: Pilot intervened and instructed the Master to remain at the bridge wing control station for engine movements.

pg_3593.label: Rely on the two tugs already made fast to complete the berthing manoeuvre.

pg_3594.label: Resolve the bow thruster control transfer so it was available if required.

pg_3595.label: Reinforce verbal helm orders with a hand movement indicating direction.

pg_3596.label: Encourage helmsmen to alert bridge team members of distracting issues or fatigue.

pg_3597.label: Relieve helmsmen on a regular basis.

pg_3598.label: Assign a team member to monitor the rudder angle indicator.

pg_3599.label: Incorporate these personnel and procedural factors into company procedures.

pg_3600.label: Pilot and Master immediately detect and rapidly correct the helm error when the helmsman steers the wrong way.

pg_3601.label: Reinforce verbal helm orders with a hand direction signal when the helmsman fails to respond.

pg_3602.label: Maintain close monitoring of helmsman performance throughout pilotage, especially during midnight to 0300 hours.

pg_3603.label: Take time to assess the relative movement of the two vessels before transferring onto the ladder.

pg_3604.label: Confirm lee was requested from the vessel before transfer.

pg_3605.label: Confirm the pilot ladder is correctly rigged and an officer is in attendance.

pg_3606.label: Use available wave-rider or swell data to plan transfer timing before leaving harbour.

pg_3607.label: Assess every pilot transfer task individually before it is carried out.

pg_3608.label: Ensure bridge personnel, pilot ladder crew, pilot launch crew member, and launch skipper remain fully alert throughout the transfer.

pg_3609.label: Rig pilot ladders on fishing vessels safely per the forthcoming report's guidance.

pg_3610.label: Inspect man ropes and pilot ladder arrangement before use during embarkation/disembarkation.

pg_3611.label: If man ropes are found non-compliant, use the pilot ladder itself for support instead of the man ropes when conditions allow.

pg_3612.label: Report the unsafe man rope condition to the relevant authority (e.g., CHIRP) after disembarking.

pg_3613.label: Contact the launch master by VHF to agree a safe disembarkation plan.

pg_3614.label: Complete the transfer inside the harbour in sheltered waters.

pg_3615.label: Recommend a Port State Control inspection on the vessel's next arrival.

pg_3616.label: Report the deficiency to CHIRP/relevant authority rather than ignoring it.

pg_3617.label: Rig pilot ladder in accordance with SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 23 and IMO Resolution A.1045(27) as amended by A.1108(29).

pg_3618.label: Consult the IMPA Pilot Boarding Arrangements poster and CHIRP publications page for guidance.

pg_3619.label: Fit two man-ropes of 28-32 mm diameter, properly secured to ring plates on deck, ready for use at the point of access.

pg_3620.label: Prefer natural fibre (e.g. manila) man-ropes over synthetic.

pg_3621.label: Allow the pilot to refuse a non-compliant ladder arrangement.

pg_3622.label: If in doubt about whether the situation is overtaking or end-on, treat it as overtaking/end-on and act accordingly.

pg_3623.label: Alter course substantially (e.g. 30° to starboard) to open distance and let the other vessel pass at a safe margin.

pg_3624.label: Accept deviation from intended track when ample sea room exists rather than hold course and risk a close-quarters situation.

pg_3625.label: Assess the relative heading/aspect of the other vessel to determine whether Rule 13 (overtaking) or Rules 15/16 (crossing) applies.

pg_3626.label: Apply Rule 13(c) to resolve doubt in favour of treating it as an overtaking situation.

pg_3627.label: Recognize own vessel's role as stand-on vessel under Rule 17 regardless of which rule applied.

pg_3628.label: Contact the other vessel via VHF to ascertain her intentions when no avoiding action was observed.

pg_3629.label: Fasten the retrieval/tripping line at or above the last spreader step and lead it forward.

pg_3630.label: Ensure the retrieval line does not hinder the pilot or obstruct the pilot boat's safe approach.

pg_3631.label: Carefully inspect all pilot ladders prior to use and maintain them properly.

pg_3632.label: Test the main engine prior to departure by turning it over on both air and fuel.

pg_3633.label: Raise the gangway and station personnel standing by moorings before conducting the engine test.

pg_3634.label: Submit reports detailing any cases of engine failure to start or sluggish response to CHIRP.

pg_3635.label: Transfer engine control from bridge to manual local control in the engine room when main engine fails to start.

pg_3636.label: Retain the aft tug attached for the outbound passage until clear of the channel.

pg_3637.label: Keep speed to a minimum during outbound transit.

pg_3638.label: Proceed to anchor once clear of the channel and carry out repairs before continuing the voyage.

pg_3639.label: Loosen/ease affected push rods on the non-operational spill valves to restore engine function.

pg_3640.label: Investigate and verify fuel oil quality and engage manufacturer in root-cause discussion.

pg_3641.label: When another vessel fails to keep clear as required, briefly use VHF only to request the other vessel's intentions, not to negotiate or coordinate avoidance maneuvers.

pg_3642.label: As stand-on vessel, take early and ample independent action to avoid collision once it is apparent the give-way vessel is not complying with COLREGS.

pg_3643.label: In open waters, maintain distance and avoid close proximity to other vessels unnecessarily.

pg_3644.label: Before every pilot transfer, inspect the pilot ladder rigging for correct installation: continuous side-ropes passing under steps, intact chocks, horizontal and evenly spaced steps, no tripping lines below the spreader, and secure fitting at the correct distance from the gangway/ladder bottom.

pg_3645.label: Ensure a qualified officer, not a cadet, supervises pilot transfer operations at the boarding station.

pg_3646.label: Maintain direct radio contact between the pilot and the bridge during transfer.

pg_3647.label: Consider allowing the pilot boat to request a course alteration directly to the bridge.

pg_3648.label: Ensure a responsible officer, not just a cadet, is present at the pilot ladder/boarding point.

pg_3649.label: Relay any urgent pilot instructions (e.g. course alterations) promptly and accurately to the bridge.

pg_3650.label: Hold the elevator for the pilot or direct the pilot to use the stairs without delay.

pg_3651.label: Fit an appropriate mat at accommodation entry points instead of loose towels for crew/pilot to wipe feet.

pg_3652.label: Know the vessel's exact freeboard and rig the correct pilot transfer arrangement unless specifically instructed otherwise.

pg_3653.label: Request or provide precise written/verbal instructions specifying ladder side, height above water, and conditions for combination ladder use.

pg_3654.label: Ensure supervising officers enforce PPE use and safe practices for crew working over the side.

pg_3655.label: Advise the vessel's responsible officer that the boarding arrangement is non-compliant with SOLAS V/23.

pg_3656.label: Request removal of the combination arrangement and rigging of the pilot ladder directly.

pg_3657.label: Crew to rig the compliant ladder promptly, independent of other deck operations.

pg_3658.label: If arrangement cannot be corrected in time and traffic/weather conditions allow, pilot may proceed via non-compliant arrangement as last resort, then report the deficiency.

pg_3659.label: Revise ship's communication procedures prior to pilot boarding to clearly state SOLAS compliance requirements in advance.

pg_3660.label: Observe crew members having difficulty boarding vessels at night and move to assist proactively.

pg_3661.label: Raise the alarm immediately upon witnessing a man-overboard event.

pg_3662.label: Proceed to assist the person in the water to the best of one's ability after alarm is raised.

pg_3663.label: Review own vessel's planning, risk assessment, toolbox talks and job execution procedures, e.g. via a 'Spot the Hazards' exercise.

pg_3664.label: On alarm, return to cabin to collect warm jacket, hat, medication, and life jacket before proceeding to the muster station.

pg_3665.label: If smoke is present, keep low and crawl to reach the stairs and muster station.

pg_3666.label: Crew to identify cabins occupied by wheelchair users and send designated crew members to collect them and carry them down stairs using a stair chair.

pg_3667.label: Gather wheelchair users together at a separate area of the muster station and allow them to leave before able-bodied passengers fill the lifts.

pg_3668.label: Pre-position lifejackets at muster stations rather than in individual cabins

pg_3669.label: Have crew guide wheelchair-using passengers directly to muster stations from wherever they are on the ship

pg_3670.label: Keep passageways clear of stewards' trolleys

pg_3671.label: Assign a trained crew member (or members) to assist each disabled passenger in an emergency.

pg_3672.label: Have a ship representative discuss with the disabled passenger in advance what assistance they may require in an emergency.

pg_3673.label: Prepare a 'grab-bag' in readiness for disabled passengers' potential emergency needs.

pg_3674.label: Consider relocating lifejackets closer to lifeboats/muster stations rather than only in cabins.

pg_3675.label: During an emergency, instruct disabled passengers to remain where they are and request assistance rather than attempt to join the main muster group.

pg_3676.label: Review and document company-specific procedures for assisting disabled passengers during emergencies.

pg_3677.label: Refer to CHIRP's Insight article and the included IMO Resolutions and IMPA Pilot Boarding Poster when assessing pilot/accommodation ladder rigging.

pg_3678.label: Identify and remove from service any portable ladder that has been modified outside manufacturer design parameters.

pg_3679.label: Report unauthorised equipment modifications found during inspections.

pg_3680.label: Verify that all information printed on a chart is up to date before relying on it for navigation.

pg_3681.label: Report inaccurately charted navigational aids to the Hydrographic Office (e.g. via British Admiralty Charts process).

pg_3682.label: Consult The Mariners Handbook (NP100) Chapter 8 for further guidance on reporting and chart accuracy.

pg_3683.label: Report obstructed or defective navigational aids to the relevant port authority as soon as identified.

pg_3684.label: Escalate unresolved navigational safety reports to a higher authority (e.g. Chief Hydrographer) if the port the other vessel does not respond.

pg_3685.label: Exercise increased caution and use alternative navigational references when approaching the berth, especially in strong northerly or southerly winds.

pg_3686.label: Use the right tool for the right job rather than improvising modifications.

pg_3687.label: Challenge local practices that have become accepted norms.

pg_3688.label: Assess whether the onboard and shore safety culture genuinely values safety.

pg_3689.label: Maintain situational awareness by regularly asking what may have been missed.

pg_3690.label: Follow established procedures for any job rather than defaulting to convenience.

pg_3691.label: Consult COSWP sections 11.8.4-11.8.5, 17.3, A17.2/3-A17.2/4, 22.2.9, 22.6, and 28.6.3 for portable ladder guidance.

pg_3692.label: Verify the expiration dates of all provisions upon delivery and before storage in the provision rooms.

pg_3693.label: Return expired provisions, and those due to expire shortly, to the supplier.

pg_3694.label: If the ship has already sailed, notify the company as soon as possible with supporting evidence such as photographs.

pg_3695.label: Ensure cooks and galley personnel never use expired foods in preparation or service.

pg_3696.label: Arrange consumption of provisions to prioritise items with the earliest expiry dates, following 'first in – first out' stock rotation.

pg_3697.label: Where the master controls provisioning funds and chandler choice, balance cost against quality rather than always selecting the cheapest supplier.

pg_3698.label: Where the company maintains a preferred chandler list, ensure those chandlers are audited by the company.

pg_3699.label: Apply good stock rotation and order provisions in sensible quantities.

pg_3700.label: Check temperature of provisions at the point of loading; reject frozen goods that are not actually frozen and verify chilled products are delivered between 0°C and +5°C.

pg_3701.label: Avoid cross contamination between out-of-date or defrosted frozen/chilled products and in-date stock.

pg_3702.label: Extend expiry vigilance beyond provisions to medical stores, pyrotechnics, safety equipment, and consumables such as grinding discs.

pg_3703.label: Fresh water wash the holds and remove all previous cargo residues.

pg_3704.label: Eliminate any infestation in the holds.

pg_3706.label: Ensure holds are free of odour before inspection.

pg_3707.label: Present holds for inspection prior to loading grain.

pg_3708.label: Designate any crane and associated equipment used for transferring personnel as 'man-riding' equipment before such use.

pg_3709.label: Ensure the crane is fitted with a failsafe brake.

pg_3710.label: Confirm the crane is Class approved for use in transferring personnel.

pg_3711.label: Hold a safety meeting with all personnel involved before the transfer task begins.

pg_3712.label: Observe the surveyor's positioning in the basket before commencing transfer.

pg_3713.label: Stop and review the operation when incorrect positioning is identified.

pg_3714.label: Fully discuss and re-confirm the correct transfer procedure with the surveyor before proceeding.

pg_3715.label: Proceed with the transfer only once correct procedure is confirmed.

pg_3716.label: Record identified hazards and the status of remedial actions in handover notes for onboard personnel.

pg_3717.label: Have the company request positive confirmation that remedial action has been completed.

pg_3718.label: Watchman reports suspicious smell/odor immediately to the OOW.

pg_3719.label: Call the Electrician immediately to investigate the cause.

pg_3720.label: Replace the overheated capacitor and renew burnt cables.

pg_3721.label: Check vessel stock/fitted status of the affected capacitor type and replace with updated product across the fleet.

pg_3722.label: Modify PMS to require inspection every six months and capacitor renewal every four years.

pg_3723.label: Ensure replacement capacitors received on board are promptly fitted, not left in storage.

pg_3724.label: Ensure all personnel involved in personnel transfer wear full PPE including life vests.

pg_3725.label: Verify that lifting equipment used is specifically designed or adapted for lifting persons.

pg_3726.label: Ensure lifting equipment designed for persons has suitable devices to prevent it from falling.

pg_3727.label: Do not lift any person except with equipment designed/adapted for that purpose, or in rescue/emergency situations.

pg_3728.label: Consult COSWP section 31.13 and Standard P+I Club guidance for detailed personnel transfer procedures.

pg_3729.label: Check fuel quantity before departing to sea

pg_3730.label: Check fuel quality for diesel bugs or water if engine has been unused for a long time

pg_3731.label: Wear a lifejacket and lifeline when working near the side, and preferably at all times in a small boat

pg_3732.label: Drop anchor until the engine is working again, if water depth allows

pg_3733.label: Wear a lifejacket at all times when at risk of falling overboard.

pg_3734.label: Apply non-slip paint on decks and wear appropriate footwear.

pg_3735.label: Fit additional railings or temporary grab lines where needed.

pg_3736.label: Conduct a personal safety risk assessment covering these factors.

pg_3737.label: Read and act upon MCA/RNLI fisherman safety guidance and codes of practice.

pg_3738.label: Conduct a dynamic risk assessment before and during any task that involves working outside the gunwales/bulwarks.

pg_3739.label: Determine and verify the means of re-boarding (e.g. external grab lines or rope ladder) before starting the activity.

pg_3740.label: Carry and register a Personal Location Beacon (PLB) with the Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre.

pg_3741.label: Wear a Personal Floatation Device (PFD) as constant wear outside other clothing, including waterproofs.

pg_3742.label: Consider wearing buoyant clothing appropriate to the activity.

pg_3743.label: For single-handed operations, ensure someone ashore or aboard knows your location and expected return time.

pg_3744.label: Rig the pilot ladder with loose ends of the side ropes lashed to eye bolts or deck pads, not shackles, spreaders, or angle-iron bars.

pg_3745.label: Position ladder securing points at least 915mm from the ship's side railings.

pg_3746.label: Check the ladder rigging before each use to confirm it is safe.

pg_3747.label: Pilots should refuse to embark/disembark via a ladder believed to be unsafe and report unsatisfactory arrangements to port authorities and Port State Control.

pg_3748.label: Master must verify pilot ladder is properly secured to a fixed point before confirming vessel is ready to sail/receive pilot.

pg_3749.label: Crew should inspect and test ladder security using proper fastening points, not improvised methods such as hooking onto angle-iron or human body weight.

pg_3750.label: Pilot should report ladder deficiencies immediately to the master upon boarding.

pg_3751.label: Company should investigate and implement corrective steps when such safety failures are reported.

pg_3752.label: Conduct a personal risk assessment before undertaking routine tasks such as washing down decks.

pg_3753.label: Wear non-slip footwear while washing down decks instead of going barefoot or wearing flip flops.

pg_3754.label: Ensure risk assessments and safe operating procedures are established for routine tasks such as washing down at height.

pg_3755.label: Have senior officers actively police and enforce adherence to risk assessments and safe operating procedures.

pg_3756.label: Provide targeted hazard awareness training for less experienced crew or those temporarily working outside their usual department.

pg_3757.label: Foster a strong onboard safety culture that governs behaviour for all tasks, routine or not.

pg_3758.label: Consider wearing a waist belt harness when accessing areas with fall potential.

pg_3759.label: Use longer-handled tools and stand behind a rail when working in hazardous zones.

pg_3760.label: Evaluate whether a personal floatation device (PFD) is appropriate for the task.

pg_3761.label: Assess timing and location of work even within port.

pg_3762.label: Hold an onboard safety meeting or informal discussion to review photos and identify improvements.

pg_3763.label: Refuse to perform a task perceived as inherently unsafe, even under duress.

pg_3764.label: Report similar safety experiences to CHIRP Maritime.

pg_3765.label: Advise the master that the vessel is entering the narrowest and shallowest part of the passage.

pg_3766.label: Require the master to remain on the bridge during this critical phase of the transit.

pg_3767.label: Conduct a thorough Master/Pilot information exchange covering speed adjustments throughout the pilotage.

pg_3768.label: Agree and clearly state the amount of notice required to reduce RPM to manoeuvring speed, based on realistic transit timing.

pg_3769.label: Explicitly confirm mutual understanding of notice times and emergency exceptions between master and pilot.

pg_3770.label: Acknowledge that in an emergency, no notice will be given before RPM reduction.

pg_3771.label: Clarify with the pilot the actual time required to reach manoeuvring/full speed rather than relying on standard '10 minutes notice' terminology.

pg_3772.label: Confirm engine response timing and terminology understanding in the Master/Pilot Information Exchange, accounting for possible language barriers.

pg_3773.label: Ensure the master does not leave the bridge during critical sections of a passage, including critical pilotage areas.

pg_3774.label: Ensure the master is well-rested during critical pilotage periods.

pg_3775.label: Incorporate personnel/bridge-presence requirements for specific pilotage stages into the Master/Pilot Information Exchange.

pg_3776.label: Conduct and record a pre-arrival engine test before critical maneuvering.

pg_3777.label: Master and bridge team coordinate directly with chief engineer via telephone when engine fails to respond.

pg_3778.label: Confirm tug availability and connection status before relying on them during critical maneuvers.

pg_3779.label: Chart company notifies outlets when new chart editions are issued and encourages return of old stock for a refund.

pg_3780.label: Chart company publishes chart corrections via its website and maintains a printing history list of current charts.

pg_3781.label: Reporter advises mariners to check the chart company's printing history/corrections list before purchase or use.

pg_3782.label: Assign individual functions to bridge team members instead of all gathering around the telegraph/telephone (acknowledge alarms, check with engine room, conduct navigational check e.g. anchoring option, ensure crew awareness).

pg_3783.label: Continue to monitor unfolding events and assess/adjust plans accordingly.

pg_3784.label: Practice these emergency scenarios in table-top drills.

pg_3785.label: Test the engine prior to arrival as part of standard procedure.

pg_3786.label: Use closed-loop communication in all work aspects, including toolbox talks, safety briefings, and instructions, especially when language is not a party's first language.

pg_3787.label: Maintain open communication between bridge and engine room at all stages of the voyage, including during 'Stand By Engines' and 'Full Away on Sea Passage' transitions.

pg_3788.label: After an incident, discuss what went wrong and apply lessons learned rather than blaming an individual.

pg_3789.label: Call the ECR and request a specific engine and thrust configuration rather than issuing vague commands like 'start-up'.

pg_3790.label: Have the ECR repeat back the instruction to the bridge.

pg_3791.label: Stop cargo operations before clutching in the main propulsion plant and confirm the clutch and pitch system is not causing uncontrolled vessel movement.

pg_3792.label: Report concerns through CHIRP if unable to report through the Company for any reason, including mistreatment.

pg_3793.label: Verify the chart edition date online against the official current edition before purchase or use.

pg_3794.label: Apply all relevant corrections (Notices to Mariners) to any chart purchased.

pg_3795.label: Check availability of corrections for any chart before relying on it for navigation.

pg_3796.label: When purchasing electronic or paper charts, verify they are the latest edition before use.

pg_3797.label: Check chart supplier websites regularly for latest editions and corrections.

pg_3798.label: Be alert to the possibility of counterfeit charts and software, and use the British Admiralty guide to identify them.

pg_3799.label: Secure safety chains or handrail openings at all times when not in use.

pg_3800.label: Protect and clearly mark garbage/waste areas, and provide segregated bins for plastics.

pg_3801.label: Store lifebuoy lines coiled in a container for immediate release.

pg_3802.label: Mark boundaries and post KEEP CLEAR notices near Fireman's outfit lockers.

pg_3803.label: Abort the cat flap disembarkation option if the pilot cutter cannot land safely or is damaged.

pg_3804.label: Inform the vessel Owner of the design difficulties caused by the cat flap placement.

pg_3805.label: Review pilot boarding arrangements before constructing any similar vessels.

pg_3806.label: Keep fireman's outfit lockers free of any obstructions at all times.

pg_3807.label: Adopt simple, low-cost housekeeping improvements onboard.

pg_3808.label: Self-assess the ship's safety standard against the example shown and take corrective action if deficient.

pg_3809.label: Use the CHIRP Reference Library (Excel workbook) to access incident investigations, near-miss reports, and safety alerts.

pg_3810.label: If using an Apple Macintosh and a PDF link fails to open, copy and paste the link into the browser.

pg_3811.label: Consult the original agency websites linked at the top of each library sheet for the most current data.

pg_3812.label: Classification societies should work with shipyards to ensure compliance with both the letter and spirit of SOLAS pilot boarding regulations.

pg_3813.label: Flag states should ensure compliance with pilot boarding regulations directly or through oversight of classification societies.

pg_3814.label: Ship owners should actively scrutinise vessel design (including pilot transfer arrangements) at purchase.

pg_3815.label: Avoid using an alternative pilot door located in the aft quarter length near the propellers, even if it requires less rigging.

pg_3816.label: Design out potential hazards at the design stage rather than relying on permissive/ambiguous regulatory wording.

pg_3817.label: Require stevedores and crane crew to wear hard hats when working near suspended loads.

pg_3818.label: Use unambiguous, whole-arm hand signals for crane operations.

pg_3819.label: Keep personnel clear of and out of reach of a suspended load.

pg_3820.label: Report observed unsafe port operations to CHIRP and the shipping company for follow-up.

pg_3821.label: Encourage all personnel, ship or shore based, to intervene if someone is working unsafely (Stop Work Authority).

pg_3822.label: If a port operates at lower safety standards, have the master 'note protest'.

pg_3823.label: Alternatively, have the company send a letter to the port raising the safety concern.

pg_3824.label: Apply the Code of Safe Working Practices signalling procedures to all lifting operations.

pg_3825.label: Do not assume the give-way vessel will actually give way; prepare own avoiding action (e.g. crash gybe) as a last resort.

pg_3826.label: Maintain visual/radar lookout independent of VHF contact attempts.

pg_3827.label: Maintain a proper visual lookout appropriate to eye height and conditions, recognizing that visibility judged from a low eye height (6 feet) differs significantly from that at higher conning positions (30 feet).

pg_3828.label: Identify and monitor the correct local VTS/working VHF channel (Channel 71) in addition to Channel 16 when operating in an area with published General Directions.

pg_3829.label: Be aware that pleasure vessels may be exempt from local General Directions and therefore unlikely to use or expect to use the VTS working channel.

pg_3830.label: Seek early VHF confirmation of another vessel's intentions and awareness when bearing appears steady and a risk of collision is suspected.

pg_3831.label: Call the first (larger) overtaking vessel to state intention to keep to the south side of the traffic lane

pg_3832.label: Attempt contact with the second, faster vessel on VHF Channel 16 and then Channel 02

pg_3833.label: Contact Pilot Maas to report the collision-course situation and inability to reach the other vessel, requesting they advise the vessel to pass on the reporter's starboard side

pg_3834.label: Monitor the other vessel's course alteration and actual passing distance as it closed to 1.2 miles and then attempted to overtake at 1.5-2 cables

pg_3835.label: Alter own course to starboard under Rule 2 of COLREGs (Article 2) to increase passing distance to 2-3 cables

pg_3836.label: Call the first overtaking vessel (now on starboard side) to advise of the course change

pg_3837.label: Alter course to resume giving way to the vessel approaching on the starboard side once the port-side vessel has passed at a safe distance.

pg_3838.label: CHIRP follow up with the company and master of the vessel involved to understand their intentions and perception.

pg_3839.label: Monitor approaching vessel by radar/visual from long range (10 miles) and track bearing/aspect.

pg_3840.label: Assert own vessel's COLREGS status and insist the give-way vessel alter course to starboard for port-to-port passing.

pg_3841.label: Continue close monitoring of the target vessel's course and speed as range closes.

pg_3842.label: Re-query the other vessel's intentions as range closed to 2 miles.

pg_3843.label: Take avoiding action (hard-over to port) when the other vessel confirmed it was maintaining course.

pg_3844.label: Detect and track the target vessel's range, CPA and TCPA from initial detection (8nm, CPA <0.35nm, TCPA ~40min)

pg_3845.label: Continue monitoring the target's movements as TCPA decreases

pg_3846.label: Attempt to establish radio communication with the target vessel via voice and DSC on a regular basis

pg_3847.label: Maintain course and speed while monitoring the situation.

pg_3848.label: Sound horn signals when range reduced to 1nm and continue as range closed to 0.5nm.

pg_3849.label: Keep engines and steering at immediate readiness and maintain a proper lookout, including binocular observation of the other vessel's bridge.

pg_3850.label: Continue attempting VHF contact even after the other vessel altered course.

pg_3851.label: Attempt VHF Channel 16 and DSC calls to the non-responsive vessel to establish intentions.

pg_3852.label: Communicate with other nearby vessels to inform them of an impending course change.

pg_3853.label: Alter course (e.g., turn to starboard, then later to port) based on coordination with other traffic, not assuming the non-responsive vessel will react.

pg_3854.label: Explain intentions to a third vessel that queries the maneuver.

pg_3855.label: Report the non-compliant vessel's conduct to CHIRP/managers after the event.

pg_3856.label: Move outside the main channel when larger vessels (dredger, tanker) are transiting it.

pg_3857.label: Monitor the other vessels' movements continuously after giving way.

pg_3858.label: Start the engine and take positive helm action (hard to port) when a collision risk develops suddenly.

pg_3859.label: Ask the Port Authority what further action will be taken and whether other bodies should be informed.

pg_3860.label: Interview the Master and confirm bridge watchkeeping arrangements at the time of the alleged incident.

pg_3861.label: Confirm VHF watchkeeping on Ch.12 and Ch.16 during the transit.

pg_3862.label: Attempt to obtain VTS radar and AIS replay data for independent verification.

pg_3863.label: Raise the matter with the vessel owners and document the investigation outcome.

pg_3864.label: Maintain good housekeeping standards within port premises

pg_3865.label: Conduct risk assessments and establish controls per HSE ACOP guidance

pg_3866.label: Comply with Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 duties if controlling dock premises, supplying plant/equipment, or employing dock workers

pg_3867.label: Reference MCA/DfT Port Marine Safety Code and relevant national legislation when operating internationally

pg_3868.label: As stand-on vessel, take your own avoiding action or reduce speed as soon as you are in doubt about the other vessel's intentions.

pg_3869.label: Concentrate on applying the collision regulations rather than engaging in VHF discussion, including heated exchanges.

pg_3870.label: Identify and monitor the specific VHF working channel appropriate to your operational area, noting whether it is Simplex or Duplex.

pg_3871.label: Maintain full situational awareness by putting yourself in the position of the other vessel(s).

pg_3872.label: Take any avoiding action early and substantially.

pg_3873.label: When overtaking, where practicable overtake to starboard keeping your own starboard side open.

pg_3874.label: Investigate root causes such as personnel qualifications and actual experience rather than simply apportioning blame for actions/inactions.

pg_3875.label: Ensure all crew at mooring stations and on derrick/hatch operations wear full PPE (safety shoes, helmets, gloves).

pg_3876.label: Walk the anchor back to water level before letting it go near small craft or line handlers.

pg_3877.label: Communicate any anchor-drop or similar manoeuvre to all parties via VHF before executing it.

pg_3878.label: Check all sides of the vessel (including the side opposite current crew focus) before letting go the anchor or similar actions.

pg_3879.label: Night watchman spots person in water and immediately throws a lifebelt/life ring to the casualty

pg_3880.label: Night watchman raises the alarm to the Coastguard

pg_3881.label: RNLI lifeboat locates casualty using the deployed life ring and brings him aboard

pg_3882.label: Transport casualty short distance to shore and hand over to crew members then ambulance crew

pg_3883.label: Maintain proper communication between the bridge team (pilot and master) and the forward mooring station throughout anchor operations.

pg_3884.label: Check the area over-side to ensure it is clear before dropping anchor.

pg_3885.label: Keep the line handling boat clear of the vicinity until the anchor-dropping operation is completed, if this is a regularly conducted operation.

pg_3886.label: Lower the anchor to the waterline before letting go rather than dropping it from height.

pg_3887.label: Ensure personal protective equipment (PPE) is provided and worn during deck/mooring operations.

pg_3888.label: Report the observed deficient lifting operation to the vessel operator.

pg_3889.label: Vessel operator conducts an investigation into the incident.

pg_3891.label: Do not use wooden pallets with web strops not designed for lifting duty.

pg_3892.label: Cordon off lifting operation areas and secure gangway access before lifting over it.

pg_3893.label: Conduct a considered, lift-specific risk assessment treating each lift as an independent operation rather than using a generic risk assessment.

pg_3894.label: Hold an on-site toolbox talk prior to commencement of the lifting operation.

pg_3895.label: Ensure correct lifting apparatus and suitable load-bearing equipment (e.g. pallets designed for the purpose) are used.

pg_3896.label: Factor in training needs and the physical location/layout of the lifting operation.

pg_3897.label: Conduct a risk assessment before any lifting operation.

pg_3899.label: Ensure appropriate supervision is in place during the lift.

pg_3900.label: Carry out the lift in a safe manner using correct signalling per regulatory requirements.

pg_3901.label: Stop the job if a risk assessment and toolbox talk have not been conducted.

pg_3902.label: Deliver a thorough safety briefing before departure, repeating key safety instructions multiple times.

pg_3903.label: Instruct passengers to sit toward the back of the boat.

pg_3904.label: Depart and transit at reduced speed (5 knots) in calm conditions.

pg_3905.label: Stop the boat immediately when an injury occurs

pg_3906.label: Check the passenger's condition, monitoring hand squeeze and toe movement

pg_3907.label: Keep the injured passenger warm with blankets and do not move her

pg_3908.label: Drive slowly back to the bay/pontoon

pg_3909.label: Make a VHF call to the operations base in the marina to request an ambulance

pg_3910.label: Brief passengers before excursions and offer postponement in rougher weather

pg_3911.label: Post a notice at the boarding point stating passengers are 'required' (not 'requested') to remain seated.

pg_3912.label: Where practicable, add notices on the rear of seats or on athwartships seating.

pg_3913.label: Have the company, not the passenger, assess whether weather conditions are suitable for the trip or require postponement.

pg_3914.label: Consult MAIB report 10-2017 on RIB collisions and related guidance.

pg_3915.label: Cross-check PPU/AIS displayed position against visual/ECDIS bearings when a discrepancy is suspected.

pg_3916.label: Ask the master/bridge team to verify a landmark or beacon bearing using the ECDIS as an independent check.

pg_3917.label: Request access to and review the GPS settings, specifically the GPS SETUP/GPS SMOOTHING menu.

pg_3918.label: Reset GPS smoothing values (Position, Speed, Average Speed) to zero.

pg_3919.label: Confirm accuracy of displayed positions after departure following the setting change.

pg_3920.label: Check the antenna offsets entered for the AIS GPS antenna against the ship's antenna plan.

pg_3921.label: Use the GPS selector switch to change the AIS external GPS source to No 1 GPS, which was located close to the AIS antenna.

pg_3922.label: Post a notice on the AIS requiring the external GPS input to always be sourced from No 1 GPS.

pg_3923.label: Regularly check GPS, ECDIS, and AIS positions against visual and radar positions.

pg_3925.label: Do not use AIS for position reference.

pg_3926.label: Periodically enter a manual position into the ECDIS.

pg_3927.label: Ensure antenna height is input correctly into ECDIS/GPS equipment.

pg_3928.label: Confirm which GPS unit is the designated master unit among the bridge team.

pg_3929.label: Verify correct speed inputs and WGS84 offsets are applied to master equipment.

pg_3930.label: Use GPS smoothing cautiously rather than removing it entirely.

pg_3931.label: Build in checks and balances for electronic positioning equipment.

pg_3932.label: Installers must provide proper advice and warning during equipment installation.

pg_3933.label: Ship managers must exercise due diligence when signing off an installation, ensuring testing and thorough operator familiarisation (including manufacturer training and commissioning engineer instructions).

pg_3934.label: Cross-check ECDIS positions using manual positions, visual bearings, and radar distances, especially in confined waters.

pg_3935.label: Question any discrepancy between ECDIS display and visual observation (e.g., a beacon shown on the bow but observed on the beam).

pg_3936.label: Send advisory letters to managers/charterers/agents identified as non-compliant with pilot ladder requirements.

pg_3937.label: Require the ship's pilot ladder certificate as part of the pre-arrival regime.

pg_3938.label: Offer seamanship advice freely to ships needing guidance on fixing points or stanchions.

pg_3939.label: Supply loaned pilot ladder and magnet equipment to ships on a 'you use it, you own it' basis.

pg_3940.label: Port Authority inspects and documents all pilot transfer arrangement deficiencies at boarding.

pg_3941.label: Port Authority manager formally writes to vessel's managers detailing deficiencies.

pg_3942.label: Vessel instructed to replace any equipment not meeting required standard.

pg_3943.label: Managers warned that future deficient presentations will result in pilot service refusal.

pg_3944.label: Port institutes industry-wide advance notice (two months) of stricter prescriptive enforcement from a set date.

pg_3945.label: Require certificates for pilot ladders and related equipment to be submitted as part of pre-arrival information.

pg_3946.label: Port State Control/regulator takes immediate action (e.g., delaying the ship) when deficiencies are found rather than deferring to 'next visit'.

pg_3947.label: Pilots should test the pilot ladder by placing weight on it before using it for disembarkation.

pg_3948.label: Properly action and follow up on deficiency reports to prevent repetition.

pg_3949.label: Obtain reporter consent via ISWAN before engaging with CHIRP

pg_3950.label: Provide the reporter with a breakdown of relevant MARPOL Special Area regulations

pg_3951.label: Request further details on location and nature of the discharged oil/garbage

pg_3952.label: Notify Flag State and ITF of the welfare/fatigue concerns

pg_3953.label: Flag State to investigate with the company

pg_3954.label: Report fatigue, heat, or welfare issues to CHIRP and/or ISWAN rather than staying silent.

pg_3955.label: Escalate unresolved onboard welfare complaints beyond the ship level to the company, and if necessary to the Flag State.

pg_3956.label: Incorporate fatigue considerations into the Safety Management System under the ISM Code.

pg_3957.label: Apply the updated IMO fatigue guidelines (MSC.1/Circ.1598) in ship design, manning, and training.

pg_3958.label: Install a dedicated talk-back communication system with microphones/speakers in the engine control room and at all bridge conning positions (centre and both wings).

pg_3959.label: Use the talk-back system for all verbal bridge/engine room communication going forward, retaining phones only as a backup.

pg_3960.label: Ensure the person conning the ship can broadcast an immediate problem/delay call to the engine room from any position.

pg_3961.label: Install instant talkback (closed-loop) communication systems between bridge and engine room instead of relying on third-party relay.

pg_3962.label: Apply a systematic risk management programme to identify, analyse, evaluate and mitigate risks in bridge-engine room communications and any retrofit changes.

pg_3963.label: Incorporate Human Centred Design analysis into ship design from concept stage through retirement, including bridge ergonomics and mooring systems.

pg_3964.label: Engage ship owners and mariners more actively in new-build design decisions rather than accepting standard 'off the shelf' designs.

pg_3965.label: Monitor the rudder angle indicator after giving a helm order to confirm it matches the order given.

pg_3966.label: Immediately repeat the helm order and point to the rudder angle indicator if a discrepancy is noticed.

pg_3967.label: Have the master independently cross-check and reinforce the correction.

pg_3968.label: Install a low-cost bridge-to-engine-control-room communication/intercom system.

pg_3969.label: When approach speed is not reducing as expected, put both engines astern.

pg_3970.label: If the stern begins moving downwind, put the starboard engine ahead to check the movement.

pg_3971.label: If sternway increases and grounding/collision with a breakwater becomes likely, shift the con to the opposite (danger-side) bridge wing.

pg_3972.label: Establish direct communication with the engine control room during the critical maneuver.

pg_3973.label: Allow at least 30 minutes for eyes to fully adapt to night vision before relying on it for lookout duties.

pg_3974.label: Avoid rapidly switching between bright light and dim, dark-adapted conditions.

pg_3975.label: Adjust lighting levels on the bridge/workplace to suit individual needs, including age and use of spectacles.

pg_3976.label: Use peripheral (rod-based) vision for detecting movement at night and direct central (cone-based) vision for detailed tasks or screens.

pg_3977.label: Avoid staring directly at a light, star, or object for several seconds at night.

pg_3978.label: Look slightly to the side of an object (e.g., a flickering star or distant light) to detect it at night.

pg_3979.label: Allow adequate time for the eyes to acquire good night vision before relying on it for navigation decisions.

pg_3980.label: Repeat back any instruction or helm order (closed-loop reporting) to confirm it has been clearly received.

pg_3981.label: Double-check critical orders by an independent means (e.g. both master and pilot monitoring the execution).

pg_3982.label: Use standard marine vocabulary and be mindful of whether parties are communicating in their native or second language.

pg_3983.label: Avoid overly bright pre-shift environments and overly dim bridge conditions before taking over a watch.

pg_3984.label: Spend time in a reddish-light environment before or during low-light bridge duty.

pg_3985.label: Question the crew when unsafe practice (removed indicator cock covers) is observed.

pg_3986.label: Raise the matter with the Company when unsafe behaviour is identified.

pg_3987.label: Amend checklists to explicitly require fitting indicator cock covers.

pg_3988.label: Continue to challenge the unsafe behaviour despite lack of positive response.

pg_3989.label: Ensure future ISM audits or classification surveys can identify the conscious decision to bypass the safety control.

pg_3990.label: Ensure all surfaces with temperatures above 220°C that could be impinged by a fuel system failure are properly insulated.

pg_3991.label: Use non-combustible, non-oil absorbing insulation material fit for purpose.

pg_3992.label: Pay particular attention to insulating flanges, indicator cocks, bolts, studs and other protruding parts, including exhaust manifold overlaps and turbocharger flanges.

pg_3993.label: Conduct regular thorough inspections of all engine insulation and hot surfaces.

pg_3994.label: Use infra-red thermal imaging equipment to search for hot spots and insulation defects.

pg_3995.label: Report the fatigue/hours-of-rest/harassment issue to CHIRP in confidence.

pg_3996.label: If the company does not resolve the issue, allow CHIRP to confidentially approach Port State Control and/or the flag administration.

pg_3997.label: Maintain accurate, unfalsified Hours of Rest records.

pg_3998.label: Continue correspondence with CHIRP and supply evidence as requested.

pg_3999.label: Treat any water collected from tank tops as bilge water requiring proper handling.

pg_4000.label: Isolate the affected tank immediately once contamination is discovered.

pg_4001.label: Deliver tank contents to a shore facility as oily bilge water.

pg_4002.label: Report any incident, near-accident, nonconformity, or unsafe act/condition to the supervisor immediately upon noticing it.

pg_4003.label: Take 'time out for safety' to plan before operations and 'stop the job' if in doubt about a safe outcome.

pg_4004.label: Exercise the authority and duty to stop any work considered unsafe and report it to the proper onboard authority.

pg_4005.label: Operate a pump to reduce the flood level in the engine room once bilge level reached 0.3m.

pg_4006.label: Make additional isolations to stop water continuing to enter the space.

pg_4007.label: Hold contaminated bilge/floodwater in the bilge holding tank before discharging through the oily water separator.

pg_4008.label: Suspend pilot boarding operations immediately upon identifying unsafe rigging.

pg_4009.label: Direct crew to rectify the deficiency (rig stanchions/ropes fully) before resuming boarding.

pg_4010.label: If the ladder is not secured to the ship's side, turn the vessel around and take corrective action.

pg_4011.label: Secure the pilot ladder and gangway using magnets as needed.

pg_4012.label: Treat all water from engine room bottom plates or tank tops as bilge water.

pg_4013.label: Route this water through the oily water separator before any discharge.

pg_4014.label: Only deviate from MARPOL discharge rules if doing so is necessary to save the vessel in a genuine emergency.

pg_4015.label: Suspend pilot boarding until a compliant ladder arrangement is rigged.

pg_4016.label: Fit a scupper plug prior to each pilot transfer operation.

pg_4017.label: Positively confirm that any identified discharge has stopped before the pilot commences climbing.

pg_4018.label: Apply the hierarchy of controls (elimination, substitution/engineering, administrative, PPE) to mitigate the hazard.

pg_4019.label: Ensure checklists and training regimes are fit for purpose and manpower demands are realistic.

pg_4020.label: Engage shipyards, naval architects, and regulators on new builds to design out discharge proximity issues.

pg_4021.label: Ensure the pilot embarkation area is clear of any water accumulation before boarding begins.

pg_4022.label: Ensure no water can drain from scuppers during pilot boarding or disembarking.

pg_4023.label: Responsible officers must properly understand and act on safety concerns raised by the pilot.

pg_4024.label: Company to issue fleet-wide instructions following investigation of reported hazards.

pg_4025.label: Ensure life-saving appliances, including life rafts, are effectively secured on deck in their intended abandonment-ready position, not stored in accommodation.

pg_4026.label: Review whether severe weather and safety checklists are genuinely followed rather than used as a 'tick box' exercise.

pg_4027.label: Investigate and address the onboard and company culture that discourages crew from reporting safety concerns to the master or DPA.

pg_4028.label: Strengthen the DPA's self-monitoring function to ensure it can detect and respond to safety failures.

pg_4029.label: Validate all navigation and steering instruments on board against actual physical readings.

pg_4030.label: Have personnel confirm the actual rudder angle at the steering gear matches the helm or rudder indicator display.

pg_4031.label: Verify rudder angle indicator accuracy is within +/- 1 degree per Class requirement.

pg_4032.label: Recognise the potential seriousness of an un-housed stabilizer fin during narrow channel transit.

pg_4033.label: Abort the port entry to allow time to resolve the issue.

pg_4034.label: Have ship's engineers manually override the automatic stabilizer system to house the fin.

pg_4035.label: Recommence port entry once the stabilizer was successfully housed.

pg_4036.label: Apply port helm to clear the anchored vessel ahead

pg_4037.label: Apply hard port helm when initial port helm produced no response

pg_4038.label: Apply hard starboard helm when collision appeared inevitable

pg_4039.label: Anchor the vessel after clearing the close-quarters situation

pg_4040.label: Advise management and have the steering gear inspected

pg_4041.label: Locate and re-adjust the near-invisible alignment markings on the steering gear

pg_4042.label: Further investigate to confirm what the indicator actually measures

pg_4043.label: Ascertain on any ship how the rudder angle indicator actually works and inform management if it only shows helm angle, requesting modification

pg_4044.label: When any automatic system is suspected of malfunctioning, have responsible personnel carry out all necessary checks to positively confirm its actual status.

pg_4045.label: Rectify any confirmed defect before relying on the system again.

pg_4046.label: Test and verify safety-critical systems, including manual override of remote-control systems, well ahead of when they may be needed.

pg_4047.label: Maintain good ER/Bridge communication throughout the approach.

pg_4048.label: Identify and act decisively at the 'final abort position' when committing to a port approach is no longer safe.

pg_4049.label: Maintain a proper lookout at all times on all vessels.

pg_4050.label: Keep engines at immediate readiness for both vessels in a developing close-quarters situation.

pg_4051.label: Use VHF communications early and proactively, but do not rely on VHF if immediate action is needed.

pg_4052.label: Identify that the ladder's weight is being supported by a bracket/step fitting instead of the side ropes.

pg_4053.label: Explain the rigging issue to the master and advise that the weight should be supported by the side ropes.

pg_4054.label: After berthing, go to the ladder and explain to the Chief Mate how ropes should be secured to the side-ropes to take the weight.

pg_4055.label: Exhibit anchor ball by day and anchor light by night while at anchor on a fishing mark.

pg_4056.label: Monitor surrounding vessel traffic periodically using radar/visual checks.

pg_4057.label: Attempt to attract attention by shouting and sounding the foghorn when a vessel closes dangerously.

pg_4058.label: Cut the anchor rope and start the engine to motor away when time does not permit raising the anchor.

pg_4059.label: Report the near miss to the Harbour Master's office having jurisdiction over the area.

pg_4060.label: Report the non-compliant pilot ladder rigging arrangement to CHIRP/the company

pg_4061.label: DPA acknowledges the observation and engages with the reporting body

pg_4062.label: DPA initiates rectifying actions across the vessel series

pg_4063.label: Report suspected illegal discharge confidentially to CHIRP.

pg_4064.label: CHIRP requests further details from the reporter while preserving confidentiality.

pg_4065.label: CHIRP offers to contact flag state administration and USCG (Port State Control) given the vessel's trading area.

pg_4066.label: Reporter separately contacts the ITF, who liaise with Port State Control.

pg_4067.label: PSC boards and inspects the vessel at its next port visit.

pg_4068.label: CHIRP closes the case with no further action once PSC confirms the vessel has been placed on regional watchlists.

pg_4069.label: Notify Port State Control / flag state authorities of credible pollution reports, with reporter consent.

pg_4070.label: Maintain strict confidentiality of the reporter's identity throughout and after the investigation.

pg_4071.label: Delete reporter's name from all records upon completion of correspondence.

pg_4072.label: Encourage seafarers to approach the Designated Person Ashore (DPA) directly with concerns.

pg_4073.label: Ensure necessary safety tools and equipment (harnesses, life vests) are available and used before crew undertake tasks in hazardous areas.

pg_4074.label: Intervene immediately if work is being conducted unsafely.

pg_4075.label: Consider design shortcomings (lack of handrails/securing points) when planning routine tasks such as washing down or inspections, and adapt work methods or equipment accordingly.

pg_4076.label: Master must declare all equipment defects in advance of pilot boarding, not just verbally minimize them during MPX.

pg_4077.label: Pilot must independently verify navigation equipment status (radar mode, gyro repeaters, rate of turn indicator) rather than relying solely on the master's assessment.

pg_4078.label: Pilot should assess whether degraded equipment (unstabilised head-up radar with no heading, failed gyro repeaters) permits safe pilotage, or whether transit should be limited to daylight and fair weather.

pg_4079.label: Arrange for a technician to attend upon arrival alongside only after confirming the defects do not compromise the immediate inward passage.

pg_4080.label: Attempt to engage engine astern to stop headway

pg_4081.label: If engine fails to start astern after repeated attempts, use tugs to arrest headway

pg_4082.label: Once stopped, test main engine ahead and astern before continuing

pg_4083.label: Master must inform pilots that engine requires speed below 3 knots to start astern

pg_4084.label: Exchange this engine limitation information during the Master-Pilot Exchange (MPX)

pg_4085.label: Order midships (or test helm command) when the rudder angle indicator shows an unexpected or unresponsive reading.

pg_4086.label: Verify actual vessel response to helm independently of the indicator (e.g., observe vessel behaviour/heading change).

pg_4087.label: Continue the transit with additional precautions, such as tug escort, once it is confirmed the rudder is responding correctly despite the faulty indicator.

pg_4088.label: Report any rudder angle indicator defects to the pilot/relevant parties during the Master-Pilot Exchange (MPX), including recurring issues from previous ports.

pg_4089.label: Assign completion of the pilot card (per IMO Res A601(15)) to bridge staff, even junior watchkeepers or cadets.

pg_4090.label: Master must assiduously check the completed pilot card before it is presented to the pilot.

pg_4091.label: Master must report defects, deficiencies and anomalies affecting vessel operability to shore management.

pg_4092.label: Follow up reported deficiencies thoroughly to satisfactory closure, including rectification and preventive measures.

pg_4093.label: Pilot should report defects, deficiencies and anomalies impinging on vessel operability to port authorities.

pg_4094.label: Disclose all known defects openly to relevant parties (e.g. during PSC inspections or MPX), following the aviation industry's open disclosure model.

pg_4095.label: Conduct a full, frank and comprehensive Master-Pilot Exchange before and during pilotage.

pg_4096.label: As Master, seek guidance and confirmation that information from pilot books and other sources matches the pilot's input.

pg_4097.label: Comply fully with the Collision Regulations, including Rule 10, in TSS areas.

pg_4098.label: Deep draft vessels should advise local VTS and/or Coastal Radio Station of ETA, position, and transit speed.

pg_4099.label: Report rogue vessels that blatantly contravene the Collision Regulations to the authorities, especially where radar surveillance/monitoring exists.

pg_4100.label: Rig man ropes correctly per pilot transfer arrangement requirements.

pg_4101.label: Attach the pilot ladder to the ship's side at least 1.5m above the accommodation ladder platform.

pg_4102.label: Resolve the non-compliant trap door/shackle arrangement as soon as possible, especially given regular calls to this and other ports.
