pg_4946.label: Organization may convene a revision Conference on its own initiative or must convene one if requested by at least one-third of Contracting Parties.

pg_4947.label: A Contracting Party proposing an amendment to the Regulations requests consideration by the Organization.

pg_4948.label: Maritime Safety Committee adopts proposed amendment by two-thirds majority of those present and voting, then communicates it to all Contracting Parties and Members at least six months before Assembly consideration.

pg_4949.label: Assembly adopts the amendment by two-thirds majority of those present and voting; Secretary-General communicates it to all Contracting Parties for acceptance.

pg_4950.label: Amendment enters into force on date set by Assembly unless more than one-third of Contracting Parties object by a prior deadline also set by the Assembly (itself decided by two-thirds majority).

pg_4951.label: On entry into force, the amendment replaces prior provisions for all non-objecting Contracting Parties; Secretary-General informs all Parties/Members of requests, communications, and entry-into-force dates.

pg_4952.label: A Contracting Party may denounce the Convention only after five years from its entry into force for that Party, by depositing an instrument with the Organization.

pg_4953.label: Secretary-General informs all other Contracting Parties of receipt and deposit date of the denunciation instrument; denunciation takes effect one year (or longer if specified) after deposit.

pg_4954.label: Use all available means appropriate to the prevailing circumstances and conditions (e.g. radar, AIS, binoculars, sound signals).

pg_4955.label: Continuously assess the situation to determine risk of collision.

pg_4956.label: Maintain a speed that allows proper and effective action to avoid collision and permits stopping within a distance appropriate to prevailing circumstances and conditions.

pg_4957.label: Assess visibility, traffic density (including fishing vessel concentrations), own manoeuvrability/stopping distance/turning ability, background night lighting, wind/sea/current state, proximity of navigational hazards, and draught versus available water depth.

pg_4958.label: If operating radar, additionally assess radar equipment characteristics/limitations, range scale constraints, effects of sea state/weather/interference on detection, risk of missing small vessels/ice/floating objects, number/location/movement of radar-detected vessels, and use radar for more exact visibility/range assessment.

pg_4959.label: Use all available means appropriate to prevailing circumstances to determine if risk of collision exists.

pg_4960.label: If any doubt exists about risk of collision, treat risk as existing.

pg_4961.label: Properly use fitted and operational radar, including long-range scanning and systematic plotting or equivalent observation.

pg_4962.label: Avoid making assumptions based on scanty information, especially scanty radar data.

pg_4963.label: Deem risk of collision to exist if the compass bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change.

pg_4964.label: Consider that risk may still exist despite an appreciable bearing change, especially near very large vessels, tows, or vessels at close range.

pg_4965.label: Make any alteration of course and/or speed large enough to be readily apparent to another vessel visually or by radar; avoid successive small alterations.

pg_4966.label: If sufficient sea room exists, consider alteration of course alone as the most effective action, provided it is made in good time, is substantial, and does not create a new close-quarters situation.

pg_4967.label: Ensure the action results in passing at a safe distance and continuously monitor its effectiveness until the other vessel is finally past and clear.

pg_4968.label: If necessary, slacken speed, stop, or reverse propulsion to avoid collision or to gain more time to assess the situation.

pg_4969.label: If required not to impede another vessel's passage, take early action to allow sufficient sea room for that vessel's safe passage.

pg_4970.label: Even when obligated not to impede another vessel, continue to take action having full regard to the Rules of this Part if risk of collision develops.

pg_4971.label: Keep as near to the outer limit of the channel/fairway on your starboard side as is safe and practicable.

pg_4972.label: If less than 20m in length or a sailing vessel, do not impede vessels that can only navigate safely within the channel.

pg_4973.label: If engaged in fishing, do not impede the passage of any other vessel navigating within the channel.

pg_4974.label: Do not cross a narrow channel if it would impede a vessel that can only navigate safely within it.

pg_4975.label: If in doubt about a crossing vessel's intentions, sound the Rule 34(d) signal.

pg_4976.label: When overtaking requires the overtaken vessel to take action, the overtaking vessel must sound the Rule 34(c)(i) signal to indicate intent.

pg_4977.label: The vessel being overtaken, if in agreement, sounds the Rule 34(c)(ii) signal and takes steps to permit safe passing; if in doubt, sounds Rule 34(d) signals.

pg_4978.label: Remember that overtaking in a narrow channel does not relieve the overtaking vessel of her Rule 13 obligations.

pg_4979.label: When nearing a bend or obstruction that may obscure other vessels, navigate with particular alertness and caution and sound the Rule 34(e) signal.

pg_4980.label: Avoid anchoring in a narrow channel if circumstances permit.

pg_4981.label: Determine whether the restricted-in-ability-to-manoeuvre vessel is engaged in a safety-of-navigation maintenance operation or a submarine cable operation within the TSS.

pg_4982.label: Allow such vessel to depart from Rule 10 requirements only to the extent necessary to carry out the specific operation.

pg_4983.label: Proceed in the appropriate traffic lane in the general direction of traffic flow.

pg_4984.label: Keep clear of traffic separation lines and separation zones so far as practicable.

pg_4985.label: Join or leave a traffic lane normally at the lane's termination; if joining/leaving from the side, do so at the smallest practicable angle to traffic flow.

pg_4986.label: Avoid crossing traffic lanes where practicable; if crossing is unavoidable, cross on a heading as near as practicable to right angles to traffic flow.

pg_4987.label: Do not use the inshore traffic zone if the adjacent traffic lane can be safely used, unless the vessel is under 20m, a sailing vessel, or engaged in fishing.

pg_4988.label: A vessel may use the inshore traffic zone when en route to/from a port, offshore installation, pilot station, or other place in the zone, or to avoid immediate danger.

pg_4989.label: Do not normally enter a separation zone or cross a separation line except in emergency to avoid immediate danger or to fish within the zone.

pg_4990.label: Navigate with particular caution near the terminations of traffic separation schemes.

pg_4991.label: Avoid anchoring in a TSS or near its terminations so far as practicable.

pg_4992.label: If not using the TSS, avoid it by as wide a margin as practicable.

pg_4993.label: Fishing vessels must not impede vessels following a traffic lane.

pg_4994.label: Vessels under 20m or sailing vessels must not impede the safe passage of power-driven vessels following a traffic lane.

pg_4995.label: Alter course to starboard so that each vessel passes on the port side of the other.

pg_4996.label: Identify a head-on situation by observing the other vessel ahead or nearly ahead with masthead lights in line and/or both sidelights (night) or corresponding aspect (day).

pg_4997.label: If in any doubt as to whether a head-on situation exists, assume that it does and act accordingly by altering course to starboard.

pg_4998.label: Determine whether you are approaching another vessel from more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam (i.e., you would only see her sternlight at night, not her sidelights).

pg_4999.label: If any doubt exists as to whether you are overtaking, assume that you are and act accordingly.

pg_5000.label: As the overtaking vessel, keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken, regardless of other Part B Section I and II rules.

pg_5001.label: Maintain the duty to keep clear even if the bearing between the two vessels subsequently changes, until finally past and clear.

pg_5002.label: Identify that the other power-driven vessel is on your own starboard side.

pg_5003.label: Keep out of the way of the vessel on your starboard side.

pg_5004.label: Avoid crossing ahead of the other vessel if circumstances of the case admit.

pg_5005.label: Determine which side of each vessel the wind is on.

pg_5006.label: If each vessel has the wind on a different side, the vessel with wind on the port side must keep out of the way of the other.

pg_5007.label: If both vessels have the wind on the same side, the windward vessel must keep out of the way of the leeward vessel.

pg_5008.label: If a vessel with wind on the port side sees a vessel to windward and cannot determine with certainty which side the other vessel has the wind on, she shall keep out of the way of the other.

pg_5009.label: Determine windward side as the side opposite to where the mainsail is carried (or largest fore-and-aft sail for square-rigged vessels).

pg_5010.label: Comply with the shape and light rules in all weather conditions.

pg_5011.label: Exhibit prescribed navigation lights from sunset to sunrise.

pg_5012.label: Do not display any other lights that could be mistaken for, impair visibility of, or interfere with recognition of prescribed lights, or that interfere with proper lookout.

pg_5013.label: Exhibit prescribed lights (if carried) from sunrise to sunset when visibility is restricted, and may exhibit them at other times when deemed necessary.

pg_5014.label: Display prescribed shapes during daylight hours.

pg_5015.label: Ensure all lights and shapes conform to the technical specifications in Annex I.

pg_5016.label: As a power-driven vessel underway, keep out of the way of a vessel not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, engaged in fishing, or under sail.

pg_5017.label: Unless not under command or restricted in ability to manoeuvre, avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draught exhibiting Rule 28 signals, if circumstances admit.

pg_5018.label: As a vessel constrained by draught, navigate with particular caution having full regard to her special condition.

pg_5019.label: As a seaplane on the water, keep well clear of all vessels and avoid impeding navigation generally; comply with Part B Rules if risk of collision exists.

pg_5020.label: As a WIG craft taking off, landing, or in flight near the surface, keep well clear of all vessels and avoid impeding navigation; when operating on the water, comply with Part B Rules as a power-driven vessel.

pg_5021.label: Have engines ready for immediate manoeuvre (power-driven vessels).

pg_5022.label: Apply Section I steering/sailing rules with due regard to restricted visibility conditions.

pg_5023.label: When another vessel is detected by radar alone, determine if a close-quarters situation or risk of collision is developing.

pg_5024.label: If risk exists, take avoiding action in ample time.

pg_5025.label: If hearing a fog signal apparently forward of the beam, or unable to avoid a close-quarters situation with a vessel forward of the beam, reduce speed to the minimum at which the vessel can be kept on course.

pg_5026.label: If necessary, take all way off.

pg_5027.label: Navigate with extreme caution until the danger of collision is over.

pg_5028.label: Recognize that the give-way vessel remains obligated to keep out of the way regardless of stand-on vessel's actions.

pg_5029.label: Exhibit a masthead light forward, a second masthead light abaft and higher than the forward one, sidelights, and a sternlight.

pg_5030.label: If the vessel is less than 50 meters in length, the second (aft) masthead light may be omitted, though it may still be carried.

pg_5031.label: If operating as an air-cushion vessel in non-displacement mode, exhibit an all-round flashing yellow light in addition to the standard lights.

pg_5032.label: If the vessel is a WIG craft taking off, landing, or flying near the surface, exhibit a high intensity all-round flashing red light in addition to the standard lights.

pg_5033.label: If the vessel is less than 12 meters in length, may substitute an all-round white light and sidelights in lieu of the standard masthead/sternlight configuration.

pg_5034.label: If the vessel is less than 7 meters in length and max speed does not exceed 7 knots, may exhibit only an all-round white light, and should exhibit sidelights if practicable.

pg_5035.label: If centreline fitting of the masthead light or all-round white light is not practicable on a vessel under 12 meters, it may be displaced off-centreline, provided sidelights are combined in one lantern on the centreline or as near as practicable to the masthead/all-round light's fore-and-aft line.

pg_5036.label: If towing astern, exhibit two masthead lights in a vertical line instead of Rule 23(a)(i)/(a)(ii) lights (three if tow length exceeds 200m), plus sidelights, sternlight, and a towing light above the sternlight.

pg_5037.label: If tow length exceeds 200 metres, exhibit a diamond shape where it can best be seen (on both towing vessel and the tow).

pg_5038.label: If pushing ahead or towing alongside (not a composite unit), exhibit two masthead lights in a vertical line, sidelights, and a sternlight.

pg_5039.label: If pushing vessel and pushed vessel are rigidly connected as a composite unit, exhibit lights prescribed in Rule 23 as for a single power-driven vessel.

pg_5040.label: Ensure vessels/objects being towed exhibit sidelights and a sternlight, and a diamond shape if tow exceeds 200 metres.

pg_5041.label: For vessels towed alongside or pushed in a group, light the group as one vessel, with pushed vessel showing sidelights forward and towed-alongside vessel showing sternlight and forward sidelights.

pg_5042.label: Also comply with Rule 23(a)(ii) (additional light requirement) when paragraph (a) or (c) applies.

pg_5043.label: If the towed object is less than 25 metres in breadth, exhibit one all-round white light at or near the forward end and one at or near the after end (dracones exempt from forward light).

pg_5044.label: If the towed object is 25 metres or more in breadth, add two additional all-round white lights at or near the extremities of its breadth.

pg_5045.label: If the tow exceeds 100 metres in length, add intermediate all-round white lights so spacing between lights does not exceed 100 metres.

pg_5046.label: Exhibit a diamond shape at or near the aftermost extremity of the last vessel/object towed; if tow length exceeds 200 metres, add another diamond shape as far forward as practicable.

pg_5047.label: If it is impracticable to exhibit the prescribed lights/shapes for the towed vessel/object, take all possible measures to light it or otherwise indicate its presence.

pg_5048.label: If a vessel not normally engaged in towing cannot display the normal towing lights while towing a vessel in distress or needing assistance, it is exempted from those lights but must take all possible measures (e.g., illuminating the towline) to indicate the towing relationship per Rule 36.

pg_5049.label: Exhibit sidelights and a sternlight while a sailing vessel is underway.

pg_5050.label: If vessel is less than 20 metres, may combine sidelights and sternlight into one lantern carried at or near the masthead.

pg_5051.label: Optionally exhibit two all-round lights in a vertical line (red over green) at or near the masthead, in addition to paragraph (a) lights.

pg_5052.label: For vessels under 7 metres, exhibit lights of (a) or (b) if practicable; otherwise keep an electric torch or lighted lantern with white light ready at hand and show it in time to prevent collision.

pg_5053.label: For vessels under oars, exhibit sailing vessel lights if possible; otherwise keep a torch/lantern with white light ready and show it in time to prevent collision.

pg_5054.label: When a sailing vessel is also being propelled by machinery, exhibit a conical shape, apex downwards, forward where it can best be seen.

pg_5055.label: If engaged in fishing, exhibit only the lights/shapes prescribed in this Rule and no others.

pg_5056.label: If trawling, show two all-round lights vertical (green over white) or two cones apex-to-apex vertically.

pg_5057.label: If trawling and 50m or more in length, also show a masthead light abaft and higher than the green all-round light (optional if under 50m).

pg_5058.label: If making way through the water while trawling or fishing, add sidelights and a sternlight to the prescribed fishing lights.

pg_5059.label: If outlying gear extends more than 150 metres horizontally, exhibit an all-round white light or a cone apex upward in the direction of the gear.

pg_5060.label: When in close proximity to other fishing vessels, apply the additional signals in Annex II.

pg_5061.label: When not engaged in fishing, do not display fishing lights/shapes; show only lights prescribed for the vessel's length.

pg_5062.label: Exhibit the normal power-driven vessel lights required under Rule 23.

pg_5063.label: Additionally exhibit, where they can best be seen, three all-round red lights in a vertical line (at night) or a cylinder (by day) to indicate constrained-by-draught status.

pg_5064.label: If not under command, exhibit two all-round red lights in a vertical line and two balls/similar shapes in a vertical line where best seen.

pg_5065.label: If not under command and making way through the water, also show sidelights and a sternlight.

pg_5066.label: If restricted in ability to manoeuvre (except mineclearance), exhibit three vertical all-round lights (red-white-red) or three shapes (ball-diamond-ball) where best seen.

pg_5067.label: If restricted in ability to manoeuvre and making way, add masthead light(s), sidelights, and sternlight to the prescribed lights.

pg_5068.label: If restricted in ability to manoeuvre and at anchor, add the anchor light/shape prescribed in Rule 30 to the restricted-manoeuvrability lights/shapes.

pg_5069.label: If a power-driven vessel is towing in a manner that severely restricts the tow's ability to deviate course, exhibit Rule 24(a) towing lights/shapes plus the restricted-in-ability-to-manoeuvre lights/shapes (b)(i) and (ii).

pg_5070.label: If engaged in dredging/underwater operations and restricted in ability to manoeuvre, exhibit (b)(i),(ii),(iii) lights/shapes, and when an obstruction exists, show two red lights/balls on the obstructed side and two green lights/diamonds on the passing side.

pg_5071.label: If the dredging/underwater operations vessel is at anchor, exhibit the obstruction-indicating lights/shapes in lieu of the Rule 30 anchor light/shape.

pg_5072.label: If impracticable to exhibit all diving-operation lights/shapes, display three all-round lights in a vertical line (red-white-red from top to bottom) where best seen, plus a rigid replica of Code flag 'A' at least 1 metre high with all-round visibility.

pg_5073.label: For mineclearance operations, exhibit power-driven vessel lights (Rule 23) or anchor lights/shape (Rule 30) as appropriate, plus three all-round green lights or three balls positioned near the foremast head and at each end of the fore yard.

pg_5074.label: Do not require vessels under 12 metres (except diving vessels) to exhibit the Rule 27 lights and shapes.

pg_5075.label: Do not interpret Rule 27 signals as distress signals; refer to Annex IV for actual distress signals.

pg_5076.label: When combining Not Under Command (NUC) red lights with Restricted Ability to Manoeuvre (RAM) lights, ensure vertical/horizontal spacing complies with COLREG and that the RAM white light can be switched on independently from the two NUC red lights.

pg_5077.label: Exhibit two all-round lights in a vertical line at or near the masthead, upper white and lower red, at all times while engaged on pilotage duty.

pg_5078.label: When at anchor, additionally exhibit the light(s) or shape prescribed in Rule 30 for vessels at anchor, in addition to the masthead pilotage lights.

pg_5079.label: When not engaged on pilotage duty, exhibit the lights or shapes prescribed for a vessel of her length instead of pilotage lights.

pg_5080.label: Exhibit an all-round white light or ball forward, and a second all-round white light aft at a lower level, when at anchor.

pg_5081.label: If vessel is less than 50 metres in length, may exhibit a single all-round white light instead of the two-light configuration.

pg_5082.label: Use working or equivalent deck lights to illuminate decks; mandatory for vessels 100 metres and more in length.

pg_5083.label: If aground, exhibit the anchor lights/shape from (a) or (b) plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line and three balls in a vertical line.

pg_5084.label: If vessel is less than 7 metres and not anchored in or near a narrow channel, fairway, or anchorage, or where vessels normally navigate, anchor lights/shapes are not required.

pg_5085.label: If vessel is less than 12 metres and aground, the additional red lights/balls under (d)(i) and (ii) are not required.

pg_5086.label: Equip vessels of 12 metres or more in length with a whistle.

pg_5087.label: Equip vessels of 100 metres or more in length with a gong whose tone cannot be confused with the bell, in addition to whistle and bell.

pg_5088.label: Ensure whistle, bell, and gong comply with Annex III specifications.

pg_5089.label: If replacing bell or gong with other equipment, ensure manual sounding capability is always retained.

pg_5090.label: For vessels less than 12 metres, provide some other means of making an efficient sound signal if whistle/bell/gong are not carried.

pg_5091.label: Sound one short blast when altering course to starboard.

pg_5092.label: Sound two short blasts when altering course to port.

pg_5093.label: Sound three short blasts when operating astern propulsion.

pg_5094.label: Optionally supplement whistle signals with light signals (flashes matching blast counts) during the manoeuvre.

pg_5095.label: Ensure light signal flashes last about one second with one second intervals, and at least ten seconds between successive signals, using an all-round white light visible at least 5 miles complying with Annex I.

pg_5096.label: In a narrow channel or fairway, when intending to overtake, sound two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast (overtake on starboard) or two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts (overtake on port).

pg_5097.label: As the vessel being overtaken, if in agreement, sound one prolonged, one short, one prolonged and one short blast in that order.

pg_5098.label: Sound one prolonged blast when nearing a bend or obstructed area of a channel/fairway.

pg_5099.label: Answer with a prolonged blast if you are an approaching vessel within hearing around the bend or behind the obstruction.

pg_5100.label: Use only one whistle for manoeuvring and warning signals if whistles are fitted more than 100 metres apart.

pg_5101.label: Optionally supplement the manoeuvring/warning sound signal with a light signal of at least five short and rapid flashes.

pg_5102.label: If power-driven and making way through the water, sound one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

pg_5103.label: If power-driven, underway but stopped and making no way, sound two prolonged blasts with about 2 seconds between them, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

pg_5104.label: If not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, constrained by draught, a sailing vessel, engaged in fishing, or towing/pushing another vessel, sound one prolonged followed by two short blasts at intervals of not more than 2 minutes instead of (a) or (b) signals.

pg_5105.label: If a fishing vessel at anchor or a vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre while working at anchor, sound the Rule 35(c) signal instead of the anchor signal in paragraph (g).

pg_5106.label: If being towed (last vessel of a tow, if manned), sound one prolonged followed by three short blasts at intervals of not more than 2 minutes, made immediately after the towing vessel's signal when practicable.

pg_5107.label: If a pushing vessel and pushed vessel are rigidly connected as a composite unit, treat the unit as a power-driven vessel and use signals (a) or (b).

pg_5108.label: If at anchor, ring the bell rapidly for about 5 seconds at intervals of not more than one minute; vessels 100m or more in length must also sound the gong in the after part immediately after the bell in the forepart.

pg_5109.label: A vessel at anchor may sound one short, one prolonged, one short blast in addition to required signals to warn an approaching vessel of her position and collision risk.

pg_5110.label: A vessel aground shall give the bell signal (and gong signal if required) plus three separate distinct strokes on the bell immediately before and after rapid bell ringing.

pg_5111.label: A vessel aground may additionally sound an appropriate whistle signal.

pg_5112.label: A vessel 12m to <20m in length not giving the prescribed bell signals shall instead make some other efficient sound signal at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

pg_5113.label: A pilot vessel engaged on pilotage duty may sound an identity signal of four short blasts in addition to signals under paragraphs (a), (b) or (g).

pg_5114.label: Make light or sound signals that cannot be mistaken for any signal authorized elsewhere in the Rules, if necessary to attract another vessel's attention.

pg_5115.label: Alternatively, direct the beam of a searchlight toward the direction of danger.

pg_5116.label: Ensure the searchlight beam does not embarrass (dazzle/confuse) any vessel.

pg_5117.label: Ensure any attention-attracting light cannot be mistaken for an aid to navigation.

pg_5118.label: Avoid using high intensity intermittent or revolving lights, such as strobe lights, for this purpose.

pg_5119.label: Verify the vessel complies with the 1960 Collision Regulations and was laid down/under corresponding construction stage before the 1972 Regulations' entry into force.

pg_5120.label: Apply the four-year exemption for light range (Rule 22) and light colour specification (Annex I Section 7) installations.

pg_5121.label: Treat repositioning of lights due to Imperial-to-metric conversion and rounding as permanently exempt.

pg_5122.label: Apply permanent exemption for masthead light repositioning on vessels under 150 meters under Annex I Section 3(a); apply nine-year exemption for vessels 150 meters or more.

pg_5123.label: Apply nine-year exemptions for masthead light repositioning (Annex I Section 2(b)), sidelight repositioning (Annex I Sections 2(g) and 3(b)), and sound signal appliance requirements (Annex III).

pg_5124.label: Treat repositioning of all-round lights under Annex I Section 9(b) as permanently exempt.

pg_5125.label: Subject the Contracting Party to periodic audits per the audit standard.

pg_5126.label: Secretary-General administers the Audit Scheme per Organization guidelines.

pg_5127.label: Contracting Party facilitates the audit and implements a programme of actions addressing findings.

pg_5128.label: Conduct audits based on an overall schedule and at periodic intervals set by the Secretary-General.

pg_5129.label: Measure 'height above the hull' vertically from the point directly beneath the light's position to the uppermost continuous deck.

pg_5130.label: On a power-driven vessel of 20 metres or more, place the forward (or sole) masthead light at least 6 metres above the hull, increasing to match the vessel's breadth if it exceeds 6 metres, up to a maximum of 12 metres.

pg_5131.label: When carrying two masthead lights, position the after light at least 4.5 metres vertically higher than the forward light.

pg_5132.label: Ensure vertical separation of masthead lights is sufficient that the after light remains visible over and separate from the forward light at 1,000 metres from the stem, viewed from sea level, in all normal trim conditions.

pg_5133.label: On a power-driven vessel of 12 to less than 20 metres in length, place the masthead light at least 2.5 metres above the gunwale.

pg_5134.label: Space two prescribed masthead lights horizontally not less than half the vessel's length apart, up to a maximum of 100 m.

pg_5135.label: Place the forward masthead light no more than one quarter of the vessel's length from the stem.

pg_5136.label: On power-driven vessels of 20 m or more, position sidelights at or near the side of the vessel and not forward of the forward masthead light.

pg_5137.label: When all-round lights under Rule 27(b)(i) or Rule 28 are placed vertically between masthead lights, position them at least 2 m horizontally from the vessel's fore-and-aft centreline.

pg_5138.label: If only one masthead light is prescribed, exhibit it forward of amidships, except vessels under 20 m may exhibit it as far forward as practicable.

pg_5139.label: Interpret 'near the side' as no more than 10% of the vessel's breadth inboard from the side, up to a maximum of 1 metre.

pg_5140.label: Space two or three vertically arranged lights not less than 2 metres apart on vessels 20 m or more in length, with the lowest light at least 4 m above the hull (unless it is a towing light).

pg_5141.label: Equally space the lights when three are carried in a vertical line.

pg_5142.label: Place the lower of the two all-round fishing lights at a height above the sidelights not less than twice the distance between the two vertical lights.

pg_5143.label: When two anchor lights are carried, separate the forward anchor light from the after one by not less than 4.5 metres; on vessels 50 m or more in length, place the forward anchor light at least 6 metres above the hull.

pg_5144.label: When a masthead light or Rule 23(c)(i) all-round light is carried in addition to sidelights and sternlight, mount it at least 1 metre higher than the sidelights.

pg_5145.label: For a power-driven vessel towing or pushing another vessel, place one of the two/three masthead lights in the position of the forward or after masthead light, and if on the aftermast, keep the lowest after masthead light at least 4.5 metres higher than the forward masthead light.

pg_5146.label: Position Rule 23(a) masthead lights above and clear of all other lights and obstructions, except where Rule 27(b)(i)/28 all-round lights cannot be placed below them.

pg_5147.label: If all-round lights cannot be placed below the masthead lights, carry them above the after masthead light(s) or vertically between the forward and after masthead lights, complying with Annex I Section 3(c).

pg_5148.label: Place sidelights of a power-driven vessel at a height above the hull not exceeding three-quarters of the forward masthead light's height, and keep them clear of interference from deck lights.

pg_5149.label: For vessels under 20 metres with a combined sidelight lantern, mount it at least 1 metre below the masthead light.

pg_5150.label: Verify navigation light colours fall within the specified CIE chromaticity coordinate boundaries for white, green, red, and yellow.

pg_5151.label: Calculate or verify minimum luminous intensity using the formula I = 3.43×10^6 × T × D^2 × K^-D, or reference the provided table for required range of visibility.

pg_5152.label: Ensure maximum luminous intensity is limited, but not via variable control.

pg_5153.label: Ensure electric navigation lights (except on sailing vessels underway) maintain at least the required minimum intensity from 5° above to 5° below horizontal, and at least 60% from 7.5° above to 7.5° below horizontal.

pg_5154.label: Match these intensity specifications as closely as possible for non-electric lights.

pg_5155.label: Comply with minimum intensities for non-electric lights as specified in the Table in Section 8 of the Annex, so far as practicable.

pg_5156.label: Fit sidelights so minimum required intensity decreases to practical cut-off between 1 and 3 degrees outside prescribed sectors.

pg_5157.label: Maintain minimum required intensity of sternlights, masthead lights, and sidelights (at 22.5 degrees abaft the beam) up to 5 degrees within sector limits, then decrease to cut-off at no more than 5 degrees outside prescribed sectors.

pg_5158.label: Locate all-round lights so they are not obscured by masts, topmasts, or structures over sectors exceeding 6 degrees, except anchor lights.

pg_5159.label: If one all-round light cannot meet the obscuration requirement, use two all-round lights positioned or screened to appear as one light at one mile, with screened angles satisfying θ2 ≤ 360 - θ1.

pg_5160.label: Place the outlying gear direction light of a fishing vessel 2-6 metres horizontally from the two all-round red and white lights, no higher than the all-round white light and no lower than the sidelights.

pg_5161.label: Place obstructed-side/safe-passing-side lights or shapes on a dredging/underwater-operations vessel at maximum practical horizontal distance (minimum 2 metres) from the Rule 27(b)(i)/(ii) lights or shapes, with the upper light/shape never higher than the lowest of the three Rule 27(b) lights/shapes.

pg_5162.label: Fit inboard matt black screens to sidelights on vessels 20 metres or more in length, meeting Section 9 requirements; fit similar screens on vessels under 20 metres only if needed to meet Section 9.

pg_5163.label: Omit external screens where a combined lantern uses a single vertical filament with a very narrow green/red division.

pg_5164.label: Use shapes of specified minimum dimensions (ball ≥0.6m diameter, cone base ≥0.6m diameter with height equal to diameter, cylinder diameter ≥0.6m and height twice diameter, diamond as two cones on common base) spaced at least 1.5 metres apart vertically.

pg_5165.label: On vessels under 20 metres, scale down shape dimensions and spacing proportionately to vessel size.

pg_5166.label: Place the manoeuvring light (Rule 34(b)) in the same fore-and-aft vertical plane as the masthead light(s).

pg_5167.label: Where practicable, mount the manoeuvring light at least 2 metres vertically above the forward masthead light, and not less than 2 metres above or below the after masthead light.

pg_5168.label: On vessels with only one masthead light, fit the manoeuvring light where best seen, at least 2 metres vertically apart from that masthead light.

pg_5169.label: On high-speed craft, masthead light height may be reduced relative to breadth provided the base angle of the isosceles triangle formed with sidelights is not less than 27 degrees.

pg_5170.label: On high-speed craft 50m+ in length, vertical separation between foremast and mainmast lights may be modified below 4.5m only if it meets the specified formula based on height, trim, and horizontal separation.

pg_5171.label: Ensure a directional whistle's sound pressure level is no more than 4 dB below the axis level within ±45 degrees of the axis.

pg_5172.label: Ensure sound pressure level in any other horizontal direction is no more than 10 dB below the axis level.

pg_5173.label: Measure sound pressure level in the 1/3rd-octave band that determines audibility range.

pg_5174.label: Install a directional whistle (when used as the only whistle) with maximum intensity directed straight ahead.

pg_5175.label: Place the whistle as high as practicable on the vessel.

pg_5176.label: Limit the vessel's own whistle sound pressure level at listening posts to not exceed 110 dB(A), and practicably not exceed 100 dB(A).

pg_5177.label: Fit a power-driven bell striker where practicable, ensuring it can still be operated manually.

pg_5178.label: Ensure the bell striker's mass is not less than 3 per cent of the mass of the bell.

pg_5179.label: Place any lights exhibited under Rule 26(d) where they can best be seen, at least 0.9 m apart, and at a lower level than the lights prescribed in Rule 26(b)(i) and (c)(i).

pg_5180.label: Ensure these lights are visible all round the horizon at a distance of at least 1 mile, but less than the distance of lights prescribed for fishing vessels generally.

pg_5181.label: If 20 m or more in length and trawling, exhibit two white lights vertically when shooting nets, one white over one red when hauling, and two red lights when the net is fast on an obstruction.

pg_5182.label: If 20 m or more in length and pair trawling, exhibit a forward-directed searchlight toward the other vessel of the pair at night, plus the paragraph 2(a) lights during shooting/hauling/fast-net situations.

pg_5183.label: If less than 20 m in length and trawling (demersal, pelagic, or pair), optionally exhibit the lights prescribed in paragraphs (a) or (b) as appropriate.

pg_5184.label: If engaged in purse seine fishing, optionally exhibit two yellow lights in a vertical line flashing alternately every second with equal light and occultation duration, only while hampered by fishing gear.

pg_5185.label: If whistles are fitted more than 100 m apart, arrange them so they cannot be sounded simultaneously.

pg_5186.label: If obstructions create a zone of greatly reduced signal level for a single whistle, fit a combined whistle system instead.

pg_5187.label: Locate whistles of a combined system not more than 100 m apart and arrange them to sound simultaneously, with frequencies differing by at least 10 Hz.

pg_5188.label: Ensure any bell, gong, or similar device produces a sound pressure level of at least 110 dB at 1 metre.

pg_5189.label: Construct bells and gongs from corrosion-resistant material designed to give a clear tone, with bell mouth diameter at least 300 mm for vessels 20 m or more in length.

pg_5190.label: Use or exhibit one or more of the listed signals (e.g., SOS, Mayday, red flares, continuous fog signal, NC flags, EPIRB) when in distress and needing assistance.

pg_5191.label: Do not use these signals for any purpose other than indicating distress, and do not use other signals that could be confused with them.

pg_5192.label: Consult the International Code of Signals and the Merchant Ship Search and Rescue Manual for supplementary signals such as orange canvas markers and dye markers.

pg_5193.label: Ensure the officer of the watch directs watchkeeping to avoid collision and stranding during their period of duty.

pg_5194.label: Adjust the composition of the watch, including lookouts, to match prevailing circumstances and conditions.

pg_5195.label: Refer to the International Code of Signals and IAMSAR Manual Volume III for supplementary signals (e.g., orange canvas with black square/circle, dye marker) for air identification.

pg_5196.label: Organise watchkeeping duties so crew are not impaired by fatigue.

pg_5197.label: Ensure the first watch at the start of a voyage is sufficiently rested and fit for duty.

pg_5198.label: Ensure subsequent relieving watches are sufficiently rested and otherwise fit when going on duty.

pg_5199.label: Never leave the bridge unattended at any time.

pg_5200.label: Assess weather conditions, visibility, and daylight/darkness before deciding watch arrangements.

pg_5201.label: Account for proximity of navigational hazards requiring additional duties by the officer in charge.

pg_5202.label: Verify the use and operational condition of radar, electronic position-indicating devices, and other safety-relevant equipment.

pg_5203.label: Consider whether the ship is fitted with automatic steering.

pg_5204.label: Account for any additional demands arising from special operational circumstances.

pg_5205.label: Check pertinent information and any course laid down.

pg_5206.label: Confirm course and speed and note any navigational hazard expected during the watch.

pg_5207.label: Check the ship's position at sufficiently frequent intervals using available navigational aids.

pg_5208.label: Ensure the manner of operation of navigational equipment is clearly understood and its operational condition is fully taken into account.

pg_5209.label: Remain on the bridge at all times until properly relieved.

pg_5210.label: If visiting the chart room, first confirm it is safe and that an efficient look-out remains maintained.

pg_5211.label: Before acting as sole look-out in daylight, carefully assess the situation each time, considering weather, visibility, traffic density, proximity of hazards, and proximity to traffic separation schemes.

pg_5212.label: Summon assistance to the bridge without hesitation when acting as sole look-out if undivided attention cannot be given.

pg_5213.label: Do not hesitate to use engine speed changes when necessary.

pg_5214.label: Give timely notice of intended engine speed variations when possible.

pg_5215.label: Keep the ship's manoeuvring capabilities, including stopping distance, prominently in mind.

pg_5216.label: Ensure the person keeping look-out gives full attention to the task and is assigned no interfering duties.

pg_5217.label: Keep look-out and helmsman duties separate, except on small vessels with unobstructed all-round view and no night-vision impairment.

pg_5218.label: Allow the officer of the watch to be sole look-out in daylight only after careful situational assessment confirms it is safe.

pg_5219.label: Account for weather, visibility, traffic density, navigational hazard proximity, and TSS presence in look-out decisions.

pg_5220.label: Summon additional assistance to the bridge immediately when the situation changes and ensure it is readily available.

pg_5221.label: Detect and report ships or aircraft in distress, shipwrecked persons, wrecks, and debris as part of look-out duties.

pg_5222.label: Master and pilot exchange information on navigation procedures, local conditions, and the ship's characteristics.

pg_5223.label: Master and OOW retain full responsibility for the ship's safety even when a pilot is aboard.

pg_5224.label: OOW takes all possible precautions to prevent operational or accidental pollution of the marine environment.

pg_5225.label: Verify the helmsman or automatic pilot is steering the correct course.

pg_5226.label: Establish standard compass error at least once a watch and after major course alterations; compare standard and gyro compasses frequently; synchronise repeaters with master compass.

pg_5227.label: Test the automatic pilot in manual position at least once a watch.

pg_5228.label: Confirm navigation and signal lights and other navigational equipment are functioning properly.

pg_5229.label: Switch steering to manual control in good time before a hazardous situation develops.

pg_5230.label: Ensure the changeover from automatic to manual steering (and vice versa) is made by, or under the supervision of, a responsible officer.

pg_5231.label: Observe the radar display carefully and plot contacts effectively on the appropriate range scale

pg_5232.label: Scan the radar at sufficiently frequent intervals

pg_5233.label: Commence any collision-avoidance action in ample time

pg_5234.label: Use available navigational equipment without hesitation in accordance with collision regulations.

pg_5235.label: Officer of the watch retains responsibility for safe navigation even with master on bridge until master explicitly and mutually confirms assumption of responsibility.

pg_5236.label: Do not hand over the watch to a relieving officer believed to be unfit for duty; report doubts to the master.

pg_5237.label: Relieving officer must ensure watch members are capable of duties, including night vision adjustment, before assuming the watch.

pg_5238.label: Relieving officer must not take over until personally satisfied on standing orders, vessel position/course/speed/draught, weather/tide factors, and navigational situation including equipment status, compass errors, nearby vessels, and hazards.

pg_5239.label: Defer relief of the officer of the watch if a collision-avoidance manoeuvre or hazard-response action is in progress.

pg_5240.label: Comply with the relevant rules of the applicable collision regulations, with particular regard to sounding fog signals.

pg_5241.label: Proceed at a moderate speed and have engines ready for immediate manoeuvres.

pg_5243.label: Post look-out(s) and helmsman, and in congested waters revert to hand steering immediately.

pg_5246.label: Take early and positive action in compliance with applicable collision regulations and check that the action is having the desired effect.

pg_5247.label: Continue to co-operate closely with the pilot while retaining responsibility for the safety of the ship.

pg_5248.label: Maintain an accurate check on the vessel's position and movements.

pg_5249.label: If in doubt about the pilot's actions or intentions, seek clarification directly from the pilot.

pg_5250.label: If doubt still exists after seeking clarification, notify the master immediately.

pg_5251.label: Take whatever action is necessary before the master arrives on the bridge.

pg_5252.label: Notify the master immediately if restricted visibility is encountered or suspected.

pg_5253.label: Notify the master if traffic conditions or movements of other vessels cause concern.

pg_5254.label: Notify the master if difficulty is experienced in maintaining course.

pg_5255.label: Notify the master on failure to sight land, a navigation mark, or obtain soundings by the expected time.

pg_5256.label: Notify the master on breakdown of engines, steering gear, or any essential navigational equipment.

pg_5257.label: Notify the master in heavy weather if in doubt about possible weather damage.

pg_5258.label: Notify the master in any other emergency or situation of doubt.

pg_5259.label: Despite notifying the master, take immediate action for the safety of the ship without hesitation when circumstances require.

pg_5260.label: Determine and plot the ship's position on the appropriate chart as soon as practicable, and check at sufficiently frequent intervals by taking bearings of fixed marks or shore objects.

pg_5261.label: Ensure an efficient look-out is maintained.

pg_5262.label: Ensure inspection rounds of the vessel are made periodically.

pg_5263.label: Observe meteorological and tidal conditions and the state of the sea.

pg_5264.label: Notify the master and take all necessary measures if the vessel drags anchor.

pg_5265.label: Ensure the state of readiness of main engines and other machinery matches the master's instructions.

pg_5266.label: If visibility deteriorates, notify the master and comply with applicable collision regulations.

pg_5267.label: Ensure the vessel exhibits appropriate lights and shapes and makes appropriate sound signals at all times.

pg_5268.label: Take measures to protect the environment from pollution and comply with applicable pollution regulations.

pg_5269.label: Issue a written statement from the responsible person declaring the company's safety and environmental protection policy.

pg_5270.label: Develop instructions and procedures for safe vessel operation and environmental protection compliant with applicable CFR and international conventions (the other vessel).

pg_5271.label: Document levels of authority and communication lines between shoreside and shipboard personnel.

pg_5272.label: Establish procedures for reporting accidents, near accidents, and non-conformities with the SMS and ISM Code.

pg_5273.label: Create procedures for preparing for and responding to emergency situations involving both shoreside and shipboard personnel.

pg_5274.label: Implement procedures for internal audits of the company's and vessel's SMS.

pg_5275.label: Conduct management review of internal audit reports and correct identified non-conformities.

pg_5276.label: Confirm vessel type and compliance deadline (July 1, 1998 for passenger vessels >12 pax, tankers, bulk/high-speed freight ≥500 GT on foreign voyage; July 1, 2002 for other freight vessels and MODUs ≥500 GT).

pg_5277.label: Document the responsible person's safety and pollution prevention policy, functional safety and operational requirements, recordkeeping responsibilities, and reporting responsibilities in the SMS.

pg_5278.label: Ensure the SMS is consistent with the functional standards and performance elements of IMO Resolution A.741(18).

pg_5279.label: Design the SMS to provide safe practices in operation, a safe work environment, safeguards against identified risks, continuous improvement of personnel safety skills and emergency preparedness, and compliance with applicable mandatory rules and industry guidance.

pg_5280.label: Draft and maintain safety and environmental policy statements meeting the objectives of §96.230.

pg_5281.label: Document company responsibilities and authority, including owner identity and personnel interrelations.

pg_5282.label: Designate in writing a person (or persons) to monitor the SMS with direct access to top company management.

pg_5283.label: Write statements defining the Master's responsibilities and authorities, including carrying out policy, motivating crew, issuing clear orders, and reporting non-conformities.

pg_5284.label: Make all SMS documents and reports available to both shore-based and vessel-based personnel.

pg_5285.label: Issue written statements affirming the Master's overriding responsibility and authority to make vessel decisions on safety and pollution.

pg_5286.label: Verify Masters are properly qualified for command and know the company's SMS.

pg_5287.label: Ensure owners/companies provide necessary support for Master's duties.

pg_5288.label: Crew each vessel with qualified, certificated, medically fit seafarers per national/international requirements.

pg_5289.label: Properly introduce new or reassigned personnel to safety/environmental duties.

pg_5290.label: Ensure personnel understand relevant rules, regulations, codes and guidelines.

pg_5291.label: Identify and provide needed training for all personnel involved in the SMS.

pg_5292.label: Communicate SMS procedures in language(s) understood by personnel.

pg_5293.label: Ensure personnel can communicate effectively while performing SMS-related duties.

pg_5294.label: Define key shipboard operational tasks and assign qualified personnel to them.

pg_5295.label: Identify, describe, and direct responses to potential emergency shipboard situations.

pg_5296.label: Set up drill and exercise programs for emergency preparedness.

pg_5297.label: Ensure the company organization can respond at any time to hazards, accidents, and emergencies.

pg_5298.label: Report non-conformities, accidents, and hazardous situations to the owner/company.

pg_5299.label: Investigate and analyze reported items to improve safety and pollution prevention.

pg_5300.label: Inspect vessel equipment, hull, and machinery at appropriate intervals

pg_5301.label: Report any non-conformity or deficiency, including possible cause if known

pg_5303.label: Keep records of inspection, reporting, and corrective action activities

pg_5304.label: Identify equipment/technical systems whose sudden failure could cause a hazardous situation

pg_5305.label: Identify reliability measures and regularly test standby arrangements or equipment not in continuous use

pg_5306.label: Integrate required inspections into the vessel's operational maintenance routine

pg_5307.label: Establish procedures to control all SMS-relevant documents and data

pg_5308.label: Ensure each vessel carries on board all documents relevant to its own operation

pg_5309.label: Route document changes through authorized personnel for review and approval

pg_5311.label: Conduct periodic internal audits evaluating SMS efficiency

pg_5312.label: Define audit types, frequency, reporting method, and corrective action process

pg_5313.label: Select audit personnel independent of the area being audited

pg_5314.label: Communicate and report internal audit findings to management for critical review and timely corrective action

pg_5315.label: Determine audit type required: initial, renewal, annual verification, or intermediate verification.

pg_5316.label: Review and verify the procedures and documents comprising the safety management system.

pg_5317.label: Ensure the audit complies with this subpart and IMO Resolution A.788(19) guidelines.

pg_5318.label: Ensure the audit is conducted by a Coast Guard audit team or an authorized recognized organization's auditors.

pg_5319.label: Complete required audits before issuance/renewal of DOC or SMC and at periodic intervals to maintain validity.

pg_5320.label: Carry a valid copy of the company's Document of Compliance certificate onboard when on a foreign voyage.

pg_5321.label: Complete a satisfactory safety management audit to extend DOC validity to additional vessel types.

pg_5322.label: Ensure the company's safety management system is verified annually by the Coast Guard or an authorized organization, within three months before or after the certificate anniversary date.

pg_5323.label: Grant full access to vessel, records, and personnel when requested by the Coast Guard or authorized organization for SMS evaluation.

pg_5324.label: If the DOC is revoked, complete a new satisfactory safety management audit before a new certificate can be reissued.

pg_5325.label: Ensure the company has completed its own safety management system audit and received a Document of Compliance certificate before any vessel-level audit is scheduled.

pg_5326.label: Have a responsible person communicate all audit requests directly to a U.S.-authorized recognized organization.

pg_5327.label: Submit audit requests within the specified time limits for annual (§96.330(f)) or intermediate (§96.340(e)(2)) verification audits.

pg_5328.label: If a non-conformity is found during an audit, the auditor must report it in writing to the company's owner (for company audits) or to both the owner and vessel's Master (for vessel audits).

pg_5329.label: Obtain and maintain a Document of Compliance certificate if the vessel is a U.S. vessel on foreign voyages, carries more than 12 passengers, or is a tanker, bulk freight, freight vessel, or MODU of 500 gross tons or more.

pg_5330.label: Complete a satisfactory safety management audit per §96.320 before a DOC certificate will be issued.

pg_5331.label: Determine if the vessel meets the passenger or gross tonnage/type thresholds requiring an SMC.

pg_5332.label: Ensure the company holds a valid Document of Compliance (DOC) under §96.330.

pg_5333.label: Complete a satisfactory safety management audit of the vessel's SMS under §96.320.

pg_5334.label: Carry a copy of the valid SMC on board.

pg_5335.label: Optionally obtain an SMC even if not required under paragraph (a).

pg_5336.label: Ensure a satisfactory initial safety management audit is completed before the SMC is issued.

pg_5337.label: Request and complete an intermediate verification audit between the 24th and 36th month of the SMC's validity period.

pg_5338.label: Maintain a valid Document of Compliance (DOC) certificate for the company.

pg_5339.label: Complete a satisfactory safety management system audit meeting all Subpart B requirements before renewing the SMC.

pg_5340.label: Request an Interim DOC through an authorized recognized organization when forming a new company, transitioning companies, or adding a new vessel type.

pg_5341.label: Demonstrate to an auditor that the company's safety management system meets the requirements of § 96.230.

pg_5342.label: Provide a plan for full implementation of a safety management system within the validity period of the Interim DOC.

pg_5343.label: Apply for an Interim Safety Management Certificate upon taking delivery of a new U.S. vessel or taking responsibility for a vessel new to the company.

pg_5344.label: Ensure the company's valid (or interim) Document of Compliance applies to the vessel type.

pg_5345.label: Ensure the SMS for the vessel includes the key elements set out in § 96.220 applicable to the new vessel type.

pg_5346.label: Confirm the SMS has been assessed during the DOC/Interim DOC audit process.

pg_5347.label: Confirm the Master and senior officers are familiar with the SMS and planned setup arrangements.

pg_5348.label: Extract written documented instructions from the SMS and provide them to the vessel prior to sailing.

pg_5349.label: Plan an internal audit of the vessel within three months.

pg_5350.label: Ensure relevant SMS information is written in English and in any other language understood by the vessel's personnel.

pg_5351.label: Carry on board valid documentation showing the company's safety management system was audited and assessed consistent with ISM Code (IMO Res. A.741(18)).

pg_5352.label: Alternatively, carry valid documentation from the vessel's Flag Administration showing the vessel's SMS was audited and assessed consistent with the ISM Code.

pg_5353.label: Alternatively, show evidence of compliance issued by a SOLAS-party government or an organization recognized to act on behalf of the vessel's Flag Administration.

pg_5354.label: Ensure evidence of compliance contains all information and substantially the same format as a Document of Compliance certificate and a Safety Management Certificate.

pg_5355.label: Coast Guard boards vessel to verify valid DOC and SMC (or equivalent evidence) are on board.

pg_5356.label: Coast Guard verifies crew and shore-based personnel are following SMS procedures and policies during operations or cargo transfer.

pg_5357.label: If a foreign vessel's condition/SMS use does not substantially agree with its certificates, COTP or OCMI may order detention at the port or terminal where violation is found.

pg_5358.label: Detaining authority may allow vessel to move to another area of the port rather than remain at the violation site.

pg_5359.label: If vessel lacks required SMC and DOC copy on board, pursue civil penalty against owner, charterer, managing operator, agent, Master, or responsible individual under 46 U.S.C. 3318.

pg_5360.label: For foreign vessels, Coast Guard may request Secretary of the Treasury to withhold or revoke clearance under 46 U.S.C. App. 91.

pg_5361.label: Coast Guard may ask Secretary to permit vessel's departure after a bond or other surety is filed.

pg_5362.label: Confirm the organization is already recognized under 46 CFR part 8, subparts A and B, before seeking ISM audit authorization.

pg_5363.label: Determine which certificates (Safety Management Certificate, Document of Compliance, Interim SMC, Interim DOC) the organization wishes to be authorized to issue.

pg_5364.label: Submit a written request for authorization to the Commandant (CG-ENG), Attn: Office of Design and Engineering Standards.

pg_5365.label: Determine whether the vessel qualifies for the force majeure exception before applying entry denial.

pg_5366.label: Verify the vessel holds a safety management system properly certificated under this subpart or SOLAS Chapter IX if it is engaged on a foreign voyage and meets the tonnage/passenger criteria.

pg_5367.label: Cognizant COTP denies port/terminal entry to any non-compliant vessel.

pg_5368.label: To obtain a current list of Coast Guard-authorized recognized organizations, submit a self-addressed stamped envelope and written request to Commandant (CG-ENG), Office of Design and Engineering Standards.

pg_5369.label: Submit a statement describing the type of authorization sought.

pg_5370.label: Provide documents showing the organization has an internal quality system meeting §96.440 requirements, ANSI/ASQC C9001, or an equivalent Coast Guard-recognized standard.

pg_5371.label: Submit a list of the organization's exclusive auditors qualified to perform safety management audits and their operational areas.

pg_5372.label: Provide a written statement confirming procedures and records related to SMS audits/certification will be available for annual or on-demand Coast Guard review.

pg_5373.label: If a foreign classification society, include a government affidavit demonstrating reciprocity under 46 U.S.C. 3316, listing authorized delegations to the American Bureau of Shipping.

pg_5374.label: Await Coast Guard evaluation of the request; if satisfactory, the organization will receive an on-site evaluation visit per §96.440(b).

pg_5375.label: Mail or deliver a written request for reconsideration to the authorized organization.

pg_5376.label: Authorized organization rules on the request and sends a written response within 30 days of receiving it.

pg_5377.label: Authorized organization sends a copy of its response to the Commandant (CG-CVC), Attn: Office of Commercial Vessel Compliance.

pg_5378.label: Coast Guard evaluates the organization's written request for evidence of 12 specific criteria (management duties, ethics, auditor training, audit procedures per IMO A.788(19), record-keeping, non-conformity reporting, certification methods, periodic/intermediate/renewal audit methods, appeals handling, overall procedures per IMO A.739(18)).

pg_5379.label: If the written evaluation is favorable, conduct an on-site evaluation of the organization's corporate and port offices.

pg_5380.label: If approved, enter into a written agreement defining scope, terms, conditions, and requirements of authorization per § 96.460.

pg_5381.label: If disapproved, Coast Guard writes to the organization explaining the deficiencies.

pg_5382.label: Allow the organization to correct deficiencies and reapply.

pg_5383.label: Submit a written appeal directly to Commandant (CG-CVC) including all supporting documentation and evidence.

pg_5384.label: Optionally request a stay of the appealed decision's effect while under review.

pg_5385.label: Await Commandant (CG-CVC) written decision, which constitutes final Coast Guard action.

pg_5386.label: Enter into a written agreement with the Coast Guard specifying validity period, authorized duties/certificates, required reports, renewal actions, and actions upon revocation.

pg_5387.label: Submit to Coast Guard evaluation at least every 12 months.

pg_5388.label: If authorization is terminated, notify all responsible persons, companies, and vessels holding certificates issued by the organization.

pg_5389.label: Include in the termination notice: reason for termination, certificate status, list of currently authorized organizations, and steps to transfer SMS to another authorized organization.

pg_5390.label: Obtain a TSMS certificate issued under § 138.305.

pg_5391.label: Ensure the TSMS certificate is obtained at least 6 months before seeking a COI for any covered vessel.

pg_5392.label: Establish management policies and procedures serving as an operational protocol for all levels of management.

pg_5393.label: Create procedures producing objective evidence of compliance with subchapter requirements.

pg_5394.label: Implement self-evaluation procedures to verify adherence to own policies and regulatory requirements.

pg_5395.label: Arrange periodic evaluation by an independent third-party organization (TPO).

pg_5396.label: Establish procedures for correcting identified problems and facilitating continuous improvement.

pg_5397.label: Demonstrate management responsibility by showing implementation and organization-wide adherence to the TSMS.

pg_5398.label: Document organizational structure, responsibilities, procedures, and resources for quality monitoring.

pg_5399.label: Establish document and data control procedures identifying controlled document types and responsible parties.

pg_5400.label: Establish a system of recordkeeping covering audit records, non-conformity reports, corrective actions, and auditor qualifications/training.

pg_5401.label: Identify and meet training needs through documented procedures.

pg_5402.label: Identify and ensure adequate resources and procedures.

pg_5403.label: Establish procedures for reporting accidents and non-conformities.

pg_5404.label: Establish procedures to prepare for and respond to emergencies.

pg_5405.label: Establish procedures for verification of vessel compliance, internal audits, external audits, and management review.

pg_5406.label: Establish procedures to evaluate recommendations from management and personnel.

pg_5407.label: Document administration and management organization policy, including responsibilities and designated person.

pg_5408.label: Document justification if any required TSMS element is not applicable.

pg_5409.label: Owner or managing operator designates in writing shoreside person(s) responsible for TSMS implementation and continuous functioning across management and fleet.

pg_5410.label: Owner or managing operator designates shoreside person(s) responsible for vessel maintenance/operable condition and for emergency assistance to each towing vessel.

pg_5411.label: Owner or managing operator defines the scope of the master's authority in writing.

pg_5412.label: Master exercises final authority to make determinations on safe operations and to cease operation when an unsafe condition exists.

pg_5413.label: Establish procedures to ensure selection of the appropriate vessel, including adequate maneuverability and horsepower.

pg_5414.label: Establish procedures for appropriate rigging and towing gear.

pg_5415.label: Establish procedures for proper management of the navigational watch.

pg_5416.label: Ensure compliance with applicable security measures.

pg_5417.label: Maintain procedures and documentation confirming each towing vessel meets operational, equipment, and personnel requirements of the subchapter.

pg_5418.label: Establish internal and external audit procedures in accordance with §§138.310 and 138.315.

pg_5419.label: Create a procedure allowing any person to report non-conformities, including initial reporting and follow-up resolution steps.

pg_5420.label: Implement employment procedures ensuring personnel qualifications, background checks, and drug/alcohol compliance.

pg_5421.label: Develop a training policy covering new-hire orientation, TSMS duties, operational duties, emergency procedures, occupational health, crew safety, and subchapter-required training.

pg_5422.label: Maintain a maintenance and survey procedure specifying requirements and surveyor qualifications, retaining documentation for 5 years.

pg_5423.label: Conduct an internal management audit annually, within 3 months of the TSMS certificate anniversary date.

pg_5424.label: Audit all levels of the organization, including all towing vessels subject to the TSMS.

pg_5425.label: Document internal audit results and retain them for 5 years, making them available to the Coast Guard upon request.

pg_5426.label: Use internal auditors who have TSMS/standard knowledge, completed a recognized ISO 9001 auditor course, are not the designated person or responsible for TSMS development/implementation, and are independent of the audited procedures (unless impracticable given organization size/nature).

pg_5427.label: Arrange an external management audit by a Third Party Organization (TPO) auditor prior to issuance of an initial TSMS certificate or any renewal.

pg_5428.label: Conduct a mid-period external management audit between the 27th and 33rd month of the certificate's validity period.

pg_5429.label: Determine if existing SMS is fully ISM Code compliant under 33 CFR part 96.

pg_5430.label: If using a non-ISM existing SMS, submit documentation to the Coast Guard based on the initial audit and one full audit cycle of at least 3 years.

pg_5431.label: Be prepared for Coast Guard inspection of SMS contents, audit evidence, non-conformity corrections, and vessel compliance records.

pg_5432.label: Obtain TSMS certificate from a Third Party Organization (TPO) once deemed compliant.

pg_5433.label: Keep the TSMS certificate on file at the shoreside office and a copy aboard each covered towing vessel.

pg_5434.label: Maintain and provide upon request a list of all vessels currently covered by each TSMS certificate.

pg_5435.label: TPO conducting the external audit submits the audit results to the Towing Vessel National Center of Expertise.

pg_5436.label: Complete submission within 30 days of audit completion.

pg_5437.label: Conduct an external audit before issuing the initial COI if the vessel has been owned/operated 6+ months prior to receiving that COI.

pg_5438.label: Conduct an external audit of all vessels under a TSMS certificate during its 5-year validity period, selecting vessels randomly and distributing audits evenly.

pg_5439.label: Use objective evidence from the corporate office where appropriate, but ensure some audit components occur via an actual vessel visit within the 5-year period.

pg_5440.label: Conduct internal audits via a designated employee or contracted individual acting as an employee, possibly in segments over time.

pg_5441.label: Ensure internal auditors have authority to examine documentation, question personnel, inspect equipment, witness testing, and observe training/drills.

pg_5442.label: Have a TPO auditor conduct the external audit covering all TSMS elements, which may be sampled.

pg_5443.label: Ensure audit depth and breadth confirm effective TSMS implementation at all organizational levels and onboard vessels.

pg_5444.label: Provide the auditor access to documentation, personnel, equipment, system testing, and training/drills.

pg_5445.label: Allow the auditor to broaden audit scope if TSMS is incomplete/ineffective, records are inconsistent with conditions, or unsafe conditions are found.

pg_5446.label: Permit the auditor to verify compliance via objective evidence (checklists, invoices, reports) and visual sampling onboard.

pg_5447.label: If a major non-conformity is found, notify the local OCMI within 24 hours and the owner/managing operator's designated representative per the TSMS.

pg_5448.label: Notify the local OCMI at least 72 hours before any external audit.

pg_5449.label: Accommodate a Coast Guard representative accompanying the auditor if required, and allow for a separate Coast Guard audit at its discretion.

pg_5450.label: TPO conducting the external audit must submit the audit results to the cognizant OCMI within 30 days of audit completion.

pg_5451.label: If submitting electronically, use a method that allows the Coast Guard to reliably verify the submitter's identity and the authenticity of the records.

pg_5452.label: Document in the TSMS the specific means to be used for electronic submission of external audit records.

pg_5453.label: TPO and owner/managing operator must explain or demonstrate TSMS areas to the Coast Guard upon request.

pg_5454.label: Make the TPO available for attendance at the vessel or the owner's/operator's office if required by the Coast Guard.

pg_5455.label: Owner/managing operator or TPO must bear all costs associated with required attendance.

pg_5456.label: Confirm the endorsement holder's authorized cargo classification (Dangerous Liquid and/or Liquefied Gas) before permitting cargo transfer duties.

pg_5457.label: Check whether the cargo is listed in table 2 of 46 CFR part 153 and whether the barge is certified for ocean service.

pg_5458.label: Verify applicant meets subpart E requirements before Coast Guard endorses MMC as Tank Vessel-Engineer.

pg_5459.label: Confirm that any person acting as PIC or Tank Vessel-Assistant for bulk liquid cargo transfer or cargo-tank cleaning holds the specific endorsement authorizing that service.

pg_5460.label: Assign primary responsibility for cargo systems and transfer equipment maintenance to the holder of the Tank Vessel-Engineer endorsement on self-propelled DL/LG vessels.

pg_5461.label: Ensure no part 11-credentialed person serves as Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, or Cargo Engineer on an inspected tank vessel carrying liquid bulk cargo or residue without holding a Tank Vessel-Engineer endorsement or equivalent.

pg_5462.label: For applicants meeting § 13.111 requirements, place a restricted Tank Vessel-PIC endorsement per the § 10.107 definition of 'restricted tank vessel endorsement'.

pg_5562.label: Wait for a reply before re-transmitting

pg_5563.label: Try low power first except for distress

pg_5564.label: Keep a listening watch on Channel 16

pg_5565.label: Send a distress alert via DSC by pressing and holding the distress button until the alert is transmitted.

pg_5566.label: Wait for a DSC acknowledgement or approximately 15 seconds if none is received.

pg_5567.label: Transmit the voice distress call and message on Channel 16: 'Mayday, mayday, mayday', vessel name (3 times), call sign/MMSI, then repeat Mayday with name, call sign and MMSI.

pg_5568.label: State position (preferably latitude and longitude), nature of distress, assistance required, number of persons on board, and other relevant information.

pg_5570.label: Select Individual DSC call type with routine priority.

pg_5571.label: Enter the MMSI of the called vessel or select it from the directory.

pg_5572.label: Indicate the inter-ship channel to be used for R/T communication.

pg_5573.label: Wait for the called vessel to acknowledge the DSC call when the radio 'rings'.

pg_5574.label: Begin the conversation on the selected inter-ship channel.

pg_5575.label: Make initial voice call on Channel 16 using low power.

pg_5576.label: Move to an inter-ship working channel once contact is established.

pg_5577.label: If no response on Channel 16, call on Channel 13.

pg_5578.label: Initiate an Individual DSC Call to the coast station with routine priority, entering the station's MMSI or selecting it from the radio's directory.

pg_5579.label: Wait for the Coastguard's acknowledgement, which will indicate the working channel for voice communications.

pg_5580.label: Set your radio to the indicated working channel and wait for the station to call you on it.

pg_5581.label: Immediately cease any transmission that may interfere with distress traffic and maintain a listening watch on Channel 16.

pg_5582.label: Wait approximately 5 minutes for a DSC acknowledgement; if none occurs and you can assist, acknowledge by voice on Channel 16 using the Mayday relay format.

pg_5583.label: In the voice acknowledgement, state the casualty vessel's name/MMSI, your own vessel's name/call sign, confirm receipt of the mayday, and state what assistance you can give including ETA if proceeding to the casualty.

pg_5584.label: Use any available means to relay the distress message to an appropriate coast station.

pg_5585.label: For urgency situations, send a DSC All Ships Urgency Call nominating a working channel, then make the Pan Pan announcement on Channel 16 and move to the nominated working channel.

pg_5586.label: For safety information to HM Coastguard, use an Individual DSC call with safety priority and the appropriate MMSI; wait for Coastguard acknowledgement and switch to the indicated working channel.

pg_5587.label: If the radio does not support DSC safety calling, make a voice call on Channel 16 instead.

pg_6335.label: Pass both mooring lines to each tug together as a single operation, as planned

pg_6344.label: Master observes vessel is out of the channel and alerts the pilot.

pg_6345.label: Pilot uses aggressive engine and rudder manoeuvres combined with escort tug pushing on the starboard bow to refloat the vessel.

pg_6346.label: Employ a tethered tug aft in the indirect towing manner as an active aid to steering when maneuvering in confined waters under pilotage.

pg_6347.label: Use the tug as a brake to reduce speed over ground (SOG) while increasing engine RPM to improve rudder response.

pg_6348.label: Establish a shared mental model with the pilot before and throughout the manoeuvre by openly exchanging information on the passage plan.

pg_6349.label: Challenge and discuss any unexpected actions or deviations from the agreed plan with the pilot immediately.

pg_6350.label: Master to intervene decisively, including taking over the con if necessary, once the vessel is assessed to be in danger.

pg_6351.label: Monitor vessel track against the dredged channel limits and cross-check actual current/set against predicted values.

pg_6352.label: Track all contacts on radar in restricted visibility, regardless of AIS fitment.

pg_6353.label: Adjust speed to reflect stopping capability relative to visible range.

pg_6354.label: Do not rely on a single unacknowledged VHF call to resolve a close-quarters situation; take independent action in good time.

pg_6355.label: Offer assistance to a crew member visibly struggling with a task.

pg_6356.label: Accept help or invoke stop work authority when struggling with a heavy or awkward task.

pg_6357.label: Apply first aid immediately following an injury.

pg_6358.label: Provide follow-up medical treatment and monitoring.

pg_6359.label: Reduce speed to a safe level appropriate for dense fog and congested traffic conditions.

pg_6360.label: Compose the bridge team based on actual prevailing conditions rather than default watch schedules.

pg_6361.label: Actively maintain bridge resource management (BRM) and situational awareness even with a reinforced bridge team.

pg_6362.label: Master of Vessel A implements a heightened bridge watch regime (Master conning, two navigation officers, helmsperson) when visibility drops to 350 m.

pg_6363.label: Bridge team should positively identify and continuously plot all radar contacts, including intermittent returns.

pg_6364.label: Both vessels should sound the fog signal (one prolonged blast every two minutes) required in restricted visibility.

pg_6365.label: OOW on Vessel B should inform the Master of reduced visibility and the presence of another vessel being overtaken.

pg_6366.label: VTS instructs Vessel A to go to anchorage/drift because visibility in the TSS is too low and traffic is suspended.

pg_6367.label: Master of Vessel A, seeing the opposite lane clear, orders slow ahead and port helm to cross the lane and comply with the suspension order, with VTS agreement.

pg_6368.label: VTS should confirm the position of all traffic, including vessels without AIS or with intermittent radar returns, before approving a maneuver.

pg_6369.label: Always dismantle and mount heavy covers using two persons, whether or not a chain block is used.

pg_6370.label: Fit two long studs at the top position of every cover before dismantling/mounting.

pg_6371.label: Ensure work permits and toolbox talks explicitly cover safe lifting techniques and assign roles.

pg_6372.label: Exercise Stop Work Authority whenever unsafe actions are observed.

pg_6373.label: Maintain supervisory presence during potentially hazardous tasks.

pg_6374.label: Establish and maintain a shared mental model of the planned manoeuvre among all bridge team members and the pilot.

pg_6375.label: Refer to tugs by position (fore/aft) or number (tug 1, tug 2) rather than by name.

pg_6376.label: Monitor vessel response against the briefed plan (e.g., expected stern or bow movement) and query the pilot immediately if the vessel behaves contrary to the plan.

pg_6377.label: Order main propulsion to dead slow astern in anticipation of the ebb current.

pg_6378.label: Order tug DC to stop once the vessel was off the berth.

pg_6379.label: Radio tug DD and instruct the operator to maintain a 90° angle with the tug line relative to the tanker.

pg_6380.label: Correct the tug operator when the actual angle (45°) and position did not match the requested configuration.

pg_6381.label: Stop the main propulsion immediately when the Master reported 'aft is too close'.
