pg_6382.label: Order tug DD to pull 'full away' and put the rudder hard to port.

pg_6383.label: Ensure fumigation personnel verbally brief all crew (not just written handover to Chief Officer) on the risks, gas properties, and precautions associated with the fumigant used.

pg_6384.label: Treat sealed/taped hatch coamings as an indicator of an active toxic gas hazard requiring restricted access and gas monitoring before any entry near or into holds.

pg_6385.label: Ensure crew receive a clear, specific safety briefing on the risks of the fumigant used, not merely paperwork sign-off.

pg_6386.label: Post warning signs at treated holds.

pg_6387.label: Implement dedicated company safety management procedures for fumigation, including risk assessment, equipment provision and shore support.

pg_6388.label: Carry phosphine gas detection equipment on board for the duration of a fumigated voyage.

pg_6389.label: Check gas concentrations regularly throughout the voyage, not only at the point of loading.

pg_6390.label: Maintain weathertight integrity of accommodation doors to the same standard as hatch covers.

pg_6391.label: Plan route and speed after fumigation with consideration of wind direction and relative vessel speed.

pg_6392.label: Exchange and agree the full manoeuvre plan between Master and pilot, including tug numbers, placement, and intended use

pg_6393.label: Record tug names and placements on the mooring plan diagram and in the pilot's notebook

pg_6394.label: Prepare a separate 'radio card' listing tug names and placements for quick reference on the bridge wing

pg_6395.label: Direct both tugs to push against the pier while mooring lines are let go fore and aft

pg_6396.label: Order the tugs by name to pull away at progressively increasing/differential power (e.g. dead slow, half, three-quarters for one tug; minimum for the other)

pg_6397.label: Familiarize crew with the IMO Recommendations on the Safe Use of Pesticides on Board Ships before and during fumigation voyages

pg_6398.label: Equip the vessel with phosphine gas detection equipment

pg_6399.label: Conduct safety inspections and concentration monitoring of phosphine gas after departure

pg_6400.label: Ensure weathertight doors fully close and ventilation is not left in recirculation mode during fumigant cargo carriage

pg_6401.label: Treat unexplained, spreading crew illness (chest tightness, nausea, vomiting, breathlessness, fatigue) as a possible toxic gas exposure rather than defaulting to food poisoning or Covid-19

pg_6402.label: Stop the vessel, anchor, and request SAR resources once the severity of crew incapacitation becomes apparent

pg_6403.label: Take freeboard measurements at various points on both sides of the vessel.

pg_6404.label: Take diagonal measurements of the hatch coamings.

pg_6405.label: Re-open the affected holds and inspect the cargo stow.

pg_6406.label: Use bulldozers to level the cargo in each hold.

pg_6407.label: Periodically re-take diagonal measurements during levelling.

pg_6408.label: Close the hatch covers once torsion is corrected.

pg_6409.label: Maintain continuous long-range radar and ECDIS scanning of the overall traffic picture, not just the immediate vessel being overtaken.

pg_6410.label: Keep the lookout continuously on the bridge during overtaking in a busy TSS.

pg_6411.label: Use VHF only early enough to establish a resolved, unambiguous plan, not as a late-stage fix when CPA is closing.

pg_6412.label: If delegating a VHF exchange, listen to it directly rather than relying on a second-hand summary, especially when a language relay is involved.

pg_6413.label: Make unambiguous course alterations decisively, not through a gradual series of small helm orders.

pg_6414.label: Before any large alteration of course, check for traffic in the direction about to be turned into, including astern.

pg_6415.label: Conduct long-range scanning as required by the Collision Regulations, not just short-range collision avoidance.

pg_6416.label: Note the position and extent of the SAR area from the SECURITE broadcast.

pg_6417.label: Plot the SAR area on the chart.

pg_6418.label: Adjust the passage plan to remain clear of the area, typically by at least two nautical miles unless the message states otherwise.

pg_6419.label: Reduce speed and post an extra lookout.

pg_6420.label: If the new track will still pass close to the area, call the issuing station (e.g., MRCC) to confirm safe passage.

pg_6421.label: Plot the hazard's reported position on the chart.

pg_6422.label: Calculate a safe passing distance of at least two nautical miles from the hazard.

pg_6423.label: Plan a new course that maintains this safe passing distance.

pg_6424.label: Inform the crew before altering course.

pg_6425.label: Act on the information and log the event.

pg_6426.label: Transmit the SECURITE announcement on Channel 16 using the standard format: SECURITE x3, ALL STATIONS x3, THIS IS [vessel name] x3, directing listeners to the working channel for the safety message, then say OUT.

pg_6427.label: Switch to the announced working channel (e.g., Channel 67) and broadcast the actual safety information.

pg_6428.label: Wait approximately 15 seconds after sending the DSC distress alert before starting the voice MAYDAY call.

pg_6429.label: If no acknowledgement is heard, repeat the full MAYDAY call unchanged after about four minutes.

pg_6430.label: If there is still no answer after several repeated attempts, allow the DSC set to automatically retransmit the DSC distress alert.

pg_6431.label: Switch briefly to Channel 70 to confirm the DSC alert itself was sent.

pg_6432.label: Return to Channel 16 to continue repeating the voice MAYDAY.

pg_6433.label: Respond promptly and slowly to the MRCC's request for repetition.

pg_6434.label: Transmit all numerical information digit by digit using standard phonetics (e.g., FIFE, TOO, the other vessel, WUN).

pg_6435.label: Do not paraphrase the original message content.

pg_6436.label: Use standard proword structure: vessel name, position, persons on board, injuries, ending with OVER.

pg_6437.label: Assess whether the situation involves grave and imminent danger to life.

pg_6438.label: If not under command or disabled but not in immediate danger, issue a PAN PAN urgency call instead of MAYDAY.

pg_6439.label: Structure the PAN PAN call with triple PAN PAN, ALL STATIONS, vessel name repeated three times, description of condition (e.g. NOT UNDER the other vessel, NO IMMEDIATE DANGER), the assistance requested, and OVER.

pg_6440.label: When MRCC requests periodic updates, acknowledge and follow the fixed schedule (e.g. every 15 minutes) on the working channel using a consistent message structure (vessel name, position, condition, next update time, OVER).

pg_6441.label: If conditions worsen before the next scheduled update, call MRCC immediately rather than waiting.

pg_6442.label: Issue a SECURITE call when a hazard is merely sighted (e.g. heavy weather developing).

pg_6443.label: Escalate to a PAN PAN urgency call if the situation worsens to an urgent but not life-threatening condition (e.g. total loss of propulsion, drifting towards rocks, requesting tow).

pg_6444.label: If a crew member becomes injured and needs medical guidance, issue a PAN PAN MEDICO call specifically requesting medical advice.

pg_6445.label: Escalate to full MAYDAY if the vessel is taking on water and lives are in immediate danger, stating vessel name, nature of distress, persons on board, and request for immediate assistance.

pg_6446.label: Always match the call level to the actual current severity, escalating or de-escalating as conditions change.

pg_6447.label: broadcast an ALL STATIONS call addressed to all stations, stating the vessel's name three times.

pg_6448.label: For a resolved urgency case, transmit 'PAN PAN the other vessel NO LONGER REQUIRED, OUT.'

pg_6449.label: For a resolved distress case, transmit 'MAYDAY the other vessel SAFE, NO FURTHER ASSISTANCE REQUIRED, OUT.'

pg_6450.label: Apply ordinary prudent seamanship in addition to the literal rules at all times.

pg_6451.label: Take extra precautions beyond bare rule compliance when circumstances (e.g., an erratically maneuvering or non-responsive nearby vessel) call for it, even if own-ship technically has right of way.

pg_6452.label: Depart from the rules if doing so is the only way to avoid immediate danger.

pg_6453.label: Apply COLREGs at all times while on open water and any connected water a seagoing vessel could reach.

pg_6454.label: Comply with any additional local traffic rules imposed by a harbour, river, or lake authority on top of COLREGs.

pg_6455.label: Maintain continuous visual and aural watch-keeping at all times.

pg_6456.label: Use every available tool (radar, AIS, binoculars, hydrophone) rather than relying on a single sensor.

pg_6457.label: Form a full appraisal of the situation and determine whether risk of collision exists.

pg_6458.label: Use all available means (visual, radar, ARPA, etc.) to assess risk of collision.

pg_6459.label: Monitor compass bearing trends on an approaching contact.

pg_6460.label: Avoid concluding no risk exists based on a thin or scattered radar picture.

pg_6461.label: Continuously assess prevailing visibility, traffic density, own stopping/turning performance, sea state, and radar range-scale/detection performance.

pg_6462.label: Reduce speed when visibility is dropping and multiple AIS contacts are present within close range, even if no single contact yet shows high collision risk.

pg_6463.label: Account for radar range-scale limitations and actual detection quality of small or distant contacts when setting speed.

pg_6465.label: Make the maneuver large enough to be readily apparent to the other vessel, visually or by radar.

pg_6466.label: Prefer a course change over a speed change when there is sufficient sea room.

pg_6467.label: Verify that the action actually creates a safe passing distance, not just a nominal/technical change in bearing or range.

pg_6468.label: Keep to the outer edge of the channel on your own starboard side when safe to do so.

pg_6469.label: Do not cross a channel if doing so would force a channel-bound vessel to take avoiding action.

pg_6470.label: Exchange whistle signals before overtaking another vessel inside a narrow channel.

pg_6471.label: Avoid anchoring in the channel if at all possible.

pg_6472.label: If crossing the scheme is unavoidable, cross on a heading as close to a right angle to the traffic flow as practicable.

pg_6473.label: If unable to determine the other vessel's wind side, assume own vessel is the give-way vessel and keep clear.

pg_6474.label: Determine which vessel has the other on its starboard side; that vessel is the give-way vessel.

pg_6475.label: As give-way vessel, alter course/speed to pass behind the other vessel's stern rather than crossing ahead.

pg_6476.label: Take action to keep clear as early as possible once give-way status is established.

pg_6477.label: Make the avoiding action substantial, not a minimal or token course/speed change.

pg_6478.label: Do not wait until TCPA shrinks to a very short interval (e.g. 90 seconds) to maneuver, even if technically collision could still be avoided at that point.

pg_6479.label: Determine if the other vessel is approaching nearly bow-to-bow on a reciprocal or near-reciprocal course.

pg_6480.label: If any doubt exists about whether it is head-on, treat it as head-on.

pg_6481.label: Do not wait to see what the other vessel does before acting.

pg_6482.label: Determine bearing of approach relative to the other vessel's beam.

pg_6483.label: If genuinely uncertain whether it is overtaking or crossing, treat it as overtaking.

pg_6484.label: As the overtaking vessel, keep clear of the vessel being overtaken.

pg_6485.label: Monitor whether the give-way vessel is actually taking appropriate action to keep clear.

pg_6486.label: When taking action, avoid turning to port toward a vessel on own ship's port side if there is room to do otherwise.

pg_6487.label: Identify the type/status of the other vessel (NUC, RAM, fishing, sailing, constrained by draught, or power-driven) by day shape, lights, or other signals.

pg_6488.label: As a power-driven vessel, keep clear of NUC, RAM, fishing vessels, and sailing vessels, in that priority order.

pg_6489.label: Give extra consideration to a vessel constrained by her draught, but do not treat her as automatically top of the hierarchy.

pg_6490.label: Override standard crossing-rule stand-on/give-way determination when the other vessel outranks own-ship in the Rule 18 hierarchy.

pg_6492.label: Treat both vessels as having a shared duty to navigate with caution; do not assume a stand-on role.

pg_6493.label: Verify masthead light visibility range matches the vessel's size class minimum (e.g., 6 nm for 50m+, 2 nm for sub-12m vessels).

pg_6494.label: If an observed light's visible range falls below the minimum required for that vessel's size class, flag it as a possible equipment fault rather than assuming it is compliant.

pg_6496.label: Display a second, higher masthead light further aft if the vessel is 50 m or more in length.

pg_6497.label: Display sidelights, green to starboard and red to port.

pg_6499.label: If vessel is under 12 m, simplify to a single all-round white light plus sidelights.

pg_6500.label: When observing a contact showing only sidelights and a sternlight with no masthead light, classify it as a sailing vessel under Rule 25 rather than a power-driven vessel.

pg_6501.label: Show sidelights and a sternlight (no masthead light) while sailing underway.

pg_6502.label: If under 20 m, may combine sidelights and sternlight into a single tricolour lantern at the masthead.

pg_6503.label: If the engine is also being used to make way, show power-driven vessel lights and display a cone shape, apex down, forward.

pg_6504.label: Display two masthead lights in a vertical line when towing (instead of the normal one or two).

pg_6505.label: Display three masthead lights in a vertical line when the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres.

pg_6506.label: Show a yellow towing light above the sternlight.

pg_6507.label: Ensure the towed vessel or object shows its own sidelights and sternlight.

pg_6508.label: Identify a trawling vessel by green-over-white all-round lights (or two cones point-to-point by day).

pg_6509.label: Identify a vessel fishing with other gear (e.g., static or line gear) by red-over-white lights instead of green-over-white.

pg_6510.label: Look for an additional white light in the direction of any outlying gear extending more than 150 m from the vessel.

pg_6511.label: When observing red-over-white lights, anticipate that gear may extend in a fixed direction rather than trailing astern, and maneuver to keep clear accordingly.

pg_6512.label: Observe the vertical light/shape configuration of the contact.

pg_6513.label: Count the lights: two red lights (or two balls by day) = NUC.

pg_6514.label: Identify three lights in red-white-red sequence (or ball-diamond-ball by day) = RAM.

pg_6515.label: Adjust expectations of the contact's behavior based on classification.

pg_6516.label: Display three red lights in a vertical line (plus normal power-driven vessel lights) if constrained by draught.

pg_6517.label: Show a cylinder shape by day in place of the three red lights for a vessel constrained by draught.

pg_6518.label: Display white-over-red lights at the masthead when engaged on pilotage duty.

pg_6519.label: If a vessel is anchored and under 50 m in length, display a single all-round white light at night (a ball shape by day).

pg_6520.label: If a vessel is anchored and 50 m or more in length, display one all-round white light forward and a lower one aft.

pg_6521.label: When assessing a contact showing a single all-round white light with zero speed over multiple position updates, classify it as an anchored vessel under 50 m rather than a power-driven vessel with a light fault.

pg_6522.label: If NUC, RAM, constrained-by-draught, sailing, fishing, or towing/pushing, sound one prolonged plus two short blasts, regardless of making way status.

pg_6523.label: On hearing one prolonged plus two short blasts from another vessel, identify it as a special-category vessel before visual contact.

pg_6524.label: Verify the vessel's construction/build date against the relevant rule amendment date to determine exemption eligibility.

pg_6525.label: Apply the exemption only to the specific technical detail affected (e.g., light positioning), not broadly.

pg_6526.label: Continue full compliance with Rules 4-19 (steering and sailing conduct rules) regardless of exemption status.

pg_6527.label: Select a light or sound signal that cannot be confused with any signal already defined elsewhere in the Rules.

pg_6528.label: Aim any attention-getting light (e.g., searchlight) carefully so as not to embarrass or blind any vessel.

pg_6529.label: Do not improvise or use actual distress signals for non-emergency attention-getting purposes.

pg_6530.label: Use only the signals listed in Annex IV (e.g., continuous fog-horn, red flares/stars, spoken 'Mayday', slow raising/lowering of both arms, specified radio/EPIRB signals) to indicate genuine distress.

pg_6531.label: Do not invent or substitute a different signal to mean distress.

pg_6532.label: When assessing an observed signal, verify it matches the exact specification (e.g., red stars, not another colour) before treating it as an official distress signal.

pg_6533.label: Conduct field phase: examine occurrence site and wreckage, interview witnesses, collect pertinent information.

pg_6534.label: Conduct examination and analysis phase: review records, test wreckage components in lab, determine sequence of events, identify safety deficiencies.

pg_6535.label: Advise appropriate authority immediately when safety deficiencies are suspected or confirmed, without waiting for final report.

pg_6536.label: Prepare confidential draft report and send to directly concerned persons/corporations.

pg_6537.label: Allow concerned parties to dispute or correct information believed incorrect.

pg_6538.label: Board considers all representations before approving final report.

pg_6539.label: Release final report to the public.

pg_6540.label: Close the quick-closing fuel valve for the main engine day tank.

pg_6541.label: Activate the vessel's carbon dioxide fixed fire suppression system.

pg_6542.label: Stop the main engine and anchor the vessel.

pg_6543.label: Arrange for the vessel to be towed to port once safe.

pg_6544.label: Sound signals prescribed in the Collision Regulations for restricted visibility to warn other vessels of presence.

pg_6545.label: Maintain visual, auditory, and radar/AIS-based lookout appropriate to conditions.

pg_6546.label: Acquire sufficient knowledge of signals, lookout, safe speed, collision avoidance, and navigation in restricted visibility before operating in such conditions.

pg_6547.label: Develop familiarity with the navigation area, including known ferry services, before transiting it.

pg_6548.label: Search and rescue authorities attempt to contact the vessel after receiving the EPIRB signal.

pg_6549.label: Launch a search using multiple vessels and aircraft when contact attempts fail.

pg_6550.label: Recover all persons from the water and transport them to hospital.

pg_6551.label: Activate the fixed fire suppression system in the engine room upon fire detection

pg_6552.label: Allow the disabled vessel to drift to a safe location and drop anchor

pg_6553.label: Extinguish the fire fully before further action

pg_6554.label: Arrange for the vessel to be towed to a port facility (Québec, Quebec)

pg_6555.label: Deploy TSB investigators to the port where the vessel is towed

pg_6556.label: Determine whether the vessel meets the definition of a pleasure vessel (owned by individual(s) or a body corporate for sport/pleasure, or owned by a members' club, with no commercial payments beyond expense contributions or club funds).

pg_6557.label: If seeking exemption from a regulatory requirement, apply to the Secretary of State.

pg_6558.label: Confirm the exemption sought is compatible with the SOLAS Convention and that compliance is impracticable or unreasonable for that ship/class.

pg_6559.label: Comply with any terms the Secretary of State specifies as conditions of the exemption.

pg_6560.label: Issue any exemption, alteration, or cancellation in writing, specifying the effective date and the terms it is subject to.

pg_6561.label: Monitor compliance with the specified terms of an exemption.

pg_6562.label: Upon granting an exemption, issue an exemption certificate matching the SOLAS Appendix model and endorse the ship's Safety Management Certificate or Interim SMC to show the exemption's scope.

pg_6563.label: Authorise Certifying Authorities in accordance with the SOLAS Convention and the RO Code, applying conditions where needed (e.g., limiting authorisation to specific ships, classes, or extent of verification).

pg_6564.label: Reserve certain verifications exclusively to the Secretary of State where specified, excluding other Certifying Authorities from performing them.

pg_6565.label: If the ISM company is not the registered owner, the owner must report the full name and details of the ISM company to the Secretary of State.

pg_6566.label: The ISM company must comply with every applicable requirement of the ISM Code.

pg_6567.label: The ISM company must take all reasonable steps to ensure the ship is operated per the safety management system underlying its SMC/Interim SMC (or equivalent document for non-Convention flag states, to the Secretary of State's satisfaction).

pg_6568.label: The master must operate the ship in accordance with the safety management system underlying the ship's SMC/Interim SMC or equivalent document.

pg_6569.label: The designated person (DP) must monitor the safe and efficient operation of the ship, with particular regard to safety and pollution prevention.

pg_6570.label: The DP must take necessary steps to ensure compliance with the ship's safety management system.

pg_6571.label: The DP must ensure proper provision is made for the ship to be manned, equipped and maintained fit to operate under the SMS.

pg_6572.label: Do not operate a United Kingdom ship unless the ISM company holds a valid Document of Compliance or Interim Document of Compliance.

pg_6573.label: Arrange for a surveyor to carry out an initial or renewal verification and confirm compliance with applicable ISM Code requirements.

pg_6574.label: Pay any prescribed fee to the Certifying Authority for issuance or endorsement of the DOC.

pg_6575.label: Schedule an annual verification within the six-month window spanning three months before and three months after the DOC anniversary date.

pg_6576.label: Complete initial verification before the ship enters operation (or before expiry of an Interim DOC), and renewal verification before expiry of the existing DOC.

pg_6577.label: Keep a copy of the Document of Compliance on board each UK ship to which it relates and make it readily available for inspection at all times.

pg_6578.label: Submit to any additional verification required by the Certifying Authority at any time.

pg_6579.label: the other vessel must issue an SMC once notified by a surveyor that a valid Document of Compliance exists for the ISM company and an initial or renewal ship verification confirms compliance with applicable ISM Code requirements.

pg_6580.label: the other vessel must endorse the SMC following a surveyor's notification of a completed intermediate ship verification confirming compliance.

pg_6581.label: Ensure initial ship verification occurs before the ship enters operation or before expiry of an Interim SMC.

pg_6582.label: Ensure intermediate ship verification occurs between the second and third anniversary dates of the SMC.

pg_6583.label: Keep the SMC and any endorsements on board the ship and readily available for inspection at all times.

pg_6584.label: Certifying Authority may require an additional ship verification at any time.

pg_6585.label: Determine whether the company's circumstances fall under ISM Code paragraph 14.1.1 (newly established company) or 14.1.2 (adding new ship types to existing DOC).

pg_6586.label: Arrange for a surveyor to carry out an interim verification of the company.

pg_6587.label: Pay any prescribed fee and obtain the Interim Document of Compliance once the surveyor notifies the Certifying Authority of compliance.

pg_6588.label: Ensure the Interim DOC issued is in the form corresponding to the model given in the Appendix to the ISM Code.

pg_6589.label: Do not allow a UK ship to proceed or attempt to proceed to sea or on any voyage unless it holds a valid Safety Management Certificate or Interim Safety Management Certificate.

pg_6590.label: Confirm the ship's circumstance matches ISM Code 14.2.1, 14.2.2, or 14.2.3.

pg_6591.label: Ensure surveyor confirms a Document of Compliance or Interim DOC exists for the ISM company responsible for the ship.

pg_6592.label: Arrange for surveyor to carry out an interim ship verification.

pg_6593.label: Obtain ISMC in the model form given in the Appendix to the ISM Code.

pg_6594.label: Keep the Interim Safety Management Certificate on board and readily available for inspection at all times.

pg_6595.label: Track validity period: Interim DOC max 12 months from satisfactory interim verification; Interim SMC max 6 months from satisfactory interim ship verification.

pg_6596.label: Apply to Certifying Authority for extension of ISMC validity (up to 6 months) if needed before expiry.

pg_6597.label: Issue initial DOC/SMC for a validity period not exceeding five years from the date of satisfactory completion of the initial verification/ship verification.

pg_6598.label: If renewal verification is completed within three months before expiry of the existing certificate, issue the new certificate starting on completion date but set it to expire no later than five years after the old certificate's expiry.

pg_6599.label: If renewal ship verification for an SMC is completed after the existing SMC has expired, issue the new SMC to run from the day after the old expiry date, for up to five years.

pg_6600.label: If a new SMC cannot be issued or placed on board before the existing one expires, request the Certifying Authority endorse the existing SMC to extend its validity by up to five months from the day after expiry.

pg_6601.label: Surrender the DOC/Interim DOC and associated SMC/Interim SMC when required by the Certifying Authority.

pg_6602.label: Do not alter, falsify, or knowingly/recklessly furnish false information in connection with verification under regulations 13, 14, 16, or 17.

pg_6603.label: Do not use, lend, or allow another to use a relevant document with intent to deceive.

pg_6604.label: Certifying Authority assesses grounds (false/erroneous info, missed verification application deadline, or major non-conformity) before suspending or cancelling a DOC/Interim DOC.

pg_6605.label: If a company's DOC or Interim DOC is suspended or cancelled, the the other vessel must also suspend or cancel any associated SMC or Interim SMC issued for that ship.

pg_6606.label: Notify the ISM company in writing of the grounds for suspension or cancellation.

pg_6607.label: Ensure the notice specifies the effective date, and for suspensions, the terms of suspension.

pg_6608.label: Give the ISM company an opportunity to make representations before issuing the notice, unless urgent safety or pollution prevention considerations require immediate action.

pg_6609.label: Certifying Authority may extend validity of existing SMC for up to three months from the day after expiry, if appropriate, solely to allow the ship to reach the agreed port.

pg_6610.label: Do not allow the ship to leave the agreed port of verification until a new SMC has been issued.

pg_6611.label: Set the validity period of the new SMC to begin the day after the expiry date of the original (pre-extension) certificate.

pg_6612.label: Request the other government to verify compliance of an ISM company responsible for a UK ship with applicable ISM Code requirements.

pg_6613.label: Have the other government issue or endorse a Document of Compliance (or Interim DOC) if satisfied of company compliance.

pg_6614.label: Have the other government issue or endorse a Safety Management Certificate (or Interim SMC) if satisfied of ship compliance.

pg_6615.label: Ensure the issuing government includes a statement that the document has the same effect as if issued by the Secretary of State.

pg_6616.label: Instruct the other government to cancel or suspend a relevant document when notified by the Secretary of State of missed annual/intermediate verification or evidence of major non-conformity.

pg_6617.label: Serve written notice on the responsible person within 21 days of receiving notice of the verification outcome.

pg_6618.label: State in the notice that a dispute exists and request referral to a single arbitrator.

pg_6619.label: Attempt to appoint an arbitrator by agreement between the applicant and the responsible person.

pg_6620.label: If no agreement is reached, request the President or Vice President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators to appoint an arbitrator (not applicable in Scotland).

pg_6621.label: Verify the appointed arbitrator holds one of the specified qualifications (master/chief mate STCW II/2, chief/second engineer STCW III/2, equivalent certificate, naval architect, qualified person, special shipping experience, or CIArb member).

pg_6622.label: Conduct verification of the ISM company's or ship's compliance with applicable ISM Code requirements.

pg_6623.label: If compliance is verified and the relevant government requests it, issue or endorse a Document of Compliance/Interim DOC (for companies) or Safety Management Certificate/Interim SMC (for ships), subject to payment of the prescribed fee by the ISM company.

pg_6624.label: Suspend or cancel a previously issued relevant document if requested by the government of the other Convention country.

pg_6625.label: Appoint an arbitrator (or in Scotland, an arbiter) to resolve the dispute, by agreement between the parties or, in default, by a sheriff in Scotland.

pg_6626.label: Confer on the arbitrator the powers of an inspector under section 259 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 for carrying out functions under this regulation.

pg_6627.label: Apply the rules for arbitration set out in Merchant Shipping Notice M.1613.

pg_6628.label: Confirm the ISM company holds a valid compliance document for the ship's type before operating a non-UK ship in UK waters.

pg_6629.label: Verify a valid certificate is in force for the ship before it proceeds or attempts to proceed to sea or on any voyage from a UK port.

pg_6630.label: Ensure copies of the compliance document and the ship's certificate are held on board and readily available for inspection at all times.

pg_6631.label: Check the relevant document for suspension, cancellation, missing verification endorsements, or expiry before relying on its validity.

pg_6632.label: Determine whether clear grounds exist that the ship contravenes the ISM Regulations before detaining it.

pg_6633.label: Serve a detention notice on the master stating the grounds for detention.

pg_6634.label: Require compliance with the notice until the ship is released by a person mentioned in section 284(1) of the 1995 Act.

pg_6635.label: Allow the detention notice to be referred to arbitration under section 96 of the 1995 Act, subject to paragraph (5) modifications.

pg_6636.label: If a non-UK ship is detained, the Secretary of State must immediately inform the ship's flag administration in writing.

pg_6637.label: If the flag administration cannot be informed directly, inform the Consul of that State, or the nearest diplomatic representative if no Consul is available.

pg_6638.label: Upon request from the ISM company or master, release the detained ship if no proceedings for a regulation 24 offence are instituted within 7 days of detention.

pg_6639.label: Release the ship if proceedings instituted within the 7-day period conclude without conviction of the relevant defendant.

pg_6640.label: Release the ship if £30,000 (or Secretary of State-approved security of not less than that amount) is paid/given on behalf of the relevant defendant.

pg_6641.label: Where the defendant is convicted, release only once any ordered costs, expenses, and fines have been paid.

pg_6642.label: Release the ship if ordered by a court or tribunal under UNCLOS 1982 Article 292.

pg_6643.label: Repay the £30,000 sum or release the security if no proceedings are instituted within 7 days of payment, or if proceedings conclude without conviction.

pg_6644.label: If the defendant is convicted, apply the paid sum/security first to costs/expenses, then to any fine, and repay any balance to the payer.

pg_6645.label: Seek Secretary of State approval before installing alternative fitting, material, appliance or apparatus instead of the Regulation-required item.

pg_6646.label: Demonstrate that the alternative is at least as effective as the required item.

pg_6647.label: Determine whether the emission was necessary to secure the safety of the ship or to save life at sea.

pg_6648.label: Determine whether the emission resulted from damage to the ship or its equipment.

pg_6649.label: After damage or discovery of an emission, take all reasonable precautions to prevent or minimise further emission.

pg_6650.label: Ensure the owner or master did not act intending to cause damage, or recklessly with knowledge that damage would probably result.

pg_6651.label: Assess if the emission originates from an offshore platform's incineration or processing of sea-bed mineral resources (e.g., flaring, burning cuttings/muds, gas release during drilling).

pg_6652.label: Assess if the emission originates from a diesel engine solely dedicated to offshore sea-bed mineral exploration/exploitation/processing.

pg_6653.label: Do not put the ship into service, or continue it in service, past the applicable date specified unless an initial survey has been completed and a valid certificate issued.

pg_6654.label: Arrange for an initial survey to verify compliance with Part 3 or an approved regulation 4 alternative before the applicable deadline (18 May 2008, first scheduled dry-docking, or regulations' commencement date).

pg_6655.label: Before the appropriate certificate expires, arrange a renewal survey and obtain a new valid certificate.

pg_6656.label: Maintain the ship and its equipment in conformity with Part 3 at all times.

pg_6657.label: Do not alter surveyed equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements or materials except by direct replacement without prior approval.

pg_6658.label: Report any accident or defect substantially affecting ship integrity or equipment efficiency at the earliest opportunity to the Certifying Authority that issued the certificate.

pg_6659.label: If the ship is in a port outside the United Kingdom, also immediately report the accident or defect to the appropriate maritime authorities of that port's country.

pg_6660.label: Do not proceed to sea or remain at sea after the end of the annual survey period (or after the third anniversary date for intermediate survey) unless the survey requirements have been met.

pg_6661.label: Arrange for a survey of the ship to be carried out within the relevant survey period.

pg_6662.label: Ensure the surveyor confirms at the date of survey that equipment/systems remain satisfactory (annual) or fully comply with Part 3/permitted alternatives and are in good working order (intermediate).

pg_6663.label: Obtain the surveyor's endorsement on the appropriate certificate (IAPP or UKAPP) in the prescribed form.

pg_6664.label: Check whether regulation 6(2) or 8(2) requirements were already met during the annual survey period, which would exempt the ship from the paragraph (1) prohibition.

pg_6665.label: Identify whether the ship has undergone a repair from a regulation 9(5) investigation or any important repair/renewal.

pg_6666.label: Do not allow the ship to proceed to sea or remain at sea unless the survey requirements in paragraph (3) are met.

pg_6667.label: Arrange for a survey (the 'additional survey') to be carried out on the ship.

pg_6668.label: Ensure the surveyor confirms the repair/renewal was made effectively, materials and workmanship are satisfactory, and the ship complies fully with Part 3.

pg_6669.label: Obtain the surveyor's issued survey report expressing satisfaction before proceeding.

pg_6670.label: Carry out an initial or renewal survey of the ship's equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements and materials.

pg_6671.label: Issue an appropriate certificate once satisfied the ship fully complies as at the date of survey.

pg_6672.label: For a ship transferring flag, verify an IAPP Certificate was issued and still valid immediately before transfer.

pg_6673.label: Cause a survey to be carried out on the transferring ship and confirm its condition conforms with Annex VI.

pg_6674.label: Confirm no unapproved changes have been made to equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements or material since the last survey, other than direct replacement with conforming equipment.

pg_6675.label: Issue the IAPP Certificate in English using the form in Appendix 1 to Annex VI, or the UKAPP Certificate in the form prescribed by the Secretary of State in Appendix 5 to MSN 1819 (M+F).

pg_6676.label: Receive request from Contracting Government to survey ship and issue/authorise/endorse an IAPP Certificate under Annex VI.

pg_6677.label: Issue the IAPP Certificate in English using the form in Appendix 1 to Annex VI, stating it was issued pursuant to the request.

pg_6678.label: Treat the Secretary of State as the Certifying Authority for that certificate.

pg_6679.label: Send a copy of the IAPP Certificate and the survey report to the requesting Contracting Government as soon as possible.

pg_6680.label: Refuse to issue an IAPP Certificate if the ship is registered in, or entitled to fly the flag of, a country whose Government is not a Contracting Government.

pg_6681.label: Ensure the appropriate certificate is issued for a period not exceeding five years from completion of the initial or renewal survey.

pg_6682.label: Treat the certificate as ceasing to be valid upon transfer of the ship to another State's flag, uncorrected repairs/renewals under regulation 10(1) without compliance with regulation 10(3), failure to complete a required survey under regulations 5-8, failure to endorse the certificate, issuance of a new certificate, or reaching the certificate's expiry date — whichever occurs earliest.

pg_6683.label: When a ship is transferred to the flag of another Contracting Government and that Government requests it within three months of transfer, the Secretary of State must send a copy of the IAPP certificate and, if available, the survey report.

pg_6684.label: If the certificate's validity period is under five years, the Certifying Authority may extend it to a maximum of five years, provided the required survey under regulation 7 or 8 has been carried out.

pg_6685.label: If a renewal survey is completed but the new certificate cannot be issued/placed aboard before expiry, have the surveyor endorse the latest certificate.

pg_6686.label: Treat an endorsed certificate as valid for the specified further period, not exceeding five months from the original expiry date.

pg_6687.label: If the renewal survey has not been completed by expiry and the ship is not in the survey port, request the Certifying Authority to extend validity by up to three months solely to allow the voyage to the survey port.

pg_6688.label: Do not depart the port of survey until a new appropriate certificate has been issued after a paragraph (4) extension.

pg_6689.label: For ships engaged solely on short voyages, the Certifying Authority may extend the latest certificate's validity by up to one month, subject to paragraph (7).

pg_6690.label: Do not permit a one-month short-voyage extension (paragraph 6) if the certificate has already been extended under paragraph (1), (3), or (4).

pg_6691.label: Once the renewal survey is completed and a new certificate issued for a ship under paragraph (5) or (6), the new certificate is valid for up to five years from the original expiry date of the previous certificate, subject to paragraph (9) and regulations 16(3) and 18(1).

pg_6692.label: When the period of validity is extended under paragraphs (1), (4) or (6), or an endorsement is required under paragraph (2), the the other vessel must endorse the appropriate certificate per paragraph (11).

pg_6693.label: Use the correct endorsement form: Appendix 1 to Annex VI for an IAPP certificate, or Appendix 5 to Merchant Shipping Notice 1819 (M+F) for a UKAPP certificate.

pg_6694.label: If an annual survey (regulation 7) or intermediate survey (regulation 8) is completed before its due survey period, amend the anniversary date by endorsement to a date no more than three months later than the survey completion date.

pg_6695.label: After amending the anniversary date, schedule subsequent annual/intermediate surveys at the prescribed intervals measured from the new anniversary date.

pg_6696.label: Alternatively, where a survey is completed early, leave the certificate's expiry date unchanged provided subsequent required surveys are still carried out within the maximum prescribed intervals.

pg_6697.label: Surveyor advises the owner or master of the corrective action required.

pg_6698.label: Surveyor notifies the Certifying Authority that issued the certificate that the owner/master have been advised.

pg_6699.label: Surveyor notifies the Certifying Authority if the corrective action is not taken.

pg_6700.label: Certifying Authority may suspend validity of the certificate until corrective action is taken.

pg_6701.label: Certifying Authority immediately gives notice of suspension to the ship's owner, and to the appropriate maritime authorities of the foreign port if applicable.

pg_6702.label: Owner notifies the master of the suspension upon receiving notice.

pg_6703.label: Serve written notice on the responsible person within 21 days of receiving notification of the survey outcome.

pg_6704.label: Select an arbitrator meeting the qualification criteria (certificated master/chief mate, chief/second engineer officer, equivalent certificate holder, naval architect, qualified person, person with shipping/fishing/port industry experience, or Chartered Institute of Arbitrators member).

pg_6705.label: In Scotland, if no agreement on an arbiter is reached, apply for appointment by a sheriff.

pg_6706.label: Apply the arbitration rules in Merchant Shipping Notice M 1613 unless both parties agree alternative procedures before arbitration begins.

pg_6707.label: Cancel the appropriate certificate if issued on false/erroneous information or if equipment/machinery is deficient since last survey.

pg_6708.label: Require surrender of an expired or cancelled certificate within a specified time and manner.

pg_6709.label: Owner and master must keep the appropriate certificate readily available on board for inspection at all times.

pg_6710.label: Do not allow the ship to proceed to sea from a UK port unless a valid IAPP certificate exists, a surveyor confirms no unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment, or a person with detention power permits transit to the nearest repair yard.

pg_6711.label: Where Annex VI survey documentation is required but no certificate issued, ensure equivalent valid documentation showing survey completion and surveyor satisfaction exists before departure, or obtain permission to sail to nearest repair yard.

pg_6712.label: Harbour authority or terminal operator must obtain written approval from the Secretary of State before operating a VOC vapour emission control system.

pg_6713.label: Harbour authority or terminal operator operating a VECS must comply with Schedule 4 of Merchant Shipping Notice 1819 (M+F).

pg_6714.label: Owner and master of a UK tanker subject to vapour emission control at an IMO-notified designated harbour/terminal must comply with Schedule 4 of MSN 1819 (M+F).

pg_6715.label: Owner and master of a non-UK tanker in UK waters subject to vapour emission control at a Secretary of State-designated harbour/terminal must ensure the tanker is fitted with an approved, fully operational vapour emission collection system.

pg_6716.label: Master must produce evidence of the flag-state approval of the vapour emission collection system on demand to the harbour authority, terminal operator, or surveyor.

pg_6717.label: Do not deliberately emit ozone-depleting substances during maintenance, servicing, repair or disposal of ship systems/equipment.

pg_6718.label: Allow only minimal releases associated with recapture or recycling of ozone-depleting substances.

pg_6719.label: Do not install new equipment containing ozone-depleting substances on non-UK ships.

pg_6720.label: For installations before 1 January 2020, treat hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) as excepted from the installation ban.

pg_6721.label: Owner may apply to the Secretary of State for a direction exempting an engine from NOx regulation if the ship was constructed or the engine underwent a major conversion before 19 May 2005.

pg_6722.label: Ensure engine NOx emissions comply with the specified limit (e.g., up to 17.0–45.0 g/kWh depending on engine rating) unless exempted.

pg_6723.label: Ensure all shipboard incineration occurs only in a shipboard incinerator (unless paragraph 6 exception applies).

pg_6724.label: If incinerator installed after 31 Dec 1999, demonstrate compliance to a surveyor on demand.

pg_6725.label: For UK ships solely on UK-waters voyages with incinerators installed on or before 18 May 2005, apply to the Secretary of State for exemption from paragraph (2) if desired.

pg_6726.label: Never incinerate Annex I/II/III cargo residues and contaminated packing, PCBs, garbage with more than trace heavy metals, or halogenated refined petroleum products.

pg_6727.label: Do not incinerate sewage sludge or sludge oil in the main/auxiliary power plant or boiler while in port, harbour, or estuary.

pg_6728.label: Do not incinerate polyvinyl chlorides unless using an incinerator with a valid Type Approval Certificate.

pg_6729.label: Carry the manufacturer's operating manual on board at all times, specifying operation within Schedule 5 of MSN 1819 (M+F) limits.

pg_6730.label: Ensure every person responsible for operating the incinerator is trained and capable per the manufacturer's manual.

pg_6731.label: Submit alternative shipboard thermal waste treatment device design, installation and operation details to the Secretary of State for approval.

pg_6732.label: Determine if the substance in question (coal in solid form, nuclear fuels, or platform-produced hydrocarbon used as platform fuel) is exempt before applying the regulation.

pg_6733.label: If using platform-produced hydrocarbon as fuel on that platform, obtain Secretary of State approval for that specific use to qualify for exemption.

pg_6734.label: Continuously monitor combustion flue gas outlet temperatures.

pg_6735.label: Do not feed waste into a continuous-feed incinerator when temperature is below 850°C.

pg_6736.label: Do not use a batch-loaded incinerator if combustion chamber fails to reach 600°C within 5 minutes of start-up.

pg_6737.label: Ensure fuel oil used on board meets the composition requirements of paragraph (4) petroleum-refined blends or (5) non-petroleum-refined fuel oil as applicable.

pg_6738.label: Obtain a bunker delivery note from the local fuel oil supplier containing required information and a signed declaration of conformity with regulations 14(1)/14(4)(a) and 18(1) of Annex VI.

pg_6739.label: Keep the bunker delivery note on board in a readily available location for inspection at all reasonable times.

pg_6740.label: Retain the bunker delivery note for three years from the date of delivery.

pg_6741.label: Certify whether any copy of the bunker delivery note is a true copy of the original when requested by an inspector.

pg_6742.label: Have the local supplier's representative collect a representative fuel oil sample in accordance with Schedule 7 and Appendix 1 to MSN 1819 (M+F).

pg_6743.label: Seal and sign the sample jointly with the local supplier's representative and the master or officer in charge of bunkering upon completion of operations.

pg_6744.label: Retain the sample under the master's or owner's control for at least twelve months from delivery, or until the fuel is substantially consumed if that takes longer.

pg_6745.label: Keep the bunker delivery note and sample available for inspection and verification at all reasonable times per Schedule 7 to MSN 1819 (M+F).

pg_6746.label: Make the bunker delivery note available for copies to be made at all reasonable times.

pg_6747.label: Detain the ship when any of the listed certificate, documentation, condition, crew-familiarity, or offence conditions are met.

pg_6748.label: Hold the ship until a surveyor of ships confirms it can proceed without presenting unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6749.label: Allow the detained ship to proceed only to the nearest appropriate repair yard if the detaining authority permits it.

pg_6750.label: If the detained ship is not a UK ship, immediately inform the consul/diplomatic representative or maritime authorities of the flag State.

pg_6751.label: At the request of the owner, master, demise charterer or manager, release the ship if £30,000 is paid as security or equivalent satisfactory security is given to the Secretary of State.

pg_6752.label: If proceedings conclude without conviction, repay the sum or release the security to the person who provided it.

pg_6753.label: Limit inspection to verifying validity of the appropriate air pollution certificate.

pg_6754.label: Verify validity of appropriate documentation referenced in regulation 19(2).

pg_6755.label: Investigate any operation regulated by the Regulations only if there are clear grounds the master/crew are unfamiliar with essential shipboard air-pollution-prevention procedures.

pg_6756.label: Verify whether the ship emitted substances in violation of the Regulations.

pg_6757.label: Inspect log book entries and bunker delivery notes made available under regulation 25(8)(a).

pg_6758.label: Do not exceed these inspection limits unless there are clear grounds the ship's condition/equipment does not substantially correspond to the certificate or documentation particulars.

pg_6759.label: When inspecting for sub-paragraph (2)(d) purposes, notify the flag State's consul/diplomatic representative or maritime authority and any requesting Party to the Convention.

pg_6760.label: When copying log book entries or bunker delivery notes, require the master to certify the copy as a true copy.

pg_6761.label: Treat certified copies as admissible evidence in judicial proceedings.

pg_6762.label: Upon evidence a UK ship emitted a substance in violation, the Secretary of State must cause the matter to be investigated.

pg_6763.label: Inform the IMO of the action taken.

pg_6764.label: Inform the reporting State of the action taken, if another State reported the violation.

pg_6765.label: Immediately release the ship if no proceedings for the offence are brought, or on payment/security of £30,000, or on a court/tribunal order under UNCLOS Article 292 with bond posted.

pg_6766.label: Repay any sum paid or release any security given under paragraph (4)(c) once proceedings conclude without conviction.

pg_6767.label: Suspend UK proceedings upon request of the foreign State once instituted but not concluded.

pg_6768.label: Transmit all evidence, court records, documents, and any sums paid or security given to the requesting foreign State.

pg_6769.label: Suspend UK proceedings if the court is satisfied the flag State instituted corresponding proceedings within six months of UK institution.

pg_6770.label: Do not suspend (or resume) proceedings if the Secretary of State certifies the flag State has repeatedly disregarded its Convention enforcement obligations.

pg_6771.label: Terminate suspended UK proceedings once the flag State's proceedings reach a conclusion.

pg_6772.label: Raise due diligence defence by proving all reasonable steps were taken to ensure compliance with the regulation in question.

pg_6773.label: Raise additional defence where the ship was not a UK ship, the emission occurred outside controlled/UK waters, or the ship was in a UK port only due to stress of weather or circumstances beyond control of master/owner/charterer/manager.

pg_6774.label: Treat a pre-existing Annex II certificate as continuing to be valid until its expiry date under regulation 10 of Annex II, unless the Secretary of State determines otherwise.

pg_6775.label: Treat such a continuing certificate as if it had been issued or endorsed under these Regulations.

pg_6776.label: Classify substances and ship types using the definitions given (Certifying Authority, NLS ship, IGC/IBC Code categories X, Y, Z) when determining applicable certification and carriage requirements.

pg_6777.label: Ensure a relevant initial survey (or renewal survey, if certificate has expired) has been carried out on the ship.

pg_6778.label: Confirm the surveyor is satisfied that structure, equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements and materials comply with relevant requirements.

pg_6779.label: Verify an approved Procedures and Arrangements Manual and Cargo Record Book are on board.

pg_6780.label: For NLS ships of 150 gross tonnage or more, confirm an approved Marine Pollution Emergency Plan or Shipboard Marine the other vessel is on board.

pg_6781.label: Ensure a relevant (or new, following renewal survey) NLS certificate has been issued and remains valid before the ship proceeds to sea or continues service.

pg_6782.label: Ensure a relevant annual survey (or, at the third anniversary, a relevant intermediate survey) is carried out in respect of the ship before the applicable deadline.

pg_6783.label: Obtain the surveyor's endorsement of the relevant NLS certificate.

pg_6784.label: Determine ship type (chemical tanker vs gas carrier) and construction/adaptation date.

pg_6785.label: Apply regulation 12.1, 12.5-12.11, Appendix 5 of Annex II, and BCH Code Chapters II & III for chemical tankers built/adapted before 1 July 1986.

pg_6786.label: Apply Regulation 5.3 of Annex II for gas carriers.

pg_6787.label: Accept alternative fittings/materials/appliances/apparatus as meeting relevant requirements only if approved under the procedure in regulation 7.

pg_6788.label: Determine whether the ship is a UK NLS ship (regulations apply wherever it is) or another NLS ship (regulations apply only while in UK waters).

pg_6789.label: Apply regulation 20(1) and (2) to non-UK ships engaged in voyages to ports/offshore installations of another Contracting State while they are in a UK port or at a UK/controlled-waters offshore installation (excluding floating platforms in transit).

pg_6790.label: Apply regulation 24 to any ship whose discharge into the sea has caused or is likely to cause pollution within UK waters.

pg_6791.label: Apply regulation 26 to any ship enabled to proceed contrary to that regulation's requirements where this has caused or is likely to cause pollution within UK waters.

pg_6792.label: If seeking relief from the Regulations, have the owner/master submit a written exemption request to the Secretary of State.

pg_6793.label: Confirm any exemption sought is of a type permitted under Annex II before expecting it to be granted.

pg_6794.label: To use an alternative fitting, material, appliance or apparatus, have the owner/master apply to the Secretary of State and obtain a surveyor's endorsement confirming it is at least as effective as the regulation-compliant equivalent.

pg_6795.label: Fit and operate the approved equivalent strictly per the conditions/limitations stated in the approval.

pg_6796.label: Determine if the repair/renewal qualifies as 'important' (addresses a defect substantially affecting ship/equipment integrity or efficiency, or is needed for Annex II compliance).

pg_6797.label: If there is a dispute about whether a repair/renewal is 'important', the owner or master may serve a written request on the Secretary of State for advice.

pg_6798.label: Treat the repair/renewal as not important unless the Secretary of State advises otherwise within 21 days of the request.

pg_6799.label: Maintain the ship and its equipment in conformity with relevant requirements at all times.

pg_6800.label: Obtain approval from the Certifying Authority that appointed the surveyor, or from the Secretary of State where the survey was carried out by a Contracting State other than the UK pursuant to regulation 16, before making non-replacement changes.

pg_6801.label: the other vessel must initiate an investigation upon report of accident/defect to determine need for additional survey or repair, and carry it out if necessary.

pg_6802.label: the other vessel must take steps to confirm that the port state notification requirement was fulfilled when the ship is in a foreign port.

pg_6803.label: Issue a relevant NLS certificate once notified by a surveyor that a relevant initial or renewal survey has been carried out and compliance confirmed.

pg_6804.label: Confirm any fee due has been paid before issuing the certificate.

pg_6805.label: For a ship transferring from another Contracting State's flag, verify an Annex II-compliant certificate was issued and valid immediately before transfer.

pg_6806.label: Cause a survey to be carried out on the transferring ship and confirm its condition poses no unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6807.label: Secretary of State may request another Contracting State to survey a UK NLS ship.

pg_6808.label: If the requested State is satisfied requirements are met, it must issue/authorise issue of an NLS certificate or endorse an existing one.

pg_6809.label: If satisfied requirements are met (and fee paid), issue a new certificate or endorse the existing one.

pg_6810.label: Ensure certificate is in the form prescribed in Annex II and states it was issued/endorsed under this arrangement.

pg_6811.label: Send a copy of the survey report and any certificate issued/endorsed to the requesting Contracting State as soon as possible after survey completion.

pg_6812.label: Do not issue or endorse a certificate for a ship registered in, or entitled to fly the flag of, a non-Contracting State.

pg_6813.label: On transfer to another Contracting State's flag, send a copy of the certificate and any current survey report to that Government if requested within three months of transfer.

pg_6814.label: Resolve disputes over whether a repair or renewal is 'important' via the procedure in regulation 14(5) and (6).

pg_6815.label: Issue the new NLS certificate with a validity period not exceeding five years from the original expiry date of the previous certificate, unless paragraph (10) circumstances apply.

pg_6816.label: If the owner wants the new validity period to start from the date the renewal survey was completed, submit a written request to the Certifying Authority.

pg_6817.label: Satisfy the Certifying Authority that the request is justified.

pg_6818.label: Comply with any reasonable additional survey requirements imposed by the Certifying Authority.

pg_6819.label: Endorse the relevant NLS certificate when its validity period is extended under paragraph (1), (4) or (6).

pg_6820.label: Endorse the relevant NLS certificate when required under paragraph (2).

pg_6821.label: Surveyor immediately advises the owner or master of the corrective action required.

pg_6822.label: If the ship holds a valid relevant NLS certificate, surveyor notifies the Certifying Authority that the owner/master has been advised.

pg_6823.label: Certifying Authority suspends the validity of the relevant NLS certificate if corrective action is not taken within the time specified by the surveyor.

pg_6824.label: Owner notifies the master of the ship of the certificate suspension.

pg_6825.label: Verify the ship holds a valid NLS certificate issued (and endorsed where appropriate) by a Contracting State before allowing departure.

pg_6826.label: If no Contracting State certificate exists, accept an equivalent certificate from a non-Contracting State government only if the Certifying Authority deems it to have equivalent force to an Annex II certificate.

pg_6827.label: Alternatively, have a surveyor conduct a survey as if regulation 9 applied and confirm the ship can proceed without unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6828.label: Alternatively, a person with power to detain may permit the ship to proceed solely to the nearest appropriate repair yard if satisfied it poses no unreasonable threat of harm.

pg_6829.label: If dissatisfied with a relevant survey outcome for a UK NLS ship, serve written notice on the responsible person within 21 days of notification, stating the dispute and requesting referral to a single arbitrator.

pg_6830.label: If no agreement is reached, a party gives written notice to the other party and requests the President or Vice President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators to appoint an arbitrator (or the parties jointly request this).

pg_6831.label: Verify the appointed arbitrator holds one of the specified qualifications (master/chief mate STCW II/2 certificate, chief/second engineer STCW III/2 certificate, equivalent certificate, naval architect, qualified person, special shipping/port experience, or CIArb membership).

pg_6832.label: Secretary of State may cancel a relevant NLS certificate if issued on false/erroneous information or if equipment/machinery has become damaged or deficient since survey.

pg_6833.label: Secretary of State may require surrender of an expired or cancelled relevant NLS certificate.

pg_6834.label: Treat all discharge of noxious liquid substances or NLS-containing mixtures as prohibited by default.

pg_6835.label: Ensure the ship is proceeding en route at a minimum speed of 7 knots (self-propelled) or 4 knots (not self-propelled) before discharging.

pg_6836.label: Discharge only below the waterline through underwater outlet(s) at or below the designed maximum rate.

pg_6837.label: Discharge only at least 12 nautical miles from nearest land and in water depth of at least 25 metres.

pg_6838.label: Ensure discharge complies with conditions in Annex II regulation 13, paragraphs 1.2 and 4 to 7.

pg_6839.label: Prohibit any NLS discharge in polar waters regardless of other conditions met.

pg_6840.label: For NLS ships constructed before 1 January 2007, discharge of Category Z substances need not meet the underwater-outlet condition (paragraph (2)(b)).

pg_6841.label: Treat water introduced into a tank after ventilation procedures under paragraph (5) as not being a noxious liquid substance.

pg_6842.label: If discharge is necessary to secure the safety of the ship or to save life, proceed without violating paragraphs (1) and (3).

pg_6843.label: If discharge results from damage to the ship or equipment, take all reasonable precautions after the damage or discovery to prevent or minimise the discharge.

pg_6844.label: Obtain Secretary of State approval if discharging to combat a specific pollution incident in order to minimise pollution damage.

pg_6845.label: Ensure no noxious liquid substance in terminal cargo hoses/piping drains back to the ship during unloading.

pg_6846.label: Do not proceed to sea or remain at sea while carrying any liquid substance not categorised, provisionally assessed, or evaluated per Annex II regulation 6.

pg_6847.label: Do not permit loading or carriage of an NLS subject to a tripartite agreement unless a valid NLS certificate is in force and loading/carriage complies with its terms.

pg_6848.label: Maintain an approved Procedures and Arrangements Manual on board in the standard Appendix 4 format, in English (UK ships) or English/French/Spanish (other NLS ships).

pg_6849.label: Record promptly in the Cargo Record Book the completion of any Appendix 2 operation.

pg_6850.label: On accidental discharge or discharge under regulation 3, enter the circumstances and reason for the discharge in the Cargo Record Book.

pg_6851.label: Have the officer(s) in charge of the relevant operation sign each entry.

pg_6852.label: Write the Cargo Record Book in English (UK NLS ships) or in/translated into English, French or Spanish (other NLS ships).

pg_6853.label: If an entry is also written in the ship's national language, treat that national-language entry as prevailing in case of dispute or discrepancy.

pg_6854.label: Keep the Cargo Record Book readily available for inspection and on board the ship (except unmanned ships under tow).

pg_6855.label: Retain the Cargo Record Book for three years after the last entry.

pg_6856.label: Ensure the plan is developed per relevant Guidelines, written in a language understood by master and officers, and contains the minimum information per regulation 17.2.1-17.2.4 of Annex II.

pg_6857.label: Where combined with another required plan, title it 'Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan'.

pg_6858.label: Ensure the ship's construction and operation complies with the environment-related provisions of the Introduction to the Polar Code.

pg_6859.label: Ensure compliance with Chapter 2 of Part II-A of the Polar Code.

pg_6860.label: Verify whether a relevant NLS certificate has been issued and is still valid.

pg_6861.label: Verify whether documentation referred to in regulation 21 has been issued and is still valid.

pg_6862.label: Inspect the Procedures and Arrangements Manual.

pg_6864.label: Inspect the Marine Pollution Emergency Plan only where there are clear grounds the ship or equipment condition does not substantially correspond with the certificate/documentation particulars.

pg_6865.label: Only board the ship if it is in a UK port or at an offshore installation in UK waters or controlled waters.

pg_6866.label: For non-UK ships inspected under the crew-unfamiliarity ground, send the inspection report to the flag State's consul/diplomatic representative or maritime authority, and to any requesting Contracting State.

pg_6867.label: Upon receiving evidence of an unlawful NLS discharge from a UK ship, cause the matter to be investigated.

pg_6868.label: If a surveyor has clear grounds for certificate, documentation, condition, crew-familiarity, or offence deficiencies, detain the ship until satisfied it can proceed without unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6869.label: A person with detention powers may permit a detained ship to proceed to the nearest appropriate repair yard.

pg_6870.label: Detain a ship if a surveyor has clear grounds to believe an offence under regulation 24 or 26(2) has been committed.

pg_6871.label: Only exercise detention power if the ship is in a UK port or at an offshore installation in UK waters or controlled waters.

pg_6872.label: Release the ship immediately upon request if no proceedings under regulation 24 or 26(2) are instituted within seven days of detention.

pg_6873.label: Release the ship, if convicted, only after any ordered costs, expenses and fines have been paid.

pg_6874.label: Harbour master assesses whether clear grounds exist to believe an offence under regulation 24 or 26(2) has occurred.

pg_6875.label: Harbour master detains the ship if grounds are established.

pg_6876.label: Apply section 144(2) and (3) of the 1995 Act to the detention as if it were a detention under section 144(1).

pg_6877.label: Apply the paid sum or security first to any costs or expenses ordered by the court to be paid by the owner, manager, demise charterer or master.

pg_6878.label: Apply any remaining amount to payment of any fine imposed by the court.

pg_6879.label: Repay any balance remaining to the person who originally paid the sum or gave the security.

pg_6880.label: Release the ship, where conviction occurs, once any ordered costs, expenses and fines have been paid.

pg_6881.label: Release the ship if ordered by a court or tribunal under UNCLOS Article 292, once any bond or financial security ordered is posted.

pg_6882.label: For offences under regulation 24 or 26(2), additionally prove the ship was not a UK ship, the discharge occurred outside controlled or UK waters, and the ship's presence in a UK port at the time proceedings began was due only to stress of weather or other reasons beyond control of master/owner/charterer/manager.

pg_6883.label: Do not institute UK proceedings against a non-UK ship for a foreign-waters contravention unless the foreign State, flag State, or an affected/threatened State requests it, or the offence caused/threatens pollution in UK/controlled waters.

pg_6884.label: Secretary of State must transmit all evidence, court records, documents and any sums paid or security given to the requesting foreign State.

pg_6885.label: Do not suspend proceedings if the contravention caused serious pollution to the UK, or if the Secretary of State certifies the flag State has repeatedly failed to enforce Convention requirements.

pg_6886.label: Determine if the ship is a UK oil tanker of 150 GT and above, or a UK non-tanker of 400 GT and above.

pg_6887.label: If the ship engages in international voyages, subject it to all surveys described in paragraph (4).

pg_6888.label: If the ship does not engage in international voyages, subject it to surveys described in paragraph (4)(a), (b) and (e) only.

pg_6889.label: Determine if the ship falls under the Regulations (UK ship anywhere, or non-UK ship in UK waters) and check for exemptions (warship, naval auxiliary, government non-commercial vessel).

pg_6890.label: If the ship has a cargo space of 200+ cubic metres used to carry oil in bulk, apply relevant construction/operation regulations (16, 26.4, 29-32, 34, 36 of Annex I), substituting regulation 34.6 for 29, 31 and 32 if capacity is under 1,000 cubic metres.

pg_6891.label: Ensure the ship has been surveyed per applicable requirements and holds a valid IOPP Certificate (international voyages) or UKOPP Certificate (non-international voyages) before allowing it to proceed or remain at sea.

pg_6892.label: Owner/master applies to Secretary of State for exemption or for approval of an alternative fitting/material/appliance/apparatus.

pg_6893.label: Secretary of State confirms the ship's construction/equipment provides equivalent protection from oil pollution before granting a construction/equipment exemption.

pg_6894.label: Record particulars of any granted exemption in the IOPP or UKOPP certificate.

pg_6895.label: Ensure any general exemption under paragraph (3) is given in writing, with stated conditions/limitations, and is compatible with Annex I requirements.

pg_6896.label: For alternative fittings, have a surveyor assess and endorse the application confirming the item is at least as effective as the Annex I requirement.

pg_6897.label: Ensure ship and equipment condition is maintained to conform with these Regulations (UK ships) or Annex I (other ships) so the ship remains fit to proceed to sea without unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6898.label: If a non-UK ship is in a UK port, report the accident/defect to the Secretary of State.

pg_6899.label: Certifying Authority, upon receiving a report, must investigate to determine if an additional survey or repair is necessary and arrange it if so.

pg_6900.label: Complete an initial survey per regulation 6.1.1 of Annex I before the ship enters service or before an IOPP/UKOPP Certificate is first issued.

pg_6901.label: Complete an intermediate survey within three months of the second or third anniversary date of certificate issue.

pg_6902.label: Complete an annual survey within three months of each anniversary date, unless an intermediate survey has already covered that period.

pg_6903.label: Complete an additional survey (general or partial) after a repair following regulation 11(5) investigations, or when an important repair/renewal is made.

pg_6904.label: Confirm the ship falls within scope (oil tanker ≥150 GT, or non-tanker ≥400 GT on international voyages).

pg_6905.label: Ensure any fee due under the Merchant Shipping (Fees) Regulations 2018 is paid.

pg_6906.label: Certifying Authority endorses the IOPP Certificate after intermediate/annual survey if Annex I requirements are satisfied.

pg_6907.label: Secretary of State may request a Contracting State to survey a ship and issue/endorse an IOPP Certificate per Annex I.

pg_6908.label: Include a statement in the certificate noting it was issued/endorsed at the request of the Convention Country's Administration.

pg_6909.label: Ensure the IOPP Certificate is in the form prescribed in Appendix II to Annex I, including Supplements.

pg_6910.label: Do not issue an IOPP Certificate to a ship flying the flag of a non-Convention Country.

pg_6911.label: Certifying Authority issues the UKOPP Certificate once satisfied that Annex I requirements are complied with.

pg_6912.label: Issue the certificate in the form prescribed in Appendix II to Annex I, with modifications substituting 'IOPP Certificate' references with 'UKOPP Certificate' and omitting annual/intermediate survey endorsement provisions.

pg_6913.label: Ensure Certifying Authority issues IOPP/UKOPP Certificate for a period not exceeding five years.

pg_6914.label: If intermediate/annual survey completed early, endorse the IOPP certificate to amend anniversary date to no more than 3 months later than survey completion.

pg_6915.label: Keep expiry date unchanged only if all required intermediate/annual surveys are completed within maximum intervals.

pg_6916.label: Issue the new certificate (after renewal survey under the short-voyage extension) for up to five years from the original expiry date.

pg_6917.label: Owner satisfies the Certifying Authority that the request is justified.

pg_6918.label: Owner complies with any reasonable additional survey requirements imposed by the Certifying Authority.

pg_6919.label: Cancel the IOPP or UKOPP certificate if false/erroneous information is suspected or post-survey deficiency is identified.

pg_6920.label: Require surrender of any expired or cancelled IOPP/UKOPP certificate to the Secretary of State.

pg_6921.label: Verify the candidate holds one of the specified qualifications (master/chief mate certificate per STCW II/2, chief/second engineer certificate per STCW III/2, equivalent certificate, naval architect, qualified person, shipping/port experience, or CIArb membership) before appointment.

pg_6922.label: Inform the owner or master of the required corrective action and notify the Secretary of State.

pg_6923.label: If corrective action is not completed within the specified reasonable period, withdraw the IOPP or UKOPP Certificate and notify the owner/master and Secretary of State.

pg_6924.label: If the ship is in a port of another Convention Country when withdrawal occurs, notify that country's appropriate authorities.

pg_6925.label: If a foreign Convention Country ship in a UK port needs its IOPP Certificate withdrawn, the the other vessel must notify the Secretary of State.

pg_6926.label: On receiving such notification, the Secretary of State must ensure the ship does not sail until it can proceed without presenting an unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment, or may only leave for the nearest appropriate repair yard.

pg_6927.label: Confirm a the other vessel has issued and (where appropriate) endorsed a valid IOPP certificate for the ship.

pg_6928.label: If not a Contracting State, confirm a non-Contracting State's IOPP certificate is deemed by the Certifying Authority to have equivalent force and remains valid.

pg_6929.label: If no valid certificate exists, arrange for a surveyor of ships to carry out a survey as if regulation 10(4)(a) applied.

pg_6930.label: Obtain surveyor's satisfaction that the ship can proceed without presenting an unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_6931.label: Ensure the ship carries an Oil Record Book Part I (Machinery Space Operations) if it is an oil tanker of 150 GT+ or any other ship of 400 GT+.

pg_6932.label: Complete ORB Part I on a tank-to-tank basis whenever a listed machinery space operation (reg 17.2 Annex I) occurs.

pg_6933.label: Complete ORB Part II on a tank-to-tank basis whenever a listed cargo/ballast operation (reg 36.2 or 36.3 Annex I) occurs.

pg_6934.label: Record the circumstances and reasons for any discharge of oil or oily mixture (reg 17.3 or 36.4 Annex I), or any accidental/exceptional discharge not excepted, in the relevant ORB part.

pg_6935.label: Fully record each oil operation in the Oil Record Book without delay.

pg_6936.label: Have the officer(s) in charge sign off the completed entry and page.

pg_6937.label: Record any failure of oil filtering equipment in Oil Record Book Part I, and any failure of the oil discharge monitoring and control system in Part II.

pg_6938.label: Keep the Oil Record Book readily available on board for inspection at all reasonable times.

pg_6939.label: Preserve the Oil Record Book for three years after the last entry.

pg_6940.label: Allow the Secretary of State or authorised person to inspect, copy, and request certification of entries.

pg_6941.label: Perform inspections and certified copying as expeditiously as possible.

pg_6942.label: Discharge oil or oily mixture if necessary to secure the safety of the ship or to save life at sea.

pg_6943.label: Use only approved substances containing oil when combating specific pollution incidents to minimise pollution damage.

pg_6944.label: For an excepted ship within UK or controlled waters, document that any damage-caused discharge was caused by a person unconnected with the ship's business acting with intent, recklessness, or serious negligence.

pg_6945.label: Establish whether the damage was caused by a person not connected with the ship's business acting intentionally, recklessly, or with serious negligence (for UK excepted ships).

pg_6946.label: Confirm that neither owner nor master acted with intent to cause damage, or recklessly with knowledge that damage would probably result.

pg_6947.label: Identify who counts as a 'person connected with the ship's business' (seafarer, master, owner, cargo owner, classification society) when assessing fault under regulations 21 to 23.

pg_6948.label: Treat discharge of oil/oily mixtures from the cargo area as prohibited by default.

pg_6949.label: Before discharging outside a special area (except Arctic waters), confirm all conditions of regulation 34.1 of Annex I are satisfied.

pg_6950.label: For a voyage only partly within a special area, ensure the discharge occurs outside the special area (except Arctic waters) and that all regulation 34.1 Annex I conditions are met.

pg_6951.label: Within a special area, prohibit any discharge of oil or oily mixture from the cargo area, subject only to regulations 21 and 27 and paragraph (4).

pg_6952.label: Do not discharge oil or oily mixtures from machinery space unless an exception applies.
