pg_6953.label: For ships 400 GT and above, verify vessel's voyage type (outside special area, part in special area, or wholly in special area) and apply the corresponding condition set (Annex I reg 15.2 or 15.3) before any discharge.

pg_6954.label: For ships under 400 GT outside Antarctic/Arctic waters, apply conditions in regulation 15.6 of Annex I before discharge.

pg_6955.label: Never discharge oil or oily mixtures in the Antarctic area, regardless of other exceptions.

pg_6956.label: Retain oil residues on board for discharge to reception facilities if they cannot be discharged in compliance with regulation 15.

pg_6957.label: Report and cooperate with any investigation launched upon observed visible oil traces, providing wind/sea conditions, track/speed, and discharge records.

pg_6958.label: Determine ship size/description and identify which Annex I requirements apply to its machinery space.

pg_6959.label: Comply with regulation 12 (tanks for oil residues/sludge), regulation 12A paragraphs 1-11 (oil fuel tank protection), regulation 13 (standard discharge connection), regulation 14 paragraphs 1-3, 6 and 7 (oil filtering equipment), and regulation 16 (segregation of oil and water ballast and carriage of oil in forepeak tanks).

pg_6960.label: For ships under 400 GT, equip the vessel to retain oil/oily mixtures on board for discharge to reception facilities, or discharge in accordance with regulation 15.6 of Annex I.

pg_6961.label: Apply for or confirm any Secretary of State waiver of regulation 14.1/14.2 if operating exclusively in special areas/Arctic waters or meeting regulation 14.5.3 conditions.

pg_6962.label: On receipt of a report of visible oil traces near a ship, launch an investigation so far as reasonably practicable to determine if the regulation has been contravened.

pg_6963.label: Examine wind and sea conditions, the ship's track and speed, other possible sources of the oil traces, and relevant oil discharge records during the investigation.

pg_6964.label: Do not discharge chemicals/substances hazardous to the marine environment, or any substance intended to circumvent discharge conditions.

pg_6965.label: Retain on board any oil residues that cannot be discharged in compliance with regulation 34 of Annex I, for later discharge to reception facilities.

pg_6966.label: Until the IMO publishes/establishes special area status for the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, or Oman area, comply with regulations 25 and 26 discharge requirements as if the area were not a special area.

pg_6967.label: Do not carry in bulk as cargo, use as ballast, or carry/use as fuel any substance listed in regulation 43.1 of Annex I while in the Antarctic Area, unless engaged in ship safety or search and rescue operations.

pg_6968.label: Do not require tank or pipeline cleaning/flushing after prior carriage/use of the prohibited Antarctic substances.

pg_6969.label: Ensure the cargo area's construction, equipment, and operation comply with the applicable Annex I requirements for the tanker's size and description (regulations 18-28, 30, 33).

pg_6970.label: Check if the tanker qualifies for the regulation 18.6-18.8 exemption (delivered on or before 1 June 1982 under regulation 2.5 conditions, subject to regulation 2.6).

pg_6971.label: Apply for Secretary of State waiver of regulation 28.6 if the tanker is listed under regulation 3.6, ensuring loading complies with approved conditions and IMO guidelines.

pg_6972.label: Do not enter any UK port or offshore terminal if the ship operates under regulation 20.5 or regulation 21.5/6 provisions.

pg_6973.label: Do not conduct ship-to-ship transfer of heavy grade oil in UK territorial waters for ships operating under regulation 21.5/6 unless necessary for safety or life-saving.

pg_6974.label: Determine if the tanker is 150 GT or above and apply regulations 29, 31 and 32 of Annex I by default.

pg_6975.label: Check if the tanker qualifies for exemption under paragraph (2): exclusively UK port-to-port trade, voyages ≤72 hours, within 50nm of land.

pg_6976.label: If claiming paragraph (2) exemption, retain all oily mixtures on board for discharge to reception facilities and confirm Secretary of State has determined adequate facilities exist.

pg_6977.label: Check paragraph (3) exemptions for regulations 31 and 32 only: pre-1982 tankers ≥40,000 dwt in specified trades, or voyages within special areas, Arctic waters, or 50nm of land under UK trade or restricted 72-hour voyages.

pg_6978.label: For tankers under paragraph (3)(b)(iii), retain all oily mixtures on board, confirm Secretary of State has verified adequate reception facilities at loading ports/terminals, ensure IOPP/UKOPP Certificate is endorsed for the specific voyage category, and record quantity, time and port of discharge in the Oil Record Book.

pg_6979.label: Provide and maintain an Operations and Equipment Manual for the crude oil washing system.

pg_6980.label: Obtain Secretary of State approval of the Manual and ensure it contains all information set out in the regulation 33.2 specifications.

pg_6981.label: Revise the Manual whenever the COW system is altered, and submit the revision for Secretary of State approval.

pg_6982.label: Crude oil wash sufficient cargo tanks prior to each ballast voyage, accounting for trading pattern and expected weather, so ballast water is only put into washed tanks.

pg_6983.label: Operate the crude oil washing system in accordance with the Operations and Equipment Manual, unless the crude oil carried is unsuitable for washing.

pg_6984.label: Retain all oil residues and contaminated washings on board the ship.

pg_6985.label: Discharge all contaminated washings to shore reception facilities.

pg_6986.label: Record the total quantity of oil and water used for washing and returned to storage tanks in the Oil Record Book Part II.

pg_6987.label: If discharging effluent to sea instead of reception facilities, ensure adequate monitoring arrangements are in place.

pg_6988.label: For tankers carrying asphalt or similar products that inhibit product/water separation and monitoring, retain oil residues on board and discharge contaminated washings to reception facilities.

pg_6989.label: Equip the installation, so far as practicable, with the systems and tanks required by regulations 12 and 14 of Annex I.

pg_6990.label: Master must keep a record, in a form approved by the Secretary of State, of all operations involving oil or oily mixture discharges.

pg_6991.label: Prohibit discharge into the sea of oil or oily mixture except when oil content without dilution does not exceed 15 ppm.

pg_6992.label: Determine whether the installation qualifies as a fixed or floating production platform exempt under paragraph (2) by checking location (designated Continental Shelf Act 1964 area) and self-propulsion capability.

pg_6993.label: Assess platform status against paragraph (4) inclusions/exclusions (e.g., converted platforms, ceased production, well testing under 90 days).

pg_6994.label: Ensure the ship complies with Chapter 1 of Part II-A of the Polar Code.

pg_6995.label: Treat only machinery space discharges as 'discharges of oil or oily mixtures' under paragraphs (1)-(4); exclude production/displacement water and offshore processing drainage.

pg_6996.label: For FPSOs and floating storage units, assess compliance against the IMO Guidelines for the Application of the Revised MARPOL Annex I Requirements.

pg_6997.label: Ensure every oil tanker of 150 GT+ and every other ship of 400 GT+ carries a Secretary-of-State-approved SOPEP on board.

pg_6998.label: Prepare the SOPEP per IMO MEPC Guidelines for Development of Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plans, including reporting procedures, contact lists, immediate control actions, and coordination points of contact.

pg_6999.label: Where Annex II regulation 17 also applies, title the combined document 'Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan'.

pg_7000.label: For oil tankers of 5,000 tonnes deadweight or more, ensure prompt access to computerised shore-based damage stability and residual structural strength calculation programmes.

pg_7001.label: Serve a detention notice on the master of the ship when it is liable to be detained under paragraph (1) or (3).

pg_7002.label: Ensure the detention notice states the grounds of the detention.

pg_7003.label: Verify the ship carries a valid IOPP certificate (Appendix II, Annex I) or UKOPP certificate (regulation 13(3)).

pg_7004.label: Verify whether oil, oily mixture, or oil residue (sludge) has been discharged in violation of the Regulations.

pg_7006.label: Treat references to master/owner in section 145 of the 1995 Act as references to owner, manager, demise charterer or master for these regulations.

pg_7007.label: Where a harbour master has clear grounds to believe an offence under the listed regulations applies, exercise detention powers under section 144(1) of the 1995 Act, applying section 144(2) and (3) accordingly.

pg_7008.label: Comply with the terms of the notice until the ship is released by the harbour authority.

pg_7009.label: Harbour master must immediately release the ship if no proceedings are instituted, proceedings conclude without conviction, security/payment of £30,000 is provided, costs/fines are paid after conviction, or release is ordered under UNCLOS Article 292.

pg_7010.label: Harbour authority must repay any security sum or release security given if no proceedings are instituted within seven days of payment, or if proceedings conclude without conviction.

pg_7011.label: Release the ship immediately upon request of the owner, manager, demise charterer or master if no proceedings for the specified offences are instituted within the period, or if instituted proceedings conclude without conviction.

pg_7012.label: Carry out a review of the regulatory provisions contained in these Regulations.

pg_7013.label: Publish a report setting out the conclusions of the review before 1st March 2024, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding five years.

pg_7014.label: In the report, set out the objectives of the regulatory provisions, assess whether those objectives are achieved, assess whether the objectives remain appropriate, and if so assess if they could be achieved with less onerous regulation.

pg_7015.label: Determine whether the flag State, a polluted/threatened State, or UK waters are affected before continuing proceedings.

pg_7016.label: Allow the accused to raise a due diligence defence (took all reasonable steps to comply).

pg_7017.label: Allow a defence where the ship is non-UK, discharge occurred outside controlled/UK waters, and the ship is in a UK port only due to stress of weather or circumstances beyond control.

pg_7018.label: Conduct an initial survey before the ship is put into service or before a the other vessel is first issued.

pg_7019.label: Conduct a renewal survey to re-verify compliance with Part 3 equipment requirements.

pg_7020.label: Conduct an additional survey after any repair or renewal of sewage equipment.

pg_7021.label: Do not allow the ship to proceed to sea or remain at sea unless an initial or renewal survey has been carried out and a valid the other vessel is held.

pg_7022.label: Equip the ship in accordance with regulation 9 of Annex IV (sewage systems).

pg_7023.label: For ships constructed before 2 October 1983, equip so far as practicable to discharge sewage in accordance with regulation 7 (prohibition on discharge of sewage).

pg_7024.label: For UK ships, ensure the sewage treatment plant is of a type approved under the Merchant Shipping (Marine Equipment) Regulations.

pg_7025.label: For non-UK ships, obtain Secretary of State satisfaction that the treatment plant, comminuting/disinfecting system, or holding tank complies with Annex IV requirements.

pg_7026.label: Fit the sewage discharge pipeline with a standard discharge connection in accordance with regulation 10 of Annex IV.

pg_7027.label: Determine whether the ship is on a voyage inside or outside a MARPOL Annex IV special area.

pg_7028.label: If outside a special area, discharge sewage only in accordance with Part A of regulation 11 (applies to non-passenger ships everywhere and passenger ships outside special areas).

pg_7029.label: If a passenger ship operating in a special area from the relevant IMO-determined date, discharge only per Part B of regulation 11.

pg_7030.label: If a UK ship in polar waters, discharge sewage only in accordance with chapter 4, part II-A of the Polar Code.

pg_7031.label: Assess whether an exception applies: necessity for safety of ship/persons, saving life at sea, accidental discharge from damage (with reasonable precautions taken), or discharge under a foreign State's less stringent jurisdictional requirements.

pg_7032.label: If sewage is mixed with waste/waste water covered by another MARPOL Annex, apply this regulation in addition to the other Annex's requirements.

pg_7033.label: Carry out the requested survey of the Contracting State ship when asked by another Contracting State.

pg_7034.label: Issue a Sewage Certificate once the survey confirms compliance with Annex IV requirements and the applicable fee has been paid.

pg_7035.label: Transmit the issued Sewage Certificate and the survey report as soon as possible after survey completion.

pg_7036.label: Confirm a valid the other vessel has been issued under Annex IV before a Contracting State ship departs a UK port.

pg_7037.label: If no valid certificate exists, obtain surveyor confirmation that the ship can proceed without presenting an unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

pg_7038.label: If neither certificate nor surveyor satisfaction applies, obtain permission from a person with detention powers to proceed to the nearest appropriate repair yard.

pg_7039.label: For non-UK, non-Contracting State ships, ensure a surveyor's satisfaction or detention-authority permission before departure.

pg_7040.label: Ensure documentation from an initial or renewal survey is valid and on board before departure when relying on surveyor satisfaction or repair-yard permission.

pg_7041.label: Arrange for a renewal survey before each subsequent the other vessel is issued.

pg_7042.label: Issue a Sewage Certificate once the the other vessel is notified that a surveyor has carried out an initial or renewal survey and any required fee has been paid.

pg_7043.label: For a ship transferring to UK flag from another Contracting State, verify a valid existing Sewage Certificate, cause a new survey to be carried out, and confirm the ship's condition conforms to Annex IV requirements before issuing a new certificate.

pg_7044.label: Issue the Sewage Certificate in English.

pg_7045.label: If the Secretary of State requests another Contracting State to survey a UK ship and that State is satisfied of compliance, allow issuance or authorisation of the Sewage Certificate by that State.

pg_7046.label: Obtain approval from the Certifying Authority (or Secretary of State if certificate issued by another Contracting State) before making any change to structure, equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements or material after a required survey, except direct replacement.

pg_7047.label: (Certifying Authority) Initiate an investigation upon receiving a report to determine if an additional survey is needed, and carry it out if necessary.

pg_7048.label: (Certifying Authority) Where the ship is in a foreign port, take steps to ascertain that the port-state reporting requirement has been complied with.

pg_7049.label: Confirm it is proper and reasonable to grant the extension solely for the purpose of enabling the ship to reach the survey port.

pg_7050.label: Surveyor may endorse (extend) a Sewage Certificate after completing a renewal survey if satisfied the ship's structure, equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements and materials fully comply with Part 3 (equipment) requirements, and the new certificate cannot yet be issued or placed aboard.

pg_7051.label: Determine the Sewage Certificate's validity start date as the date of completion of the initial or renewal survey immediately preceding issue.

pg_7052.label: Owner must submit a request to the Secretary of State for a direction if seeking to rely on the original expiry date provisions, justify the request, and comply with any additional survey requirements imposed.

pg_7053.label: Treat the Sewage Certificate as invalid upon flag transfer, failed required survey, the ship proceeding to sea without meeting regulation requirements, issuance of a new certificate, cancellation by the Secretary of State, or reaching the expiry date.

pg_7054.label: Recognize that certificates issued or endorsed under the 2008 Sewage and Garbage Regulations remain valid under the new regulations until their original date of expiry.

pg_7055.label: Do not proceed to sea, or if already at sea do not remain at sea, unless an additional survey has been carried out.

pg_7056.label: Obtain the surveyor's issued survey report expressing satisfaction before the ship proceeds or remains at sea.

pg_7057.label: Secretary of State cancels the Sewage Certificate if issued on false/erroneous information or if post-survey damage/deficiency is found.

pg_7058.label: Secretary of State requires surrender of a Sewage Certificate that has expired, been suspended, or been cancelled.

pg_7059.label: Owner and master must keep the Sewage Certificate readily available on board for examination at all times, unless surrendered.

pg_7060.label: No person may alter, forge, falsify, or misuse a Sewage Certificate, or provide false survey information.

pg_7061.label: Surveyor notifies the Certifying Authority that issued the certificate that advice was given, and whether corrective action was taken.

pg_7062.label: Certifying Authority gives written notice of suspension to the owner, and to the port State authorities if the ship is in a foreign port.

pg_7063.label: Confirm the inspection purpose falls within the permitted scope: verifying illegal sewage discharge, crew unfamiliarity with pollution-prevention procedures, Sewage Certificate validity, or other required documentation validity.

pg_7064.label: Verify the ship's location before boarding: UK port, offshore terminal in UK/controlled waters, or a fixed/floating platform in UK/controlled waters (excluding platforms in transit).

pg_7065.label: If clear grounds exist that the ship's condition or equipment does not substantially match the Sewage Certificate or documentation, proceed to a more detailed inspection.

pg_7066.label: Notify the diplomatic representative or maritime authority of the ship's flag State, and any other Convention party that requested the inspection, when an inspection under this paragraph occurs.

pg_7067.label: Surveyor assesses whether clear grounds exist for one of the listed deficiencies (missing/invalid Sewage Certificate or documentation, non-conforming condition, crew unfamiliarity, or an offence).

pg_7068.label: Harbour master immediately notifies the Secretary of State upon suspecting a ship entering or leaving the harbour is non-compliant with the Regulations.

pg_7069.label: Apply the modified regulations where references to 'inspector' are read as references to the authority detaining the ship or the harbour master, as applicable.

pg_7070.label: Apply section 145 of the 1995 Act for interpretation purposes, treating 'owner, manager, demise charterer or master' as the relevant parties and treating offences under the regulation as equivalent to section 131 offences.

pg_7071.label: Determine whether the contravention occurred outside UK waters and involves a non-UK ship before applying this regulation.

pg_7072.label: Determine the mode of conviction (summary or indictment) and apply the corresponding fine under the regulation.

pg_7073.label: Where a foreign State (flag State or affected State) requests proceedings, or where the offence has caused/threatens pollution in UK waters, assess jurisdiction and, if proceedings are already underway, suspend them upon the foreign State's request.

pg_7074.label: Secretary of State to periodically review the regulatory provisions contained in these Regulations.

pg_7075.label: Report must set out objectives, assess achievement, assess continued appropriateness, and assess less onerous alternatives.

pg_7076.label: Verify each seafarer holds an appropriate certificate of competency or certificate of equivalent competency matching their listed category and capacity in Schedule 2.

pg_7077.label: Confirm the certificate is issued and endorsed in accordance with Part requirements and matches the ship's type, GT/power, propulsion, and the particular voyage.

pg_7078.label: Where a seafarer lacks an appropriate certificate, check whether they hold a valid third-party State certificate and have applied under regulation 37 or 38 for recognition.

pg_7079.label: Consider issuance or acceptance of an alternative certificate if consistent with STCW Regulation VII.

pg_7080.label: Confirm that the master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and any seafarer with cargo-operation responsibilities hold a certificate of proficiency in advanced training for the relevant tanker type (oil or chemical).

pg_7081.label: Obtain the certificate of proficiency from the Secretary of State (for those meeting STCW V/1-1 para 4 or 6 criteria) or from an approved training provider (for non-master/officer personnel meeting the same criteria).

pg_7082.label: For masters and officers, verify that the certificate of competency has been endorsed by the Secretary of State under regulation 34 as an alternative means of satisfying the certificate of proficiency requirement.

pg_7083.label: Verify engine room watchkeepers on ships with propulsion power 350-749kW hold either an engineering certificate of competency (reg. 7) or an approved marine engine operator's licence per specified MSN criteria.

pg_7084.label: Confirm GMDSS radio duty holders are at least 18 years old and have completed training meeting STCW Code section A-IV/2 standards before issuing a certificate of competency.

pg_7085.label: Ensure personnel assigned cargo or cargo equipment duties on oil/chemical tankers hold a certificate of proficiency in basic training for tanker cargo operations, issued either by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider per STCW Regulation V/1-1 paragraph 2.

pg_7086.label: For masters/officers on tankers, confirm the certificate of competency has been endorsed under regulation 34 in lieu of a separate certificate of proficiency.

pg_7087.label: Confirm that any officer or rating assigned cargo-related duties on a liquefied gas tanker holds a certificate of proficiency in basic training for liquefied gas tanker cargo operations.

pg_7088.label: Verify that any rating forming part of a navigational watch on a ship of 500 GT or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency.

pg_7089.label: Verify that any rating forming part of an engine-room watch, or designated for periodically unmanned engine-room duty, on a ship with main propulsion of 750 kW or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency.

pg_7090.label: Confirm able seafarer deck personnel on ships of 500 GT or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW II/5.

pg_7091.label: Confirm able seafarer engine personnel on ships with propulsion of 750 kW or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW III/5.

pg_7092.label: Confirm that any seafarer with designated safety duties related to fuel on an IGF Code ship holds a certificate of proficiency in basic training for IGF Code service.

pg_7093.label: Verify the certificate was issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider to a person meeting STCW Regulation V/3 paragraph 5 criteria.

pg_7094.label: Accept equivalent certification (regulation 13(2) or 14(3) liquefied gas tanker cargo training) as satisfying basic IGF Code training requirements where applicable.

pg_7095.label: Confirm that the master, engineer officers, and any seafarer with immediate responsibility for fuel/fuel systems on an IGF Code ship hold advanced training certification.

pg_7096.label: Verify advanced certificates were issued to persons meeting STCW Regulation V/3 paragraph 8 criteria, or accept basic liquefied gas tanker certification plus compliance with paragraph 9 alternative criteria as equivalent.

pg_7097.label: Confirm any seafarer designated to launch or take charge of a survival craft or rescue boat (non-fast) holds the relevant certificate of proficiency.

pg_7098.label: Confirm the ship security officer holds a certificate of proficiency for that role before assigning security duties.

pg_7099.label: Ensure only the Secretary of State or an approved training provider issues these certificates, and only to persons meeting the specified STCW criteria.

pg_7100.label: Ensure the seafarer completes required training per their capacity, duties and responsibilities before being assigned shipboard duties on a passenger ship.

pg_7101.label: Ensure master, each officer, and seafarers designated on muster lists to assist passengers complete crowd management training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 3).

pg_7102.label: Ensure seafarers providing direct service to passengers in passenger spaces complete safety training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 2).

pg_7103.label: Ensure master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and seafarers responsible for embarking/disembarking passengers, cargo operations, or hull opening closures on ro-ro passenger ships complete passenger safety, cargo safety and hull integrity training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 5).

pg_7104.label: Ensure master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and seafarers designated with responsibility for passenger safety in emergencies complete crisis management and human behaviour training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 4).

pg_7105.label: Ensure all seafarers on board complete passenger ship emergency familiarisation training appropriate to their role (STCW Code A-V/2 para 1).

pg_7106.label: Before assigning a seafarer to duties on a high speed craft built on/after 1 Jan 1996, ensure completion of type rating training per HSC Code para 18.3.3.

pg_7107.label: Obtain documentary evidence (certificate per MSN 1740(M) for masters/officers) from Secretary of State or approved training provider upon successful completion.

pg_7108.label: Before assigning any seafarer to shipboard duties, ensure they have received safety familiarisation and basic training per STCW Code section A-VI/1 and hold a certificate of proficiency.

pg_7109.label: Before designating a seafarer to control fire-fighting operations, ensure completion of advanced fire fighting training per STCW Code section A-VI/3 and issuance of corresponding certificate.

pg_7110.label: Ensure a seafarer designated for medical first aid meets STCW Code section A-VI/4 paragraphs 1-3 and holds a certificate of proficiency in medical first aid.

pg_7111.label: Confirm certificates of proficiency are issued only by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider to seafarers meeting the specified competence paragraphs.

pg_7112.label: Ensure seafarers with designated security duties meet STCW Code section A-VI/6 paragraphs 6-8 and hold a certificate of competency in security duties.

pg_7113.label: Submit application for a certificate or licence in the form specified by the Secretary of State, with the prescribed fee and evidence of identity, age, relevant service, standards of competence and certificates/qualifications held.

pg_7114.label: Submit applications for ancillary matters (e.g. certified copies) in the specified form with the prescribed fee, plus evidence of issue by the approved training provider where applicable.

pg_7115.label: Issue certificates of competency/proficiency in the form specified in STCW Code section A-I/2, paragraph 1.

pg_7116.label: Secretary of State approves seagoing service required by the STCW Convention in accordance with STCW Code section A-I/2, paragraph 5.

pg_7117.label: Provide any approval, alteration or cancellation of seagoing service approval in writing, specifying effective date and terms, with reasonable notice given for alteration/cancellation.

pg_7118.label: Accept electronic transmission of approvals/alterations/cancellations as satisfying the 'in writing' requirement, provided it is received in legible form and retrievable for subsequent reference.

pg_7119.label: Endorse certificates of competency issued under regulation 7 (officer qualification) and regulation 9 (GMDSS radiocommunication) and certificates of proficiency issued under regulations 10-14 (tanker training).

pg_7120.label: Format endorsements in accordance with STCW Regulation I/2.

pg_7121.label: Determine seafarer category (master/chief engineer officer, radio operator, or other) before considering exemption.

pg_7122.label: For master or chief engineer officer, confirm circumstances of force majeure exist.

pg_7123.label: For a radio operator, confirm the relevant Radio Regulations requirements are also met.

pg_7124.label: Verify the general conditions in paragraph (2): the exemption is necessary, poses no danger to persons/property/environment, and the seafarer is adequately qualified.

pg_7125.label: Confirm the seafarer is properly certificated for the post immediately below, or has clearly equivalent qualification/experience and passes an accepted test.

pg_7126.label: Specify the exemption duration: shortest possible period for master/chief engineer officer, or not exceeding six months for other categories.

pg_7127.label: Ensure the post is filled by a properly certificated holder as soon as possible.

pg_7128.label: Assess whether the ship's size and voyage conditions render full compliance with STCW II/3 (or regulations 15, 16, 27) unreasonable or impracticable.

pg_7129.label: Confirm the exemption does not pose a danger to other ships in the same waters, or to persons on board, the ship, property, or the marine environment.

pg_7130.label: Apply any additional terms the Secretary of State considers appropriate to the exemption.

pg_7131.label: Monitor and be prepared for the Secretary of State to alter or cancel the exemption.

pg_7132.label: Specify the effective date of the exemption, alteration, or cancellation.

pg_7133.label: Specify any terms attached to the exemption, alteration, or cancellation.

pg_7134.label: If using electronic transmission, ensure the text is received in legible form and capable of being retained for subsequent reference.

pg_7135.label: Secretary of State recognises an eligible EEA-issued certificate (master/officer/GMDSS radio operator competency, tanker cargo proficiency, or other proficiency certificate) issued under the Directive by an EEA State party to STCW.

pg_7136.label: On application of the certificate holder, issue a certificate of equivalent competency, subject to regulation 39(1) additional requirements.

pg_7137.label: For applicants performing management level functions, require demonstration of sufficient knowledge of relevant UK maritime legislation before issuing the certificate.

pg_7138.label: Allow the applicant to choose an adaptation period (up to three years, duration set by Secretary of State) instead of demonstrating UK legislation knowledge.

pg_7139.label: During the adaptation period, issue a certificate of equivalent competency of the next lower capacity that does not require UK maritime legislation knowledge.

pg_7140.label: Determine whether the issuing third party State was recognised before IP completion day under the prior EEA/EU framework.

pg_7141.label: If the certificate holder applies, issue a certificate of equivalent competency where the Secretary of State has recognised the underlying certificate.

pg_7142.label: If the third party State's standard only partially satisfies UK requirements, specify additional standards and means of demonstrating them before issuing equivalence.

pg_7143.label: Collect all relevant information to assess the party's training and certification systems.

pg_7144.label: Verify the party meets STCW Convention requirements and has taken measures to prevent certificate fraud.

pg_7145.label: Obtain an undertaking from the party to promptly notify any significant change in its training/certification arrangements.

pg_7146.label: Optionally inspect facilities and procedures as part of the assessment.

pg_7147.label: Once satisfied requirements are met, decide to recognise the party and recognise the specified certificates.

pg_7148.label: On application, issue a certificate of equivalent competency to a holder of a recognised certificate, applying any additional standards if the foreign standard only partially satisfies UK requirements.

pg_7149.label: Confirm the certificate holder meets medical fitness standards prescribed by the Medical Certification Regulations.

pg_7150.label: Confirm the certificate holder meets professional competency standards required by the STCW Convention and this Part (or paragraph 18.3.3 of the High Speed Craft Code for regulation 26 certificates).

pg_7151.label: For endorsements under regulation 34, verify the underlying certificate has not expired, been withdrawn, suspended or cancelled.

pg_7152.label: Check applicability of regulations 42 (revalidation) and 43 (refresher training) where relevant.

pg_7153.label: Confirm the applicant demonstrates adequate knowledge of the English language per STCW Code sections A-II/1, A-II/4, A-III/1 and A-IV/2 before issuing a certificate of equivalent competency.

pg_7154.label: Issue the certificate of equivalent competency in the form specified in STCW Code section A-I/2, paragraph 3.

pg_7155.label: Conduct an evaluation (potentially including inspection of facilities and procedures) of a party whose compliance with STCW Convention standards is in doubt.

pg_7156.label: If non-compliance indications arise, notify the party that recognition will be withdrawn six months after notification unless adequate corrective measures are taken.

pg_7157.label: After withdrawal, continue to honor certificates of equivalent competency issued prior to the withdrawal decision as valid, but do not issue higher-grade certificates based on that party's certification unless the officer qualifies solely through additional sea service.

pg_7158.label: Identify which certificate/endorsement type is held (paragraph (1)(a)-(e)).

pg_7159.label: Revalidate certificates under (1)(a)-(d) at intervals not exceeding five years.

pg_7160.label: Revalidate the high-speed craft certificate under (1)(e) at intervals not exceeding two years.

pg_7161.label: Establish continued professional competence per STCW Code section A-I/11 and MSN 1861 (M) Amendment 1 before revalidating (1)(a)-(d) certificates.

pg_7162.label: Establish continued professional competence per High Speed Craft Code paragraph 18.3.3 and MSN 1740 (M) before revalidating the (1)(e) certificate.

pg_7163.label: Submit a revalidation application in the specified form with the prescribed fee and evidence of identity, age, relevant service, standards of competence, and certificates/qualifications held.

pg_7164.label: Identify seafarers holding certificates of proficiency in the listed competencies (survival, firefighting, rescue boats, IGF Code training).

pg_7165.label: Ensure each such seafarer completes approved refresher training at intervals not exceeding five years.

pg_7166.label: Ensure the master and any seafarer designated for medical care completes approved refresher training every five years for that designation.

pg_7167.label: Ensure seafarers serving on passenger ships (international voyages) or high-speed craft complete refresher training every five years relating to their required qualifications.

pg_7168.label: Submit an application to the Secretary of State for a certified copy of a lost/deprived certificate using the specified form.

pg_7169.label: Include the prescribed fee with the application.

pg_7170.label: If the certificate is a certificate of proficiency from an approved training provider, attach evidence of its original issue.

pg_7171.label: Registrar maintains a register of certificates and endorsements issued under this Part.

pg_7172.label: On request from an EEA State, third party State, or an employing/prospective employing company, Registrar provides relevant register information.

pg_7173.label: A person wishing to provide seafarer training/assessment must apply for approval by the Secretary of State.

pg_7174.label: Demonstrate qualifications/experience under STCW Code Section A-I/6, meet relevant Merchant Shipping Notices, and pay the prescribed fee.

pg_7175.label: Suspend or cancel a certificate where the holder is convicted under section 47(5) or conditions for issue/endorsement were not met.

pg_7176.label: Give written notice to the applicant/holder before refusing, revalidating-refusing, suspending, or cancelling a certificate.

pg_7177.label: Require approved training providers to give written notice when refusing to issue/revalidate a certificate of proficiency or refusing documentary evidence under regulations 26 or 49(2).

pg_7178.label: Allow the applicant to request, before a specified date, that the refusal/suspension/cancellation be reviewed at an inquiry.

pg_7179.label: Treat a failure by the Secretary of State to issue/revalidate or give notice within 28 days of application as a deemed refusal, giving the applicant a further 28 days to demand an inquiry in writing.

pg_7180.label: Hold an inquiry by one or more appointed persons when an applicant has required a review under paragraph (4) or (5).

pg_7181.label: Grant approval under paragraph (2) for a maximum of five years from the date in the approval letter.

pg_7182.label: Extend approval in increments of up to five years only if the provider still meets paragraph (2)(a)-(b) requirements and has paid the prescribed fee.

pg_7183.label: Alter, suspend or cancel an approval or extension only after giving reasonable notice.

pg_7184.label: Issue all approvals, extensions, alterations, suspensions or cancellations in writing, specifying effective date and terms.

pg_7185.label: Give written notice to the applicant if intending to refuse approval or an extension.

pg_7186.label: Require the approved provider to continue complying with paragraph (2)(a)-(b) requirements throughout the approval's validity.

pg_7187.label: Require surrender of the approval letter or certificate if directed by the Secretary of State.

pg_7188.label: Monitor and periodically evaluate approved training providers per STCW Regulation I/8 and relevant Merchant Shipping Notices.

pg_7189.label: Request the Secretary of State to hold an inquiry within 21 days of receiving notice of the decision and before the date specified in the notice.

pg_7190.label: Secretary of State must cause an inquiry to be held by one or more appointed persons once validly requested.

pg_7191.label: Do not offer or provide training or assessment of seafarers for certification under this Part without a Secretary of State approval.

pg_7192.label: Do not advertise or display an expired or unissued approval.

pg_7193.label: Surrender approval letter or approval certificate when required under paragraph (11).

pg_7194.label: Issue a certificate of proficiency in the form specified in STCW Code Section A-I/2 to every person who successfully completes required training/assessment, except for master/officer tanker training under regulations 10-14.

pg_7195.label: Issue documentary evidence (rather than a certificate) to masters/officers completing training under regulations 7-16, 25, or 43.

pg_7196.label: Master ensures navigational, engineering and radio watchkeeping arrangements are adequate at all times.

pg_7197.label: Master gives directions to deck watchkeeping officers for safe navigation during their duty periods.

pg_7198.label: Chief engineer officer ensures engineering watchkeeping arrangements are adequate for a safe watch.

pg_7199.label: Master arranges an appropriate and effective watch when ship is safely moored or anchored in port.

pg_7200.label: Ensure electronic transmission of exemption documents is legible and retrievable for subsequent reference.

pg_7201.label: Comply with any safety requirements attached to an exemption under paragraph (2).

pg_7202.label: Ensure a safe manning document is in force for the ship and kept on board at all times.

pg_7203.label: Maintain manning at or above the levels specified in the safe manning document.

pg_7204.label: Master must not allow the ship to proceed to sea unless a valid safe manning document is on board and manning complies with it.

pg_7205.label: Company applying for a safe manning document must submit proposed numbers and grades of seafarers to the Secretary of State in the specified form.

pg_7206.label: Secretary of State issues the document only if proposals meet IMO Resolution A.1047(27) principles and the fee is paid.

pg_7207.label: Company must notify the Secretary of State as soon as any pertinent circumstances change.

pg_7208.label: Confirm the hovercraft falls within scope (UK-registered, constructed on/after 1 Jan 1996) before applying Part requirements.

pg_7209.label: Ensure every seafarer on board meets the specified standards of competence to be qualified under section 47 of the Act (manning).

pg_7210.label: Owner must ensure the seafarer has completed training specified in paragraph 18.3.3 of the High Speed Craft Code (type rating training).

pg_7211.label: Training provider must issue documentary evidence to each person who successfully completes the training.

pg_7212.label: For masters/officers, issue a certificate in the form specified in Merchant Shipping Notice 1740(M), endorsed as specified.

pg_7213.label: Apply regulations 31-34, 41, 42, 44, 45, and 46 to hovercraft certificates as they apply to Part 2 certificates.

pg_7214.label: Apply regulations 48-50 to training providers delivering type rating training under regulation 51(3).

pg_7215.label: Owner may apply to the Secretary of State for an exemption from regulation 51 requirements if compliance is impracticable or unreasonable.

pg_7216.label: If an exemption is granted, comply with any additional safety requirements imposed by the Secretary of State.

pg_7217.label: For ships carrying hazardous cargo in bulk, ensure a safe deck watch and safe engineering watch are maintained via ready availability of duly qualified officer(s) and ratings as needed.

pg_7218.label: For ships carrying hazardous cargo other than in bulk, organise watchkeeping arrangements accounting for the nature, quantity, packing and stowage of the cargo and any special conditions on board, afloat, and ashore.

pg_7219.label: Apply the principles and requirements of Merchant Shipping Notice 1868 (M) Amendment 1 when setting watchkeeping arrangements.

pg_7220.label: If seeking relief from Part requirements, apply for exemption from the Secretary of State, who may grant it if compliance is impracticable or unreasonable.

pg_7221.label: Comply with any safety requirements attached to an exemption; note exemption automatically ceases if those requirements are not met.

pg_7222.label: Ensure any exemption, alteration, or cancellation is documented in writing (including electronic form that is legible and retrievable for subsequent reference), specifying effective date and terms.

pg_7223.label: Ensure every seafarer holds an appropriate certificate for any function they perform on the ship.

pg_7224.label: Ensure seafarers have completed training specified in Part 2 or Part 3 relevant to their function.

pg_7225.label: Maintain and keep readily available documentation on seafarer experience, training, medical fitness, and competency.

pg_7226.label: Provide written instructions to the master setting out policies/procedures for familiarizing newly employed officers and ratings before assigning duties.

pg_7227.label: Allocate a reasonable period for new crew to become acquainted with specific equipment and ship-specific watchkeeping, safety, environmental protection, and emergency procedures.

pg_7228.label: Designate a knowledgeable crew member to ensure new officers/ratings receive essential information in a language they understand.

pg_7229.label: Master and designated crew member must carry out their familiarization obligations.

pg_7230.label: Carry all original certificates and documents on board at all times (per Part 2/3 for UK-registered ships, or STCW Convention for non-UK ships).

pg_7231.label: Secretary of State evaluates whether proposed alternative training arrangements meet the equivalence condition in paragraph (2).

pg_7232.label: Issue approval, continuation, alteration, or cancellation in writing.

pg_7233.label: Specify in the written approval the effective date and any terms attached.

pg_7234.label: Provide reasonable notice before continuing, altering, or cancelling an approval.

pg_7235.label: Transmit written approvals electronically if the output is received in legible form and can be retained for subsequent reference.

pg_7236.label: Inspect the non-UK registered ship to verify that seafarers required to be certificated hold valid STCW certificates.

pg_7237.label: Assess the ability of seafarers to maintain required watchkeeping standards where grounds exist based on a qualifying port incident.

pg_7238.label: If a deficiency is found, notify the master of the ship and the ship's flag administration in writing.

pg_7239.label: Ensure the ship carries a valid safe manning document as required by regulation 55.

pg_7240.label: Maintain proper watchkeeping arrangements at sea and in port, including for ships carrying hazardous cargo.

pg_7241.label: Fulfil master's and crew's responsibilities under regulation 61 and carry all required documents under regulation 62.

pg_7242.label: As owner, ensure hovercraft personnel receive required type rating training per regulation 51(3).

pg_7243.label: Notify the master of the deficiency pursuant to regulation 64(2).

pg_7244.label: Determine whether the deficiency remains uncorrected and poses danger to persons, property or the marine environment, or whether an exemption term has been breached.

pg_7245.label: Apply section 284(1) of the Act to determine who may release the ship and under what conditions.

pg_7246.label: Allow reference of the detention notice to arbitration under section 96, subject to modifications (certain subsections omitted).

pg_7247.label: Treat any certificate of competency, equivalent competency, proficiency, marine engine operator's licence, or type rating training certificate issued under the 2015 Regulations as valid and issued under the new Regulations.

pg_7248.label: Treat any EEA State or third party State certificate recognition made under 2015 Regulations regulation 32/33 as a recognition under the new Regulations' regulation 36/37.

pg_7249.label: Treat any party recognised under 2015 Regulations regulation 33A as recognised under new Regulations regulation 38.

pg_7250.label: Treat any training provider approval or documentary evidence issued under 2015 Regulations regulations 41 or 42 as issued under the corresponding new Regulations (regulations 48, 26(3), 49(2), or 51(4)).

pg_7251.label: Publish a report setting out the conclusions of the review.

pg_7252.label: Publish the first report before the end of five years from the Regulations coming into force, and subsequent reports at intervals not exceeding five years.

pg_7253.label: Ensure each report sets out the objectives of the regulatory provision, assesses achievement and continued appropriateness of those objectives, and considers less onerous alternatives.

condition: Detention requires clear grounds of contravention of the ISM Regulations.

condition: Rule 5 of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGS) requires a proper lookout at all times by sight and hearing as well as by all available means.

pitfalls: Sleeping while on watch is a direct violation of the lookout requirement under Rule 5.

condition: Once a give-way vessel has signaled/committed to an alteration (e.g., to starboard), the stand-on/other vessel's subsequent maneuvers must not contradict or conflict with that committed action.

guidance: This was judged the only effective action to avoid collision once the other vessel closed to less than 0.5nm on a near-reciprocal track.
pitfalls: A vessel that appears to be safely crossing ahead with an acceptable CPA can suddenly alter course and create an extreme close-quarters situation.

condition: LED bulb must only be used in all-round light fittings, not in sectored/directional navigation lights.
Cut-off accuracy for tricolour masthead lights is compromised to approximately plus/minus 20 degrees with these bulbs, versus the sharp cut-off expected for compliant navigation lights.
guidance: All-round lights have no sector cut-off requirement, so the lack of a defined cut-off point in the LED bulb is not hazardous in that application.
pitfalls: Dual light segments can be seen up to a 40 degree horizontal range on a tricolour masthead light fitted with these LED bulbs.
Bicolour bow lights and single sidelights show a similar 20 degree visual overlap, creating ambiguous colour presentation.
This is clearly a serious accident situation waiting to happen, as another vessel may stand into danger attempting to interpret or avoid the ambiguous light.

condition: The give-way vessel must act early and substantially, so far as possible (Rule 16).

guidance: An earlier alteration to starboard would have been prudent, as identified in the yachtsman's Lessons Learned.

Failure to see a vessel's lights in good visibility and smooth sea calls into question the effectiveness of the lookout maintained.

condition: NUC status under ColReg Rule 3 requires an 'exceptional circumstance' -- a rare or extraordinary event, not routine engine stoppage.

condition: Munitions must never be handled by crew or untrained personnel.

guidance: Only qualified experts can safely assess and deal with the hazard.

condition: Pilot ladder arrangements must fully comply with SOLAS requirements.

condition: All training boat launches must use fall preventer devices (FPDs).

pitfalls: Incorrectly fitted lifting strops can cause an unstable, rotating lift of a rescue boat.

condition: Lifting strops must be attached to the strongpoints on the transom, not the hull.

condition: Own-ship action must remain in accordance with COLREGS even when taking independent avoiding action.

condition: Rule 13(c) applies when doubt exists as to whether a vessel is overtaking.

condition: A visual lookout must be maintained on the other vessel for navigation lights to be effective.
Radar reflectors only aid detection if the other vessel's radar is switched on and actively monitored.
AIS transponders, while prudent, are not infallible and do not guarantee detection.
guidance: To alert the other vessel to the near miss, even though no reply was received.
pitfalls: A vessel with clear navigation lights and good radar echo can still become effectively invisible to another vessel if that vessel lacks a proper visual/radar lookout.
Modern wheelhouses full of electronic screens can create light pollution that renders visual lookout almost impossible unless care is taken.
Mariners should always hope for the best but plan for the worst, as any voyage carries risk of encountering a vessel that fails to comply with Colregs due to poor seamanship.

Specific vessel categories must use the prescribed substitute signal instead of the general power-driven vessel signals.
guidance: Provides an audible indication of an anchored vessel's position and length category to approaching traffic.
pitfalls: Failure to sound the correct signal for vessel status/type in restricted visibility may lead to collision risk due to misidentification by other vessels.

condition: Bell/gong signal exemptions apply only to vessels under 20 metres in length.
Vessels exempted from bell signals must still signal at intervals of not more than 2 minutes using some other efficient method.
Aground vessel signal must include the distinct bell strokes before and after rapid ringing, not just the standard anchor bell signal.
guidance: Distinguishes an aground vessel's signal from a vessel merely at anchor.
pitfalls: Failure to give required or substitute sound signals in restricted visibility increases collision risk with approaching vessels.
Vessels aground must distinguish their signal from anchored vessels to avoid confusion.

condition: Height above the hull must be measured vertically from beneath the light's location to the uppermost continuous deck.
Forward/sole masthead light height on vessels ≥20m: minimum 6m, scaled to breadth if >6m, capped at 12m.
After masthead light must be at least 4.5m higher than forward light when two are carried.
guidance: Ensures the light is high enough to be visible over the vessel's own structure and proportionate to its size, while capping excessive height.

condition: Height above the hull must be measured vertically from beneath the light's location to the uppermost continuous deck.
Forward/sole masthead light height on vessels ≥20m: minimum 6m, scaled to breadth if >6m, capped at 12m.

condition: Height above the hull must be measured vertically from beneath the light's location to the uppermost continuous deck.

condition: Masthead light horizontal distance must be ≥ half the vessel's length but ≤ 100 m.

condition: Vessel length thresholds (20 m, 50 m) determine applicable spacing and height values.

condition: Masthead/all-round light must be at least 1 metre higher than sidelights when carried together with sternlight.
Lowest after masthead light (if on aftermast) must be at least 4.5 metres higher than forward masthead light for towing vessels.
Masthead lights must be above and clear of all other lights/obstructions except as permitted by subparagraph (ii).
guidance: Maintains correct visual signalling of towing configuration and vessel orientation.
pitfalls: Improper light placement may cause interference between sidelights and deck lights, obscuring correct vessel aspect.
Failure to maintain required vertical separations can cause other vessels to misread a vessel's status or towing configuration.

condition: K (atmospheric transmissivity) shall be 0.8 for prescribed lights, corresponding to ~13 nautical miles meteorological visibility.
Maximum luminous intensity must be limited to avoid undue glare.
Limiting of maximum luminous intensity shall not be achieved by variable control of the luminous intensity.
guidance: Ensures lights meet the prescribed luminous range for safe detection by other vessels.
pitfalls: Do not use variable control of luminous intensity to limit glare; this is prohibited.

condition: Minimum intensity must be maintained from 5° above to 5° below horizontal for all vessel types.

guidance: Non-electric lights cannot be engineered as precisely as electric ones but must still approximate the safety standard.

All-round lights must not be obscured over more than 6 degrees, except anchor lights per Rule 30.
guidance: Guarantees consistent visibility within the prescribed arc while allowing a defined tapering margin.
pitfalls: All-round lights must not be obscured by masts, topmasts, or structures within angular sectors of more than 6 degrees, except permitted anchor lights.

condition: Outlying gear light must be 2-6 metres horizontally from the all-round red and white lights.

Frequencies of whistles in a combined system must differ by at least 10 Hz from each other.

pitfalls: Improperly spaced or simultaneously sounded whistles more than 100 m apart can cause misleading sound signals.
Obstructions can create zones of greatly reduced whistle signal level if not addressed with a combined system.

condition: The basic principles in this Section shall at least be taken into account by all ships.

condition: Applicant must be at least 18 years old.

condition: A transfer must be between a vessel's cargo tank and a shore facility or another vessel, not an internal tank shift.

condition: Evidence must come from the owner, operator, or Master of a tankship or self-propelled tank vessel.
Cargo classification (DL or LG) must be specified in the evidence.

condition: Applicant must hold the specified base national endorsement before pursuing the limited Advanced Oil Tanker Cargo Operations endorsement.

condition: Must already hold a national endorsement as Tank Vessel-Engineer to use the (c) pathway.

condition: Applies only between two sailing vessels (not power-driven vessels).
Vessels must be in sight of one another per Section II.

condition: Applies only to power-driven vessels crossing with risk of collision.

condition: Applies only when vessels are in sight of one another (Section II context).
Own-ship must be the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.

pitfalls: Delaying maneuver until close TCPA (e.g. 90 seconds) violates the spirit of Rule 16 even if collision is still technically avoidable.

condition: Applies only when vessels are in sight of one another (Section II context).

condition: Applies specifically to two power-driven vessels

Ambiguous bearing situations must default to overtaking assumption.

condition: Stand-on vessel must not maneuver merely because another vessel is approaching.

Avoid turning to port toward a vessel on own ship's port side if room exists to do otherwise.

condition: Stand-on vessel must not maneuver merely because another vessel is approaching.

condition: Stand-on vessel must not maneuver merely because another vessel is approaching.

condition: Applies only outside narrow-channel, TSS, and overtaking exceptions.
Vessel status must be identifiable (e.g., via day shapes like diamond-over-two-balls for RAM).

condition: Applies only outside narrow-channel, TSS, and overtaking exceptions.

Hierarchy order: NUC/RAM > fishing > sailing > power-driven, with draught-constrained receiving special but not top-tier consideration.
guidance: Draught-constrained vessels receive consideration from all except NUC/RAM, but are not equivalent to NUC/RAM priority.
pitfalls: Do not rely solely on crossing-angle geometry to determine stand-on/give-way status; vessel type hierarchy can override it.
Failing to recognize a RAM or NUC vessel's shapes/lights could lead to incorrect right-of-way assumptions and collision risk.

condition: Applies only when vessels are not in sight of one another in or near restricted visibility.
No vessel has stand-on privileges under this rule.
Avoid turning to port for a contact forward of the beam unless overtaking.
guidance: Early action reduces the chance of a close-quarters situation developing.
pitfalls: Do not alter course to port for a vessel forward of the beam unless overtaking it.
Do not alter course toward a vessel abeam or abaft the beam.
Failure to slow or stop when a close-quarters situation cannot be avoided can lead to collision.

condition: Lights must be shown from sunset to sunrise and during restricted visibility during the day.
Shapes apply only during daylight hours.
Minimum light visibility range scales with vessel length (e.g., 50m+ vessel: 6 nm masthead light; sub-12m vessel: 2 nm).
guidance: Shapes are a daytime-only substitute/complement to night lights.
pitfalls: A masthead light visible from less distance than required for the vessel's size class may indicate an equipment fault, not merely a conditions-related shortfall.

condition: Lights must be shown from sunset to sunrise and during restricted visibility during the day.
Shapes apply only during daylight hours.

condition: Lights must be shown from sunset to sunrise and during restricted visibility during the day.

pitfalls: A masthead light visible from less distance than required for the vessel's size class may indicate an equipment fault, not merely a conditions-related shortfall.

condition: Masthead light is mandatory for power-driven vessels underway (except small vessel exception).
Second masthead light required only if vessel is 50 m or more in length.
Vessels under 12 m may use a single all-round white light plus sidelights instead of masthead/stern light combination.
guidance: Larger power-driven vessels must show an additional masthead light to indicate size/aspect.
pitfalls: Absence of a masthead light on an underway vessel at night should not be assumed to indicate malfunction; it may indicate the vessel is a sailing vessel, not power-driven.

condition: Tricolour lantern combination option only applies to vessels under 20 m.
A vessel under both sail and engine power must be treated as power-driven, not as a sailing vessel.
Cone shape must be displayed apex down, forward, when motor-sailing.
guidance: Rule 25 permits a simplified lighting option for smaller sailing vessels.
pitfalls: Failing to show power-driven lights/shape while motor-sailing misrepresents vessel status and risks collision due to incorrect right-of-way assumptions by other vessels.

condition: Three masthead lights (instead of two) apply only when the tow exceeds 200 m in length.
The towed vessel/object must independently display sidelights and a sternlight.
A diamond shape is required on the tow only when the tow length exceeds 200 m.
guidance: Signals specifically that the tow is a long tow exceeding 200 m, warning other vessels to keep extra clearance.
pitfalls: Misreading the number of masthead lights could cause a vessel to underestimate the length of the tow and pass too close.
Failure to display correct towing lights/shapes creates collision risk by misleading other vessels about the vessel's status.

condition: Trawling vessels must show green-over-white all-round lights or two cones point-to-point by day.
Vessels fishing with other gear must show red-over-white lights instead of green-over-white.
An extra white light is required only if outlying gear extends more than 150 m from the vessel.
guidance: Rule 26 distinguishes trawling from other fishing methods using a different light color combination.
pitfalls: Misidentifying trawling vs. other-gear fishing vessels can lead to incorrect assumptions about gear direction and length, increasing collision/entanglement risk.
Fixed-direction gear from non-trawling fishing vessels may extend well beyond the vessel's hull, posing a navigational hazard not evident from the hull's heading alone.

condition: Anchored vessel light configuration depends on whether length is under or 50 m and above.

condition: Signal pattern must be repeated every 2 minutes as specified.
Special-category vessels use the same signal (one prolonged plus two short) whether or not they are making way.
Power-driven vessels must differentiate their signal based on making-way status (one vs two prolonged blasts).

pitfalls: Ship must not be put into or continue in service past the applicable date without a valid initial survey certificate.

condition: Applies only to ships to which this regulation applies (per Part 3 scope).

condition: Ship must not proceed or remain at sea after the annual survey period ends unless survey and endorsement requirements (paragraph 2) are met.

pitfalls: A ship must not proceed to sea or remain at sea without a valid survey and endorsement for the relevant period, which would constitute a breach of the regulation.

condition: Certificate validity cannot exceed five years from the date of completion of the initial or renewal survey.
Renewal survey completed in the final three-month period or after expiry must result in a new certificate valid only up to five years from the prior certificate's expiry date.
The 'final three month period' is defined as the three months ending on the certificate's expiry date.
guidance: Ensures the receiving flag State has the necessary documentation to assess the ship's compliance history.
pitfalls: A certificate ceases to be valid if required repairs/renewals under regulation 10(1) are made without complying with regulation 10(3), even if the certificate has not formally expired.
Failure to complete a required survey or endorse the certificate per the Regulations invalidates the certificate regardless of its stated expiry date.

condition: Extension under paragraph (1) requires that the survey under regulation 7 or 8 has been carried out.
Endorsement-based extension under paragraph (3) cannot exceed five months from the original expiry date.
Extension under paragraph (4) cannot exceed three months and is granted solely to allow the ship to reach its port of survey.
guidance: Restores the standard five-year certification cycle while anchoring it to the original expiry date rather than the actual issuance date.
pitfalls: A ship must not leave its port of survey after a paragraph (4) extension until a new appropriate certificate has been issued.
Multiple extensions cannot be stacked (paragraph 6 extension barred if already extended under paragraph 1, 3, or 4).

condition: New certificate validity must not exceed five years from the date of completion of the renewal survey.

guidance: Maintains an auditable record on the certificate itself of any extension or required endorsement.

condition: Flue gas outlet temperature must be monitored at all times.

pitfalls: Do not feed waste into a continuous-feed incinerator below 850°C.
Do not operate a batch-loaded incinerator if it fails to reach 600°C within 5 minutes of start-up.
